_about: Lists used by the travel generator. Each travel day rolls weather, a Survival check to keep the way (or get lost), an encounter check and an event check. Add events to any category's 'events' list: each needs a 'name' and 'text'. Optional fields: 'terrains' (only rolled there), 'when' ('day' or 'night'), 'lose' (days of food the party loses), 'link' ('npc', 'market' or 'loot' adds a button or a find), 'twist' (a second line), 'progress' (extra days of distance, like 0.5) and 'check' (what the players roll), 'pass' and 'fail' (days of distance gained or lost on a success or failure, like 0.5 or -0.25), 'failText', 'cost', 'ride' ({name, miles a day, days, flies}: a faster way to travel, starting the next day), 'next' ('advantage' on tomorrow's Survival check, or 'safe' for no encounter check tomorrow). Ambushes are fought by the monsters in 'ambushers', or an ambush's own 'foes'. Events happen in the day unless 'when' says 'night' or 'any'. In text, {npc}, {place}, {faction}, {church} and {hook} are filled from your own wiki and saved hooks. 'rankSpeed' is how much faster each rank travels on foot; travel modes marked 'rank' use it. 'circles' is the teleport circle network: every capital and city has a circle (add other places by name to 'places', or turn one on or off from its World map entry), and 'fee' is the price per traveller in gp of spirit coins. Events may also carry: 'tone' (simple, creepy, interesting, weird, odd, rewarding, feel-good, magical, funny or grim; the Mood setting weights these), 'rarity' (common, uncommon at half the chance, or rare at a fifth, and once a campaign), 'weather' and 'magic' (only rolled in those), 'rank' (only for parties of those ranks), 'ref' (nod, riff or outworlder) with a DM-only 'nod' note, 'npc': true (the person gets a page under Minor NPCs), 'then' ({name, after: [min, max] days}: a follow-up event, marked 'follow': true, that comes later in the same journey), and 'twist': false. Terrains may say 'land' or 'sea'. A ride's 'travels' is sea (coast and open sea), river (delta and marsh, or the event's own terrains), land (anywhere but open sea), air or astral (anywhere); it is only offered where it can go, and ends when the terrain changes to one it can't cross. Text may use {a|b|c} to pick one option, or {iron:...|bronze:...} to pick by the party's rank.

replace: A Society director of Gold rank, passing the party, lets their aura brush over them in greeting. Everyone feels stronger, and very small.
A Society director of Gold rank, passing the party, nods to them in greeting, and the weight of that much power in one person makes everyone feel very small.
An invisible weight presses on everyone: a Gold-ranker's aura, from miles away. Normal-rank animals lie flat. Whatever caused it is {very angry|grieving|fighting something}, and very far off.

The ground shudders and the sky flashes from somewhere miles away: a Gold-ranker fighting at full strength. Normal-rank animals lie flat. Whatever caused it is {very angry|grieving|fighting something}, and very far off.

terrains.name: Road
scenery: Milestones carved with the distance to the next town, half of them wrong.
A waystation well with a tin cup on a chain.
Cart ruts deep enough to twist an ankle.
A shrine at a crossroads, its offering bowl full of iron coins.

terrains.name: Farmland
scenery: Raised fields of rice, and farmers who stop to watch you pass.
A scarecrow wearing an old Adventure Society badge.
Irrigation channels glinting in long straight lines.
Dogs bark from every farmstead you pass.

terrains.name: Delta and marsh
scenery: Mist on the channels until noon.
Reed beds taller than a mounted rider.
A green-stone boat drifts past, empty and tied to nothing.
Frogs fall silent all at once, then start again.

terrains.name: Forest
scenery: Light through the canopy in long green bars.
A tree marked with three claw scores at head height.
Mushrooms in a perfect ring, and nobody wants to step inside it.
Birdsong that stops when you stop.

terrains.name: Desert
scenery: Heat shimmer that turns the horizon to water.
Bleached bones of something very large, half buried.
A night so cold the waterskins grow a skin of ice.
Wind-carved rock like a row of kneeling giants.

terrains.name: Steppe
scenery: Grass to the horizon in every direction, moving like the sea.
The ring of a Host's old camp, the grass grown waist-high inside it.
A greatback's footprints, each one a small pond.
A ruined town wall standing alone in the grass.

terrains.name: Mountains
scenery: A path cut into the cliff, barely a shoulder wide.
Clouds below you, filling the valley like milk.
A rope bridge older than anyone who crosses it.
Huge birds circling the peak above, patient.

terrains.name: Jungle
scenery: Air so thick with water it is like breathing soup.
A vine as thick as a man's waist, moving very slowly.
Flowers the size of shields that close as you pass.
The noise never stops, day or night.

terrains.name: Coast
scenery: Mudflats at low tide, glittering with crabs.
A fishing village's boats pulled up in a neat row.
Mangroves with roots like grasping fingers.
Gulls fighting over something washed up on the beach.

terrains.name: Open sea
scenery: Nothing but water and sky from one horizon to the other.
Dolphins riding the bow wave all morning.
A sky ship far above, going the other way.
Phosphorescence in the wake after dark.

weather.name: Wind
weather.text: A hard wind all day; hearing is difficult at range.

weather.name: Rain
weather.text: Steady rain. Tracks wash out and everything gets wet.

weather.name: Fog
weather.text: Thick fog. Sight is 30 feet until midday at least.

weather.name: Storm
weather.text: A storm rolls in. Travel is miserable and shelter is worth looking for.

weather.name: Heat
weather.text: Punishing heat. Anyone in heavy armour makes a DC 10 Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.

weather.name: Cold
weather.text: Bitter cold. Without warm gear, a DC 10 Constitution save or gain a level of exhaustion.

weather.name: Magic squall
weather.text: The air prickles with loose magic. Spells cast today behave oddly once on a natural 1.

circles.runBy: the Church of the Journey and the Magic Society

paces.name: Slow
paces.text: Advantage on the Survival check, and the party can move stealthily.

paces.name: Fast
paces.text: -5 to the Survival check and to passive Perception.

events.name: Fresh spawn
events.text: The monsters are minutes old, still confused, standing on a natural array thick with magic.

events.name: Driven out
events.text: They are fleeing something stronger.
events.twist: Whatever drove them arrives two rounds into the fight.

events.name: Too close to the den
events.text: The road passes too near their den. They defend it rather than hunt, and won't chase far.

events.name: Someone else's fight
events.text: They are already attacking someone else when the party arrives: a farmer, a caravan, or another team.

events.name: Rising magic
events.text: One of them is far stronger than it should be: a sign the local magic is rising.

events.name: Night raid
events.text: They come in the dark. The watch-keeper's passive Perception decides who is surprised.

events.name: Stalkers
events.text: They have been following the party for an hour, waiting for a gap in the line.

events.name: From the water
events.text: They burst out of the water at a crossing.

events.name: Nesting season
events.text: The monsters are guarding a clutch of {eggs|young|cocoons} in a hollow beside the path. Back away and they let you go; step closer and they fight to the death.

events.name: Already wounded
events.text: The monsters are bleeding from fresh wounds before the party lands a blow.
events.twist: The adventurers who wounded them are hiding nearby, hoping the party finishes the job so they can claim the cores.

events.name: Lured by cooking
events.text: The smell of the party's lunch draws them in. They go for the cooking pot first and the cook second.

events.name: Herded
events.text: The monsters arrive in a tight, unnatural line, as if driven.
events.twist: Something on the ridge is herding them toward travellers, and it watches the fight with interest.

events.name: Fog fighters
events.text: They attack out of thick fog and fall back into it between strikes. Ranged attacks beyond 30 feet are at disadvantage.

events.name: Surge-born
events.text: These monsters are made of raw, unsettled magic and flicker at the edges. Their cores are worth half again the usual price.

events.name: Under the bridge
events.text: The monsters have made a lair under the {bridge|culvert|ford} and attack whoever crosses it, from below.

events.name: Fighting each other
events.text: Two kinds of monster are already locked in a fight across the road. Both turn on the party if they get involved, and neither does if they wait an hour.

events.name: The mimic waystone
events.text: One of the milestones is a monster. It has been eating travellers who sit on it for years.
events.nod: D&D's mimic, but as a roadside stone

events.name: Too many to count
events.text: A swarm of small monsters, each one weak, pours out of the {grass|scrub|reeds}. They fight as a single swarm, and they stop for nothing.

events.name: Waking up hungry
events.text: The party walks right over something dormant under the {sand|soil|leaf litter}, and it wakes up angry.

events.name: Dropping from above
events.text: They have been clinging to the {canopy|cliff overhang|rigging of a wrecked ship} above the path, waiting.

events.name: Wearing a harness
events.text: One of the monsters wears a leather harness with a noble house's brand.
events.twist: It was somebody's war beast, and its owner wants it back alive.

events.name: Out of the water
events.text: They burst out of the water at the party's flank, and drag anyone they grab back under.

events.name: Following the coin
events.text: The monsters ignore the party and go straight for the spirit coins, chewing through packs to reach them.

events.name: Chained to a post
events.text: A single monster is chained to a post at the roadside, starved and furious. Someone left it here on purpose.
events.twist: A note pinned to the post reads: 'For the next adventurers. You're welcome.'

events.name: Night hunters
events.text: Eyes in the dark beyond the firelight, more of them every minute. They attack when the fire burns low.

events.name: A lot bigger up close
events.text: From a distance it looked like a {rabbit|duck|small goat}. It was not a small anything.

events.name: Guarding a gate
events.text: The monsters stand guard around a shimmering astral space entrance, as if they came out of it, and they defend it like home.

events.name: Ancient and slow
events.text: One huge, old monster, slow and scarred, and clearly the survivor of a hundred fights. Its core would be worth a small fortune, and it knows it.

events.name: Still forming
events.text: The monster is only half made, its back legs still drifting into shape out of {coloured mist|black smoke|falling sparks}. It attacks anyway, and grows stronger every round it lives.

events.name: A rank too high
events.text: One of the pack spawned a rank above the rest, with {frost in its fur|silver in its scales|a second set of eyes}. The others follow its lead.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to spot its rank before the first blow
events.failText: the party finds out when their attacks do nothing to it

events.name: The uncapped array
events.text: Monsters keep crawling out of a natural array in a hollow beside the way, one every few minutes, until the party deals with them or moves on.
events.twist: A Magic Society cap stone lies beside the array. Someone dug it out on purpose, and recently.

events.name: Through the crack
events.text: A crack in the air weeps {pale light|cold blue fire|something like honey}, and monsters drop through it one by one, blinking at a world that is not their own.
events.twist: The crack is an astral space entrance that tore open by itself. The Society will pay to hear where.

events.name: Fleeing the rise
events.text: The monsters are thin and frantic, running from the rising magic like everyone else. They fight only because the party stands between them and quieter ground.
events.twist: Behind them, the sky over the hills shimmers with raw magic.

events.name: Core-eaters
events.text: These monsters live by eating other monsters' cores, and they can smell the ones in the party's packs from {a hundred yards|across a valley|through a closed pack} away.

events.name: Shaped by the ground
events.text: The magic here built its monsters from what lay to hand: {mud and reeds|sand and old bone|bark and moss|loose rock and ice}. They fall apart into the same stuff.
events.twist: They are made of the ground itself, and the ground is full of whatever the last travellers dropped.

events.name: Best the land can do
events.text: A single small monster, the best this thin-magic country can manage. It squares up to the whole party with total conviction.

events.name: Sharing a core
events.text: Two monsters joined at the {shoulder|tail|hip}, sharing one core between them. They fight well together but argue about which way to run.
events.twist: Kill one and the other carries on, with the shared core still inside it, now twice as strong.

events.name: Too early in the year
events.text: Spawns this strong should not come for another month. After the fight, an Arcana DC 15 check reads the ambient magic: the region is building, and early.
events.twist: The Adventure Society will want this report, and will pay for it.

events.name: Something from each fallen
events.text: Each monster that dies leaves the ground beneath it twitching. A round later, something smaller crawls out of the earth where it fell.

events.name: Glass-skinned
events.text: These monsters have hides like {stained glass|smoked crystal|mother-of-pearl}, and the light pours through them in colours. Any hide taken unbroken sells well to a crafter.
events.twist: One hide shows a face in the glass, looking out. It is not the monster's.

events.name: Survivor of the peak
events.text: A monster left over from the last surge's peak, a full rank above the party and scarred all over, crosses the way ahead. It has not seen them yet.
events.check: Stealth DC 15 for everyone to let it pass
events.failText: it turns its head, and the party should run

events.name: Ran out of magic
events.text: The array made a pack of {wolves|boars|great lizards} and ran dry partway through. Three proper beasts, and one that is mostly teeth and no legs.
events.twist: The array is still trying to finish the fourth one, and it is getting there.

events.name: The same ones again
events.text: The monsters are exactly like the ones the party killed on the last fight of the journey, down to the wounds the party gave them.
events.twist: They are not the same. Something is copying what the party fights, and it has been watching.

events.name: Inside the stone ring
events.text: The monsters circle a ring of old standing stones and cannot cross into it. The party can fight from inside the ring in safety.
events.twist: Something else already shelters in the ring, and it was hoping for company.

events.name: Hungry for mana
events.text: They ignore armour and steel and go straight for whoever holds the most mana. The party's casters can feel the monsters tugging at it from yards away.
events.twist: Anyone who runs dry of mana stops being interesting to them at all.

events.name: Lightning-fed
events.text: These monsters crackle with stolen lightning and grow brighter when the sky flashes. Anyone in {metal armour|chain mail|a steel helm} draws their sparks.
events.twist: Their cores hold a charge for weeks, and a storm-priest would pay for one.

events.name: Only in the mist
events.text: Shapes that exist only in the mist close in from every side. When the sun burns the mist away, so do they, for today.

events.name: Sniffing out an essence
events.text: The monsters are drawn to one party member's {fire|water|shadow|swift} essence and push past everyone else to reach them.
events.twist: They are not hunting. They want to touch it, and they purr when they do.

events.name: Shy no longer
events.text: {Grazing beasts|Burrowers|Night-hunters} that usually hide from people are out in broad daylight, frenzied by the building magic, and they charge without a second thought.
events.twist: A Society monitor is counting them from a hill and would like to know how many there were.

events.name: The quintessence crust
events.text: When the fight is over, the ground where the monsters spawned glitters with a crust of quintessence.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to gather it without it fading

events.name: The mother arrives
events.text: The young ones are easy. Their {mother|father|very large aunt} arrives on the second round, and she is not.

events.name: Claw marks on the trees
events.text: Deep claw marks on {trees|rocks|fence posts} and a neat pile of bones mark a boundary. Something owns the ground ahead.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to find a way around its territory
events.failText: the party crosses the line, and the owner comes to see who

events.name: The burned watchtower
events.text: Monsters have denned in a burned-out {watchtower|farmhouse|waystation} and rush out at anyone who passes within a stone's throw.
events.twist: The tower was burned by people, not monsters. The monsters moved in after.

events.name: Lined with boots
events.text: The monster's nest is lined with things it took from travellers: {buckles and boots|loose spirit coins|a cracked Adventure Society badge}.

events.name: Shedding its skin
events.text: The monster is halfway out of its old {skin|shell|scales}, soft, sore and furious about it. The shed hide lies beside it, worth good coin to a crafter.

events.name: A sleeping pack
events.text: The party walks into a {cave mouth|hollow|thicket} where a whole pack is asleep, heaped together and snoring.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 for everyone to back out
events.failText: one wakes, then all of them
events.twist: One of the sleepers is not part of the pack. It is a person, curled up among them.

events.name: The humming nest
events.text: A humming nest the size of a cottage hangs from {a cliff|an old oak|a broken tower}. One scout has found the party. In a minute, there will be hundreds.
events.twist: The nest's honey is worth a fortune to the Church of the Revels.

events.name: The only water
events.text: The only water for a day in any direction is one pool, and something lives in it. It does not share.
events.twist: Something at the bottom of the pool glints. It has been collecting.

events.name: Moved into the hut
events.text: A monster has moved into the {hut|barn|cave} the party meant to sleep in tonight. It has rearranged the furniture and seems to like it.
events.twist: It has also stockpiled food, and is willing to share if nobody makes a fuss.

events.name: Birds on the rope bridge
events.text: Huge condor-like monsters have nested on the pillars of a Cloud Clan rope bridge, and the bridge sways under their landings.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 for anyone fighting on the bridge
events.failText: they are knocked to the bridge's edge and hang on by one hand
events.twist: The Clan whose bridge this is will ask what the party did with the eggs.

events.name: Winning the border
events.text: Two packs have marked the same stretch of ground and are snarling at each other. The nearer pack decides the party is the bigger threat.

events.name: The other pack
events.text: The rival pack has moved into the ground the dead pack left. They know the party's scent now, and they come in {hard|at dusk|from upwind}.

events.name: Listening below
events.text: The ground under the camp is hollow. Something beneath it has been listening to the party's voices all evening, and it has learned where they sleep.

events.name: Standing over the fallen
events.text: A monster stands over a fallen adventurer with {an Iron|a Bronze} badge, guarding the body as its kill.
events.twist: The adventurer is still breathing.

events.name: A clutch on the array
events.text: Dozens of eggs lie warm on a natural array, rocking as they get ready to hatch. Their guardians rise from the grass.
events.twist: The Adventure Society pays a bounty for every clutch reported and destroyed.

events.name: The burrow field
events.text: The {field|meadow|dry slope} is riddled with holes. Monsters pop up, snap at ankles and vanish, then pop up somewhere else.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to guess which hole comes next
events.failText: someone takes a bite and is knocked prone

events.name: Den in the shrine
events.text: A monster has made its den inside a wayside shrine of {church}. The {offerings|candles|prayer ribbons} are scattered and the shrine's keeper is gone.
events.twist: The church will be grateful to anyone who clears and cleans it.

events.name: Answering the call
events.text: The monsters sing a warning before they attack, a {low wavering call|run of clicks|three-note whistle}. It sounds almost like a question.
events.check: Performance DC 15 to sing the right answer back
events.failText: the party's answer was an insult, and they charge

events.name: The unclaimed contract
events.text: The den the Society cleared last year has new tenants. The old contract notice is still nailed at the entrance, never taken down.
events.twist: The contract was never closed. Clear the den and the party can claim it.

events.name: Somebody else's eggs
events.text: The monster is guarding a nest of {eggs|chicks|cocoons} that plainly belong to a different kind of creature. It guards them fiercely anyway.

events.name: Calling in a friend's voice
events.text: Someone {calls for help|screams|laughs} from just out of sight, in the voice of one of the party. That party member is standing right here.

events.name: The clever one
events.nod: Jurassic Park: the raptor flanking from the side ('clever girl')
events.text: One monster stands in plain view, staring the party down. It is only there to be looked at. The rest are coming in from the side.
events.check: Perception DC 15 to spot the flankers
events.failText: the flankers get a free round

events.name: Picking the slowest
events.text: Nobody else matters to them. The pack cuts past the fighters to reach the slowest thing in the party: {the pack animal|the wounded|whoever carries the most}.
events.twist: They have done this before. The bones near the road are mostly mules.

events.name: Too old to hunt
events.text: An old monster, {sick and half blind|lame in one leg|missing half its teeth}, that can no longer catch anything faster than a traveller. It is starving, and it fights like it.

events.name: Circling all afternoon
events.text: The monsters circle at a distance for hours, never quite close enough to fight, wearing at the party's nerves.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to break line of sight and lose them
events.failText: they strike at dusk, when the party is tired
events.twist: They are not waiting for dark. They are waiting for the rest of the pack.

events.name: The lame deer
events.text: A {lame deer|tethered goat|bleating calf} stands in the open, crying. It is bait, and the things that set it are waiting in cover.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to see the setup
events.failText: the party walks straight in

events.name: Smelling the last fight
events.text: The scent of the party's last fight still clings to their gear, and the parts and cores they carry. Scavenger monsters follow it right to them.
events.twist: Leave the parts behind and they lose interest. Keep them and they follow for days.

events.name: The trapdoor
events.text: A lid of earth and moss flips open under someone's foot, and something with {a lot of legs|pincers|one huge claw} reaches up.
events.check: Dexterity save DC 13 for the lead walker
events.failText: they are dragged half into the burrow

events.name: Driven to the gully
events.text: The monsters never charge. They press and feint, steering the party toward a narrow {gully|cove|ravine}.
events.twist: Something bigger waits in the gully, and the pack hunts for it.

events.name: The young one's test
events.text: A single young monster attacks alone while the rest of its pack watches from cover.
events.twist: If the party spares it, the pack leaves them alone. If they kill it, the pack never forgets.

events.name: They know your fighter
events.text: The monsters steer around the party's best fighter, as though someone told them who to avoid.
events.twist: Someone did. A rival trained them on that fighter's scent.

events.name: Playing dead
events.text: The monster drops and lies still after {one blow|the first spell|a single arrow}. It waits until someone kneels to cut out its core, then bites.
events.check: Medicine DC 13 to tell it is shamming
events.failText: the would-be harvester takes a bite to the hand

events.name: A bigger boat
events.nod: Jaws: 'You're going to need a bigger boat'
events.text: A fin the length of a rowing boat circles the ship, closer every pass. The crew quietly agree that this ship is not big enough.

events.name: Drumming in the trees
events.text: Something drums on {hollow logs|tree trunks|its own chest} out in the trees. The drumming stops, then starts again, closer.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to find where the drumming is coming from
events.failText: the party walks into the middle of them

events.name: Dragged away
events.text: In the confusion of the fight, one of the monsters drags off {the pack animal|a hired porter|the party's food sack} and vanishes into cover.

events.name: The larder
events.text: The party finds the monster's larder: what it took is still alive, along with the gear of travellers who were less lucky.

events.name: Lantern lights
events.text: Soft lights bob in the dark like lanterns on a path. Anyone who follows them finds the lights hang from something with a very large mouth.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13 to resist following the lights
events.failText: whoever fails walks to the water's edge before they snap out of it

events.name: Backwards tracks
events.text: The tracks point the wrong way. The monster walks backwards to fool trackers, and it has been following the party, not fleeing them.
events.check: Survival DC 15 to read the tracks in time
events.failText: it is on them before they work it out

events.name: Grandmother's cottage
events.nod: Little Red Riding Hood
events.text: A figure in a shawl and bonnet waves from a cottage door, inviting the party in for {soup|tea|a nice warm pie}. Its eyes are very big, and so are its teeth.

events.name: Never hit the hen
events.nod: Zelda: attacking a cucco brings the whole flock
events.text: A plump, harmless-looking bird monster pecks at the party's boots. Whoever hits it learns why the locals never do: the whole flock arrives, furious.

events.name: Walk without rhythm
events.nod: Dune: sandworms drawn by rhythmic footsteps
events.text: The sand ahead trembles. Something huge hunts by the beat of footsteps, and the party's march has a very steady beat.
events.check: Stealth DC 15 for everyone to walk without rhythm
events.failText: it rises under them

events.name: The frozen tarn
events.text: The quickest way is across a frozen tarn. Halfway over, something {knocks|scrapes|breathes} on the ice from below.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 for everyone as the ice cracks
events.failText: they go through into freezing water

events.name: Knee-deep
events.text: {Mud|Black water|Sucking silt} to the knees, and the monsters glide over it as if it were a floor. The party fights at half speed.

events.name: Bringing the slope down
events.text: The fight shakes loose rock on the slope above. Every heavy blow risks bringing it down on both sides.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to see the rockfall coming
events.failText: 2d10 bludgeoning damage to anyone caught

events.name: Over the rail
events.text: Wet, {clawed|finned|eyeless} things haul themselves over the rail and onto a deck gone slick with seawater.
events.twist: They are fleeing something worse in the deep, and they want the ship, not the crew.

events.name: The grass is burning
events.text: The monster breathes fire, and the dry grass catches at once. The fight goes on while a wall of flame races in on the wind.
events.twist: The fire drives other monsters out of the grass, and they run straight at the party.

events.name: In the tall crops
events.text: The {corn|millet|sorghum} stands higher than a tall man. Things move through it, and the stalks shiver where they pass.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to spot the moving stalks
events.failText: they strike first, from both sides

events.name: Shapes in the sandstorm
events.text: The sandstorm turns the world brown. Shapes move inside it that the wind does not explain.
events.check: Survival DC 15 to keep the party together
events.failText: the party is split into two groups when they strike

events.name: The cliff path
events.text: On a path barely wide enough for one, the monsters try to shove the party off the edge rather than fight.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 for anyone they hit
events.failText: they slide to the lip and must be hauled back

events.name: The canopy road
events.text: The jungle path here runs along great branches forty feet up. The monsters climb faster than the party can walk.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 for anyone hit while on the branches
events.failText: they fall 20 feet to the branch below

events.name: Through the floor
events.text: Halfway through the fight among old ruins, the floor gives way into a cellar no one has opened in a century.

events.name: Halfway across
events.text: They attack when half the party is across the {river|ford|channel} and half is not.
events.twist: The water is part of their territory, and the ones on the near bank are only the start.

events.name: Inside the haze
events.text: The monsters hunt inside the heat shimmer, and nothing beyond thirty feet is where it looks. Ranged attacks past that range have disadvantage.

events.name: Hidden by the downpour
events.text: The rain is so loud that nobody hears them until they are close enough to touch.

events.name: Riding the gale
events.text: Flying monsters ride the gale, diving out of it faster than anyone can aim, then climbing away on the wind.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to track them in the wind
events.failText: they get a free round of dives

events.name: Stampede
events.text: A monster bursts into a herd of {heidels|steppe goats|wild horses} and the herd stampedes, with the party right in its path.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: 2d6 bludgeoning damage and knocked prone

events.name: After the Tide
events.text: The Wandering Tide has just left this valley. The grass is waist-high and full of the monsters it spawned, still too drunk on magic to know it has gone.
events.twist: Their cores are rich with the Tide's magic and sell well to the Drift Hosts.

events.name: The sinkhole
events.text: The ground {slumps|cracks|sighs} and opens into a tunnel, and the party slides down into a monster's runway.
events.twist: The runway leads to a nest, and the nest is full of what the monster stole.

events.name: Tide in the roots
events.text: They fight among mangrove roots while the tide comes in. Every round the water rises, and the monsters are at home in it.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 each round to keep footing in the water
events.failText: they are dragged under for a round

events.name: Both ends of the pass
events.text: In a pass too narrow for two abreast, monsters appear at both ends at once.
events.twist: The two groups are not together. They see each other at the same moment the party sees them.

events.name: No moon tonight
events.text: There is no moon, and the dark is total. The monsters come for whatever light the party lights, so the party must choose: see, or hide.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 for everyone to wait in the dark
events.failText: they find the party anyway, and from the rear

events.name: Under the hull
events.text: Something shoves the ship from below, {lazily|playfully|almost gently}, as if testing it. Then it shoves harder.
events.twist: The ship's captain admits she has been feeding it scraps for years. It wants dinner.

events.name: The whirlpool
events.text: A monster sits at the heart of a whirlpool, and the ship is sliding toward it.
events.check: Water vehicles or Athletics DC 15 to row clear
events.failText: the ship is dragged to the edge of the spiral and the monster rises

events.name: The circled wagons
events.text: A caravan has circled its wagons and is losing. {Two|Three} guards are down, and the monsters are inside the ring.

events.name: Losing team
events.text: An Iron-rank team is losing a fight just ahead. Their leader yells for help, then adds that the cores are still theirs.
events.twist: Their contract is a rank too high for them. Someone at the Society signed it anyway.

events.name: We were tracking those
events.text: As the last monster falls, a team jogs up and announces they have tracked these monsters for days and the cores are rightfully theirs.
events.check: Persuasion or Intimidation DC 13 to keep the cores
events.failText: the argument costs the afternoon, and the cores are split

events.name: Don't kill her
events.text: A monster crashes into view with a broken chain trailing from its collar. A handler sprints after it, yelling at the party not to hurt it.

events.name: The fisher's boat
events.text: Something has hold of a small fishing boat and is trying to roll it. The fisher inside is beating it with {an oar|a boot|a fish}.
events.twist: Saved, the fisher insists on cooking the party the best fish supper of their lives.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to reach the boat in time
events.failText: the fisher is in the water when they arrive

events.name: The shepherd's girl
events.text: A monster is chasing a flock of {goats|sheep|geese}, and a small girl with a big stick is chasing the monster.
events.twist: Her village feeds the party and sends them off with a basket.

events.name: On the poster
events.text: The monster has a torn ear and a {white blaze on its face|broken horn|missing eye}. It is the one on the Society bounty poster in the last town.
events.twist: The bounty pays triple if the party brings back the head.

events.name: The lure in the cart
events.text: Monsters keep going for the same cart. Someone hid a pouch of monster lure in its axle, to draw the monsters away from their village.

events.name: Take it alive
events.text: A Magic Society researcher with a cage on wheels begs the party to capture the monster rather than kill it. She pays {double|triple, if it is unhurt|in rare reagents} for a live one.

events.name: Judged by a priest
events.text: A Church of the Hero priest settles on a rock to watch the fight. Afterwards she gives each party member a score for heroism, and explains it.

events.name: Their first core
events.text: A rookie Iron-rank team arrives as the fight ends and asks, very politely, if one of them could land the last blow. None of them has earned a core yet.

events.name: Pilgrims at bay
events.text: Church of the Journey pilgrims are backed against a {wayshrine|boulder|ruined wall}, singing loudly to keep their courage up while monsters close in.
events.twist: One of the pilgrims is a Church of the Journey priest who offers a blessing for the rest of the trip.

events.name: Garlands round its neck
events.text: The monster wears garlands of fresh flowers and ribbons. Someone has been feeding it, and it expects travellers to be food.
events.twist: The nearby village worships it as a god, and they will not thank the party for killing it.

events.name: The healer's wagon
events.text: A Church of the Healer priest is defending her clinic wagon alone. She offers to heal the party mid-fight if they hold the line with her.

events.name: Taking bets
events.text: A crowd of travellers stops to watch the fight, and someone starts taking bets. The odds on the party are {not flattering|insulting|honestly fair}.
events.twist: Win, and a grateful gambler shares a cut of the winnings.

events.name: The merfolk warning
events.text: A merfolk head breaks the surface and shouts a warning, seconds before something huge strikes.
events.twist: Afterwards she asks a favour: carry a message to a merfolk family ashore.

events.name: The trappers' snare
events.text: Goblin trappers snared something far bigger than they meant to. It has torn the snare loose, and they ask the party for help in exchange for a cut of the core.

events.name: Still in the saddle
events.text: A {war beast|riding beast|cart beast} charges out of the trees with a dead rider still strapped into its saddle. It is wild with pain and fear.
events.twist: The rider's saddlebags hold a sealed order from a noble house, addressed to someone in {place}.

events.name: Dropped cargo
events.text: A sky ship passes overhead, and a crate tumbles from its hold. The crate breaks open, and its cargo stands up.
events.twist: The sky ship's crew want their cargo back, and they pay for it alive.

events.name: The Leonid's commission
events.text: A Leonid crafter has been waiting at the roadside for exactly these monsters. She pays well for their {horns|eyes|tail spines}, if the party can take them unbroken.

events.name: The Condor Riders
events.text: The fight is going badly when great birds fall out of the clouds, ridden by young Cloud Clan fighters who whoop all the way down.

events.name: Saved by the fire-breather
events.text: A Draconian adventurer bursts from the brush and breathes fire across the monsters, and across a fair bit of the party.
events.twist: He apologises a great deal and owes them a drink.

events.name: A polite bow
events.text: The monster stops, {bows low|curtsies|tips an imaginary hat} to each member of the party in turn, and then attacks with total savagery.

events.name: Half owl, half bear
events.nod: D&D's owlbear
events.text: A feathered, hooting thing with a bear's bulk and a very bad temper crashes out of the brush. The locals call it a hoot-bear, and run.
events.twist: It has a nest nearby, and in it are three very fluffy, very angry young.

events.name: The metal-eater
events.nod: D&D's rust monster
events.text: A scuttling monster with feathery feelers ignores the party and goes for their weapons and armour. Whatever it touches rusts to flakes, and it eats them.
events.check: Dexterity save DC 13 to keep a weapon from its feelers
events.failText: that weapon is ruined

events.name: The clear cube
events.nod: D&D's gelatinous cube
events.text: The way ahead seems open until someone walks into it. It is a clear cube of jelly, filling the {gully|passage|alley} wall to wall, full of old swords and bones.

events.name: Two heads for one
events.text: Cut off one of its heads and two grow back. Fire on the stump stops them, if anyone thinks of it.
events.check: Arcana or Nature DC 13 to know the trick
events.failText: it has five heads before anyone works it out

events.name: A garden of travellers
events.nod: Greek myth: Medusa and the basilisk
events.text: Stone statues of travellers line the way, each with the same look of surprise. Something nearby turns people to stone with its gaze.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13 to look away in time
events.failText: that party member is restrained as their limbs stiffen, until the fight ends

events.name: Breathing frost
events.text: The monsters breathe frost, and the ground around the fight glazes over with ice in patterns like {ferns|feathers|old writing}. Their breath leaves the air glittering.
events.twist: The frost holds a pattern. Someone studying it after the fight finds a map of the local natural arrays.

events.name: Waiting for the biggest
events.nod: Folk tale: Three Billy Goats Gruff
events.text: A monster under the {plank bridge|ford stones|culvert} lets the smallest party member pass, then the next. It is waiting for the biggest, the tastiest.

events.name: The white bunny
events.nod: Monty Python and the Holy Grail: the killer rabbit
events.text: Locals in dented helmets warn the party about a fluffy white monster by a cave. It is the size of a cat. It has killed {eleven|twenty|nobody knows how many} people.

events.name: I choose you
events.nod: Pokemon
events.text: An outworlder bursts out of the brush, hurls a red-and-white painted ball at the monster and shouts that he saw it first. Nothing happens. He seems crushed.

events.name: The whispering narrator
events.nod: Nature documentaries
events.text: An outworlder crouches behind a rock and narrates the fight in a hushed, reverent voice, like the nature shows back home. He means it as a compliment.

events.name: Aim for the glowing bit
events.nod: Video game boss fights
events.text: A breathless outworlder insists every big monster has a glowing weak spot, and the party should aim for that. Annoyingly, this one does.

events.name: The walking hill
events.nod: Shadow of the Colossus
events.text: A monster the size of a hill walks across the land, slow and calm. High on its back, under the fur, a mark glows. Someone has to climb.
events.check: Athletics DC 15 to climb to the mark
events.failText: the climber is shaken off and falls 20 feet into its fur

events.name: The scarred white
events.nod: Moby-Dick
events.text: A vast white sea monster, scarred with old harpoons, surfaces beside the ship. The captain goes very quiet, then orders the boats lowered.
events.twist: The captain has hunted this one for twenty years, and he will not let the party leave until it dies.

events.name: Too loud a feast
events.text: The {waystation|inn|farm hall} is loud with song and drink tonight. Something out in the dark hates the noise, and it is tearing at the hall door.

events.name: Singing on the rocks
events.nod: The Odyssey: the Sirens
events.text: Sweet voices sing from the rocks, and the {helmsman|cook|captain} starts to steer toward them with a happy smile.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13 for everyone, or tie someone to the mast
events.failText: the ship grinds onto the rocks and the singers come down to feed

events.name: Arms round the hull
events.nod: Norse folklore: the Kraken
events.text: Arms thicker than the mast rise out of the sea on both sides and wrap around the ship.
events.twist: Its core could buy the ship ten times over.

events.name: The hat thief
events.text: The monster wears a {fine feathered hat|bishop's mitre|straw sunhat} it stole from a traveller. That traveller is close behind, and really wants the hat back.

events.name: Mirror-faced
events.text: The monster's face is a flat {silver mirror|pool of still water|sheet of polished jet}. It fights with the style and tricks of whoever looks into it last.
events.twist: Smash its face and it fights like nobody at all, flailing and lost.

events.name: It likes the music
events.text: The monster stops mid-charge when someone {hums|whistles|sings off key}. It sways happily while the music lasts, and attacks the moment it stops.
events.check: Performance DC 13 each round to keep it calm
events.failText: a bum note, and it charges

events.name: Stuck in the fence
events.text: A monster is stuck fast in a {fence|split tree|broken wagon}, snapping and furious. It will get loose, eventually, and it will remember who laughed.

events.name: Two heads, one opinion each
events.text: A two-headed monster whose heads clearly do not get along. One wants to fight the party. The other wants lunch, which is also the party.

events.name: A swarm in the shape of a beast
events.text: From a distance it is a {bear|stag|great cat}. Up close, it is a swarm of buzzing insects holding that shape, and it comes apart when struck.
events.twist: Somewhere inside the swarm is one hard little queen, and if she dies, the rest scatter.

events.name: Wounds not yet given
events.text: The monster arrives already wounded, and the cuts match the party's own weapons exactly. Nobody has struck it yet.
events.twist: When it dies, its core is warm, and ticks like a clock.

events.name: Out of the wagon-cage
events.text: A tamed guard monster has wandered away from a Drift Host's wagon-cage. It has decided the party is its new herd, and that everything else must be driven off.
events.twist: Its Host wants it back, and will pay in goats.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 15 to calm it
events.failText: it treats the party as a rival herd and charges

events.name: Fighting on cloud
events.text: The path crosses patches of Clan-thickened cloud, solid enough to walk on. {Goat-like|Cat-like|Many-legged} monsters stalk across them, and the cloud thins wherever anyone stands too long.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 each round spent standing still
events.failText: they sink to the waist in cloud and are restrained

events.name: Up from the jungle
events.text: Something has climbed up from the jungle far below. The lowest terraces are empty, and the scratches on the steps go up, never down.
events.check: Survival DC 15 to track it to where it is resting
events.failText: it finds the party first

events.name: Under the green-stone boat
events.text: A river serpent as long as the boat slides under the party's green-stone punt and comes up on the far side, mouth first.
events.check: Dexterity save DC 13 for everyone in the boat
events.failText: they are thrown into the water

events.name: Leeches the size of dogs
events.text: The reeds are full of leeches the size of dogs. They are {slow, stupid|quick, clever|blind, patient} and very, very thirsty.
events.check: Constitution save DC 12 for anyone bitten
events.failText: they are poisoned until the next short rest

events.name: Over the farm wall
events.text: Monsters are spilling over the wall of a spirit coin farm. The guards are down, and the manager shouts an offer of coins to anyone who stops them.
events.twist: The guards were paid to be elsewhere today.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to close the gate while the fight goes on
events.failText: more spill out every round until someone does

events.name: The one that got away
events.text: The last monster breaks off, wounded, and {limps|slithers|flaps} away faster than anyone can follow.

events.name: It brought friends
events.text: The wounded monster is back, scarred and limping. It has brought the rest of its kind, and it points the party out to them.

events.name: Tracks beside the road
events.text: Footprints as wide as {a cartwheel|a table|a wagon bed} run beside the party's route for miles, keeping pace. They are fresh.

events.name: The maker of the tracks
events.text: The track-maker is grazing in the open: a vast, calm monster a rank above the party. It watches them pass and does nothing unless they attack.
events.twist: Smaller monsters shelter near it. Anyone who attacks those has to answer to it.

events.name: A wounded cub
events.text: After the fight, one of the monsters' young is left behind, hurt and crying. Someone could tend its wounds and let it go.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13 to treat it without being bitten

events.name: The cub returns
events.text: Monsters close in on the party, and the cub they saved, bigger now, crashes in on the party's side and drives them off.

events.name: Marked by spit
events.text: A monster lands in front of one party member, spits on their {boots|cloak|shield}, and leaves without attacking. The spit glows faintly and will not wash off.

events.name: Hunting the marked
events.text: They come for the marked one tonight, all of them, from every side. The glowing spit leads them in like a beacon.

events.name: An egg in the pack
events.text: After the fight, someone finds an egg nestled in their pack, warm and {humming|ticking|glowing}. Nobody put it there.

events.name: The parent comes looking
events.text: The egg hatches at dawn and the hatchling decides the party is its mother. Its real mother arrives an hour later and disagrees.
events.twist: Give the hatchling back unharmed and the mother leaves in peace.

events.name: The cracked core
events.text: One of the cores from today's fight has a hairline crack, and magic seeps from it like {steam|smoke|slow light}.

events.name: Drawn to the leak
events.text: Every monster for miles can smell the leaking core. They arrive in a long, hungry stream, fighting each other to get to it first.
events.twist: Throwing the core away ends it. It is worth a lot of money.

events.name: A flawless core
events.text: The monster dies, and its core is flawless: clear, bright and bigger than any the party has seen at this rank. The Magic Society will pay well over the usual price.

events.name: The Society tag
events.text: The monster wears a Society tracking tag in {one ear|a horn|its hide}, stamped with a contract number. Taking the tag back to any branch earns a finder's fee.

events.name: Old arrowheads
events.text: The monster's hide is studded with old {arrowheads|crossbow bolts|spear tips}, each one stamped with the same team's mark.
events.twist: That team went missing two years ago. Their families will pay to hear where the party met it.

events.name: Bread after the fight
events.text: When the last monster falls, the farmers who were hiding behind their shutters come out with {bread, beer|cake, cider|cheese, ale} and a lot of handshakes.

events.name: A stone in its gut
events.text: The monster swallowed something hard and bright. An awakening stone sits in its gut, still whole.
events.check: Medicine or Survival DC 13 to cut it out cleanly
events.failText: the stone cracks and is worth half

events.name: The last word
events.text: As the monster dies it speaks one word, clearly, in a person's voice: {place}.

events.name: The cowbell
events.text: The monster wears a cowbell on a leather strap. A farmer runs after it, insisting it is a perfectly tame guard animal. It is eating his {fence|scarecrow|cart}.

events.name: Exactly at noon
events.text: The locals warned the party: the monsters here attack at noon, every day, and at no other time. It is a quarter to.
events.twist: The village sets its clocks by them, and will be upset if the party kills them all.
events.check: History or Insight DC 13 to learn from the locals how to avoid them
events.failText: noon arrives, and so do they

events.name: His pet Biscuit
events.text: A small boy swears the monster is his pet, Biscuit, and that Biscuit never bites. Biscuit bites.

events.name: Painted blue and numbered
events.text: The monsters are painted bright {blue|yellow|red}, each with a white number on its flank. Someone was racing them.
events.twist: The bookmaker who owns them wants them back before the race tomorrow.

events.name: No core inside
events.text: The monster is missing its core. Someone cut it out long ago and {sewed|stapled|bound} up the wound, and it lived. It is very angry about it.

events.name: The woman with the pan
events.text: An old woman is fighting a monster with {an iron frying pan|a rolling pin|a broom}, and winning. She is furious when anyone tries to help.

events.name: Mind the face
events.text: A taxidermist on a mule rides up mid-fight, begging the party to spare the monster's face. He has a buyer waiting, and offers a share.

events.name: The roadside wedding
events.text: A monster crashes into a roadside wedding. The couple refuse to stop the vows, and the priest of {church} keeps reading, louder.
events.twist: Save the day, and the party is now honoured guests at the feast.

events.name: Silver under the moon
events.text: Silver {hares|wolves|stags} that exist only under the full moon slip out of the moonlight. Their cores look like small pieces of it.

events.name: The singing cores
events.text: As each monster dies its core rings like a struck bell. By the end of the fight the cores lie in the grass, humming a chord together.

events.name: Born of the sky lights
events.text: Green and violet lights ripple in the night sky, and monsters made of the same light drift down to hunt.

events.name: The petal storm
events.text: Monsters like walking flower beds shake out clouds of {pink|white|golden} petals. Anyone who breathes them in feels very, very sleepy.
events.check: Constitution save DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: they fall asleep until shaken awake

events.name: Stinging lights
events.text: Glowing jellies rise around the ship in their thousands, beautiful as lanterns. Then they start climbing the hull.
events.check: Constitution save DC 13 for anyone stung
events.failText: they are poisoned for an hour

events.name: A core like a key
events.text: The monster's core is shaped exactly like a key, teeth and all.
events.twist: It fits a lock in a ruin a day's walk from here.

events.name: Falling upward
events.text: The monster moves as if the sky were the ground, walking along the undersides of {branches|clouds|the ship's spars} and dropping upward onto its prey.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 for anyone it grabs
events.failText: they are yanked 20 feet into the air before it lets go

events.name: Waiting their turn
events.text: The monsters attack one at a time, in strict order. The others wait in a neat queue and {hiss|snap|tut} at any monster that pushes in.
events.twist: The last in the queue is the biggest, and it has been watching how the party fights.

events.name: Webs across the way
events.text: Thick webs strung across the way, and spiders the size of {goats|ponies|large dogs} waiting at the edges.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to see the strands
events.failText: the lead walker is caught and restrained

events.name: Bandits
events.text: Bandits block a choke point and demand a toll.
events.twist: They want spirit coins, not blood: pay the toll and they step aside.

events.name: Core poachers
events.text: Core poachers have been following the party since its last fight.
events.twist: They want the cores and parts the party is carrying.

events.name: Slavers
events.text: Slavers with chained captives, heading for a Storm Kingdom port.
events.twist: Freeing the captives earns the Church of Liberty's quiet favour, and the slavers' employer's anger.

events.name: Cultists
events.text: Cultists come for one party member in particular: a priest, an outworlder, or someone with a rare essence.
events.twist: They have a description of their target, and it is very accurate.

events.name: Rival team
events.text: A rival adventuring team wants the party to arrive late, or not at all.
events.twist: They will talk if the fight turns against them, and someone paid them.

events.name: House retainers
events.text: Retainers of a noble house the party has crossed, or one that wants something they carry.
events.twist: Their orders are to bring something back, not to kill.

events.name: Deserters
events.text: A broken Iron-rank team gone bad after a surge, desperate rather than cruel.
events.twist: They will surrender for food and a fair word.

events.name: Testing the strong
events.text: Young riders of a Host circle the party to see who is strongest.
events.twist: Win and they offer to ride with the party for a day; lose and they take a mount.

events.name: Pirates
events.text: A fast ship closes in flying no colours.

events.name: Fake broken wagon
events.text: A wagon with a broken wheel and a crying driver blocks the road. The bandits are under the tarp.

events.name: The toll bridge
events.text: Bandits have built a toll booth on a public bridge, with a painted sign and a price list.
events.twist: They argue among themselves about the prices while trying to rob you.

events.name: The claim jumpers
events.text: Prospectors have found an awakening stone deposit by the road and attack anyone who gets close enough to see it.
events.twist: They're Normal rank and terrified, and they'd share for protection.

events.name: Cultists with a schedule
events.text: Cultists in plain clothes fall in beside the party on the road and attack at a signal.
events.twist: They need one live captive by tonight's moonrise.

events.name: Disguised as pilgrims
events.text: A group in Church of the Journey robes asks to walk with the party. Three miles later, the knives come out.

events.name: The deserters
events.text: Deserters from a noble house's levy, hungry and desperate, attack without much plan or hope.
events.twist: They can be talked down with food and a promise not to report them.

events.name: Archers on the ridge
events.text: Arrows from high ground, and a voice telling the party to drop their packs and walk away.

events.name: Wreckers
events.text: False lights on the shore lure ships onto rocks, and the wreckers wade in with hooks and clubs.

events.name: Boarded
events.text: Grapples over the rail and pirates swarming aboard.

events.name: The mage's test
events.text: A Magic Society researcher attacks with constructs and wards, taking notes the whole time.
events.twist: It's a field trial. If the party wins, she offers them payment to fight it again tomorrow.

events.name: The bounty hunters
events.text: Bounty hunters with a wanted poster that looks almost exactly like one of the party.
events.twist: It isn't them, but the real one is close by.

events.name: A trap in the sand
events.text: The ground gives way into a pit lined with stakes, and figures appear at the rim.

events.name: Kidnap, not kill
events.text: Nets, sleep poison and blunt clubs. Someone is paying for the party alive.

events.name: Defending their land
events.text: Locals with old weapons, convinced the party is with the noble house that burned their village.
events.twist: Nobody needs to die if someone listens.

events.name: The one-man ambush
events.text: A single bandit leaps out and demands everything. He insists his forty friends are hiding in the bushes.
events.twist: His friends really are in the bushes. There are three of them, and they are asleep.

events.name: Assassin in the caravan
events.text: Someone travelling alongside the party strikes at night, aiming at one specific person.

events.name: Zealots of Purity
events.text: Church of Purity zealots decide one of the party is a cult member and attack to cleanse them.

events.name: Burned-out ambushers
events.text: The bandits have clearly done this every day for a decade. Their threats sound rehearsed and their hearts aren't in it.

events.name: Storm-crossers
events.text: Raiders attack in the middle of a storm, counting on the noise and rain.

events.name: The lone gunslinger
events.nod: Westerns: a duel at high noon
events.text: An outworlder in a wide-brimmed hat stands in the middle of the road and challenges the party's best fighter to a duel at noon, 'like back home'. His friends are on the rooftops.

events.name: Stand and deliver
events.nod: English highwaymen: 'Stand and deliver!'
events.text: A masked rider on a {black|grey|piebald} horse levels two crossbows at dusk and demands, very politely, that the party stand and deliver.
events.twist: He signs a receipt for whatever he takes, and his signature is on a lot of wanted posters.

events.name: The rope across the way
events.text: A rope snaps taut across the {road|trail|track} at chest height, and the bandits come running.
events.check: Perception DC 13 for the lead rider to see it in time
events.failText: the lead rider is knocked from the saddle

events.name: A tree behind them
events.text: A {tree|dead pine|great oak} crashes down across the way behind the party. A second later, figures step out ahead.

events.name: Only the cheese
events.text: The bandits do not want coin, weapons or mounts. They want {the cheese|all the bread|the sausage}, and they are prepared to die for it.

events.name: The badgeless captain
events.text: The bandit leader wears the faded outline of a removed Society badge on her coat. Before the fight, she offers the party a job.
events.twist: She was stripped of rank for refusing an order that killed her team. She wants that officer.

events.name: The ferry men
events.text: Men in flat green-stone boats offer to pole the party across a wide channel. Halfway over, they ship their poles and draw {knives|hooks|short swords}.

events.name: Robbing the rich
events.nod: Robin Hood
events.text: Outlaws in {green|brown|patched hoods} step out of the trees, ask the party's rank, and look over their purses. They rob the rich and give to the poor.
events.twist: If the party looks poor enough, the outlaws give them coin instead.

events.name: Running from the bait
events.text: A ragged band of bandits attacks, then breaks and runs at the first blood. They are running somewhere on purpose.
events.check: Insight DC 13 not to give chase
events.failText: the party follows them into a much bigger ambush

events.name: A friendly inn
events.text: The village is friendly, the inn is cheap and the {stew|ale|pie} is good. Everyone in the common room watches the party a little too carefully.

events.name: The innkeeper's signal
events.text: Past midnight the innkeeper sets a lamp in the window, and the whole village comes for the party with knives and pitchforks.
events.twist: The village has done this for a generation. There is a cellar full of travellers' gear.

events.name: The thieves' cave
events.nod: Arabian Nights: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves
events.text: The party sees riders say two words to a {rock face|cliff|great boulder} and ride inside as the rock slides open. A sentry has seen the party too.

events.name: Riders along the greatbacks
events.nod: Westerns: the great train robbery
events.text: Masked riders gallop alongside the greatback caravan, swinging up ropes and climbing for the cargo platforms.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to fight on a moving platform
events.failText: they are thrown off and must catch up

events.name: The pulled planks
events.text: The planks of the footbridge have been pulled up. On the far side, figures wait with {crossbows|slings|long bows}, hoping someone tries to jump.

events.name: Testing the coins
events.text: The robbers carry a coin-tester and want only spirit coins. They test every coin they take, holding each one to the light.
events.twist: One of the party's coins fails the test. It is a fake, and somebody passed it to them.

events.name: A rank above
events.text: The bandits are Iron rank, but their leader is a rank above the party, and he tells them so with a smile.
events.twist: He does not want a fight he cannot lose. He wants the party to beg.

events.name: Smoke pots
events.text: Clay pots shatter around the party and pour out choking {yellow|green|black} smoke. Shapes move inside it.
events.check: Constitution save DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: they are poisoned for the first two rounds
events.twist: The smoke is a Magic Society alchemist's recipe, and the pots carry a batch mark.

events.name: After the mounts
events.text: In the small hours, quiet figures cut the picket line and lead the mounts away. They fight only if someone wakes.
events.check: Perception DC 13 for whoever is on watch
events.failText: the party wakes to find two mounts gone
events.twist: The thieves leave a trail any tracker could follow, straight to their camp.

events.name: Arrows from the reeds
events.text: Arrows hiss out of the reed beds on both sides of the channel. The archers can see out, and the party cannot see in.
events.twist: The archers are guarding a channel full of stolen boats.

events.name: The scarecrows
events.text: Every scarecrow along the field edge is a person in sacking, standing very still. One of them {breathes|blinks|coughs}.
events.twist: The farmer is tied up in his barn and will reward whoever frees him.

events.name: The bandits' clerk
events.text: A small man with {a ledger|an abacus|a quill behind each ear} follows the bandits, writing down everything they take and asking the party to spell their names.
events.twist: The ledger is evidence. The Society would pay well for it.

events.name: Bandits by vote
events.text: The bandits are a democracy. They stop mid-ambush to vote on whether to rob the party, and the vote is close.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to swing the vote
events.failText: the motion carries, and they attack

events.name: The crying child
events.text: A child sits crying at the edge of the {trees|marsh|ruins}, begging the party to help find her mother. She leads them into a hollow, then vanishes.

events.name: A gift with a ribbon
events.nod: Greek myth: the Trojan horse
events.text: A big {crate|wooden statue|wardrobe} tied with a ribbon waits for the party, with a note from 'grateful admirers'. It is heavy, and it smells of people.

events.name: The drugged wine
events.text: Their host pours generously and laughs at every joke. After the second {cup|glass|bowl}, the party's hands go numb.
events.check: Constitution save DC 13 for everyone who drank
events.failText: they are poisoned when the knives come out

events.name: A battle of wits
events.nod: The Princess Bride: the battle of wits
events.text: A masked stranger sets down two cups, one poisoned, and challenges the cleverest of the party to a battle of wits. His friends wait in the dark.
events.check: Insight DC 15 to see through him
events.failText: someone drinks, and is poisoned for an hour

events.name: The forged badges
events.text: {Three|Four|Five} adventurers with Society badges offer to escort the party through dangerous country. The badges look right. The rank marks are a fraction too bright.
events.check: Insight or Investigation DC 13 to spot the forgery
events.failText: they strike when the party is most exposed

events.name: The man on the ground
events.text: A man lies groaning beside the way, clutching {a bloody side|a broken leg|his chest}. When someone kneels to help, he stops groaning.

events.name: The quiet passengers
events.text: The quiet group who have shared the journey for days, polite and dull, were only waiting for the party to sleep.
events.twist: Their leader carries a list of names, and the party's are not the only ones.

events.name: The signal in the chorus
events.text: A travelling {bard|fiddler|piper} plays a song with a long chorus, watching the party the whole time. On the last verse, someone joins in from the dark.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to notice the chorus is a countdown
events.failText: the ambush gets a surprise round

events.name: The house of cakes
events.nod: Hansel and Gretel
events.text: A cottage beside the path smells of fresh baking, and a kind old woman waves the party in to eat. Her very large sons are already sharpening the knives.

events.name: Wearing your faces
events.text: The ambushers look exactly like the party: same clothes, same faces, same weapons. In the fight, nobody is sure who is who.
events.check: Insight DC 15 each round to pick the real ally
events.failText: someone strikes a friend

events.name: The moving crate
events.nod: Metal Gear Solid: the cardboard box
events.text: A wooden {crate|barrel|cask} is a little closer every time the party looks away. When someone stares straight at it, it goes very still.

events.name: The courier's letter
events.text: A wounded courier staggers up, presses a sealed letter into someone's hand and begs them to deliver it. His pursuers arrive a minute later.
events.twist: The letter is addressed to someone in {place}, and they will pay the party for it.

events.name: Too curious by half
events.text: A charming {merchant|scholar|young priest} falls in beside the party and chats about everything, especially what they carry and where they are going.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to see what she is doing
events.failText: her friends strike while the party is relaxed

events.name: The false checkpoint
events.text: Guards in a noble house's colours have set up a checkpoint and want to search the party's packs. The house is real. The guards are not.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to spot what is wrong with their livery
events.failText: they are behind the party when they reveal themselves

events.name: The kidnapped bride
events.text: A woman in a muddy {wedding dress|ball gown|silk coat} begs the party to save her from bandits. She leads them straight to the bandits, who seem to take orders from her.

events.name: The guide's family
events.text: The guide the party hired leads them into a narrow place and steps aside, white-faced. The ambushers have his family.
events.twist: Win, and he begs the party to help him get his family back.

events.name: The caravan's real plan
events.text: The caravan the party joined for safety stops in a lonely place. The drivers climb down, and all of them are armed.

events.name: Among the refugees
events.text: A column of people fleeing the surge files past. {Some|A dozen|Too many} of them are not refugees.
events.twist: The real refugees are terrified of them and will thank anyone who drives them off.

events.name: The friendly message bird
events.text: A message bird lands on someone's shoulder with a note: 'Stop here and wait. A friend.' The party has no friends who know where they are.

events.name: Help from the water
events.text: Someone splashes and shouts for help from the water near the {rocks|wreck|sandbar}. When the party comes close, the rocks are crowded with armed people.

events.name: The second son
events.text: A young noble with {three|five|a dozen} hired swords blocks the way and demands satisfaction for an insult. Nobody in the party has ever met him.
events.twist: He has the wrong party. The insult was real, and the right people are a day ahead.

events.name: A dart from nowhere
events.text: A dart sinks into someone's {neck|arm|shoulder}, and nobody saw where it came from. A second is already on its way.
events.check: Perception DC 15 to spot the shooter
events.failText: a second party member is hit before the shooter is found

events.name: The team you beat
events.text: An adventuring team the party beat to a contract has been waiting. They do not want to kill anyone. They want the party humiliated.
events.twist: Their leader's rank assessment depended on that contract.

events.name: Paid to delay
events.text: The attackers fight carefully, keep their distance and keep glancing at a {sand-timer|pocket watch|marked candle} one of them is holding.
events.twist: They were paid only to hold the party up until the sand runs out. Someone wants them late.

events.name: Whatever you carry
events.text: Hired blades want one thing the party is carrying, and they know exactly which pack it is in.
events.twist: Only someone who saw the party pack could know that.

events.name: The duellist
events.text: A famous duellist in a {crimson|black|gold-laced} coat challenges the party's best fighter. A crowd gathers to watch.
events.twist: The duel is a distraction. Her pickpockets are working the party's packs.
events.check: Perception DC 15 to catch the pickpockets
events.failText: a purse of spirit coins is gone

events.name: No insignia
events.text: {Three|Four} mages in plain {grey|brown} robes demand the party's monster cores and awakening stones. Their spells are textbook Magic Society, and they wear no insignia.

events.name: Which one is the outworlder
events.text: Hunters with {nets|chains|silvered manacles} ask which of the party is the outworlder, as if there obviously is one.
events.twist: Someone is paying for outworlders, alive. The hunters will say who, if the fight goes badly.

events.name: Watched from far off
events.text: The ambushers are Iron rank and clumsy. Far off, a lone figure watches the whole fight without moving.
events.twist: The watcher is a Silver-ranker testing the party for a job. They leave a card.

events.name: The escort turns
events.text: The guards the party hired for this stretch draw their swords on their employers.
events.twist: They were paid twice: once by the party, and once by someone else.

events.name: A shot from above
events.text: A crossbow bolt from high above, from {a ruined tower|the masthead|a cliff top}. The shooter is good, and reloads fast.

events.name: The ransom note
events.text: The kidnappers have already written the ransom note. They show it off proudly. Every one of the party's names is spelled wrong.

events.name: The wrong target
events.text: An assassin leaps from cover, stabs at someone, then stops and checks a {sketch|portrait|description}. He apologises sincerely, then looks at the sketch again, less sure.

events.name: The Crown's people
events.text: Storm Kingdom agents in good {cloaks|boots|grey coats} try to seize something the party carries, in the Crown's name, and far outside the Crown's lands.
events.twist: If the party wins, the agents insist this never happened, and offer coin to keep it that way.

events.name: Killers with a code
events.text: The contract killers follow strict rules: no killing before {noon|tea|sundown}, never a blow from behind, and always state the fee first.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15 to find a loophole in their code
events.failText: noon arrives

events.name: The crew with a plan
events.nod: Ocean's Eleven
events.text: An outworlder in a sharp suit leads a crew of specialists who have planned this robbery to the minute. He keeps calling it 'the job'.
events.twist: Everything goes to plan, except the part where the party were meant to be asleep.

events.name: We were here first
events.text: Two gangs were hired by different people to ambush the party in the same spot. They arrive together and argue about who has the right.

events.name: The hound handlers
events.text: Baying in the distance, getting closer. Trackers with {hounds|tame monsters|great cats} are running the party down, and they will not stop.
events.check: Survival DC 15 to throw the hounds off the scent
events.failText: the hounds catch them in the open

events.name: The archmage's toll
events.text: A Silver-rank mage blocks the way with a ring of {hovering|chanting|nervous} apprentices. She wants one item from the party, and she will name it.
events.twist: She knows something about that item the party does not, and will trade the knowledge for it.

events.name: Who sold the route
events.text: The ambushers knew the party's route, their timing and their numbers. Someone told them.

events.name: The informant
events.text: The party catches the one who sold their route, and they are not the person anyone expected.
events.twist: The informant was paid in a currency that leads straight to their employer.

events.name: The widow's hire
events.text: A woman in {black|grey|mourning white} has hired swords to avenge her husband, a bandit the party killed. She stands back and watches.
events.twist: She does not want them dead. She wants them to say his name.

events.name: A faster path
events.text: Polished Iron-rankers offer the party a fast path to Bronze rank, with no cores needed. They ask for a sample of someone's essence. Refusal makes them less friendly.
events.twist: Their leader is Bronze rank, and remembers being Iron last month.

events.name: Collecting for the door
events.text: Cultists in matching {grey|white|blue} ask the party politely for their monster cores, and for one volunteer. They are building a door, they explain.

events.name: The quiet servants
events.text: Pale {attackers|figures in plain clothes|men and women} who never speak come out of the dark. They barely bleed, and they keep coming when they should stop.
events.twist: Each one wears the same small charity badge.

events.name: For the god in the marsh
events.text: Delta villagers with {eel spears|fishing tridents|boat hooks} and offering garlands surround the party. They need a gift for the thing in the marsh, and the party will do.

events.name: Supper in the sand
events.text: A long table set with {silver and white linen|crystal and gold|black lace and candles} stands alone in the desert. Elegant diners invite the party to sit. There are no plates of food.

events.name: Mistaken for the hunters
events.text: Ragged worshippers of Undeath, fleeing Purity hunters, attack the party in a panic. They think the party is the hunters.
events.twist: The real hunters arrive soon, and they will not care who they burn.

events.name: Driven to the god
events.text: Villagers with torches and {drums|bells|bone rattles} push the party, step by step, toward a cave mouth. Something lives in the cave that they call holy.

events.name: The far voice
events.text: The sky dims, and a voice from very far away speaks through the cultists' mouths at once. It is curious about the party.
events.twist: It offers each party member a gift for the asking. The cultists fight hardest when anyone says no.

events.name: The caged captive
events.text: Cultists with a {caged|gagged|bound} captive turn as the party approaches, and decide they do not need witnesses.
events.twist: The captive is a noble house's missing heir.

events.name: War's recruiters
events.text: Priests of the Church of War attack without warning, fighting hard but fair. Whoever impresses them most gets an offer.

events.name: The blank masks
events.text: People in plain {white|black|silver} masks surround the party without a word. They do not want coin or blood. They want each party member to give them a name, any name.
events.twist: Anyone who gives a false name is left alone, and is somehow sure they will need it later.

events.name: Break it
events.text: Faithful of the Church of Destruction demand the party hand over {a magic item|their most precious thing|the oldest thing they carry} to be smashed. It is holy work to them.

events.name: The polite cultists
events.text: Cultists invite the party, very kindly, to join. When refused, they attack. When losing, they apologise and leave {a pamphlet|a cake|a calling card}.

events.name: The hymn
events.text: Hooded figures sing a slow {hymn|lullaby|dirge}, and with every verse the party's limbs grow heavier.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: they are slowed until someone silences a singer

events.name: Revellers attack
events.text: Church of the Revels pilgrims, very drunk, charge the party with {wine skins and roasting spits|cheese wheels and ladles|garlands and kegs}. They are sure it is a festival game.
events.check: Performance or Persuasion DC 13 to end the game
events.failText: it ends in a brawl, but a cheerful one

events.name: The prophesied one
events.text: Cultists kneel when they see one party member, weeping with joy. Then they draw knives. The prophecy, it seems, ends badly.

events.name: Just a little blood
events.text: Cultists with ritual knives promise they do not want to kill anyone. They need a {cupful|thimble|bowl} of blood from someone with a confluence.

events.name: Chalk marks
events.text: Someone has drawn small chalk marks on the party's packs in the night: {a circle|an eye|a door}, one on each.

events.name: Collected
events.text: They come for the marked packs and the people carrying them, with nets and sacks, very efficiently.

events.name: Pitchforks and hunger
events.text: Thin villagers with {pitchforks|scythes|threshing flails} block the way. Their harvest failed, and they want the party's food.
events.twist: Share two days of food and they let the party pass, and pray for them.

events.name: The surge orphans
events.text: Teenagers wearing a dead adventurer's mismatched gear try to rob the party. They lost everyone in the last surge.
events.twist: A Church of the Hearth house two days off would take them in, if someone brought them.

events.name: Owing the house
events.text: Farmers in borrowed {armour|helmets|livery} rob travellers to pay a noble house's rent. They hate every moment of it.

events.name: For her partner's healing
events.text: A lone Iron-ranker steps out with her sword drawn and demands spirit coins. Her partner lies sick in a cart behind her.
