events.twist: A Church of the Healer clinic could save him, for more than she has.

events.name: The runaways
events.text: Escaped slaves with shackle scars attack the party in desperation, sure they are slave-catchers sent to take them back.
events.twist: A Church of Liberty safehouse is a day away. They do not know the way.

events.name: The fever cart
events.text: Armed men surround the party with a sick {child|grandmother|young mother} in a cart. They do not want gold. They want a healer, now, whatever it takes.

events.name: The ruined merchant
events.text: A merchant in his best {velvet|silk|brocade} suit robs the party with a dress sword, apologising throughout. His creditors took everything else.

events.name: Lifeboat survivors
events.text: The ship picks up a boat of shipwreck survivors. Once aboard and dry, they draw hidden knives and try to take the ship.

events.name: A Host without a Khan
events.text: Riders of a broken Host, their Khan dead, circle the party. They need a greatback to carry their families, and they will take one.
events.twist: They would rather follow someone strong. Beat their best rider and they might follow the party.

events.name: Hungry for coins
events.text: Haggard essence users with no coins of their rank, half-starved, attack the party for spirit coins to eat.
events.twist: They fled a coin farm whose owner stopped feeding his guards.

events.name: His brother's ransom
events.text: A young man robs the party with shaking hands. Real bandits hold his brother, and want coin by tonight.

events.name: The bandits with the brother
events.text: The party finds the bandits holding the young man's brother. The bandits are expecting a payment, not a fight.

events.name: Still in chains
events.text: Escaped prisoners, still in their chains, attack for {weapons and food|keys and horses|a smith's file}. Their guards are dead behind them.
events.twist: One of them swears he was framed, and can name who did it.

events.name: The grieving father
events.text: A father with a {hunting bow|boar spear|wood axe} shoots at the party because they are adventurers. Adventurers were meant to save his son in the surge.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15 to talk him down
events.failText: he fights until he can't

events.name: Water thieves
events.text: Desert raiders want only one thing: water. They slash {waterskins|barrels|gourds} as they fight, and drink from the ones they take.

events.name: On the rooftops
events.text: Flood survivors on the rooftops of a drowned village rush the party's boat. They need it more, they say.
events.twist: There is room for them all, if the party will share.

events.name: The worst gang
events.text: Three teenagers with sticks and a gang name they clearly invented this morning try to rob the party. They are terrible at it.
events.twist: A stern word and a decent meal and they might go home. A job, and they might become something.

events.name: Riders on the storm
events.nod: European folklore: the Wild Hunt
events.text: Riders in {antlered|horned|bone} masks pour down out of the storm wind, horns blaring, hounds at their heels. They hunt whoever is out of doors.

events.name: The stolen greatback
events.text: Raiders cut a greatback out of the caravan the party travels with, family tent and all. The worst crime on the steppe, and in broad day.

events.name: Cutting the ropes
events.text: Halfway across a Cloud Clan rope bridge, the party sees figures on the far side sawing at the ropes.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 for everyone to cross in time
events.failText: the bridge drops and they hang from the slats

events.name: Out of the cloud
events.text: Raiders step out of the cloud bank, walking on cloud the party cannot see, and strike from angles that should be empty air.

events.name: Punts in the mist
events.text: Flat punts slide out of the dawn mist, with no sound but a drip from the poles. There are more of them than there should be.

events.name: Blowpipes
events.text: Tiny {darts|thorns|needles} from the canopy, tipped with something that makes the limbs heavy.
events.check: Constitution save DC 13 for anyone hit
events.failText: they are poisoned and slowed for a minute
events.twist: The darts are meant to sleep, not kill. Someone wants the party carried somewhere.

events.name: Sand-skiffs
events.text: Sand-skiffs under taut sails come skimming over the dunes, faster than horses, raiders leaning out with {spears|nets|hooked poles}.
events.twist: A skiff left behind would carry the party fast across the dunes, if anyone can sail it.

events.name: Breathing through reeds
events.text: Raiders lie buried under the sand, breathing through hollow reeds. They rise all around the party at once.
events.check: Perception DC 15 to spot the reeds
events.failText: the raiders get a surprise round

events.name: The white flag
events.text: A pirate ship comes alongside flying a {white|green|blue} flag and asks, very civilly, to parley.
events.twist: The parley is real. They want to hire the party, and they will be offended if refused.

events.name: Out of the sea fog
events.text: A dark hull slides out of the fog, close enough to touch, and grapples bite into the rail.

events.name: Muffled oars
events.text: {Small boats|Canoes|Long rowing boats} with muffled oars creep toward the ship in the dark, raiders lying flat in them.
events.check: Perception DC 13 for the watch
events.failText: they are aboard before anyone shouts
events.twist: The boats come from a ship lying dark a mile off, with its lamps out.

events.name: The parrot's warning
events.nod: Treasure Island: the parrot's 'pieces of eight'
events.text: The cook's parrot will not stop squawking about pieces of eight. Then it squawks a sailor's name, and the word 'tonight'.
events.twist: Half the crew plans to mutiny, and they want the party's cargo.

events.name: No witnesses
events.text: The party stumbles on smugglers landing {crates|barrels|people} in a hidden cove. The smugglers decide they cannot have been seen.

events.name: Down the ropes
events.text: A sky ship with {no markings|its name painted over|black sails} drops out of the clouds overhead, and raiders slide down ropes all around the party.
events.twist: The sky ship is stolen. Its owners will pay well for news of it.

events.name: Knives in their teeth
events.text: Swimmers cut the anchor rope in the night and climb the hull with knives in their teeth.
events.twist: They are not after the ship. They want one passenger, and they have a sketch.

events.name: Burning the ricks
events.text: Riders set the {haystacks|barns|hedges} alight on both sides of the lane, and wait in the smoke for whoever runs out.

events.name: Starting the slide
events.text: A shout from above, then a roar: raiders have set off a snowslide, and they will pick through what is left.
events.check: Dexterity save DC 15 for everyone
events.failText: they are half-buried and restrained when the raiders arrive

events.name: The core poachers' camp
events.text: The party walks into a hidden camp of core poachers working an unlicensed hunting ground. The poachers decide the party must not leave.

events.name: The wardens
events.text: The wayside wardens who are meant to keep this road safe close the gate behind the party, smiling.
events.twist: The local lord gets a cut and will not want to hear about it.

events.name: Fire behind them
events.text: Smoke rises behind the party: raiders have lit the grass upwind. The fire drives them toward a line of archers on the next rise.

events.name: At the well
events.text: The only well for a day in any direction has guards, and a price. They charge in blood if anyone argues.

events.name: The charcoal burners
events.text: Charcoal burners with soot-black faces watch the party pass in silence. Then they all pick up their {axes|shovels|long knives} at once.
events.twist: Their kilns hide something they will kill to keep secret.

events.name: A price on the captain
events.text: The bandit captain has a face the party knows from a Society bounty notice. Alive, he is worth {fifty|a hundred|two hundred} iron spirit coins.

events.name: Still sealed
events.text: The ambushers carry the haul from their last robbery, still sealed with a merchant house's wax. The merchant will pay handsomely to have it back.

events.name: Seen them first
events.text: The party spots the ambushers settling into position before the ambushers spot them.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 for everyone to circle behind them
events.failText: someone treads on a stick, and it is a straight fight

events.name: The map in his boot
events.text: After the fight, the bandit leader's boot holds a folded map with a cross on it, a day's ride off.

events.name: The bandit cache
events.text: The cross on the map marks a hollow {tree|cairn|wreck}. Inside is the bandits' cache, and the last of the gang is guarding it.

events.name: The grateful merchant
events.text: The party arrives just as raiders close on a merchant's {wagon|barge|mule train}. Save it, and the merchant opens her stock at cost.

events.name: Good horses
events.text: The ambushers rode better mounts than they deserved. When they flee on foot, the horses stay behind, saddled and fresh.

events.name: The bandits' prisoner
events.text: Tied up in the bandits' camp is a Bronze-rank smith they meant to ransom.
events.twist: Freed, she offers to rework one weapon for each of the party, free of charge.

events.name: The paymaster's box
events.text: One ambusher fights from behind the others, guarding a small {iron|brass|ironwood} box. It is the gang's pay, in bronze spirit coins.

events.name: On the Society's list
events.text: The ambushers are a gang the Adventure Society has been hunting for months. Bringing proof to the branch earns a commendation and a contract fee.

events.name: Pitchforks to the rescue
events.text: The fight is going badly until a mob of villagers with pitchforks and {frying pans|rolling pins|hoes} charges in on the party's side.
events.twist: The villagers have been robbed by this gang for years, and they throw the party a feast.

events.name: The one who won't
events.text: One young bandit throws down his {club|spear|knife} and refuses to fight. He shouts a warning to the party about the archers.

events.name: Back for the harvest
events.nod: Seven Samurai
events.text: The party reaches a village just as bandits ride in for their yearly share of the harvest. The village elder asks, very quietly, for help.
events.twist: Win, and the village carves the party's names over the well.

events.name: The boy and the traps
events.nod: Home Alone
events.text: Bandits are trying to rob a farmhouse, and keep falling over things. A small boy inside has trapped every door.

events.name: The bandits' dog
events.text: When the bandits run, their big scruffy {dog|goat|goose} stays behind, wagging. It follows the party for the rest of the journey.

events.name: An old friend in the fight
events.text: The ambush is closing in when {npc} arrives, out of nowhere, swinging. They heard the party was on this road.

events.name: The freed captives
events.text: Behind the ambushers' lines is a wagon of bound captives. Once free, they sing the whole way to the next town.

events.name: Surrender and tea
events.text: Outnumbered, the bandits surrender, boil a kettle and share their {tea|cider|soup}. They are tired, and they just want to go home.
events.twist: Their leader gives up the name of the noble house that hired them.

events.name: The road that isn't
events.text: The way ahead runs on smoothly, but it is an illusion laid over {a cliff edge|a deep bog|a sinkhole}. The illusionist is waiting below.
events.check: Investigation DC 15 to see the illusion
events.failText: the lead walker steps into it

events.name: Scrolls they can't read
events.text: The bandits have a satchel of stolen spell scrolls and no idea how to read them. Every round, someone reads one aloud and something unexpected happens.
events.twist: Any scrolls left unread afterwards are worth a fortune.

events.name: Out of the door in the air
events.text: A door hangs in the air beside the way, and ambushers step out of the small astral space behind it, then step back to heal.
events.twist: Inside the door is the gang's hideout, and their loot.

events.name: The silence
events.text: All sound stops at once. Inside the circle of silence, spells will not come, and the ambushers attack with {blades|clubs|garrottes}.

events.name: The pinning circle
events.text: Runes flare on the ground under the party, and a circle of light pins them in place while the ambushers close in.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to break the circle
events.failText: the party fights the first round restrained

events.name: The closing trees
events.text: The trees bend and knit their branches together behind the party. {A druid|An old woman|A young man} sits in the canopy, and her friends wait among the roots.

events.name: The bright wards
events.text: They attack inside a ring of old ward-stones. Every drop of blood spilled makes the stones glow brighter, and the attackers stronger.
events.twist: Smash a stone and the glow goes out, for both sides.

events.name: Called-down lightning
events.text: A renegade priest of the Church of the Storm stands up and calls lightning down on the party out of {a clear sky|a single small cloud|nowhere}.

events.name: Ambushers ambushed
events.text: Halfway through the fight, a second group bursts out of hiding and attacks the ambushers.
events.twist: They have been after this gang for weeks and want to know which side the party is on.

events.name: The same gang again
events.text: The same bandits ambush the party at the same spot as yesterday, unhurt and with no memory of meeting before.
events.twist: They have been doing this every day for a month, and the dead ones are back too.

events.name: Giggling in the air
events.text: Unseen attackers strike from all sides, {giggling|humming|counting aloud}. A dusting of flour, or a splash of water, shows where they are.

events.name: Strings of light
events.text: The ambushers move in jerks, like puppets. Fine strings of light run from their backs to someone hidden out of sight.
events.twist: The attackers are victims. Cut the strings and they collapse, weeping.

events.name: Hanging like bats
events.text: The bandits hang upside down from {branches|the rigging|a bridge}, wrapped in dark cloaks, waiting to drop.

events.name: The appointment
events.text: A neat letter arrives by courier announcing that the party will be ambushed, with the place and the hour, and wishing them well.

events.name: Right on time
events.text: Exactly at the promised place and hour, the ambush comes, as advertised. The sender has a seat to watch.

events.name: Three inches tall
events.text: A gang of bandits no taller than a hand rides on {mice|frogs|rats} and threatens the party with needle-swords.
events.twist: They are shrunk adventurers from a Magic Society accident, and they want help getting their size back.

events.name: One voice
events.text: Every one of the ambushers speaks at once, in the same voice, saying the same words.

events.name: Just a scratch
events.nod: Monty Python and the Holy Grail: the Black Knight
events.text: A lone knight in black guards a bridge and will let no one pass. However badly he is beaten, he insists it is only a scratch.

events.name: Arguing over the recipe
events.nod: The Hobbit: the trolls arguing until dawn
events.text: The brutes who grab the party argue at length about whether to {roast|boil|stew} them. The longer the party keeps them arguing, the closer it gets to dawn.
events.check: Deception or Persuasion DC 13 to keep the argument going
events.failText: they settle on roasting

events.name: It's a trap
events.nod: Star Wars: 'It's a trap!'
events.text: An outworlder travelling with the party yells that it is a trap, in a voice that suggests a famous quote from home. He is right, and very pleased.

events.name: A ten-foot pole
events.nod: D&D: the ten-foot pole
events.text: The way ahead is laced with tripwires and pressure plates. The pedlar who sold the party a ten-foot pole last week looks very wise now.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to find the triggers
events.failText: a net falls and the ambushers rush in

events.name: The retired couple
events.text: An elderly couple have robbed this stretch for {forty|fifty|sixty} years. They still do it, mostly from habit, with a crossbow and a very sharp walking stick.

events.name: The rehearsal
events.text: The party walks in on bandits rehearsing an ambush with {wooden swords|chalk marks|a script}. Everyone freezes.

events.name: Opening night
events.text: The same bandits from the rehearsal spring the real ambush. They have practised hard, and still forget their places.

events.name: The scout who ran
events.text: A lone scout spies on the party, then bolts the moment she is seen.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to catch her
events.failText: she gets away

events.name: Back with the gang
events.text: The scout who got away is back, with the whole gang behind her, and they know how the party fights.

events.name: Caltrops
events.text: Caltrops scattered in the grass lame the mounts, and the ambushers stand up out of the {ditch|reeds|rocks}.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to spot them in time
events.failText: a mount is lamed and has to be led
events.twist: The caltrops are stamped with a noble house's armoury mark.

events.name: The falling net
events.text: A weighted net drops from above onto the middle of the party. Clubs, not blades: they want prisoners.
events.check: Dexterity save DC 13 for anyone under it
events.failText: they are restrained until cut free
events.twist: Their wagon has a cage on it, and a list of buyers.

events.name: Archers in the windmill
events.text: Arrows from the slits of a {windmill|grain store|bell tower} on the hill. The sails turn slowly, and someone is still grinding grain inside.

events.name: Both sides call for help
events.text: The party comes upon an ambush already under way. Both the ambushers and their victims shout that the other side are the criminals.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to tell who is lying
events.failText: the party picks the wrong side for the first round

events.name: A job interview
events.text: The ambush is a test. A nervous recruit has to rob the party while the gang watches from cover with {scorecards|notes|snacks}.
events.twist: If the recruit fails, the gang wants to hire the party instead.

events.name: In the ship's hold
events.text: Someone has been hiding in the hold since {the last port|before the ship sailed|three days ago}. Tonight they come up the ladder with friends.

events.name: An unreported astral space
events.text: An astral space entrance in a hillside, freshly opened.
events.twist: Report it for a Society bounty, or go in first.

events.name: A village feeding something
events.text: Offerings at the edge of the water, a monster that leaves the village alone, and a traveller who went missing here last week.

events.name: The overdue team
events.text: An Iron-rank team left on a contract three days ago. The party finds their camp, but not them.

events.name: A coin farm under pressure
events.text: Coin farm guards are outnumbered and offer a share of the week's coins for help holding until dawn.

events.name: A stolen greatback
events.text: A Host is hunting the thieves who took a greatback, and the party is the only other group in sight.

events.name: A child who just awakened
events.text: A village has its first essence user: a frightened child, and parents more frightened still.

events.name: An outworlder
events.text: Someone sits dazed by the road, smelling faintly of springtime, with no idea where they are.

events.name: A town that tried
events.text: A ruin: walls, a shrine, a cellar no one emptied, and whatever has spawned in it since.

events.name: A dying messenger
events.text: A dying messenger presses a sealed letter on the party, meant for someone at their destination.

events.name: A god's small request
events.text: A wayside shrine of {church} asks something of whoever stops there.
events.twist: Do the task for a minor blessing.

events.name: Missing posters
events.text: Every tree for a mile carries the same missing poster: a young {woman|man} last seen on this road, a month ago.
events.twist: The face on the posters changes each time someone looks away.

events.name: A map in a bottle
events.text: A sealed bottle washed up with a hand-drawn map to an unreported astral space.

events.name: The silent village
events.text: A village where everyone goes about their day perfectly normally, and nobody makes a single sound.

events.name: Coin farm under siege
events.text: A spirit coin farm's workers are holed up in the main building while monsters circle outside. The owner offers a share of this month's coins for help.

events.name: The wrong grave
events.text: A grieving family at a fresh roadside grave insists the body inside isn't their son. They want someone to dig it up.

events.name: A stolen awakening stone
events.text: A courier gasps out that the awakening stone he was carrying was stolen, and the thieves went that way.
events.twist: The stone is fake, and the courier is a decoy.

events.name: Bells under the water
events.text: Bells ring beneath a lake at dusk. The locals say there was a town there before the flood.

events.name: A plea from the Healer
events.text: A Church of the Healer clinic is out of medicine and two days from the next town. The priest asks the party to fetch herbs from a dangerous gully.

events.name: Smuggler's cache
events.text: Fresh digging and a carefully hidden trapdoor under a lone tree.
events.twist: The smugglers are coming back tonight to collect.

events.name: The haunted waystation
events.text: The waystation keeper begs the party to stay the night. Something knocks on every door at midnight, and he can't keep anyone on staff.

events.name: Lost expedition journal
events.text: A Magic Society expedition journal, with the last pages describing 'a door in the rock that wasn't there yesterday'.

events.name: The door in the rock
events.text: The party finds it: a door cut into bare rock, exactly as the journal described, standing open and lit from inside.

events.name: Feuding farmsteads
events.text: Two neighbouring farms have been at war for three generations over a single apple tree on the boundary. Both want the party to settle it.

events.name: A summons from the Society
events.text: An Adventure Society runner has been chasing the party with a sealed contract: urgent, nearby, and well paid.

events.name: The crying statue
events.text: A roadside statue of {church}'s god weeps real tears, and pilgrims are gathering.
events.twist: Something is living inside the statue.

events.name: Kidnapped heir
events.text: A noble house's banner lies in the ditch with an overturned carriage. There is no sign of the passenger, but there are clear tracks.

events.name: Ring-bearer
events.nod: The Lord of the Rings: a small hero taking a ring to a volcano
events.text: A small, grim traveller with one plain ring on a chain refuses all offers of help. He is walking to the nearest volcano. It is very far away, and he has no map.

events.name: Sword in the market stone
events.nod: Arthurian legend: the sword in the stone
events.text: A sword stuck in an anvil at a market cross, with a queue of forty would-be kings, a pie stall and a Society clerk taking names.
events.twist: Nobody has pulled it out, because the anvil is a monster and the sword is its tongue.

events.name: The pied musician
events.nod: Folklore: the Pied Piper of Hamelin
events.text: A village has paid a travelling musician to rid it of monsters, then refused to pay him. This morning, the children are gone.

events.name: The Society's oversight
events.text: A village asked the Adventure Society for help three times. Nobody came, and the villagers have stopped asking.

events.name: Footprints that stop
events.text: A child's footprints lead off the road into soft ground and stop dead in the middle of a field. A {shoe|doll|wooden sword} lies where they end.
events.check: Survival DC 15 to find where the trail picks up again
events.twist: The trail picks up again a mile away, walking backwards.

events.name: The search party
events.text: A dozen villagers with lanterns and sticks are combing the {reeds|trees|gullies} for a missing shepherd. They beg the party to join, and offer what little they have.
events.check: Survival or Perception DC 13 to find him first

events.name: The lost apprentice
events.text: A Magic Society enchanter is frantic. Her apprentice went to gather a rare reagent near here two days ago, carrying her best focus. She will pay well for both.
events.twist: The apprentice ran away on purpose and does not want to be found.

events.name: A note in the boot
events.text: An abandoned {boot|glove|hat} by the roadside holds a folded note: 'If found, tell my sister at {place} I did not leave her. I was taken.'

events.name: Ransom on a stick
events.text: A ransom note is nailed to a waystation post, asking for forty iron spirit coins for the return of a {miller's|smith's|reeve's} daughter. The deadline is tomorrow at dusk.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to work out where the note was written
events.twist: The daughter wrote the note herself, to pay for passage to Rimaros.

events.name: The boat that came back empty
events.text: A fishing boat drifts in with its nets out, {a pot still warm on the stove|a lamp still lit|a cat asleep on the bow}, and nobody aboard. The crew's families are already gathering on the shore.

events.name: Taken by the hill folk
events.text: A farmer insists his wife was taken by the hill folk, who he says live in the barrow behind his farm. Nobody believes him. Smoke rises from the barrow every evening.
events.twist: The barrow holds a small, very polite goblin family, and his wife is visiting them by choice.

events.name: The Iron-rank's last signal
events.text: A Society signal flare goes up from the {hills|woods|marsh} to the east, the colour that means a team needs help now. Nobody else is closer.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to reach them in time
events.twist: Only one of the team is still alive, and she was the one who fired it.

events.name: A trail of coins
events.text: A line of iron spirit coins, one every ten paces, runs off the road. Someone was leaving a trail for someone else to follow.

then.name: The end of the coin trail

events.name: The end of the coin trail
events.text: The coin trail ends at a {cave mouth|collapsed barn|sunken boat}. Inside are signs of a struggle, a broken coin pouch and a scrap of a Healer's robe.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to learn who was taken and how long ago

events.name: Wanted: one husband
events.text: A furious woman is pinning up posters of her missing husband. He went for bread four days ago. She wants him found, and then she wants to shout at him.
events.twist: He is at the next waystation, hiding from her, and pays the party to say they never saw him.

events.name: The pilgrim count
events.text: A Church of the Journey priest is counting her pilgrims for the third time. She set out with twelve. She keeps counting eleven, but nobody is missing.
events.twist: The twelfth pilgrim is a spirit who joined them at the last shrine and wants to finish the walk.

events.name: The lost Cloud Clan child
events.text: A small Cloud Clan child fell from a cloud path above and landed, unhurt, in a pile of soft moss. He wants to go home, which is straight up.
events.check: Athletics DC 15 to climb the path, or find another way up

events.name: The torn contract
events.text: Half of an Adventure Society contract flaps on a {bramble|mast|signpost}. The reward is a Bronze-rank sum, but the part describing the target has been torn away.

then.name: The other half of the contract

events.name: The other half of the contract
events.text: The other half of the torn contract is clutched in the hand of a dead Bronze-ranker by the road. It describes the target, and the target is a person.

events.name: A contract too cheap
events.text: A village has pooled everything it has to post a contract: twelve iron coins to kill whatever is taking their goats. No team will take it for that.
events.twist: Whatever is taking the goats is Bronze rank.

events.name: Assessment on the road
events.text: A Society assessor is travelling between branches and offers to watch the party fight their next monster. A good showing goes on file.

events.name: The rival team's contract
events.text: A rival team has nailed their claimed contract to a tree with a note: 'Ours. Hands off.' The {monster|giant boar|swamp hydra} in question is asleep twenty yards away, right now.

events.name: The Society's sealed crate
events.text: A Society wagon has thrown a wheel. The driver must stay with a sealed crate marked 'Do not open, do not shake, do not sing near'. He needs a runner to the next town.
events.twist: Something inside the crate is humming along to the driver's whistling.

events.name: Monster parts wanted
events.text: A Magic Society notice offers good bronze for the {glands|horns|eyes} of a monster that nests near here. A smaller note below says three teams have tried.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to find the nest

events.name: Missed check-in
events.text: A Society waypost keeper says a team due to check in yesterday never came. He has their route and a map, but no one to send.
events.twist: The team is fine, and drinking. They forgot. The monster they were sent for is not fine, and is coming.

events.name: A Magic Society test
events.text: A Magic Society researcher offers ten iron coins a head to anyone who will walk through a ring of chalk marks on the ground and describe what they feel.
events.twist: Each person feels something different, and one of them hears their name.

events.name: The bounty on the board
events.text: A waystation's contract board has one card left, pinned with a knife: a bounty on a {bandit chief|rogue elementalist|deserter from the Storm Kingdom navy}, with a sketch that looks oddly familiar.

events.name: The survey markers
events.text: Someone has pulled up the Magic Society survey markers along the road and laid them in a perfect circle around a dead tree.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to read what the circle is measuring

events.name: A licence on the ground
events.text: An Adventure Society licence lies face down in the mud. The name on it belongs to someone the party knows died last year.

events.name: The nest under the bridge
events.text: Locals refuse to cross the old bridge. Something has nested under it and takes anything that lingers. The ford is a day out of the way.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 to cross without waking it, or fight it for its core

events.name: Fresh spawn site
events.text: The ground is scorched in a neat ring and the air tastes of metal: a monster has spawned here within the hour, and it went {north|uphill|towards the village}.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to track it

events.name: The surge counters
events.text: A village elder has carved a mark on the {gatepost|church door|well lid} for every monster seen this month. The marks have filled it and started on the wall.
events.twist: One mark is not a monster. The elder will not say what it is.

events.name: The tame monster
events.text: A farmer has been raising a monster in her barn since it spawned as a tiny thing. It is now the size of the barn and she would like advice.

events.name: Coin farm short-handed
events.text: A coin farm foreman is hiring guards for one night only. Half his crew went down with {a fever|bad fish|a curse}, and the farm's magic is peaking tonight.
events.check: Perception DC 13 on watch to catch the spawn before it reaches the coin vats
events.twist: The fever was no accident: someone wants the farm overrun tonight.

events.name: The monster with a collar
events.text: A monster wanders out of the trees wearing a jewelled collar and a little brass tag: 'If found, return to House {Ardent|Whitlow|Osmere}. Reward.'

events.name: Cores in the riverbed
events.text: Low water has exposed the riverbed, and something glints among the stones: monster cores, dozens of them, washed down from somewhere upstream.
events.twist: Something upstream is killing monsters faster than they spawn.

events.name: The unlit candle
events.text: A shrine of the Church of Death has one black candle that will not light, whatever anyone tries. The priest says it means someone in the party is overdue.
events.twist: It lights the moment the party leaves, and goes out again when the next traveller arrives.

events.name: The broken shackle
events.text: A Church of Liberty sign, a broken shackle chalked on a milestone, points off the road. Someone nearby is hiding a person who needs to get away.
events.twist: The person hiding is a convicted murderer, and believes Liberty has blessed his escape.

events.name: Temple without a priest
events.text: A village temple of the Church of the Hearth has had no priest for a year. The villagers ask if anyone in the party could lead tonight's supper prayer.

events.name: The weighing of hearts
events.text: A Church of Justice circuit judge has a trial to hold in a village ahead and nobody to stand for the accused. She asks the party to speak for him.
events.check: Investigation or Persuasion DC 15 to clear his name
events.twist: The accused is guilty, but not of the crime he is charged with.

events.name: Healer's tithe
events.text: A Church of the Healer cart is collecting donations of {healing potions|clean bandages|herbs} for a clinic in a surge zone. Anyone who gives gets a token the priests honour.

events.name: The wrong god's shrine
events.text: A shrine of the Church of Purity has been repainted overnight in the colours of the Church of the Revels, with a barrel of wine on the altar. Both churches are coming to look.

events.name: A door with no house
events.text: A heavy oak door stands alone in a field, frame and all, with nothing behind it. When knocked, it knocks back.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to tell it is an astral space entrance

events.name: The flooded crypt
events.text: The ground has given way beside the road, opening into a flooded crypt. Coffins bob in the black water, and one of them is moving against the current.
events.twist: The moving coffin holds a living Smoulder, sealed in by rivals, and the water is cooling him to death.

events.name: The cartographer's error
events.text: The party's map shows a town here. There is no town, only a ring of foundation stones and a single working well.
events.twist: The well water tastes of salt, and the sea is two hundred miles away.

events.name: The watchtower light
events.text: An old watchtower, abandoned for years by every account, has a lamp burning in its top window tonight.

events.name: Astral space rumour
events.text: A drunk at a waystation is selling directions to an unclaimed astral space for one bronze coin. Everyone else there says he sells the same directions every week.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to tell he is telling the truth this time
events.twist: He is telling the truth, and so did the people who went in last week.

events.name: Stairs in the dune
events.text: The wind has scoured a dune down to bedrock, uncovering a flight of carved stairs going down. Cool air breathes up from below.

events.name: The forged seal
events.text: A courier's satchel lies split open in the ditch. The letters inside carry the seal of House {Ardent|Whitlow|Osmere}, and every one is a forgery.
events.check: Investigation DC 15 to work out who the forger was copying

events.name: Smugglers' lantern code
events.text: Lanterns flash from a {cliff|ridge|tower} at dusk: three long, two short, again and again. Somebody is waiting for an answer.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to crack the pattern and answer it

events.name: Too many guards
events.text: A plain farm cart rolls past with six Silver-rank guards walking beside it. It is carrying {turnips|hay|empty barrels}, as far as anyone can see.
events.twist: The guards are guarding the driver, an heir travelling in disguise.

events.name: The poisoned well
events.text: A waystation well has a crude skull scratched on its lid. Two dead {heidels|goats|dogs} lie nearby. Whoever did it wanted the next village to go thirsty.
events.check: Medicine DC 13 to name the poison and who sells it

events.name: A cult sign on the milestone
events.text: The same symbol, {a hand with an eye in its palm|a crown of thorns|a circle with a bite out of it}, is scratched on every milestone for ten miles, each one a little fresher.

events.name: The burned toll house
events.text: A noble house toll house has burned to the ground. The tollkeeper's family sits in the ashes, and the tolls box is missing.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to tell it was set from inside

events.name: A deal at the crossroads
events.text: A smiling stranger in good clothes waits at a crossroads, offering any one wish for a small favour later. He has a list of names, and some are crossed off.
events.nod: Folklore: the deal at the crossroads

events.name: The bought witness
events.text: A frightened clerk says she saw a Society official take a bribe to bury a contract. She will swear to it, if someone gets her safely to the next branch.

events.name: Stolen church bell
events.text: A village's Church of the Earth bell has been stolen overnight. It weighs as much as a {heidel|small house|full wagon}, and the thieves left a trail of very deep footprints.
events.check: Survival DC 10 to follow the obvious trail
events.twist: The thieves are three young Leonids from the next village, and they want it back for their own wedding.

events.name: Contraband cores
events.text: A broken crate by the {road|shore|riverbank} has spilled Bronze-rank monster cores stamped with a Storm Kingdom customs mark. Someone will be very upset to lose them.
events.twist: The customs mark is fake, and the people who faked it are on their way back.

events.name: The slaver's wagon
events.text: A barred wagon heads for the coast, the driver holding a Storm Kingdom licence. The people inside are bound by magical contracts, and one of them catches the party's eye.

events.name: The hidden ledger
events.text: A loose stone in a waystation wall hides a smuggler's ledger: dates, coin amounts and the name of a {church|noble house|Society clerk} paid to look away.

events.name: Two masks at the fire
events.text: Two figures in blank masks sit by the roadside at a dead fire. When the party passes they stand, bow and walk away in step. A Church of Disguise sign is chalked where they sat.

events.name: The hungry mill
events.text: A miller's waterwheel has been turning the wrong way for a week. The flour comes out grey and tastes of {rust|tears|old pennies}. She wants it fixed before market day.
events.check: Arcana or Nature DC 13 to find the cause upstream

events.name: Feud over the bridge
events.text: Two villages on either side of a river both claim the bridge. Each one has built a toll booth at its own end, and they charge for each other's half.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to broker a peace and cross free
events.twist: Both reeves are the same man, who moved house and never told anyone.

events.name: Scarecrows that move
events.text: A farmer swears his scarecrows {walk the fields at night|turn their heads to watch him|keep turning up in the kitchen}. He offers supper and a bed to anyone who will sit up and watch.

events.name: The drought dowser
events.text: A village's wells are dry, and its last hope is an old dowser who can barely walk. She asks someone to carry her across the hills while she feels for water.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to carry her far enough

events.name: A curse on the herd
events.text: Every goat in a village has gone blind on the same night. The villagers blame a woman who arrived last month, and they are gathering outside her door.
events.check: Medicine or Insight DC 15 to find the real cause before they act

events.name: The night market's missing stall
events.text: A village's monthly night market has one empty pitch. The stallholder has had it every month for forty years, and nobody knows where she lives.
events.twist: She is sitting in the empty pitch, but only children can see her.

events.name: Too many weddings
events.text: A village has seven weddings in one week and only one priest of the Church of the Hearth, who has lost his voice. He writes out a plea for help on a slate.
events.twist: All seven grooms are the same man.

events.name: The flooded cellar
events.text: A widow's cellar has flooded, and something has moved in with the water. She would sleep better if someone checked. She offers a jar of {honey|plum brandy|pickled eggs}.
events.check: Athletics DC 10 to pump it out, or go in and see

events.name: The village that votes
events.text: A village elects its headman every morning by tossing a coin. Today's headman is seven years old and has declared a tax on strangers of one song each.
events.twist: The coin always lands the same way, and an old woman has been choosing the headman for thirty years.

events.name: Prize heidel stolen
events.text: A farmer's prize two-headed heidel has been stolen the day before the county fair. Both heads, he notes, were very distinctive.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to follow the tracks

events.name: The witch in the wood
events.text: Villagers say a witch lives in the wood and sends them luck if they leave milk out. This year the milk is untouched and the luck has stopped.

events.name: A cold hearth
events.text: In one village, every fire in every house went out at the same moment last night and will not relight. The Church of the Hearth shrine is cold too.
events.check: Religion DC 13 to learn what the Hearth wants
events.twist: Someone in the village stole a coal from the shrine, and the god wants it back.

events.name: Tithe barn trouble
events.text: A noble house's steward is about to empty a village tithe barn before winter. The villagers say they paid already, and have the receipt.
events.check: Persuasion or Investigation DC 13 to settle it

events.name: A name for a name
events.text: A small, nasty creature has spun a farmer's straw into spirit coins. Now it wants his firstborn, unless someone can guess its name by sundown.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Rumpelstiltskin
events.check: Investigation or Arcana DC 15 to learn its name

events.name: The beanstalk
events.text: A vine as thick as a tower has shot up overnight from a pauper's garden, straight into the clouds. His mother is furious about the cow.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Jack and the Beanstalk
events.check: Athletics DC 15 to climb it

events.name: Grandmother's cottage
events.text: A girl in a red hooded cloak asks the way to her grandmother's cottage in the woods. The party has just passed it. The door was open and the bed was full of fur.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Little Red Riding Hood

events.name: The gingerbread house
events.text: A cottage made entirely of {gingerbread|toffee|honey cake} stands in a clearing. A sweet old woman waves from the window and says she's just warming the oven.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Hansel and Gretel

events.name: Ten-foot pole for sale
events.text: A pedlar has set up outside a ruin, selling ten-foot poles, rope and chalk at triple price. He says the last team that didn't buy a pole never came out.
events.nod: D&D: the ten-foot pole

events.name: The cursed princess
events.text: A thorn hedge has grown around a manor house, and everyone inside has slept for a year. The thorns part only for {the kind|the brave|the honest}.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Sleeping Beauty

events.name: The goblin market
events.text: A night market in a hollow sells fruit no one has ever seen. The traders insist on payment in memories, and they are very generous with change.
events.nod: Poem: Goblin Market

events.name: The hero's statue
events.text: A village is raising a statue to the adventurer who saved it from a surge. The carver can't remember her face and asks if the party has heard of her.
events.check: History DC 13 to recall her

events.name: Message for the Khan
events.text: A dying heidel carries a saddlebag marked with a Drift Host sign. Inside is a message for a Khan whose Host is two days north, by the old rider's count.

events.name: The Khan's answer
events.text: Riders of the Host find the party, read the message, and their Khan sends back thanks: fresh heidels for a day and a place by any Host's fire.

events.name: The deserted outpost
events.text: A Society outpost stands empty, door swinging. The log ends mid-sentence: 'The surge readings jumped again this morning, and the instruments are...'

events.name: The wishing well's debt
events.text: A wishing well is stuffed with iron spirit coins. A sign reads: 'Take what you need. You will be asked to pay it back.'
events.twist: Months later, a polite voice from any well the party passes asks for the coins back.

events.name: Pearls in the shallows
events.text: Merfolk children are diving for pearls near a wreck, and they want help shifting a beam. There's a strongbox under it they cannot lift.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to lift the beam

events.name: The astral key
events.text: A {glass|bone|silver} key hangs in the air at head height, turning slowly. When touched it grows warm and pulls gently in one direction.
events.twist: It opens an astral space that has been locked from the inside.

events.name: A claim marker
events.text: A Society claim marker has been planted beside a fresh astral entrance. The claim is three months old, and the team that made it has never come back to work it.
events.twist: The team is still inside, and has not noticed any time pass.

events.name: The rule of the space
events.text: A scrawled warning outside an astral entrance reads: 'Inside, everyone must {rhyme|sing|walk backwards}. We learned this the hard way.'
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to tell whether the warning is real

events.name: Something came out
events.text: An astral space entrance stands open, and the grass around it is dead in a perfect circle. Tracks lead away from it, but none lead in.
events.twist: The tracks belong to someone the party has met.

events.name: The space that wants visitors
events.text: An astral space entrance keeps drifting closer to the party all day, a few yards at a time, like a dog that wants a walk.
events.twist: Inside is a tiny, perfect garden and a door labelled with the party's names.

events.name: The sealed vault
events.text: A collapsed ruin hides a vault door carved with the symbol of {a forgotten noble house|the Church of Knowledge|a long-dead Khan}. It is still locked.
events.check: Thieves' tools or Arcana DC 15 to open it

events.name: Treasure map tattoo
events.text: A dead sailor has a map tattooed across his back, with an X in a place the party can name. Someone has tried to cut part of it away.
events.twist: The missing part is tattooed on his twin, who is alive and wants a cut.

events.name: The underwater door
events.text: A shimmering door hangs just beneath the surface, lit from within. Merfolk avoid this stretch, and their children dare each other to touch it.
events.twist: It opens onto a dry astral space full of seashells that whisper.

events.name: The ghost ship's bell
events.text: A ship's bell rings out across the water, but there is no ship. The sound comes from {below|behind|all around} the party, and it is getting closer.

events.name: Castaway's signal
events.text: A mirror flashes from a tiny island: a castaway, sunburnt and delighted, who has been keeping a goat and a very detailed diary.
events.twist: He was a Bronze-rank captain, and his crew mutinied for his map.

events.name: The kraken bounty
events.text: A harbour notice offers a Silver-rank bounty on a sea monster sinking fishing boats. {A fisherman|A merfolk diver|An one-eyed cook} says he knows its feeding ground and will sell the secret.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to tell whether he is honest
events.twist: The monster is a mother defending her young, and the fishermen took one.

events.name: Wreck on the reef
events.text: A merchant ship lies broken on a reef at low tide, cargo still in its hold. The tide turns in an hour.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to get in and out with something worth having

events.name: The drowned chapel
events.text: At low tide a Church of the Ocean chapel rises from the sand, its doors still sealed. The priest at the next town says it sank two hundred years ago.

events.name: A merfolk plea
events.text: A merfolk elder surfaces beside the party. Her people's reef is dying, and she believes something poured into the water upstream is to blame.

events.name: The floating auction
events.text: A barge has anchored offshore, flying a flag that means a private auction is under way. Rowboats bring bidders. Whatever is for sale, nobody is saying.
events.twist: The lot is an awakening stone stolen from the Magic Society.

events.name: The buried caravan
events.text: A sandstorm has uncovered a caravan buried long ago: wagons, bones and heidel harness. One wagon is still locked, and something inside {taps back|hums|is breathing}.

events.name: The oasis tax
events.text: An oasis has a fence, a gate and a polite Leonid charging one iron coin a {cup|bucket|waterskin}. He insists he owns the water, and has a deed to prove it.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to tell the deed is forged
events.twist: The deed is real. The Leonid is the last heir of a family that dug the oasis by hand.

events.name: Glass in the sand
events.text: A patch of desert has fused into glass in the shape of a giant figure, arms spread. At noon it rings like a bell.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to learn what made it

events.name: The empty walking camp
events.text: A greatback stands alone in the grass, its tent still lashed to its back, calm and well fed. There is no sign of its family.

events.name: The family in the grass
events.text: The greatback's family is found camped in a gully, safe but stranded after the beast wandered off in the night. They are overjoyed, and they cook.

events.name: Tide-reader's warning
events.text: A young Drift Host tide-reader stops the party. The Wandering Tide is pooling {behind them|ahead of them|right where they stand}, and she cannot get word to her Host in time.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to carry her message

events.name: The rope bridge toll
events.text: A Cloud Clan bridge-keeper will let the party cross for the price of {a song|a story|one secret}. He is quite strict about the quality.
events.check: Performance DC 13 to pass

events.name: The condor's egg
events.text: A giant condor egg has rolled down a scree slope and sits by the path, warm and whole. Cloud Clan riders would pay a fortune for it.
events.twist: The mother is circling overhead, and she has seen the party.

events.name: The temple in the canopy
events.text: A ruined temple sits in the jungle canopy, held up by vines. A rope ladder dangles from it, recently mended.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to climb up
events.twist: A Church of Knowledge scholar lives up there and resents visitors who interrupt her reading.

events.name: Fever village
events.text: A jungle village is closed by a ring of white stones: fever inside. A child calls from the edge for medicine from the Healer's clinic a day back.
events.check: Medicine DC 15 to help without catching it

events.name: The avatar's footprint
events.text: A footprint ten feet long is pressed into the {stone|earth|deck}, glowing faintly. Priests of {church} are arriving to argue about it.

events.name: The heretic's book
events.text: A battered book of sermons lies by the {road|shore|rail}. Every page argues that the Church of Purity has misread its own god, citing chapter and verse.
events.twist: A Purity inquisitor is three hours behind the party, looking for it.

events.name: The god's errand
events.text: A priest of the Church of the Journey says her god told her to give a {map|lantern|pair of boots} to the first strangers she met today. She did not expect them to be armed.

events.name: The vow of silence
events.text: A Church of Truth novice has taken a vow not to speak until someone tells her a truth she has never heard. She holds out a {slate|wax tablet|bit of chalk} expectantly.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to find the right truth
events.twist: The truth she needs is something only one of the party knows about themselves.

events.name: The prayer that answered
events.text: A sailor prayed to the Church of the Storm for a wind, and now the wind follows him everywhere. He is very cold and wants it to stop.

events.name: A relic for sale
events.text: A pedlar is selling a finger bone he swears belonged to a saint of the Church of the Hero. A Hero priest nearby is turning purple.
events.twist: The bone is genuine, and it points to wherever a hero is needed.

events.name: The undead pilgrim
events.text: A pilgrim walks with a skull-and-flower badge pinned inside his cloak. He is a follower of Undeath, and he is begging for an escort past the Purity checkpoint ahead.

events.name: The second shadow
events.text: When the sun comes out, one of the party has two shadows. The second one keeps pointing at something {north|behind them|underground}.
events.twist: It belongs to someone who died nearby and wants to be found.

events.name: The cursed coin
events.text: An iron spirit coin turns up in someone's {pocket|boot|bedroll} every morning, however many times they spend it. It is always slightly warmer than it should be.

events.name: A dream shared
events.text: Everyone in the party wakes having dreamed of the same {tower|ship|well}, and the same voice asking them to come. It is a day's walk away.

events.name: The runaway golem
events.text: A clockwork construct the size of a cart thunders past, chased by a breathless Magic Society enchanter shouting that it is fine, completely fine.
events.check: Athletics DC 15 to catch it
events.twist: It is running from something, not away from its maker.

events.name: The ferryman's riddle
events.text: A ferryman will only take the party if they solve his puzzle: a wolf, a goat and a cabbage, a tiny boat, and a very hungry goat.
events.check: Intelligence DC 10
events.nod: Folk puzzle: the wolf, goat and cabbage

events.name: A bargain with the trees
events.text: The trees ahead have shuffled across the path. A voice in the leaves says they will part for one thing the party is willing to leave behind.

events.name: A tremor beneath
events.text: The ground shudders three times, then stops. A small sinkhole opens nearby, revealing a tunnel with old torch brackets.
events.twist: The tunnel is still in use, and the torches are warm.

events.name: The lantern bearers
events.text: A procession of hooded figures carrying green lanterns crosses the way at dusk, silent, heading for the {hills|marsh|old quarry}.

events.name: Where the lanterns went
events.text: The party finds where the lantern bearers gathered: a ring of green lanterns around a pit, all still lit, and a fresh rope tied off at the edge.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to climb down

events.name: A wounded merfolk scout
events.text: A merfolk scout clings to a {buoy|rock|floating spar}, badly cut. Raiders hit her patrol, and she needs her warning carried to the reef.
events.check: Medicine DC 13 to stop the bleeding

events.name: The reef's thanks
events.text: Merfolk surface around the party, the scout among them. They bring a net of pearls and promise fair currents for the rest of the voyage.

events.name: The bard's lost song
events.text: A Church of the Revels bard has lost the last verse of a famous drinking song and swears she will die without it. She asks the party to keep an ear open.

events.name: The last verse
events.text: A {shepherd|sailor|tollkeeper} is humming the bard's song, last verse and all. When the party passes it on, she weeps, sings it and buys every round.

events.name: The stopped clock
events.text: Every clock, sundial and hourglass in a village stopped at the same moment, and the villagers have not aged since. That was eleven years ago.

events.name: The clockmaker
events.text: A tired old Runic in a cave is holding a tiny glowing hourglass very still. He says if he lets it fall, the village will catch up with eleven years at once.

events.name: The dragon's census
events.text: A Draconian herald in full regalia is stopping travellers to ask whether any of them are dragons. It is for a count, he says. He seems very hopeful.
events.twist: One of the old stories is true, and a dragon has asked to be counted.

events.name: The world tree's seed
events.text: A seed the size of a fist falls at the party's feet, glowing gold. Every bird for a mile goes quiet, and a Church of the Earth priest arrives running.

events.name: Diamond-rank duel
events.text: Far off, two Diamond-rankers are fighting. The sky shifts colour with every blow. A frightened herald needs someone to carry a message of surrender between them.
events.check: Athletics or Constitution DC 18 to reach them alive

events.name: The empty throne
events.text: A stone throne sits at the {crossroads|top of a dune|bottom of a clear lake}, and anyone who sits in it hears every voice within a hundred miles at once.
events.twist: One of those voices is whispering the party's names.

events.name: A god's lost dog
events.text: A huge silver hound with stars in its fur trots up and drops a stick. A priest of the Church of the Journey nearly faints: it belongs to the god.
events.twist: The god will want it back, and is grateful to whoever keeps it safe.

events.name: The phoenix feather
events.text: A burning feather drifts down, lands without scorching anything, and keeps burning. Every alchemist in the next town will want it.
events.nod: Myth: the phoenix

events.name: The coin that talks
events.text: A bronze spirit coin in the party's purse has started giving advice. It is mostly about money, and mostly wrong.
events.twist: Once, at the worst moment, it is completely right.

events.name: Message in a loaf
events.text: A {loaf of bread|pie|wheel of cheese} bought at the last stop has a note baked into it: 'Help. They make us bake all night. Third oven.'

events.name: A child with a sword
events.text: A child of about nine is waiting by the {road|dock|gate} with a wooden sword, determined to join an adventuring team. He has packed sandwiches.
events.twist: His sister is an adventurer who went missing, and he is going to find her.

events.name: The knight's last oath
events.text: A dying knight asks the party to finish her oath: deliver her sword to the house of the person she failed to protect. She will not say what happened.

events.name: The hidden heir
events.text: An old servant recognises one of the party as the image of {a dead lord|a lost princess|a famous Khan}, and will not stop bowing.
events.twist: She is right about the face, but very wrong about the reason.

events.name: The goblin's grudge
events.text: A goblin {merchant|sailor|priest} demands an apology from whoever called him a monster at the last town. Nobody in the party did, but he has a list and a pencil.

events.name: The singing stones
events.text: A circle of standing stones hums a low chord. Anyone who hums along feels their mana fill a little.
events.twist: The chord grows louder each time, and something below it is waking.

events.name: The awakening stone in the egg
events.text: A cook cracks an egg at the waystation and an awakening stone drops out into the pan. Everyone in the room looks at everyone else.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to come to a fair deal with the cook

events.name: A favour owed
events.text: A merchant the party once helped waves from a {wagon|boat|window}. She owes them, and she knows of a job going nearby.

events.name: The rescued pet
events.text: A tiny Smoulder girl's pet fire-lizard has climbed a tree and set it smouldering. She asks very politely for help.
events.check: Athletics DC 10 to get it down before the tree catches

events.name: The bones that walk at noon
events.text: A skeleton climbs out of a ditch at noon, dusts itself off and walks towards the nearest town. It ignores everyone it passes.
events.twist: It is going home, and its family still lives there.

events.name: A message from the future
events.text: A letter is addressed to the party in their own handwriting, dated a month from now. It says only: 'Don't trust the {bridge|priest|third door}.'

events.name: The cracked mirror
events.text: A mirror propped by the {roadside|rail|well} shows the party with one extra person standing behind them. It always stands one step closer.

events.name: The lost bet
events.text: Two adventurers have bet their team names on a race to the next town. One asks the party to slow the other down, and offers half the winnings.
events.check: Deception DC 13 to send the rival the wrong way

events.name: Old soldier's map
events.text: A veteran of an old war sells a map of a battlefield where his company buried their pay chest. He is too old to dig.
events.check: History DC 13 to tell if the map is genuine
events.twist: His company did not bury pay. They buried their captain, with everything she owned.

events.name: The banquet in the ruin
events.text: In a ruined hall a banquet is laid, hot and fresh, with places set for exactly as many people as the party.
events.nod: Folklore: the fairy feast
events.twist: Anyone who eats cannot leave until they have danced till dawn.

events.name: Rest at the bonfire
events.text: A shrine with a fire that never goes out. Anyone who rests here wakes healed, but the monsters the party killed yesterday are back where they fell, and angry.
events.nod: Dark Souls: the bonfire

events.name: The mimic chest
events.text: A treasure chest sits alone in the middle of the {path|deck|clearing}, lid slightly open, with gold glinting inside. It is breathing very quietly.
events.nod: D&D: the mimic
events.check: Perception DC 13 to notice before someone touches it

events.name: The giant's causeway
events.text: A line of huge stepping stones runs out to sea, and a sign carved on the first reads: 'To the other giant. Don't keep him waiting.'
events.nod: Irish legend: the Giant's Causeway

events.name: The emperor's tailors
events.text: Two tailors are selling a robe they say is invisible to fools. A Silver-ranker is about to pay a silver coin for one, and is already wearing it.
events.nod: Fairy tale: The Emperor's New Clothes

events.name: The lamp seller
events.text: A pedlar offers new lamps for old. Anyone who trades him a battered lamp finds he looks oddly hungry for it.
events.nod: Arabian Nights: Aladdin, new lamps for old
events.twist: The party's old lamp has a genie in it, and he knows.

events.name: A drowned bell tower
events.text: A bell tower rises out of the {lake|sea|flooded field}. Its bell is still ringing for a service nobody attends.

events.name: The surveyor's stakes
events.text: Survey stakes painted in House {Ardent|Whitlow|Osmere} colours run right through a village's graveyard. The villagers want to know who ordered it.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to find the plans

events.name: The broken sky ship
events.text: A small sky ship has come down hard, its crew missing. The cloud-shaped hull is half deflated, and the cargo hold is still sealed.
events.twist: The crew jumped out on purpose, and they want the cargo to stay sealed.

events.name: The silver ring in the fish
events.text: Supper is a fresh fish, and inside it is a {silver ring|tiny key|glass eye} engraved with a name and the words 'Return me'.
events.twist: The name belongs to a merfolk noble who threw it away on purpose.

events.name: Too quiet
events.text: The birds and insects go silent for a full hour. Something big is moving nearby and has chosen not to attack.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to work out what it is
events.twist: It is following the party out of curiosity.

events.name: Wrestlers at the fair
events.text: A Leonid wrestler at a village fair is being cheated by a crooked referee. She asks the party to watch the next bout and say what they see, and offers {a bronze coin|her lucky belt|free lessons}.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to catch the trick

events.name: The weeping ship
events.text: A ship's figurehead is crying {salt tears|seawater|blood} and the crew is terrified. The captain will pay for anyone who can tell him why.
events.check: Religion DC 13 to recognise an Ocean curse

events.name: The doorstep basket
events.text: A basket by the {road|gangplank|gate} holds a sleeping baby and a note: 'Please take her to the Church of the Healer. I could not.'
events.twist: The baby is a Celestine, and someone powerful is looking for her.

events.name: The wrong way sign
events.text: Every signpost for a day's walk has been turned to point the wrong way, very neatly, with fresh nails. A hammer has been left on the last one.
events.twist: The hammer belongs to a Church of the Journey priest teaching travellers to read the stars.

events.name: Seven brothers' camp
events.text: Seven identical brothers are camped by the {road|shore|wreck}, each insisting he is the eldest. Their dead father's will goes to the eldest.
events.check: Insight DC 15 to find the truth

events.name: Pull the sword, win the hand
events.text: A notice on a tree: whoever lifts the stone from the well in the next village may marry the reeve's daughter. The daughter has written underneath: 'Please don't.'
events.nod: Folklore: the impossible suitor's task

events.name: The towel left behind
events.text: A neatly folded towel sits on a rock with a note: 'Never travel without one. Trust me.' Wrapped inside are a few iron spirit coins.
events.nod: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy: always know where your towel is

events.name: A wanted poster of the party
events.text: A wanted poster with a fair likeness of {one of the party|the whole party|the party's mount} is nailed up, offering a small reward. The charge is misspelt.
events.twist: It was posted by someone who wants to meet them, and this was the easiest way.

events.name: Pilgrims
events.text: Pilgrims of the Church of the Journey, glad of an escort and full of rumours.

events.name: A merchant caravan
events.text: A caravan willing to trade from its wagons.

events.name: A Society courier
events.text: An Adventure Society courier with news, a contract, or a summons for the party.

events.name: Refugees
events.text: Refugees from a region in surge, carrying what they could.
events.twist: They have news of how bad it is, and someone among them is hurt.

events.name: A noble entourage
events.text: A noble entourage that expects the road cleared for it.

events.name: A surveyor
events.text: A Magic Society surveyor measuring the local magic, quietly worried by the numbers.

events.name: A lone high-ranker
events.text: A lone traveller of much higher rank, who says little and asks the party one strange question.

events.name: A guide for hire
events.text: A local guide offers to lead the party for the rest of the journey: advantage on Survival checks for a fee.

events.name: The backward walker
events.text: A man walking the road backwards. He has done it for nine years and won't say why, but he knows every pothole for a hundred miles.

events.name: A wedding party
events.text: A wedding party walking to the bride's village, with music, flowers, and a goat in a hat. They insist the party joins them for at least one song.

events.name: Rookie team
events.text: A brand-new Iron-rank team on their first contract, wildly overconfident and badly equipped.
events.twist: Their contract is far more dangerous than they think.

events.name: The pedlar of exactly one thing
events.text: A pedlar whose cart is full of {spoons|left boots|bells|very small hats}. Only that, hundreds of them.

events.name: A Celestine on the road
events.text: A young Celestine travelling alone, which almost never happens. Several people seem to be following her at a distance.

events.name: The washed-out veteran
events.text: A former Silver-rank adventurer who lost his nerve, now selling advice at a crossroads for a copper. The advice is excellent.

events.name: Family moving house
events.text: A family with everything they own on one cart, moving to start again after a surge flattened their farm.

events.name: The talking monster
events.text: An intelligent monster, polite and well spoken, asking for directions to the nearest Magic Society office. It wants to register as a person.

events.name: Heir in disguise
events.text: A 'farmhand' with perfect teeth, soft hands and a family crest sewn inside his coat.

events.name: The Drift Host scout
events.text: A rider from one of the Drift Hosts, ahead of her walking town, scouting for water and willing to trade news.

events.name: A Cloud Clan exile
events.text: A Cloud Clan exile, banished from the sky, walking the earth for the first time and hating every step.

events.name: Priest of the Revels
events.text: A Church of the Revels priest, hungover, lost, and looking for the festival he was supposed to lead yesterday.

events.name: The tax collector
events.text: A noble house's tax collector with two bored guards, assessing anyone who looks rich.

events.name: The core merchant
events.text: A monster core buyer travelling between towns, paying a fair price for cores and parts.

events.name: Sisters of the Hearth
events.text: Two Church of the Hearth priestesses with a cart of bread, giving it to anyone on the road who needs it.

events.name: A storyteller from elsewhere
events.nod: Real-world technology told as tall tales
events.text: An outworlder in a tavern swears that where they come from, people fly in metal birds and talk through little glass windows. It's all true, and nobody believes them.

events.name: The galaxy saga
events.nod: Star Wars: a farm boy, a space wizard and an evil father
events.text: An outworlder at a campfire tells the 'true story' of a farm boy, a desert wizard and a masked lord who turns out to be the boy's father. The listeners are furious about the twist.

events.name: Late, on purpose
events.nod: Gandalf: 'A wizard is never late'
events.text: An old man in a grey travelling cloak catches up with the party at a run, insisting he is not late and has arrived precisely when he meant to.

events.name: The rival who isn't
events.text: An adventurer who has decided the party are her great rivals. The party has never met her.

events.name: Smuggled passenger
events.text: A merchant's cart is too heavy for what it carries. Something in a crate knocks twice when the party walks past.

events.name: The barefoot pilgrim
events.text: A Church of the Journey pilgrim walking barefoot to every shrine of her god in the world. She is on shrine four hundred and twelve, and her feet are like boots.
events.twist: She has kept a map of every shrine, and some of them are not on any other map.

events.name: The Purity inquisitor
events.text: A Church of Purity inquisitor in white, with two armed acolytes, stops the party to ask if they have seen {an outworlder|a Celestine|a priest of Undeath}. He is polite. He is also taking notes.
events.check: Deception DC 13 to send him the wrong way

events.name: Healer on the road
events.text: A Church of the Healer priest walking between villages with a pack of {bandages|herbs|stinking poultices} offers to look at anyone's wounds for free, and scolds them about it.
events.twist: He is out of everything except bandages, and too proud to say so.

events.name: The Death priest's cart
events.text: A Church of Death priest with a small cart, travelling to bury those the roads have killed. He has three on the cart now, and room for more.
events.twist: He asks whether anyone in the party wants to leave a name with him, just in case.

events.name: The new convert
events.text: A young man who joined the Church of the Revels last week is preaching on the road with tremendous enthusiasm, a {lute|drum|wine jug} and a very loose grasp of the doctrine.
events.twist: He used to be a Church of Purity inquisitor, and his old colleagues are looking for him.

events.name: The war chaplain
events.text: A Church of War chaplain is marching to join a company in the {east|hills|delta}. He travels light, talks little and checks the party's weapons with an expert eye.

events.name: The god-touched child
events.text: A small girl walks alongside the party for a mile, chatting. Flowers grow in her footprints. Her family, catching up, are a little worried by this.

events.name: The Liberty runners
events.text: Two Church of Liberty priests are escorting a pale, hooded figure at a brisk pace. They ask the party, quietly, not to have seen them.
events.twist: The hooded figure escaped a Storm Kingdom contract and is still bound by it.

events.name: Knowledge on tour
events.text: A Church of Knowledge scholar is walking the road with a quill and a ledger, asking every traveller one question for a survey: 'What do you know that nobody else does?'
events.twist: Her ledger already holds a secret about one of the party, from someone they met long ago.
events.check: Deception DC 15 to give her a false answer she believes

events.name: The Hero's squire
events.text: A Church of the Hero squire is travelling to her first posting. She has memorised the lives of {forty|ninety|three hundred} heroes and will tell them all, given half a chance.

events.name: Earth priest and his stone
events.text: A Church of the Earth priest is rolling a boulder along the road ahead of him. He says it is a penance. He has {three hundred|eleven|nine thousand} miles left.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to help him with the next hill
events.twist: The boulder is a sleeping earth spirit, and it is enjoying the ride.

events.name: The Truth-teller
events.text: A Church of Truth priest who cannot lie, by her own vow, tells each of the party exactly what she thinks of their {face|sword|singing|cooking}. She is very specific.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 12 to take it gracefully

events.name: Ocean pilgrims
events.text: A boat of Church of the Ocean pilgrims is singing hymns to the waves, flowers strewn on the water behind them. They wave and offer the party a blessing for the voyage.

events.name: The Disguise mendicant
events.text: A beggar with a blank wooden mask asks for a coin. Each time someone looks at him, he seems to be someone else they know.
events.twist: He is a Church of Disguise priest, and he is testing which face the party trusts most.
events.check: Insight DC 15 to see his real face

events.name: Storm pilgrims
events.text: Church of the Storm pilgrims are walking towards a black cloud, singing. They want to stand under it when the lightning comes.
events.twist: One of them is struck, and stands up glowing, with a message for the party.

events.name: The Dominion tithe-taker
events.text: A Church of Dominion priest in a carriage, with a column of bound servants walking behind. He nods to the party as an equal, and asks their price.
events.twist: One of his servants slips a note into a party member's hand: a name and a village.

events.name: The Destruction hermit
events.text: A priest of the Church of Destruction sits by a ruin he says he made. He is delighted to have company and explains, at length, how.

events.name: The Hearth sister's soup
events.text: A Church of the Hearth priestess has set up a pot of {soup|stew|porridge} at a crossroads, free to all. She asks only that each person adds one thing to the pot.
events.twist: Whatever each person adds, the soup tastes of their own mother's cooking.

events.name: The relic carrier
events.text: Six monks are carrying a sealed reliquary on poles towards a temple of the Church of the Hero. They will not stop, sleep or put it down.
events.twist: The reliquary is knocking, gently, from the inside.

events.name: The Trade blessing
events.text: A Church of Trade priest is blessing travellers' purses at a {crossroads|dock|toll gate} for one iron coin. Those who pay find their next deal a little sweeter.
events.check: Persuasion DC 10 to get the blessing free

events.name: The Undeath wedding
events.text: A wedding party in black and green, flowers in their hair. The {bride|groom} is alive. The other is a very well-kept skeleton, and very happy.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to talk an approaching Purity patrol out of a fight

events.name: The spice caravan
events.text: A Yaresh spice caravan with its outriders. The merchant's bales smell of {cinnamon|saffron|something unnameable}, and she is willing to trade or hire guards for a day.

events.name: The tinker's wagon
events.text: A tinker's wagon jangles past, hung with {pots and pans|clocks|cages of songbirds} and broken enchanted lamps. He mends anything for a few coppers.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12 to get a second item mended free

events.name: The smuggler's grin
events.text: A cheerful trader with a cart of {fish|cabbages|turnips} that do not smell of anything. He offers the party a very good price on anything they might want, no questions asked.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to spot the false bottom
events.twist: Under the false bottom is a sleeping Celestine child.

events.name: The auctioneer on the move
events.text: A travelling auctioneer and her guards are carrying lots to a sale in {place}. She invites the party to a preview by the roadside.
events.twist: One of the lots is something the party has been looking for.

events.name: Core-buyer's rival
events.text: Two monster core buyers have parked their carts side by side, each undercutting the other by a coin. They are {married|twins|old flames}, and this is how they spend their holidays.

events.name: The salt train
events.text: A long line of heidels loaded with salt blocks, roped nose to tail, moving at walking pace. The drovers want news of the road ahead.
events.twist: One salt block has a face pressed into it from the inside.

events.name: The cloudsilk merchant
events.text: A Cloud Clan trader is carrying cloudsilk down from the mountains, light as air and worth a fortune. He needs an escort and pays in silk.
events.twist: The silk is stolen from a chieftain, and Condor Riders are hunting him.

events.name: The essence pedlar
events.text: A pedlar whispers that he has essences for sale, far below market price. His wares are in a locked box and he will not open it in daylight.
events.twist: The essences are real, and they were taken from the dead.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to tell where the essences came from

events.name: Coin farm convoy
events.text: An armoured wagon of fresh-minted spirit coins, guarded by a Bronze-rank team who are sure every traveller is a bandit.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to calm them enough to pass
events.twist: They are right. Bandits have hidden in the convoy's own baggage wagon.

events.name: The monster-meat cook
events.text: A Smoulder cook with a portable grill sells monster kebabs. The menu changes depending on what attacked her this morning.
events.twist: Today's special is still twitching.

events.name: The sky ship trader
events.text: A small sky ship drifts low, and a trader leans over the rail with a hooked pole to take orders. She sells what the party can afford and drops it down in a basket.
events.check: Sleight of Hand DC 13 to catch the basket without dropping it

events.name: The bankrupt merchant
events.text: A merchant whose whole caravan was lost to a monster surge sits by the {road|harbour|ford} with one mule and one barrel. He is selling the barrel, and himself, as a guide.
