events.name: The bargain fishmonger
events.text: A fishing boat comes alongside with its morning catch. The skipper trades fresh fish for news, rope or a few coppers.

events.name: The perfume caravan
events.text: A caravan of perfume makers, every wagon a different scent. The party smells of {roses|cedar|the sea} for three days whatever they do.

events.name: The awakening stone dealer
events.text: A Magic Society dealer travelling with a strongbox of awakening stones. He sells at list price and will not haggle, but he lets the party look.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to spot the one mislabelled stone
events.twist: One stone in the box is not for sale at any price, and he will not say why.

events.name: The barrel maker
events.text: A cooper and his apprentice are rolling {barrels|casks of ale|empty vats} to the next town. They are behind schedule and would pay for help on the hills.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 to keep up

events.name: The book barge
events.text: A barge loaded with books drifts down the river, run by an old elf who lends them to villages along the way and collects them on the return trip.

events.name: Rival guild couriers
events.text: Two couriers from rival merchant guilds are racing to {place}, sprinting, then walking, then sprinting again, neither willing to let the other pass.

events.name: The wine merchant's cart
events.text: A wine merchant from {Vitesse|Yaresh|Rimaros} with a cart of flower wine. He insists the party try a cup and says it tastes of home, whatever home was.

events.name: The debt collector
events.text: A Church of Trade debt collector, polite and armoured, carries a ledger with someone in the party's name in it, from a debt they do not remember.
events.twist: The debt is real, but it was signed by someone using their name.

events.name: The braggart
events.text: A Bronze-rank adventurer in gleaming armour tells the party about the {dragon|kraken|giant worm} he killed last week. His armour has never been scratched.
events.twist: He really did kill it, by accident, and is terrified someone will ask him to do it again.
events.check: Insight DC 12 to see he is terrified

events.name: The silent team
events.text: A team of {four|five|three} adventurers walk past in single file, mud to the knees, not speaking. One of them is carrying another person's weapons.
events.twist: They were cursed in an astral space to say nothing until they reach a Healer.

events.name: The lost Iron team
events.text: A brand-new Iron-rank team has been walking in circles for two days, too proud to ask the way. They will accept directions if nobody calls them lost.
events.check: Persuasion DC 10 to get them to admit it

events.name: The retired Gold-ranker
events.text: An old woman fishing by the {river|shore|lake} turns out to be a retired Gold-ranker. She has opinions about the party's stances, and offers one lesson.

events.name: The team in mourning
events.text: An adventuring team carrying their leader home on a stretcher. They ask the party to walk with them to the next village, because they cannot face it alone.
events.twist: Their leader is not dead, only cursed into a deep sleep, and they do not know it.

events.name: The rookie healer
events.text: A nervous Iron-rank healer has been left behind by her team, who said she was too slow. She offers to travel with the party and heal for free if they will have her.
events.twist: She is far better than her team realised, and they will want her back.

events.name: The duelling champions
events.text: Two adventurers are about to fight a duel over who saw {a monster|an astral space|a lost purse} first. Neither wants to fight, and both are looking for someone to stop them.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to make peace

events.name: Contract hunters
events.text: A team of Bronze-rankers are racing to the same {monster contract|escort job|astral space} the party might want. They offer to share the work and the reward, or to race for it.

events.name: The rival team again
events.text: The rival Bronze-rank team turns up again, battered, without their contract. They admit the monster was too much and ask if the party has any ideas.

events.name: The cursed adventurer
events.text: An adventurer who cannot stop telling the truth since he opened the wrong chest in an astral space. He is very sorry about what he thinks of the party's cooking.
events.twist: He knows something about the party's next destination, and cannot stop himself saying it.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to lift the curse

events.name: The recruiter
events.text: A recruiter for a big adventuring house offers the party a {contract|signing bonus of bronze coins|place at their training hall}. The small print is very small.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to read the small print

events.name: The armour that walks
events.text: A full suit of Silver-rank armour clanks along the road on its own, carrying a backpack. It says its owner is inside, napping.
events.twist: The owner is inside. He fell asleep a month ago and the armour has been walking him home.

events.name: The lone monster hunter
events.text: A scarred hunter with a crossbow and a cage on her back, tracking one specific monster across three countries. She asks if the party has seen {a white boar|a two-tailed fox|a bird with a woman's face}.

events.name: Rank-up party
events.text: A team has just reached Bronze rank and is celebrating on the road with a {cask|bonfire|very loud drum} and fireworks. They insist the party joins them for one drink.

events.name: The washed-out captain
events.text: A ship's captain who lost her ship and crew to a sea monster now works as a deckhand, staring at the water. She knows where the monster lairs.
events.twist: The monster still has her ship, intact, at the bottom of its lair.

events.name: The adventurer's widow
events.text: A woman travelling to the Society branch to collect her husband's last reward. She asks the party to tell her honestly whether it is worth the road.

events.name: The team who swapped bodies
events.text: Two adventurers in a heated argument, each wearing the other's armour and using the other's voice. They swapped bodies in an astral space and want a ritualist.
events.check: Arcana DC 18 to swap them back

events.name: The party fan
events.text: A young adventurer has heard of the party, gets every detail wrong, and is thrilled. She wants their autographs on her shield.
events.twist: She has been telling everyone she is in the party, and someone believed her.

events.name: The deserter
events.text: A young Leonid soldier in a torn uniform, hiding in a ditch. He deserted after a surge battle and is heading for {place}, where no one knows him.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to learn what he ran from

events.name: The champion with a cold
events.text: A famous Silver-rank adventurer is travelling incognito with a terrible cold. She sneezes lightning and asks the party to please not tell anyone.
events.check: Medicine DC 13 to ease her cold, earning a powerful friend

events.name: The mentor's ghost
events.text: An old adventurer walks beside a translucent figure in armour, chatting easily. He says it is his old mentor, who never quite left.

events.name: The runaway bride
events.text: A woman in a wedding dress, carrying her shoes, sprinting away from a village. She begs the party not to tell anyone which way she went.
events.twist: The groom is right behind her, also running away, and they have not seen each other yet.

events.name: The shepherd boy
events.text: A shepherd boy is driving a flock of {goats|sheep|very small heidels} to market. One of them has decided the party is its mother and follows them.

events.name: The goose woman
events.text: An old woman driving forty {geese|ducks|turkeys} down the road, all of them wearing tiny knitted scarves. She will not explain, but she is very proud of the scarves.
events.twist: One goose has a Society licence tied to its leg, and it outranks the party.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 12 to get past the geese

events.name: The grieving father
events.text: A father walking to the city to buy a healing potion for his daughter, carrying everything he owns to trade. It will not be enough.
events.check: Medicine DC 13 to help the daughter yourselves
events.twist: His daughter's illness is a curse, and the man who laid it is on this road too.

events.name: The village choir
events.text: A village choir on their way to a {festival|funeral|wedding} sing in harmony as they walk. They have room for one more voice.
events.check: Performance DC 12 to join in

events.name: The weaver's caravan
events.text: A family of weavers on their way to market, their cart piled high with {rugs|blankets|sailcloth}. Their youngest is selling small scarves for a copper each.

events.name: The man with the ladder
events.text: A man carrying a very long ladder along the {road|beach|deck}. He says he is going to the top of something. He will not say what.

events.name: The lost goat herd
events.text: A herd of goats has scattered across the {hillside|dunes|marsh}, and a frantic herder needs help gathering them before dark.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 12

events.name: The fishing family
events.text: A fishing family invites the party to share their fish stew on the beach. The grandmother tells the story of every scar on her hands.

events.name: The runaway apprentice
events.text: A young smith's apprentice running away to become an adventurer. He has stolen a sword he can barely lift.
events.twist: The sword is enchanted, and its maker is very angry.

events.name: The midwife
events.text: A midwife hurrying to a birth at a farm ahead asks to ride with the party, because her heidel is lame and the baby will not wait.
events.twist: The baby is the child of two outworlders, and she knows it will be a Celestine.

events.name: The man selling his house
events.text: A man pushing a wheelbarrow with his {front door|chimney pot|kitchen sink} in it. He says it is the only part of the house worth keeping.

events.name: Surge refugees from the delta
events.text: A column of delta families carrying children and chickens, fleeing a monster surge. Some are hurt and all are hungry.

events.name: The mapmaker's daughter
events.text: A girl with a pack full of maps, finishing the survey her late father started. She asks the party for any landmarks they have seen.
events.check: History DC 13 to share something she can use
events.twist: One of her father's maps shows a place that should not exist.

events.name: The wandering potter
events.text: A potter travelling with a wheel on her back stops to make each of the party a {cup|bowl|tiny pot} with their name on it, and will not take payment.

events.name: The kite flyers
events.text: Children on a {hilltop|beach|deck} are flying kites shaped like monsters. One kite has caught in a tree and they want it down.
events.check: Athletics DC 10

events.name: The village drunk's map
events.text: The village drunk, ejected from a tavern, follows the party insisting he knows a shortcut. He does, but he also sings all the way.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to follow his directions

events.name: The heidel breeder
events.text: A heidel breeder is driving a dozen young beasts to the market. Both heads of each animal want to go a different way.

events.name: The quiet family
events.text: A family of five walking in a perfect line, smiling, saying nothing. They give the party a pressed flower and walk on.
events.twist: Their village is empty, and they are the only ones who came out.

events.name: The pie seller
events.text: A girl with a tray of {pies|honey cakes|pasties} balanced on her head is walking to the next town. She will sell one for a story, and she has heard most of them.

events.name: The heir's tutor
events.text: A harried tutor is searching the {hedgerows|reeds|docks} for the noble heir he was meant to be teaching. The heir left a note: 'Gone adventuring. Do not wait up.'
events.twist: The heir is following the party, and wants to join them.

events.name: A courier at the gallop
events.text: A noble house courier on a lathered heidel shouts for the road to be cleared. A sealed tube falls from his saddlebag as he passes.
events.twist: The message inside names one of the party.

events.name: The noble picnic
events.text: A noble family has set up an elaborate picnic in the middle of the {road|ford|only shade for miles}, servants and all, and expects the party to go around.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to be invited instead

events.name: The disgraced lady
events.text: A noblewoman stripped of her name walks with one loyal maid and a small chest. She was cast out for marrying beneath her, and her husband died on the road.
events.twist: Her husband was murdered, and the killer wore her family's colours.

events.name: The hunting party
events.text: A noble hunting party crashes through the {trees|reeds|grass}, hounds baying, after a monster they have wounded. The lord offers a reward to whoever finishes it.

events.name: The steward's ledger
events.text: A noble steward travelling with an iron-bound ledger and four guards. He offers the party a contract to deliver a sealed letter to {place}.

events.name: The fallen knight
events.text: A knight in a noble house's colours sits by the road, sword across his knees, waiting for an enemy he says will come at noon.
events.twist: The enemy is his brother, and neither wants to win.

events.name: The heidel race
events.text: Young nobles are racing heidels along a {beach|stretch of road|dry riverbed}, and one of them has fallen behind. She offers a share of her prize for a shortcut.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to guide her

events.name: The Storm Kingdom envoy
events.text: An envoy of the Storm Kingdom in sapphire silks, with a bodyguard of Bronze-rankers, is travelling to Greenstone. She asks the party what the city thinks of the Crown.
events.twist: She is not going to Greenstone. She is fleeing it.

events.name: The servant's escape
events.text: A {kitchen girl|stable boy|footman} has run away from a noble house with nothing but a cookbook. The runaway is very good with a knife, and offers to cook for the party.

events.name: Cloud house on the water
events.text: A floating cloud house drifts by, owned by a wealthy family on holiday. They wave from the balcony and toss down {apples|sweets|a few iron coins}.

events.name: The Duke's surveyors
events.text: Two Ducal surveyors in Greenstone livery measure the road with a long chain, arguing about the {numbers|weather|Duke's taste in hats}. They ask the party to hold one end.

events.name: The young lord's first command
events.text: A young lord with a company of soldiers is trying to lead them across a {river|marsh|field} he has never seen. His sergeant gives the party a long-suffering look.

events.name: The house in exile
events.text: A noble family, deposed in a far-off land, travels with all their portraits strapped to the carts. The portraits seem to watch the road.
events.twist: One portrait shows a man who is walking beside the carts, very much alive.

events.name: A Celestine twin
events.text: Twin Celestines, a boy with silver hair and a girl with copper, travelling with their outworlder grandparents. The grandparents argue about which world the twins should visit.

events.name: The halfling cook
events.text: A small, round outworlder cook with very hairy feet shares second breakfast with the party. She cannot understand why nobody here eats elevenses.
events.nod: Tolkien's hobbits: second breakfast, elevenses
events.check: Constitution DC 12 to manage a third breakfast

events.name: The gnome inventor
events.text: An outworlder gnome is trying to build a {flying machine|steam wagon|self-cooking pot} from monster parts. It has exploded nine times. He wants volunteers for the tenth.
events.nod: D&D: tinker gnomes

events.name: The detective
events.text: An outworlder with a deerstalker cap and a pipe deduces, at a glance, where each of the party has been and what they had for {supper|breakfast|a bet}. He is usually right.
events.nod: Sherlock Holmes
events.twist: He deduces something about one of the party that they would rather he had not.

events.name: The time-lost knight
events.text: An outworlder in old plate armour asks which king rules here and swears he is a knight of a round table. He calls everyone 'good sir' and challenges hedges.
events.nod: Arthurian legend and A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court

events.name: The wizard's apprentice
events.text: An outworlder in a robe with stars on it shows the party his school's four house colours and asks which house they would be sorted into.
events.nod: Harry Potter: the sorting into houses

events.name: The ring cook
events.text: An outworlder serves the party stew at a roadside fire and tells them about a famous show where cooks shout at each other. He shouts at the stew a little.
events.nod: Reality cooking shows like Hell's Kitchen

events.name: The road movie
events.text: An outworlder on a borrowed heidel says she has always wanted to do a road trip. She asks the party what music they travel to and hums a few bars.
events.nod: Real-world road trip culture

events.name: The plumber from elsewhere
events.text: An outworlder in red overalls, with a big moustache, asks whether any princesses are being held in any castles nearby. He keeps jumping on things.
events.nod: Super Mario
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 to match one of his jumps

events.name: The cartoon-watcher
events.text: An outworlder child is delighted by everything, says this world is like her favourite cartoon, and keeps waiting for a talking dog to appear.
events.nod: Scooby-Doo

events.name: A dwarf in the rain
events.text: A dwarf with a braided beard is sheltering under a tree, the only dwarf anyone here has ever seen. He asks, in a strange accent, where the mountains are.
events.twist: He arrived only this morning, and he died in his own world.

events.name: The new arrival
events.text: A naked stranger sits in a ring of flattened grass, smelling of springtime and shivering. She speaks no language anyone knows, but her eyes are bright with questions.

events.name: The traveller from the north
events.text: A fur-clad traveller from the frozen north carrying a carved horn. She has never seen {a palm tree|the sea|a goblin} and is fascinated.

events.name: The Draconian scholar
events.text: A Draconian scholar travelling the world to prove his people descend from dragons. He has a cart of bones and nobody believes him.
events.twist: One of the bones is genuinely a dragon's.

events.name: The goblin envoy
events.text: A goblin envoy in court dress, on her way to argue for her people's rights at a {city council|noble court|Society hearing}. She asks the party to proofread her speech.
events.check: History DC 13 to help her make it better

events.name: The Smoulder blacksmith
events.text: A Smoulder smith travelling with no forge, because she is the forge. She heats metal in her bare hands and will mend a {blade|pot|shield} for a meal.

events.name: The Runic hermit
events.text: A Runic covered in shifting markings, walking slowly with his eyes shut. He says he is listening to the magic of the land, and it is unhappy.
events.twist: He is right. A surge is building, and he is the only one who has noticed.

events.name: The merfolk traveller
events.text: A merfolk woman is travelling inland in a wheeled barrel of seawater, pushed by her patient husband. She wants to see a desert before she dies.

events.name: The Leonid crafter
events.text: A Leonid crafter with a cart of carved wooden {toys|animals|soldiers}, travelling between villages. He gives each child he meets one, and asks only for a smile.

events.name: The man from the sea
events.text: A man walks out of the sea fully dressed, dry, and asks the date. He is told and says, 'Ah. Later than I hoped.'
events.twist: He sailed out of this harbour a hundred years ago, and his granddaughter lives nearby.

events.name: The outworlder storyteller
events.text: An outworlder tells a story of a great ship that hit ice and sank on its first voyage, and of the musicians who played until the end. The listeners are in tears.
events.nod: The Titanic

events.name: The time traveller's box
events.text: An outworlder in a long scarf is looking for his blue box. He says it is bigger on the inside and he left it here, or will leave it here, next week.
events.nod: Doctor Who: the TARDIS

events.name: The dog that went home
events.text: An outworlder tells a story about a loyal dog who waited at a train station every day for ten years for his master. Everyone around the fire goes quiet.
events.nod: Hachiko

events.name: The polite troll
events.text: A troll sits under a {bridge|cliff|rock arch} reading a book of manners. It asks the party for a toll of one compliment each, and corrects their grammar.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12 for a compliment it accepts

events.name: The lost spirit
events.text: A small spirit of the {wells|marsh mist|old oaks} follows the party, asking in a tiny voice whether they have seen its home. Its home was cut down last year.
events.twist: It will settle in anything the party offers it, and then belong to them.

events.name: The construct pilgrim
events.text: A rusty construct is walking to the Magic Society to ask whether it has a soul. It has been walking for a hundred years and has many questions.

events.name: The talking heidel
events.text: One head of a heidel can talk, and it complains endlessly about the other head's {breath|singing|table manners}. The other head just eats.
events.twist: The other head can talk too, and has been choosing not to.

events.name: The sphinx at the pass
events.text: A lion-bodied monster with a woman's face lies across the {pass|ravine|road}. She will let the party by if they answer her riddle, and eat them if they don't.
events.nod: Greek myth: the Sphinx's riddle
events.check: Intelligence DC 15

events.name: The dragon hatchling
events.text: A dragon hatchling no bigger than a cat has followed the party for a mile, chirping. It breathes tiny puffs of {fire|frost|lightning} when it is happy.
events.twist: Its mother is looking for it, and she is not small.

events.name: The intelligent ooze
events.text: A gelatinous blob glides along the path, full of coins, a boot and a surprised {fish|chicken|clerk's hat}. It introduces itself and asks if the party has eaten.
events.nod: D&D: the gelatinous cube

events.name: The wolf who wants to be a dog
events.text: A huge Bronze-rank wolf trots up, sits, and offers a paw. It wants to belong to someone and has been practising.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13
events.twist: The wolf is a Bronze-ranker. Its gratitude, and its appetite, are huge.

events.name: The sea serpent's question
events.text: A sea serpent lifts its head beside the boat and asks politely, in a voice like wind, why humans go to sea at all.

events.name: The goblin's monster
events.text: A goblin rides a monster the size of a house, which carries his luggage. He insists it is just a large dog, and the monster wags its tail.
events.twist: The monster can talk, and quietly asks the party to rescue it.

events.name: The scarecrow spirit
events.text: A scarecrow climbs down from its pole and asks the party which way the {crows|farmer|children} went. It has been looking for them for a long time.

events.name: The kraken's messenger
events.text: A small octopus climbs onto the deck holding a shell with a message scratched inside: 'Please stop dropping your anchors on my garden.'
events.check: Survival DC 13 to drop anchor somewhere less rude

events.name: The fox spirit
events.text: A fox with three tails trots beside the party, asking riddles and offering small favours for small prices. It has a beautiful voice.
events.nod: East Asian folklore: the kitsune
events.twist: It wants one hair from each of the party, for reasons it will not say.

events.name: The desert djinn
events.text: A djinn of smoke and heat rises from a cracked jar half-buried in the sand. It owes three favours to whoever freed it, and it is a stickler for wording.
events.nod: Arabian Nights: the djinn and three wishes

events.name: The jungle king
events.text: A huge ape with a silver back and a crown of flowers blocks the path. It speaks slowly and asks why the party is in its jungle.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15
events.twist: It is a Silver-rank monster, and it is asking for help against something worse.

events.name: The Khan's challenger
events.text: A young Hostfolk warrior is riding to challenge her Khan. She asks the party to witness, because a challenge needs outsiders as well as kin.

events.name: The challenge witnessed
events.text: The party arrives in time to witness the challenge between the young warrior and her Khan. Whoever wins, the Host remembers the strangers who stood as witnesses.

events.name: The greatback calf
events.text: A greatback calf, already the size of a wagon, has lost its herd and keeps leaning on the party for comfort. It is very heavy.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13 to lead it home
events.twist: Its herd is a stolen Host's herd, and the thieves are nearby.

events.name: Hostfolk traders
events.text: A band of Hostfolk traders with {monster hides|cores|steppe cheese}, driving a hard bargain but fair. They want news of the Tide.

events.name: The Condor Rider
events.text: A young Condor Rider lands her giant bird on a ledge beside the path and asks if anyone has seen a band of bandits from the jungle.
events.twist: The bandits are her brothers, and she wants them warned, not caught.

events.name: The bridge mender
events.text: A Cloud Clan bridge mender is hanging upside down beneath a rope bridge, singing as she works. She asks the party to cross one at a time and to step lightly.

events.name: The jungle herbalist
events.text: An old elf woman with a basket of jungle herbs walks barefoot through the undergrowth, {humming|whistling|chatting to the trees}. She knows a cure for any bite in this jungle.

events.name: The marsh ferryman
events.text: A ferryman with a pole and a lantern offers to take the party through the marsh for a coin each. He never looks at his passengers.
events.twist: He was drowned here forty years ago, and he still takes the fare.

events.name: The desert caravan master
events.text: A caravan master with a dozen heidels and their drivers, crossing the desert by {night|starlight|the light of a Runic's markings}. She knows every well for a hundred miles.

events.name: The sandship crew
events.text: A sail-skiff glides over the dunes, its crew of {goblins|Smoulders|Leonids} waving. They offer to race, and will bet anything on it.
events.check: Survival DC 14 to win the race

events.name: The pearl diver
events.text: A merfolk pearl diver surfaces beside the boat, laughing, with a pearl in her teeth. She offers to trade it for a story about the land.

events.name: The island hermit
events.text: A hermit who lives on a rock in the sea rows out to meet every passing ship and asks for the latest news. He is {twenty|fifty|three} years behind.

events.name: The jungle explorers
events.text: A Magic Society expedition hacking through the jungle in pristine white clothes, insisting they know exactly where they are. They are lost.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to set them right

events.name: The cheerful tinker, again
events.text: A tinker named Oskel Brannoch the party met before pulls up his wagon with a grin. He has kept a special pot aside for them since last time.

events.name: Oskel's warning
events.text: Oskel Brannoch the tinker catches up, flustered. Someone has been asking about the party at every stop, and paid him to say where they were going.

events.name: The old woman with the cats
events.text: An old woman named Mother Kettlewick walks the roads with a dozen {cats|owls|hedgehogs} in a hand cart. She is always here, wherever here is.

events.name: Mother Kettlewick's gift
events.text: Mother Kettlewick appears again on the road, and hands one of the party a kitten. 'It chose you,' she says. The kitten has eyes like stars.

events.name: The postman
events.text: A Society postman named Doran Felk, who always seems to be on the same road as the party. He has a {letter|parcel|very damp package} for one of them.

events.name: The postman's last letter
events.text: Doran Felk the postman arrives with a letter addressed to the party, in a hand they do not know, sealed in black. He says it was in his bag when he woke.

events.name: The singing drover
events.text: A drover named Wenna Halloway, who the party has heard before. Her voice carries for a mile, and her {heidels|goats|geese} walk in time to it.

events.name: The fortune-teller
events.text: A fortune-teller named Aunt Moth, whose caravan is always parked at the next crossroads. She waves, and her fortunes have all come true so far.

events.name: Aunt Moth's last fortune
events.text: Aunt Moth is waiting by the road, packing up. She tells the party she has only one fortune left, and it is about them.

events.name: The fishing captain
events.text: Captain Haddrell Spume, whose fishing boat always seems to be passing when the party is at sea. He shouts greetings and throws a {fish|crab|very surprised eel}.
events.check: Dexterity DC 10 to catch the fish

events.name: The book pedlar
events.text: A bookseller named Ines Varro who always has exactly the book the party needs, and always wants something odd in exchange.
events.twist: She asks for a book of their own, written by one of them.

events.name: The goat herder
events.text: Bertil Ashgrove the herder, whose {goats|sheep|geese} always seem to be blocking the road when the party arrives. He apologises every time.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 10 to get past

events.name: The night watchman
events.text: A Society night watchman named Orrin Hask who always seems to be on duty at the waystations the party visits, and who always knows what they did last.
events.twist: He is a Church of Disguise priest keeping an eye on the party for his god.

events.name: The cartographer
events.text: A cartographer named Lissel Dawn-Feather keeps turning up with a new map of the road ahead, drawn on {vellum|bark|a pillowcase}. She sells it cheap, as a friend.

events.name: The lady and her parrot
events.text: A noblewoman named Dame Peregrine Stoat who always seems to be travelling the same way, with a parrot that repeats everything the party said last time.

events.name: The wandering Healer
events.text: A Healer named Brother Tamsk, who the party met before, waves from the {roadside|dock|rail} with his kit. He asks after every wound he treated.

events.name: The rival again
events.text: The adventurer who decided the party were her rivals is back, with a new team, new armour and a new nickname for the party. It is not flattering.
events.twist: Her new team has quietly asked the party to let her win something, once.

events.name: The pilgrim who keeps passing
events.text: The same pilgrim the party passed three days ago is ahead of them again. He has not hurried. He waves, and does not look tired.
events.twist: He is a messenger of the Church of the Journey, sent to watch over the party.

events.name: The core buyer who knows
events.text: A core buyer named Fenwick Darrow always seems to know what the party has killed lately. He offers {slightly|well|suspiciously} over the going rate, and asks how they did it.
events.twist: He is buying for a cult that needs a great many cores.

events.name: The two old soldiers
events.text: Two old soldiers who walk the roads together, arguing about a war that ended fifty years ago. One of them has been dead for ten years, but no one has told the other.

events.name: The lamplighter
events.text: A lamplighter named Ysolde Wick who walks the roads at dusk, lighting lamps that are not there. Where she has been, the road is safe at night.

events.name: The weeping automaton
events.text: A brass automaton sits on a {milestone|crate|rock}, leaking oil from its eyes. It says its maker sent it to buy bread forty years ago and it has forgotten the way home.

events.name: The automaton's maker
events.text: An ancient Runic enchanter, very frail, bursts into tears at news of her lost automaton. She pays the party in the only thing she has left: a finely made enchanted tool.

events.name: The masked rider
events.text: A rider in a black mask and cape carves a letter into a {tree|signpost|tax collector's door} with a sword tip, bows from the saddle and gallops off.
events.nod: Zorro: the masked rider and his carved Z

events.name: The rider unmasked
events.text: The masked rider is caught in a bramble, mask askew. She is the local lord's mild-mannered clerk, and she begs the party to keep her secret.

events.name: An unharvested kill
events.text: A dead monster no one has harvested.
events.twist: Cores and materials are there for the taking, if the party can work out what killed it.

events.name: An abandoned camp
events.text: Bedrolls, a journal, half a meal, and no sign of a fight.

events.name: A body with a pack
events.text: A traveller's body, days old, with their pack still on.

events.name: A natural array
events.text: A spot humming with magic: good for a ritual, bad for staying the night.

events.name: Rare herbs
events.text: Wild reagents worth good coin to crafters and the Magic Society.

events.name: A warded cache
events.text: A cache left by some past adventurer, with a riddle or a ward on it.

events.name: Old waystones
events.text: A line of old waystones, or a map fragment, pointing somewhere not on any map.

events.name: A small wonder
events.text: A spring that heals, a grove that glows at night, or a stone that sings in the wind.

events.name: A shrine nobody tends
events.text: A tiny shrine to a god nobody in the party recognises. Leaving an offering grants one reroll before the next dawn.

events.name: The drowned pack
events.text: A Silver-rank's pack caught in the reeds, holding a sealed letter and a pouch of spirit coins.

events.name: A field of glass
events.text: A circle of ground turned to green glass, a hundred feet across. Something very powerful fought here.

events.name: An unfinished letter
events.text: A traveller's skeleton beneath a tree, with a letter to their child, unfinished. The address is two towns away.

events.name: Old Society cache
events.text: A hollow tree marked with an old Adventure Society sign. Inside is an emergency cache: healing potions, rations and a note asking finders to restock it.

events.name: The wrong footprints
events.text: Footprints leading into the camp the party left this morning. They walk in a circle around where everyone slept, then leave.

events.name: Monster bones, recently picked
events.text: A huge carcass picked clean overnight. Whatever ate it took the core as well, which monsters don't do.

events.name: A wagon of clocks
events.text: An abandoned wagon full of clocks, every one of them still ticking, all set to different times.

events.name: A rare plant
events.text: A {moonbloom|ghost orchid|blood-red lichen} growing right beside the path, worth a good price to any alchemist.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to harvest it without ruining it

events.name: An empty astral space
events.text: An astral space entrance, already cleared by someone else, still open. The rooms inside are empty except for the loot they missed.

events.name: Graffiti from home
events.nod: WWII graffiti: 'Kilroy was here' (an outworlder left it)
events.text: Scratched into a ruin wall: a big-nosed face peeking over a line, and the words 'was here'. Someone has added a date in no calendar anyone knows.

events.name: A key with no lock
events.text: A heavy iron key in the middle of the road, warm to the touch. It turns slightly in the hand, like a compass, pointing somewhere.

events.name: A crashed sky skiff
events.text: A small sky skiff crashed in the {treetops|scrub|marsh}, pilot gone, cargo intact.

events.name: Bones in armour
events.text: A full set of rusted armour standing upright at the roadside, a skeleton still inside it, facing the way the party came.

events.name: The singing stones
events.text: Standing stones that hum a chord when the wind blows. Anyone who hums along can see magic for an hour.

events.name: A ruined chapel
events.text: A chapel of a church that no longer exists. The pews are dusted, and fresh candles are lit.

events.name: A box with teeth
events.nod: D&D's mimic
events.text: A treasure chest sitting alone in a clearing, with drool on the lid.

events.name: The boulder run
events.nod: Raiders of the Lost Ark: the golden idol and boulder
events.text: Inside a cave off the path, a golden idol sits on a pedestal. The tunnel slopes down from a very round boulder overhead.
events.check: Sleight of Hand DC 15 to swap it with something of the same weight

events.name: Coins in the stream
events.text: The streambed glitters with iron spirit coins. Somebody upstream has a hole in their purse, or a reason to throw them away.

events.name: A hidden garden
events.text: Behind a collapsed wall, a hidden, well-kept garden with ripe fruit, a bench, and a sign: 'Take what you need.'

events.name: A cairn of badges
events.text: A roadside cairn topped with {six|nine|a dozen} Iron-rank Adventure Society badges, wired together. A team name is scratched into the top stone.
events.twist: The Society branch in the next town still lists the team as active, and someone is still drawing their pay.

events.name: The duellists
events.text: Two skeletons locked together, each with a blade through the other. Both purses hold the same {three|five|seven} bronze spirit coins, minted the same year.

events.name: A pilgrim's grave
events.text: A fresh grave marked with a Church of the Journey walking staff. Passers-by have left {bread|flowers|iron coins} on it. Anyone who adds something walks easier tomorrow.

events.name: The lantern by the milestone
events.text: A dead man sits against a milestone, his lantern still burning. It has burned for days with no oil.
events.twist: It is a core-powered lamp worth 40 gp, and the core inside is far too strong for an Iron-ranker to own.

events.name: The ploughed battlefield
events.text: A farmer's plough keeps turning up old {arrowheads|helmets|belt buckles}. He sells a bucket of finds for 5 silver, unsorted.
events.twist: One helmet has a noble house crest, and the house has been looking for its heir's body for sixty years.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to spot the one worth keeping

events.name: The Healer's empty tent
events.text: A Church of the Healer field tent, empty but for a cot and a list of {twelve|twenty|forty} names. Every name is crossed out except the last.

events.name: The sunken sky ship
events.text: At low tide, the ribs of a sky ship stand out of the shallows. Its cloud-cushioned {deck chairs|cargo nets|lanterns} are crusted with barnacles.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to reach the hold before the tide turns

events.name: Bones of a greatback
events.text: The bleached skeleton of a greatback, its platform still lashed to the spine and a family's round tent collapsed inside.
events.twist: The family's tally stick counts four greatbacks. The other three were never found.

events.name: The man of stone
events.text: A statue of a startled {man|woman|Leonid} mid-stride, with a real pack on his back. The coins in his purse have turned to stone as well.
events.twist: He is still alive in there, and his eyes follow the party.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to know what did this, and how it might be undone

events.name: The sleeping crew
events.text: A fishing boat drifts with its nets out and every sailor asleep at their post. Nothing will wake them until the sun goes down.
events.twist: The one sailor awake is the cabin boy, who has kept the ship afloat alone for three days.

events.name: A burial raft
events.text: A Church of the Ocean burial raft drifts past, garlanded with kelp, a single bronze coin on the dead woman's chest.
events.twist: Sailors say whoever pushes the raft on without taking the coin gets a calm sea tomorrow.

events.name: The trophy wall
events.text: A hunter's lean-to with dozens of monster {skulls|horns|jawbones} nailed in neat rows. The last skull in the row is human, and it still wears a Society badge.

events.name: The last stand
events.text: {Five|Seven|Eight} dead monsters in a ring around a broken spear, and no body. Whoever held them off walked away bleeding.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to follow the blood trail

events.name: The spearman's cave
events.text: The blood trail ends at a cave where a grey-haired Bronze-ranker is healing slowly, alone. She is grateful, gruff, and owes the party a favour now.

events.name: Graves dug early
events.text: Six graves dug beside the road, open and empty, with blank wooden markers. A spade still stands in the last one.
events.twist: There are exactly as many graves as there are people in the party, plus one.

events.name: The red-rag cairns
events.text: Little stacks of stones every hundred paces, each with a strip of {red|yellow|black} cloth. They lead off the path and stop at a cliff edge.
events.twist: A narrow ledge runs along the cliff from the last cairn. Someone meant for travellers to find it.

events.name: The empty Silver armour
events.text: The armour of a Silver-rank adventurer lies in the grass, buckled shut, as if the body inside simply vanished. A storage ring is still on the gauntlet.
events.twist: The ring is locked to its owner. A Magic Society specialist can open it, for half of what is inside.

events.name: The full waterskin
events.text: A traveller dried hard by the sun, crouched as if resting, still clutching a waterskin. It is completely full.

events.name: A shrine of black candles
events.text: An overgrown Church of Death shrine: a closed eye carved in stone, and a bowl of black candles. Light one, and the dead nearby will answer one yes-or-no question.

events.name: The sword that guards the road
events.text: A sword planted at a crossroads, a Church of War blessing tied to its hilt. Locals keep it oiled and say it has kept the road safe for forty years.

events.name: The riddle headstone
events.text: A lone headstone with a riddle where the name should be. The locals say the answer is where the old {miser|smuggler|priest} buried their savings.
events.twist: The savings were spent long ago. In their place is an IOU from a party member's family.
events.check: Intelligence DC 13 to solve it

events.name: The goblin barrow
events.text: A grassy barrow with a carved round door and a polite sign, in Goblin, asking visitors to knock. If anyone knocks, someone inside says 'Not today, thank you.'

events.name: The password door
events.nod: Arabian Nights: Ali Baba's 'open sesame' cave
events.text: A seam in the rock shaped like a door. Beside it, someone has carved {forty|ninety|two hundred} failed passwords, each crossed out, ending with 'please'.
events.check: Arcana DC 15, or one inspired guess

events.name: A cart over the edge
events.text: A merchant's cart has gone over the edge of the road, the mule grazing calmly nearby. The cargo is mostly {pots|cheap wine|onions}, plus one strongbox.
events.check: Thieves' tools DC 13 to open the strongbox

events.name: A barrel under a float
events.text: A fishing float with no net, tied to a sealed barrel just under the surface. Inside, packed in salt, are untaxed Bronze cores.
events.twist: Whoever sank it is coming back for it at dusk, in a fast boat.

events.name: Spilled farm coins
events.text: A broken wagon from a spirit coin farm has spilled half-formed coins across the road. They are soft as jelly, humming, and slowly going hard.
events.twist: A crafter would pay well for them before they set. They set by tomorrow.

events.name: The Society dead drop
events.text: A loose stone in a bridge hides an Adventure Society contract tube, sealed and addressed to a team that hasn't collected it in a month.
events.twist: The contract inside concerns {hook}.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to find out who the team were

events.name: A satchel with a cat in it
events.text: A dimensional satchel lies in the mud. Inside is an entire {kitchen|library|wardrobe}, neatly packed, and one very surprised cat.
events.twist: The cat is a familiar, and its owner will pay to have it back.

events.name: The honesty box
events.text: An empty tollbooth with a sign asking for one iron coin, and a box full of other people's honesty.
events.twist: The keeper is watching from the hill with a crossbow and a sense of humour.

events.name: A mile of wreckage
events.text: Wreckage spread across a mile of water: crates, a figurehead, and one chest floating a little too well.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to see the ward on the chest before opening it

events.name: The buried wagon
events.text: The wind has uncovered the canopy of a caravan wagon under a dune. Digging it out takes the afternoon.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 to clear it before the sand slides back

events.name: The hollow saint
events.text: A roadside statue of a Church of the Hero saint, raised sword chipped. One knock shows it is hollow, and something rattles inside.
events.check: Sleight of Hand DC 13 to open it without breaking the saint

events.name: A cache with a ledger
events.text: An old adventurer's cache with a ledger inside. Thirty years of travellers have taken one thing and left another, and written their names.
events.twist: Leave something good, and the ledger's last entry says the next good thing is buried under the oak.

events.name: The forgotten essence case
events.text: A warded essence case, half buried in a ditch, still humming faintly. Whatever essence is inside is still unabsorbed.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to open the wards safely

events.name: A message in a bottle
events.text: A bottle bobbing in the water, sealed with wax and a {Rimaros|Vitesse|Yaresh} customs stamp. The letter inside gives a reef, a date and the word 'sorry'.

events.name: The noble's lost luggage
events.text: A trunk stamped with a noble house crest lies in a ditch, lock smashed. Most of the silks are ruined, but the letters inside are very much intact.
events.twist: The house would pay for the letters back. Its rivals would pay more.

events.name: Coins under the floorboards
events.text: A loose board in the floor squeaks. Under it, wrapped in a sock, are {twelve|twenty|thirty} iron spirit coins and a note: 'For the next one who needs it.'

events.name: Saddlebags in a tree
events.text: A pair of saddlebags hangs from a branch {forty|sixty|eighty} feet up. There's no horse, no rope, and no way anyone could have put them there.
events.twist: A sky ship dropped them by mistake. Its crew comes looking tomorrow.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to climb up

events.name: A cloudsilk bundle
events.text: A bundle of Cloud Clan cloudsilk caught on a crag, light as breath, worth a fortune in any great city. It must have blown off a caravan.
events.twist: A Clan trader is two hours behind, looking for it, and very polite about it.

events.name: The cellar door
events.text: A cellar door in an empty {field|meadow|stretch of grass}, no house in sight. It is barred from the outside, and the bar is new.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to hear what is moving below

events.name: A mimic among chests
events.nod: D&D: a mimic hidden among real chests
events.text: {Three|Four|Five} treasure chests in a row in an abandoned shed. One of them is breathing.
events.check: Perception DC 12 to pick the right ones

events.name: The tide chest
events.text: An iron chest chained to a rock in the shallows. Its key hangs on a post far out of reach, showing only at the lowest tide.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to time the tide

events.name: The hoard of buttons
events.text: A magpie-monster's nest stuffed with shiny things: {buttons|thimbles|teaspoons}, keys, a Society badge and one awakening stone it is clearly most proud of.
events.twist: The Society badge belongs to someone the party knows.
events.check: Athletics or Stealth DC 13 to take the stone before the bird gets home

events.name: A core in a gizzard
events.text: A dead {gull|vulture|crow-monster}, swollen and stinking. Something hard and red-brown shows through a split in its belly: a monster core it swallowed.
events.check: Medicine DC 12 to cut it out without gagging

events.name: The shed skin
events.text: A shed snakeskin {thirty|sixty|ninety} feet long, still soft. It is worth good coin to an armourer, and whatever left it is not far off.

events.name: Too many cores
events.text: A pile of {eight|fifteen|forty} Iron-rank monster cores, neatly stacked like an offering. No carcasses anywhere, and no tracks.
events.twist: Whatever made the pile is collecting them. It will notice if any go missing.

events.name: A nest of eggs
events.text: A nest of {three|five|seven} leathery eggs, warm and twitching. A hatchling monster can be raised, sold, or destroyed before it grows.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to know what will hatch

events.name: The fresh spawn
events.text: The air tightens and shimmers, and a monster forms out of nothing a stone's throw away, still blinking. For a moment it is too dazed to move.
events.check: Stealth DC 12 to slip away, or a free round to strike first

events.name: Claw marks on the hull
events.text: Deep {claw|tooth|tentacle} marks run along the ship's hull below the waterline, fresh this morning. Nobody on watch heard a thing.
events.twist: The marks spell a word in Merfolk script: 'leave'.

events.name: The washed-up leviathan
events.text: A dead sea monster the size of a {barn|chapel|small ship} lies on the sand, gulls on it in thousands. Its core is still inside, somewhere.
events.check: Athletics DC 15 to dig it out before the tide takes the carcass back

events.name: A tooth in the rock
events.text: A monster tooth as long as a spear is wedged deep in a boulder, as if something bit the rock and gave up.
events.twist: A Magic Society scholar would pay to know where. The rock is still warm.

events.name: The harvesters' leftovers
events.text: A team has butchered a monster here and taken only the best parts. The {hide|horns|glands} they left would still fetch a few silver.

events.name: A trail of slime
events.text: A glistening trail as wide as a cart, perfectly straight, going over rocks, through a {hedge|cottage garden|thicket} and across a pond without a single bend.

events.name: The monster's larder
events.text: A cave stacked with carcasses, all wrapped in silk and labelled with scratch marks. One of the bundles is still moving.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to free it before the owner returns

events.name: Tracks of the Wandering Tide
events.text: The grass here is waist-high and the ground is littered with small monster carcasses. The Tide has just left this valley, and it left gifts.
events.twist: A Drift Host is riding in to harvest them, and they consider the valley theirs.

events.name: A tamed condor's harness
events.text: A huge saddle harness made for a condor-sized bird lies broken on a ledge. Cloud Clan knots, and no rider.

events.name: The riderless condor
events.text: A huge tamed condor circles low over the party, then lands on a rock and waits. It wants to be led home, and its home is a Cloud Clan village.
events.twist: Its chieftain owes a debt to whoever brings it back.

events.name: The ink cloud
events.text: The water around the ship turns {black|purple|deep blue} with ink for a mile in every direction. Something very large has just been badly frightened.

events.name: Moulted feathers of gold
events.text: A drift of moulted feathers, each one edged in real {gold leaf|silver|copper}. A monster with expensive taste must roost nearby.
events.twist: Each feather is worth an iron coin to a jeweller, and there are hundreds.

events.name: Burrow mouths
events.text: The ground is pocked with burrows the width of a barrel. A careful walker avoids them; a careless one finds out what lives inside.
events.check: Perception DC 12 for everyone to keep clear

events.name: The gelatinous clearing
events.nod: D&D: the gelatinous cube
events.text: A perfectly cube-shaped trench runs through the undergrowth. A sword, three boots and a coin purse hang suspended in something wobbling at the end of it.
events.check: Sleight of Hand DC 14 to fish out the purse

events.name: A ring of dead monsters
events.text: {A dozen|Twenty|Thirty} monsters of different kinds lie dead in a perfect ring, untouched, cores still inside. None of them has a mark on it.

events.name: Merfolk hunting marks
events.text: Merfolk sign carved into a rock: a fish, a wave and a crossed-out spear. The local hunters are warning everyone off something nearby.
events.check: History or Nature DC 13 to read it fully

events.name: The shrinking carcass
events.text: A monster carcass that is noticeably smaller every time someone looks away. Within the hour it will be the size of a {cat|teacup|mouse}, and so will its core.

events.name: A spring of mana
events.text: A spring where the water fizzes and glows {blue|green|silver}. Anyone who drinks recovers one expended spell slot, once.

events.name: A natural array at noon
events.text: {Stones and roots|Coral and rock|Bones and reeds} that happen to form a perfect ritual array. Any ritual cast here today takes half the usual time.

events.name: Awakening stone in a riverbed
events.text: Something glints among the pebbles: a small awakening stone, smoothed by the water, tied to the {water|earth|swift} essence.
events.check: Perception DC 14 to spot it

events.name: A pocket of thin magic
events.text: A patch where the magic simply stops. Spells fizzle, magic items go dull, and everyone's essence feels muffled until they walk out the far side.

events.name: The singing well
events.text: An old well where the echo sings back a word in a voice nobody recognises. Shout a question down it, and the answer comes back {in rhyme|as a song|backwards}.

events.name: A puddle of quintessence
events.text: A puddle of something thicker than water, rainbow-sheened and smelling of {lightning|cinnamon|rain}. Crafters call it quintessence and pay well for every jar.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to bottle it safely

events.name: The glowing swell
events.text: Every wave rolling past the ship glows {green|gold|violet} from inside, and fish leap through the light like sparks. It lasts until dawn.

events.name: The essence-sick tree
events.text: A tree that has soaked up a loose essence. Its bark is now {iron|glass|fur}, and it moves slightly when watched.

events.name: Magic pooling
events.text: Every insect, bird and beast has left this valley. The air feels heavy, and the Society's surge markers here have all been knocked flat.
events.twist: The markers were knocked down from inside the valley, on purpose.

events.name: A pillar of light
events.text: A column of soft light stands in the {water|grass|sand}, warm to the touch. Anyone who stands in it feels their wounds close: one Hit Die, free.

events.name: The fused-glass ripple
events.text: A dune fused into rippling glass, with something dark trapped inside it like a fly in amber.
events.check: Athletics DC 14 to break it out

events.name: The weightless hollow
events.text: In a small dip, everything weighs {half|a third|a tenth} as much. Packs feel light, jumps go far, and the party's dropped coins float back up to them.

events.name: Monster-touched honey
events.text: A wild hive swollen to the size of a cart, dripping golden honey that hums with magic. A spoonful tastes like a whole day's rest.
events.check: Nature or Stealth DC 13 to take some without the swarm

events.name: A storm-charged stone
events.text: A {boulder|standing stone|dead oak} struck by lightning so often it has become a battery. Its crackle charges anything metal touched to it for an hour.

events.name: Stars in the water
events.text: The still water shows a sky full of stars at midday. The stars in it are not the stars overhead.

events.name: The breathing hill
events.text: A low {hill|dune|ridge} rises and falls, very slowly, like something asleep. The grass on it has never been grazed.

events.name: A crystal of frozen magic
events.text: A finger-long crystal of solid magic, the kind that forms only where a surge peaked long ago. The Magic Society buys these without asking questions.

events.name: The luck stone
events.text: A smooth, holed stone. Whoever carries it has amazing luck with small things and terrible luck with big ones.
events.twist: It has already decided which party member it belongs to, and keeps turning up in their pocket.

events.name: A whirl of loose essence
events.text: A tiny whirlwind of coloured light skitters about like a lost animal. It is a raw essence that never found a monster to become.
events.check: Arcana DC 16 to coax it into an essence case

events.name: The well of rest
events.text: A spot where the magic feels like a warm bath. Anyone who rests an hour here wakes as if they slept the whole night.
events.twist: Anyone who sleeps there a whole night dreams of the last person who did.

events.name: A door in the air
events.text: A {red|blue|plain wooden} door hangs in the air, a foot above the ground or the waves, with nothing behind it. It is an astral space entrance nobody has charted.
events.twist: It has a brass knocker, and someone inside knocks back.

events.name: A Society licence plaque
events.text: An astral space entrance with an Adventure Society plaque: licensed, Bronze rank, cleared {two|five|eleven} years ago. The plaque has been bent, as if from inside.

events.name: The space that grew back
events.text: A Society runner catches the party up. The entrance they passed has opened again and something came out of it. The branch will pay for a look inside.

events.name: A shimmer in the spray
events.text: In the spray of a breaking wave hangs a ring of still air, like a window. Through it is a sunlit meadow that has never seen the sea.

events.name: The astral campsite
events.text: Outside a sealed astral space entrance, a team's campsite: bedrolls, a cold fire, a {Society|Magic Society|noble house} banner. They went in four days ago and planned for one.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to learn their plan from what they left

events.name: The door no one can open
events.text: An entrance carved like a great stone mouth, its lips sealed shut. Gods' marks are scratched all around it, as if someone tried every church in turn.
events.twist: It opens for anyone who whispers a secret they have never told.

events.name: A ranking stone
events.text: A small stone obelisk beside an astral space, glowing the colour of its rank. This one shows {iron grey|bronze|faint silver}, and it has never been entered.

events.name: The loot pile at the threshold
events.text: Just inside an astral space entrance, a neat pile of loot left by someone who ran out of room. A note says 'Back for this. Don't.'
events.twist: They are back tomorrow, and they counted it.

events.name: A space too small
events.text: An astral space entrance the size of a {cat flap|letterbox|teacup}. Anyone who squeezes through finds a full-sized dungeon, and has to squeeze back out with any loot.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 to get through without getting stuck

events.name: The tower on the water
events.text: A tower stands on the open sea, its base in the waves, no island beneath it. Its door is an astral space entrance, and its windows show daylight at night.
events.twist: Inside, a Silver-rank elf has been studying the space for forty years and is glad of company.

events.name: The wardrobe in the snow
events.nod: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe: a wardrobe that opens onto snow
events.text: An old wardrobe stands alone, doors ajar. Cold air and a few snowflakes drift out of it, though the day is warm.
events.twist: It is an astral space, always winter, with a lamp post in the middle of it.

events.name: The rabbit hole
events.nod: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland: down the rabbit hole
events.text: A rabbit hole that drops far deeper than it should, and from the bottom comes the faint sound of {a tea party|croquet|someone being very late}.

events.name: A rope into nothing
events.text: A climbing rope hangs from a tree branch and ends in a black hole in the air. Something on the other end tugs it, twice, politely.

events.name: A map of the inside
events.text: A dead adventurer's notebook has a careful map of an astral space's rooms, traps marked, and its entrance just a day off the route.
events.twist: The last room on the map is marked only with a skull and the word 'friendly'.

events.name: The doorway in the dune
events.text: The wind has scoured a dune down to a buried stone archway, and the darkness inside it is warm and smells of rain. It is an astral space.

events.name: A space for sale
events.text: A man with a folding table sits beside an astral space entrance, selling 'tours' at one iron coin a head. He has never been inside.

events.name: A sunken shrine
events.text: Below the clear water, a drowned shrine: pillars, an altar, and a statue of the Church of the Ocean's god, its hand held up toward the surface.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to dive down to the altar

events.name: The walking house's grave
events.text: A Drift Host walking camp left behind: round tents in the grass, cook-pots still out, every greatback gone. The Tide came faster than they thought.

events.name: A milestone with a secret
events.text: A milestone giving the distance to a town that burned {a hundred|three hundred|fifty} years ago. Its back is hollow, and something has been left inside recently.

events.name: The tower with no stairs
events.text: An old watchtower with a door at the top and none at the bottom. A wooden sign at its base reads 'Back soon.'
events.twist: Whoever built it could fly. Their journal is still inside, if the party can get up there.

events.name: The faceless statues
events.text: A row of statues along the old road, every face chipped smooth. The newest one still has a face, and it looks like {a party member|the last innkeeper|someone they passed today}.

events.name: The broken sky ship dock
events.text: A mooring mast for sky ships, abandoned, rising from nowhere. Its winding stair still climbs to a landing with a speaking-tube that hums.
events.check: Arcana DC 14 to work out who is on the other end

events.name: A temple of a forgotten god
events.text: A temple to a god that is not one of the twenty. The altar is clean, the floor swept, and the god's face is covered with a cloth.
events.twist: Under the cloth, the god's face is the face of whoever lifts it.

events.name: The old waystation
events.text: A roofless waystation from the old road, its well still sweet. The walls hold travellers' names going back two hundred years.
events.twist: One of the oldest names is the same as a party member's.

events.name: A causeway of heads
events.text: An old causeway through the marsh, every post topped with a carved stone head. Locals say each one marks a bandit hanged here.

events.name: The aqueduct to nowhere
events.text: A great stone aqueduct runs for miles across the land, carrying fresh water from nowhere in particular to nowhere at all.

events.name: The sword in the anvil
events.nod: Arthurian legend: the sword in the stone
events.text: A sword stuck in an anvil on a hilltop, with a worn path around it and a sign: 'Ten tries, one iron coin.' Nobody has ever won.
events.twist: It comes out easily for anyone who isn't trying.
events.check: Athletics DC 20, for fun

events.name: The upside-down chapel
events.text: A small {Church of Knowledge|Church of Truth|Church of the Earth} chapel lying upside down, roof sunk in the earth, its door now a hatch in the floor. The library inside is in perfect order.

events.name: The stone heidel
events.text: A huge carved heidel beside the road, worn smooth by children climbing it. Its nose is polished bright. Rubbing it is said to bring safe travel.

events.name: A lighthouse with no keeper
events.text: A lighthouse on a lonely point, its lamp lit, its door unlocked, the keeper's dinner warm on the table. No one has lived there in ten years.
events.twist: The keeper's ghost wants someone to finish the logbook, which ends mid-sentence.

events.name: The broken bridge
events.text: A ruined bridge over a gorge, half of it still standing. Among the rubble below lies an old toll box, probably still full.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to climb down and back

events.name: A carved jungle face
events.text: A stone face twice the height of a tall man stares out of the jungle. Its mouth is a doorway, and fresh {flowers|fruit|candles} have been left inside.

events.name: Rails in the grass
events.text: Two iron rails, rusted and perfectly parallel, run across the land for a few hundred yards and then stop. An outworlder would know what they are.
events.twist: An outworlder is camped at the end of them, waiting for a train that never comes.

events.name: A temple-tavern ruin
events.text: The ruin of an old Church of the Revels temple-tavern. The roof is gone, but the cellar is sealed, and nobody has ever opened the cellar.
events.twist: Inside is a cellar of perfect wine and a Revels priest who has been asleep down there for a century.
events.check: Strength DC 13 to force the door

events.name: The hermit's library
events.text: A tiny stone hut with a sign in six languages: 'Library. Borrow one, return one.' Inside are two hundred books and a sleeping {goblin|Leonid|elf} librarian.

events.name: A fallen colossus
events.text: A vast stone statue lies broken across a valley, a finger the size of a cottage. Its stone eye still tracks anything that moves.

events.name: A shrine of the Hearth
events.text: A ring of stones around a fire that has never gone out, a Church of the Hearth shrine. A kettle hangs over it, and there is always tea.
events.twist: Anyone who adds a stick to the fire sleeps warm tonight, whatever the weather.

events.name: The pillar of names
events.text: A tall pillar carved with names, hundreds of them, under the words 'The last surge'. The space at the bottom has been left blank for the next.
events.twist: A party member's family name is on it, three times.

events.name: The reef fort
events.text: An old stone fort built on a reef, half underwater, its cannons rusted shut. Merfolk children use it as a playground and charge a toll to tour it.

events.name: A bush of healing berries
events.text: A bush heavy with {red|blue|silver-skinned} berries that the party's healer knows on sight. Each handful works like a weak healing potion, for a day.

events.name: Truffles under the oak
events.text: A pig belonging to nobody is rooting furiously under an old oak. Whatever it has found smells {wonderful|expensive|like a cellar}.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 12 to get the pig out of the way

events.name: A bed of pearl oysters
events.text: The water here is shallow and clear, and the bottom is crowded with oysters. One in {ten|twenty|fifty} holds a pearl.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 to dive for an hour

events.name: The fish that glows
events.text: The ship's line comes up with a fish that glows {blue|pink|gold} from the inside. The cook says it is good eating, and the glow lasts a week.

events.name: Salt crust
events.text: A dry lakebed crusted with pure {white|pink|grey} salt, easy to cut into blocks. Any town ahead will buy it, if the party can carry it.
events.twist: Under the crust is a perfectly preserved caravan, still in its harness.

events.name: The ghost-pepper patch
events.text: A patch of tiny, shining peppers. One bite gives fire resistance for an hour, and nobody who tries one can speak for most of that hour.

events.name: A floating island of weed
events.text: A raft of weed half a mile wide drifts past, thick enough to walk on. Crabs as big as shields scuttle across it, and something glints at its heart.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 to cross it

events.name: Driftwood from far away
events.text: A huge piece of driftwood bumps the hull, carved all over with {faces|stars|tally marks} in a style no one aboard has ever seen.

events.name: The bird with a message
events.text: A tired messenger bird lands on the nearest shoulder and will not leave. Its leg tube holds a letter from a mother in {place} to a son nobody has found.
events.twist: The son is in the next town, too ashamed to write back.

events.name: A shoal of silver fish
events.text: A shoal of fish with scales like {iron|bronze} spirit coins rises right under the boat. A net brought up now would feed the crew and sell well.
events.check: Athletics or Survival DC 12

events.name: Wild heidels
events.text: A herd of wild heidels grazes by a {stream|salt lick|lonely tree}. A patient rider might tame one, and on the steppe a good heidel is worth a month's pay.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 15

events.name: The amber seam
events.text: A cut bank shows a seam of amber the length of an arm. Inside one chunk, a tiny {monster|dragon-like lizard|fish with legs} is frozen mid-leap, perfectly preserved.

events.name: A map drawn on skin
events.text: A map tattooed on a square of leather, showing a {coast|mountain pass|marsh} the party knows, with an X and the words 'still there'.

events.name: The X on the map
events.text: The landmarks on the leather map match. Under the X is an iron box, and a second map with an X somewhere much more dangerous.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 to dig it out quickly

events.name: A letter for a party member
events.text: A sealed letter lies in the party's path, addressed by name to {the party's leader|the youngest of them|whoever reads this first}. The ink is still wet.

events.name: The letter-writer
events.text: The person who wrote the letter is waiting at a crossroads. They are a {Church of Truth priest|tide-reader|retired spy} who saw the party in a dream.

events.name: A purse of foreign coins
events.text: A purse of {square|holed|wooden} coins from no kingdom anyone knows. A Magic Society appraiser says they are from another world.

events.name: The coin's owner
events.nod: Outworlder with real-world money: bus fare, loyalty cards and a lottery ticket
events.text: An outworlder stops the party, frantic. The strange purse is his. He swears the coins are worth a fortune at home, and offers a story as a reward.

events.name: Kilroy's cousin
events.nod: Outworlder graffiti: a smiley face and a joke on 'Kilroy was here'
events.text: Carved into a rock: a stick figure with a round head, and the words 'I was not here', signed with a smiley face. The date is next year.
events.twist: The outworlder who carved it is camped nearby and wants to know the date.

events.name: A trail of breadcrumbs
events.nod: Hansel and Gretel: the breadcrumb trail
events.text: A neat trail of breadcrumbs leads off the path into the {trees|reeds|fog}. The birds will not touch them.
events.twist: At the end is a cottage with sweet-smelling walls and an oven already lit.

events.name: The singing skull
events.text: A skull on a post sings a {sea shanty|lullaby|drinking song} whenever anyone walks past. It knows one verse, and it is very proud of it.

events.name: A riddle in the sand
events.text: A riddle written in the {sand|frost|mud} that does not blow away or wash out. Answer it aloud, and the letters rearrange into directions.
events.check: Intelligence DC 14

events.name: The ring of mushrooms
events.nod: Folklore: fairy rings and lost time
events.text: A perfect ring of white mushrooms. Inside, the air smells of music. Anyone who steps in loses an hour and comes out with a {song|silver coin|new freckle}.

events.name: The cardboard box
events.nod: Metal Gear Solid: the sneaking cardboard box
events.text: A large wooden crate sits in the middle of nowhere. When nobody is looking, it moves a little closer. It has eye holes.
events.twist: Inside is a goblin scout from a rival company, mortified and hungry.

events.name: The tiny door
events.nod: Folklore: brownies who clean in return for a bowl of milk
events.text: A tiny wooden door, the height of a hand, set into a {tree root|harbour wall|ship's beam}. A thimble of milk left outside is gone by morning, and the boots are clean.

events.name: A wanted poster for the party
events.text: A wanted poster nailed up, offering 10 iron coins for a group that looks quite a lot like the party. The drawing is terrible, and the price is insulting.
events.twist: It was put up by an old rival as a joke. The joke is spreading.

events.name: The prophecy scrap
events.nod: Classic fantasy: the half-burned prophecy
events.text: A scrap of burned paper with half a prophecy: 'when the {bronze|silver|glass} road opens, the third shall'. The rest is ash.
events.twist: A Church of Knowledge priest would give a lot for the scrap, and won't say why.

events.name: A wish in the well
events.text: A wishing well with a sign: 'One wish, one silver coin.' The bucket holds a thousand coins, every one of them iron.
events.twist: Drop a silver coin, and something in the well wishes for something back.

events.name: The bottle with a voice
events.nod: Arabian Nights: the genie in the bottle
events.text: A corked bottle that complains loudly whenever anyone sits near it. It says it is a powerful genie, and would very much like out.
events.twist: It is a small, sulky spirit who grants only small wishes, and mostly the wrong ones.

events.name: The compass that points home
events.text: A battered compass whose needle points to wherever its holder thinks of as home. For one party member, it spins and spins.
events.twist: When the needle stops spinning, it points somewhere that party member has never been.

events.name: The ten-foot pole
events.nod: D&D: the ten-foot pole
events.text: A ten-foot pole leaning against a rock, with a tag that says 'You'll want this.' Every adventurer who has passed has signed it.
events.twist: Somewhere ahead today, the party will want it.

events.name: The tablet of rules
events.text: A stone tablet carved with the rules of an astral space nearby, in Society shorthand. Rule three is scratched out, and the scratching is fresh.

events.name: A trapped spirit in a lamp
events.text: An old oil lamp with a spirit trapped inside, flickering in panic. Free it and it promises a gift. Sell it and the Magic Society pays well.
events.twist: The spirit was put there by a Church of Purity priest for a reason.
events.check: Arcana DC 14 to free it safely

events.name: A love letter in a tree
events.text: A hollow tree holds a bundle of love letters, sixty years of them, from two people in villages a day apart. The last letter says 'Tomorrow, then.'
events.twist: The writers are alive, ninety, and still have not met. One village is ahead.

events.name: The game left half-played
events.text: A board game set up on a {rock|barrel|ship's hatch}, half played. It is clearly someone's move, and the pieces are warm.
events.check: Intelligence DC 13 to make a good move

events.name: A stamped passport
events.nod: A real-world passport, explained by its outworlder owner
events.text: A small booklet with a stern face drawn on the first page and stamps from {France|Japan|somewhere called Ohio}. It belongs to an outworlder who wants it back badly.

events.name: The broken crown
events.text: A crown of {black iron|bone|cold bronze}, snapped in two, lying where someone threw it. A Church of Dominion priest would kill for it, and might.
events.twist: Whoever wears even half of it hears orders whispered in their ear.

events.name: The ghost light
events.text: A pale light bobs ahead of the party, always a hundred yards away, leading somewhere. It goes out the moment anyone stops following.

events.name: Where the light leads
events.text: The pale light comes back and settles over a spot. Beneath it, a lost child's shoe, and further on, a trail no one has followed yet.
events.check: Survival DC 14 to follow it

events.name: The talking statue head
events.text: A stone head lies in the grass, nose broken off. It speaks, and it wants its nose back. The nose is in the next village, used as a doorstop.

events.name: The returned nose
events.text: The stone head is overjoyed to have its nose back. In thanks, it tells the party where its old owners buried {their treasury|a sword|a full set of armour}.

events.name: A seashell that remembers
events.text: A large spiral shell. Held to the ear, it plays back the last thing said near it, which was a captain arguing about {smuggling|a mutiny|a wedding}.

events.name: A lost familiar
events.text: A small spectral {owl|lizard|fox} follows the party, glowing faintly and lost. It is someone's familiar, and it can lead them to its owner.

events.name: The fortune in the fish
events.text: The cook guts a fish and finds a {gold ring|silver key|Society badge} inside, engraved with a name. The name belongs to a sailor on this very ship, who lost it ten years ago.
events.twist: The ring was thrown overboard by his wife, and she is aboard too.

events.name: The figurehead
events.text: A ship's figurehead floats by, a woman's face, eyes painted open. It turns slowly in the water to keep watching the party's ship.
events.twist: Its ship sank with a strongbox, and the figurehead is trying to lead someone back to it.

events.name: The sealed jar of wine
events.text: A clay jar sealed with Church of the Revels wax, {three hundred|five hundred|a thousand} years old. A collector in Yaresh would pay a fortune, unless it has turned.
events.check: Medicine or Nature DC 13 to tell

events.name: A bell under the waves
events.text: A bell rings somewhere under the water, slow and steady. Sailors say a drowned temple is calling its faithful home.
events.twist: Anyone who answers the bell with a prayer to the Ocean has calm water all of tomorrow.

events.name: The arrow to the knee
events.nod: Skyrim: 'I used to be an adventurer like you'
events.text: A broken arrow and a dented knee-guard on the ground, with a note in shaky handwriting: 'Retiring. Good luck out there.'

events.name: A message on the mast
events.text: Carved into the ship's mast, low down: a list of {five|seven|nine} names, the last one cut deep. None of the crew will say who carved it.

events.name: A festival
events.text: A village festival of the Church of the Revels.
events.twist: Stay and lose half a day, but gain goodwill and a rumour.

events.name: A follower
events.text: A strange animal starts following the party and will not leave.

events.name: A contest
events.text: A contest at a waystation, with a real prize and a sore loser.

events.name: A peddler
events.text: A peddler selling a 'guaranteed' magic item that is one-third genuine.

events.name: A lure
events.text: A mirage, a light or a voice calling from off the path.

events.name: A face from the past
events.text: Someone recognises a party member, for better or worse.

events.name: Dice at the inn
events.text: Gambling for spirit coins at a roadside inn, and the house is cheating.

events.name: Goat reeve
events.text: A goat has been elected reeve of a hamlet, and it takes its toll in turnips. The villagers are completely serious.

events.name: The arm-wrestling champion
events.text: A waystation's arm-wrestling champion, a grandmother of eighty, challenges the party's strongest member.
events.check: Athletics DC 16
events.twist: She is a retired Bronze-rank adventurer.

events.name: A puppet show
events.text: A puppet show at a crossroads tells the legend of a local hero. Children have walked miles to see it.

events.name: The tavern with one song
