events.text: A roadside tavern where the bard only knows one song, and sings it every hour. By evening, everyone is singing it too, and so is the party, for a week.

events.name: A race
events.text: Locals racing {horses|heidels|very large chickens} along the road. Anyone can enter for an iron coin, and the winner takes the pot.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 14

events.name: The lost dog
events.text: A lost dog with a name tag from a village a day back down the road. It walks with the party and will not leave.
events.twist: The village wants it back badly and will pay.

events.name: Lovers' quarrel
events.text: Two lovers having a screaming argument on opposite banks of a river. Each asks the party to carry a message across.

events.name: The poet
events.text: A travelling poet who insists on writing an epic about the party. It is terrible, and he wants to read all of it.

events.name: The fortune teller
events.text: A fortune teller at a waystation reads one party member's palm, goes pale, and refuses to say what she saw. She returns their coin.

events.name: A market day
events.text: Market day in a small town on the route: cheap supplies, local gossip and a stall with something unusual.

events.name: The dancing bear
events.text: A dancing bear and its handler. The bear is clearly the one in charge.

events.name: A swimming hole
events.text: A perfect swimming hole on a hot day. Stop for an hour and everyone feels better.
events.twist: Something large lives in the deep end, and it just wants to watch.

events.name: The lost tourist
events.nod: Tourist culture: a stranger with a guidebook
events.text: An outworlder who has written their own guidebook to the region and is getting every single thing wrong. They want a photo, which they draw.

events.name: A heated game of stones
events.text: Off-duty guards playing a dice game at a waystation, very happy to take strangers' money.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to spot the loaded dice

events.name: A chorus of frogs
events.text: Every frog in the marsh croaks in unison, a single note, every time someone speaks.

events.name: The duel for honour
events.text: Two young nobles have stopped their carriages to fight a duel over an insult neither can remember. They need a witness.

events.name: The tasting
events.text: A family of winemakers giving away tastings at the gate, hoping travellers will spread the word.

events.name: Sky ship show
events.text: A sky ship putting on a light show for a town festival, sparks falling like snow.

events.name: A shrine to bad luck
events.text: A shrine where travellers leave something they can't stand, for luck. It's full of socks, love letters and one very angry cat.

events.name: A kid with a sword
events.text: A village kid with a wooden sword challenges the party to a duel. The whole village watches.

events.name: The grape-treading
events.text: A Church of the Revels vineyard needs extra feet for the grape-treading, and the party's boots will do. The vintner pays in {wine|raisins|a very large hat}, and a lot of it.
events.check: Constitution DC 12 to still walk straight tomorrow
events.failText: a slow, sore-headed morning

events.name: A harvest supper
events.text: A village is laying long tables for its harvest supper, and travellers eat free. Stay, and the whole village knows the party's names by morning.
events.twist: The oldest farmer knows a back path that saves an hour tomorrow.

events.name: The Hearth day
events.text: It is a Church of the Hearth feast day, and every door on the {street|harbour|lane} is open, every pot on the boil. Refusing a bowl is very rude.

events.name: A masked parade
events.text: A Church of Disguise parade winds through town, everyone masked. A masked figure presses a {key|note|coin} into a party member's hand and vanishes into the crowd.

events.name: The mask's errand
events.text: A stranger stops the party and asks, very quietly, for what the masked figure gave them. They offer {a good price|a threat|a story} for it.

events.name: A Journey blessing
events.text: Church of the Journey priests are blessing every traveller who passes, with chalk stars on their {boots|packs|foreheads}. The blessing is real, if small.
events.twist: One priest takes a party member aside: their star smudged, which has never happened before.

events.name: The Liberty bonfire
events.text: A Church of Liberty bonfire, with broken chains thrown on the flames. The crowd is cheerful, and the local lord's men are watching from the hill.
events.twist: Someone in the crowd is collecting names for a cause, and asks for the party's.

events.name: Ocean day at the docks
events.text: It is the Church of the Ocean's feast day, and no boat may sail before noon. Every sailor in port is {drinking|singing|fishing for luck} to the waves.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15 to find a captain who will sail early
events.failText: the party waits for noon with everyone else

events.name: A Purity sermon
events.text: A Church of Purity preacher on a cart is shouting at a crowd about outworlders and their 'false flesh'. The crowd is listening, and some of them are nodding.
events.twist: The preacher points at the party and asks if any of them would like to deny it.

events.name: A wedding on the road
events.text: A wedding party has blocked the road with dancing. The bride's father insists that strangers bring luck, and the party must stay for {one dance|one drink|the whole night}.

events.name: A deck-side wedding
events.text: The captain is marrying two of the crew on deck, with a cake made of ship's biscuit. The party is asked to {witness|play music|give the toast}.

events.name: The lantern float
events.text: At dusk, the whole town floats paper lanterns down the {river|harbour|canal}, one for every soul lost this year. They glow brighter as they drift.

events.name: The festival of fools
events.text: A town has crowned its Fool for the day, and the Fool's first law is that every stranger must speak in {rhyme|a whisper|the third person} until sundown.
events.twist: The Fool is the local lord in disguise, listening to what people really think.
events.check: Performance DC 12 to keep it up

events.name: The Healer's free day
events.text: A Church of the Healer clinic is treating everyone free today, and the queue reaches round the square. Waiting costs the morning, but heals anything mundane.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to be seen quickly
events.failText: the morning goes to the queue

events.name: A Drift Host feast
events.text: A small Drift Host has made a kill and is roasting it whole on a {spit|bed of stones|greatback's cooking platform}. Guests are welcome if they bring a gift and a good story.
events.check: Performance or Persuasion DC 13

events.name: A night of the dead
events.text: A village leaves its doors open and a place set for its dead. The party is offered a seat, and one of the empty chairs is pulled out for them already.
events.twist: Whoever sits in the empty chair is told one true thing about a dead relative.

events.name: The War parade
events.text: A Church of War procession marches veterans of the last surge through town. Most are missing {an arm|an eye|a friend}. The crowd is silent, then cheers.
events.twist: One veteran recognises a party member's weapon. It belonged to his captain.

events.name: A Trade fair
events.text: A Church of Trade fair in a market town: honest scales, sharp dealers and a priest who checks every contract. A good day to buy.

events.name: A Revels drinking hall
events.text: A Church of the Revels drinking hall on the road. The priest pours first and asks questions never, and the party's {quietest|most sensible|most serious} member is the guest of honour.

events.name: A Cloud Clan sky-dance
events.text: A Cloud Clan village is dancing on a terrace of walkable cloud, lit from below by lamps. Visitors are invited to step out onto it.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 to dance without sinking

events.name: A festival nobody remembers
events.text: A whole village in costume, dancing and feasting. Nobody can say what the festival is for, only that it has been going on for three days.
events.twist: It started when a stranger arrived with a fiddle, and he has not stopped playing since.

events.name: The Journey's crossroads fair
events.text: A crossroads fair where travellers swap news, maps and stories. The party can trade one rumour for one rumour.

events.name: The pie-eating contest
events.text: A pie-eating contest, open to all, with a {cooked ham|barrel of ale|live pig} as the prize. The reigning champion is a Leonid the size of a door.
events.twist: The Leonid champion is throwing the contest so a hungry child can win.
events.check: Constitution DC 14

events.name: A wager on the weather
events.text: An old sailor bets anyone a silver coin that it will {rain|blow|go dead calm} before sundown. He has never lost, and nobody knows why.
events.twist: He has a weather essence and is too shy to admit it.

events.name: Liar's dice on deck
events.text: The crew are playing liar's dice on an upturned {barrel|crate|bucket}, for spirit coins. They are good at it, and better at hiding it.
events.twist: The bosun is cheating, and the rest of the crew would love to see him caught.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to keep from losing your stake

events.name: The strongest arm
events.text: A {blacksmith|dock worker|Leonid farmhand} is taking on all comers at arm-wrestling for a bronze coin a go, and has not lost all day.
events.check: Athletics DC 15

events.name: The rope-climb race
events.text: Sailors race up the rigging for a {cask of rum|week off mopping|captain's hat}. They want a passenger to try, mostly for the laugh.
events.check: Athletics DC 13

events.name: The heidel race
events.text: Drift Host riders are racing heidels across a {river|ridge|dry lake}, betting greatback calves on the result. A guest may ride for honour.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 15

events.name: The riddle duel
events.text: A Church of Knowledge acolyte sits at the side of the road, offering a silver coin to anyone who can ask her a riddle she cannot answer.
events.twist: She is cheating with a sense ability. A Church of Truth priest would be scandalised.
events.check: Intelligence DC 15

events.name: Shove-coin at the inn
events.text: Locals play shove-coin with iron spirit coins on a long {table|bar|ship's plank}. The landlord takes a cut, and the ceiling has holes from the times it went badly.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13

events.name: The fishing contest
events.text: A village fishing contest, prize to the biggest catch. A small {child|goblin girl|very old man} is winning, and the adults are very upset about it.
events.check: Survival DC 14

events.name: The sword-catching challenge
events.text: A juggler with {three daggers|five knives|two burning torches} challenges anyone to catch one. Nobody has caught one by the handle yet.
events.check: Dexterity DC 15, or a cut hand

events.name: A tug of war across a river
events.text: Two villages are having a tug of war across the river, the losers to get very wet. Each side begs the party to join it.
events.check: Athletics DC 13

events.name: The singing contest
events.text: A singing contest in the {square|harbour|caravan camp} with a cheese the size of a wheel for a prize. The judge is tone deaf and proud of it.
events.check: Performance DC 13

events.name: A game of stones with a monster
events.text: A talking spirit sits by a stone board, playing a game nobody has heard of. It wins every time, and it is lonely.
events.twist: If anyone wins, it gives them a monster core it has been saving.
events.check: Intelligence DC 16

events.name: The longest stare
events.text: A competition to outstare the {village goat|town's oldest elf|captain's cat}. The record is two hours, and the goat is very good at it.
events.check: Wisdom DC 14

events.name: The duel of insults
events.nod: Monkey Island: insult swordfighting
events.text: A pair of pirates on the dock are settling a quarrel by insults, not swords. They demand a judge, and then a challenger.
events.twist: The loser has to buy everyone on the dock a drink, and is already very poor.
events.check: Performance or Deception DC 14

events.name: An unwinnable game
events.text: A man at a crossroads offers a game: three {cups|shells|hats}, one ball. The ball is not under any of them, ever.
events.check: Sleight of Hand or Perception DC 14 to prove it

events.name: The heaviest stone
events.text: A stone in the square carved with the names of everyone who has lifted it. The last name is two hundred years old.
events.twist: Lifting it uncovers a coin hidden by the last person to lift it.
events.check: Athletics DC 18

events.name: Archery at the fair
events.text: An archery contest at a fair, three arrows a shot, a silver coin for a bullseye. The target is a painted {Church of Purity preacher|tax collector|dragon}.
events.twist: A real Church of Purity preacher is in the crowd, and he has noticed.
events.check: Ranged attack against AC 16

events.name: A wager on the party
events.text: Two old women are betting on whether the party will survive the {week|month|next river}. One of them is very confident, and it is not the kind one.

events.name: The rank test
events.text: A travelling show has a rank-tester: a bell you hit with a hammer to see your rank. It always rings one rank too high, and the crowd loves it.
events.twist: It rings true for one party member, and the show-master goes pale.

events.name: Racing snails
events.text: Children are racing monster {snails|beetles|toads} the size of dogs. Each snail has a name, a trainer and a betting price, and one has a secret.
events.check: Animal Handling or Insight DC 12 to pick the winner

events.name: The bargain essence
events.text: A pedlar is selling a 'genuine {fire|dragon|hero} essence' for ten iron coins. It is a painted pebble in a very nice box.
events.twist: The box is a real essence case, worth far more than he is asking.

events.name: The bumboat
events.text: A little boat rows out to the ship, loaded with {fruit|fresh bread|cheap knives}, and the woman rowing it will not take no for an answer.

events.name: A potion with side effects
events.text: A smiling seller offers a potion of {strength|charm|flight} at half price. The label lists the side effects in very small writing, and they go on for a while.
events.twist: It works perfectly. The side effect is a week of hiccups.

events.name: A travelling auction
events.text: A travelling auction wagon has stopped for the day with city stock: {a pair of boots|a warded box|a monster-hide coat} and a dozen curios. Bidding starts at noon.

events.name: The map seller
events.text: A man sells hand-drawn maps of the road ahead, all different, all slightly wrong in the same place.
events.twist: The same place is wrong on every map because something there moves.

events.name: A stall of cursed things
events.text: A quiet stall with a sign: 'Cursed. Cheap. No refunds.' The stallholder swears every item is harmless as long as it is never {named|washed|given away}.

events.name: The haggler's challenge
events.text: A Church of Trade priest at a stall offers a discount to anyone who can out-haggle her. Nobody has managed it in {a year|ten years|her whole life}.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15

events.name: A goblin tinker
events.text: A goblin tinker with a cart of pots offers to mend anything broken for a song, literally. She wants a new song for her collection.
events.check: Performance DC 11

events.name: Cores, no questions
events.text: A nervous man is selling Bronze-rank cores very cheap from a sack. Each one still has a little blood on it, and none of it is monster blood.
events.twist: He is fencing for someone who killed a Bronze team for them.

events.name: The fish market
events.text: The fish market is in full cry as the party passes. A fishwife offers a {fresh|smoked|very strange} fish at a price that seems too good.

events.name: The ten-foot-pole man
events.nod: D&D: the ten-foot pole in every starting kit
events.text: A pedlar selling nothing but poles, from five feet to fifteen. He insists every adventurer needs one, and has a long sales pitch about {pits|doors|suspicious floors}.
events.twist: One of his poles is a staff of real power, and he has no idea.

events.name: The cloud-furniture seller
events.text: A trader has a sofa made of thickened cloud on a lead, bobbing above his cart. He wants someone to help him walk it to {place}.

events.name: A spirit coin changer
events.text: A coin changer offers to turn bronze into iron at a terrible rate. She also buys anything that {glows|hums|bites}, no questions asked.

events.name: The Drift Host traders
events.text: Hostfolk traders lay out hides, cores and {steppe goats|heidel cheese|greatback wool} on blankets. They judge every customer's rank before naming a price.
events.check: Persuasion DC 14 for a fair price

events.name: The merfolk market
events.text: A merfolk market floats on rafts of woven kelp, with {coral jewellery|pearl combs|shark-tooth knives}, sea-silk and fish no one on land has ever eaten.

events.name: Guaranteed lucky charms
events.text: A pedlar's charms each guarantee luck against one thing: {wolves|tax collectors|mothers-in-law}. He has sold out of the dragon ones.

events.name: A Celestine silversmith
events.text: A Celestine silversmith, hair and eyes like polished copper, makes rings while customers watch. Each one hums faintly when finished.
events.twist: She is looking for the outworlders she comes from, and asks if anyone has met them.

events.name: The pet seller
events.text: A cart of caged pets: a {two-headed hen|glowing toad|tiny furious owl} is going cheap. The seller badly wants it gone before dark.

events.name: A shop that wasn't there
events.text: A little shop stands where the party is sure there was nothing yesterday. Its prices are in years, not coins.
events.twist: It sells exactly one thing a party member has been looking for.

events.name: A brewer's samples
events.text: A brewer gives away samples of a new ale she has called after the {Duke|Society|weather}. She needs honest opinions, and gets them.

events.name: A puppet war
events.text: Two rival {puppet shows|preachers|pie sellers} have set up side by side and are trying to drown each other out. Both want the party to choose the better one, loudly.

events.name: The sky ship acrobats
events.text: Acrobats tumble between the ropes of a moored sky ship, catching each other in mid-air with flashes of wind magic. The crowd throws iron coins.

events.name: The story of the party
events.text: A bard is singing a heroic ballad about the party's last deeds. Almost every detail is wrong, and the crowd loves him.
events.twist: He will change the words for a fee, or a better story.

events.name: A song from the crew
events.text: The crew sings a {working song|sad ballad|very rude ditty} while hauling the sails. Anyone who joins in is one of them by evening.

events.name: The illusionist
events.text: A street illusionist fills the air with glowing birds that settle on the watchers' shoulders. One of them stays with a party member long after the show.
events.twist: It is not an illusion. It is a tiny bird-spirit, and it has chosen them.

events.name: The fire-eater
events.text: A Smoulder {fire-eater|sword-swallower|glass-chewer} who is very bored by fire. She asks the party for anything else she might eat, for a new act.
events.twist: Feed her a pinch of quintessence and she breathes a dragon of flame, and owes the party a favour.

events.name: The bad play
events.text: A troupe is performing a play about a famous surge. It is very long, and the {dragon's head|monster's tail|hero's trousers} falls off in the second act.
events.check: Performance DC 12 to save the scene from the audience

events.name: The dancing bear's rival
events.text: A dancing {monster-boar|heidel|goat} and its handler have set up opposite a dancing bear. The animals are getting competitive.

events.name: A shadow-play of the gods
events.text: A shadow-play tells the story of the twenty gods, and the puppeteer has the old rivalries all wrong, on purpose.
events.twist: Two priests of rival churches in the crowd have started arguing, and it is getting heated.

events.name: The silent musician
events.nod: Folklore: the Pied Piper of Hamelin
events.text: A musician plays a fiddle with no strings, and everyone who listens hears a different tune. Children follow him, smiling.
events.twist: He is leading them to the river. He thinks he is helping.

events.name: The ghost singer
events.nod: Greek myth: the sirens
events.text: A sweet voice sings across the {water|fog|empty fields} at dusk. Everyone hears it. The sailors stuff their ears with wax.
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 not to walk toward it
events.failText: the party loses an hour hauling each other back

events.name: A story-off
events.text: Two old storytellers at the fire are competing for the best tale of the road. They want the party to tell one, and to be honest about the ending.
events.check: Performance DC 12

events.name: The knife-thrower's assistant
events.text: A knife-thrower's assistant has quit mid-show. He asks for a brave volunteer to stand against the board. He has only missed {once|twice|recently}.
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 to stand still

events.name: The street magician's real trick
events.text: A street magician makes a coin vanish, then cannot make it come back. He is panicking, and the coin was the party's.
events.check: Arcana DC 14 to find where it went

events.name: The juggling contest
events.text: A juggler offers a prize to anyone who can keep {three apples|four knives|two live chickens} in the air for a count of ten.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13

events.name: The masked actor
events.text: An actor in a blank mask plays every part in a long tragedy, alone. Afterwards, he will not take the mask off for anyone.
events.twist: He is a Church of Disguise priest, and he has been watching one of the party.

events.name: An outworlder's concert
events.nod: An outworlder playing pop and rock songs from Earth on a lute
events.text: An outworlder with a strange stringed instrument plays songs that nobody knows, and swears they were famous where he comes from.

events.name: The puppet that talks back
events.text: A ventriloquist's {puppet|stuffed crow|wooden goblin} keeps interrupting the act to warn the audience about the ventriloquist. The ventriloquist seems genuinely upset.
events.twist: The puppet is right. The ventriloquist has a stolen ring in his pocket.

events.name: The sea shanty contest
events.text: Two ships moored side by side are singing shanties at each other, each crew trying to outlast the other. Passengers count as crew.
events.check: Performance or Constitution DC 13

events.name: The singing frogs' show
events.text: A man with a trained frog chorus, each frog in a tiny hat. They know {two songs|one hymn|a very long ballad}, and they will sing all of it.

events.name: The duckling parade
events.text: A mother {duck|monster-goose|heidel} and her young insist on crossing in front of the party, very slowly, in single file. Nobody wants to rush them.

events.name: The gull thief
events.text: A gull lands, snatches a party member's {lunch|map|hat}, and sits just out of reach, looking pleased with itself.
events.check: Dexterity or Animal Handling DC 13 to get it back

events.name: A dolphin escort
events.text: A pod of {dolphins|small whales|merfolk riders} rides the bow wave all morning, leaping and chattering. Sailors say it means a safe crossing, and today they are right.

events.name: The cat that adopts
events.text: A thin {ginger|black|three-legged} cat has decided the party is its family now. It sleeps on the warmest pack and catches a mouse for them every night.
events.twist: It is a mouser of rare talent, and the next inn wants to buy it.

events.name: The goat that follows
events.text: A goat follows the party, eating anything left unguarded: {bootlaces|a spellbook page|half a tent}. It cannot be chased off, only outwitted.

events.name: The goat's owner
events.text: A furious farmer catches the party up and accuses them of stealing her prize goat. The goat stands behind the party, chewing, and says nothing.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13

events.name: The parrot with secrets
events.text: A parrot on a branch, or a ship's rail, keeps repeating a password, a name and the words 'under the third stone'.

events.name: Under the third stone
events.text: Three stones in a row beside the path, just like the parrot said. Under the third is a smuggler's tin of {iron coins|a ring|a letter}.

events.name: The monster pup
events.text: A monster pup, eyes barely open, waddles up and sneezes sparks. Its mother is nowhere to be seen, and it wants to be carried.
events.twist: Its mother is a Bronze-rank monster, and she is on her way.

events.name: The leaping fish
events.text: Flying fish leap across the deck all {afternoon|morning|through the dinner bell}, and the cook is running around with a pot. A quick hand catches tonight's supper.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12

events.name: The heidel stand-off
events.text: A heidel has lain down across the path and will not get up. Its owner says it does this when it disapproves of someone, and it is staring at the party.
events.twist: It is not staring at the party. It is staring at something following them.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13 to win it over

events.name: The crow court
events.text: Dozens of {crows|ravens|gulls} sit in a ring around one crow in the middle. They caw, the middle crow bows its head, and the ring falls on it all at once.
events.twist: The crows drop the dead crow's treasure at the party's feet: a lost signet ring.

events.name: A herd crossing
events.text: A Drift Host herd is crossing ahead: thousands of heidels and steppe goats, and the walking houses behind them. It takes the whole morning to pass.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to be let through
events.failText: the party waits for the herd

events.name: The whale song
events.text: A whale sings beneath the ship all night, so deep the hull hums. In the morning, everyone aboard remembers the same dream.

events.name: The bee swarm
events.text: A bee swarm has settled on the party's {pack|mule|wagon}, and the beekeeper chasing it is offering honey if they will stand very still.
events.check: Wisdom DC 12 not to flinch

events.name: The monkey bandits
events.text: A troop of {monkeys|monster-lemurs|very small goblins' pets} raids the party's camp, making off with shiny things. Their leader is wearing a stolen Society badge.
events.check: Dexterity DC 14 to get things back

events.name: The horse that won't move
events.text: A riderless, saddled horse stands in the middle of the way and will not budge. A note in its saddlebag reads 'Please take her to my sister.'

events.name: The turtle island
events.text: The little island the ship anchored by for lunch slowly turns around. It is a very old turtle, and it would like the anchor back.
events.twist: Tied to the anchor when it comes back up is a barnacled box of old coins.

events.name: The cart of geese
events.text: A cart of geese has overturned and {fifty|a hundred|two hundred} angry birds are loose. The goose girl begs for help catching them before the market.
events.twist: One goose is the market's prize bird, and it has a monster core in its crop.
events.check: Animal Handling or Athletics DC 12

events.name: The fox in a hat
events.nod: Folklore: the trickster fox who courts travellers
events.text: A fox in a tiny hat trots up, bows, and lays a {flower|coin|dead mouse} at a party member's feet. Then it runs off, looking back.
events.twist: It wants to be followed to its den, which is full of other people's lost hats.

events.name: The mating dance
events.text: Two monster cranes are performing a long, elaborate mating dance across the whole path. Interrupting them would be very rude.

events.name: Two villages, one bridge
events.text: Two villages each claim the bridge between them and charge a toll at both ends. Each wants the party to say which side is right.
events.check: Persuasion DC 14 to cross without paying twice

events.name: The feud over a pig
events.text: Two farmers are arguing at a gate over who owns a pig. The pig has a priest's collar on, and a Church of Justice priest is on the way.

events.name: The election
events.text: A hamlet is electing a new reeve, and the candidates are a {farmer|cooper|very old dog}. The party is asked to count the votes, because nobody trusts anyone.

events.name: The ban on singing
events.text: A town has banned singing after a Church of Purity preacher came through. Everyone is humming very loudly instead.
events.twist: The Church of the Revels has sent a priest to stage a protest concert tonight.

events.name: The neighbour's wall
events.text: Two {neighbours|brothers|old friends} are building a wall between their houses, one stone at a time, each taking the other's stones in the night.

events.name: The missing bell
events.text: A village's chapel bell has been stolen, and the whole village blames the next village. The next village has a suspiciously new bell.

events.name: The bell trade
events.text: Both villages' priests meet the party on the road with a deal: return the bell secretly, and they will each say the other started it.

events.name: The hanging judge
events.text: A village has caught a thief and wants to hang him at noon. He is fourteen and stole a loaf. The reeve wants the party to say it is fair.

events.name: The ghost tax
events.text: A town collects a tax to keep its ghost happy. The collector is very serious about it, and the ghost has a {receipt book|ledger|very small quill}.
events.twist: The ghost is real, and it would like to complain about the collector.

events.name: The lord's hunt
events.text: A noble hunting party is crashing through the countryside, and the huntsmen insist all travellers stand aside until the hunt has passed.
events.check: Persuasion DC 14
events.failText: the party waits for the hunt

events.name: The village that counts
events.text: Everyone in this village counts their {steps|breaths|blinks} out loud. A child explains that it is the only way to stop the road from adding more.
events.twist: Anyone who stops counting finds the road ahead is a little longer tomorrow.

events.name: The mayor's portrait
events.text: The mayor wants a party member to sit for a portrait, because she thinks they look heroic. The painter is slow, and the mayor keeps adding things.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to keep it to an hour
events.failText: the portrait takes the afternoon

events.name: The two captains
events.text: Two captains are arguing over who has right of way, their {ships|barges|fishing boats} nose to nose. Both crews are watching, and both want a passenger to decide.

events.name: The lost child
events.text: A small child has wandered off from a family's {cart|boat|camp} and is sitting by the way, crying. The family is an hour back, frantic.

events.name: The haunted mill
events.text: The miller swears his mill grinds by itself at night. He offers free flour to anyone who will sleep there.
events.twist: It is an Iron-rank mill spirit that just wants someone to talk to.

events.name: The quarrel of priests
events.text: A Church of Justice priest and a Church of Liberty priest are arguing in the square about a runaway, and the runaway is hiding behind the party.

events.name: The leaking boat
events.text: A ferryman's boat has sprung a leak and he has three fares waiting. He offers the party free passage forever if they help him patch it.
events.twist: His idea of 'forever' is a punch card with ten holes.
events.check: Carpenter's tools or Dexterity DC 12

events.name: The ancient feud
events.text: Two families on either side of the path have fought for {forty|a hundred|three hundred} years. Today they have a funeral each, and both blame the other.

events.name: The surge refugees
events.text: A column of refugees from a surge in another region, carrying what they could. They have news, and some of it is about the road ahead.

events.name: The village of mutes
events.text: Nobody in this village speaks, by choice. They communicate in signs, and they seem very worried about something behind the party.

events.name: The festival permit
events.text: A town clerk insists the party needs a permit to {enter|leave|stand still in} the town during festival week. The permit costs an iron coin and an hour.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to skip the queue
events.failText: the hour is spent in a queue

events.name: The perfect picnic spot
events.text: A sunny spot with a view, soft grass and a cool breeze. Everyone wants to stop for {an hour|lunch|a nap}, and nobody can think of a reason not to.
events.twist: Stopping is worth it: everyone ends the day in a better mood and sleeps well.

events.name: The hot spring
events.text: A natural hot spring steams beside the way, {mineral-rich|faintly glowing|smelling of eggs} and wonderful. An hour's soak cures aches and one level of exhaustion.

events.name: The calm-day swim
events.text: The wind drops to nothing, the sea goes flat and clear, and the captain declares a swimming afternoon. The water is warm, and so is the mood.

events.name: The island of the lotus
events.nod: The Odyssey: the lotus-eaters
events.text: A small island where the fruit is sweet and everyone who eats it forgets, for a while, that they were going anywhere.
events.check: Wisdom DC 14 for anyone who eats
events.failText: the crew loses half a day lazing on the beach

events.name: The sweet cottage
events.nod: Hansel and Gretel: the gingerbread house
events.text: A cottage with gingerbread walls and sugar windows sits beside the way. A kind old woman at the door waves the party in for tea.
events.twist: She is a retired Church of the Hearth priest who just likes baking. Probably.

events.name: The shortcut that isn't
events.text: A friendly sign points to a shortcut. Under it, a smaller sign reads 'It isn't.' Under that, a smaller one: 'It is, honestly.'
events.twist: The smallest sign is right.

events.name: The gambling ship
events.text: A pleasure barge is moored nearby, lit up and noisy, offering card games, wine and a Church of Trade-blessed table. Stakes are spirit coins.
events.twist: The owner is a Church of the Revels priest who listens to every secret spilled at the tables.
events.check: Insight or Sleight of Hand DC 14

events.name: The singing waterfall
events.text: A waterfall that hums a slow melody as it falls. Anyone who sits beneath it for an hour regains a spent awakening stone ability.

events.name: The cliffside view
events.text: A cliff path opens on a view of {the sea|three valleys|a distant wonder of the world}. The party stops and, for once, just looks.
events.twist: A Church of the Journey pilgrim sitting there shares her flask and a tip about the road.

events.name: The ruins with a guide
events.text: A cheerful local offers a tour of famous ruins just off the route for {a copper|an iron coin|a song} a head. He makes most of it up, but some of it is true.

events.name: The book that must be finished
events.text: A party member picks up a {novel|ship's log|diary} left by a previous traveller and cannot put it down. The last chapter is missing.

events.name: The last chapter
events.text: The missing chapter turns up in an inn's guest book, written by the author, who is the innkeeper. She is delighted anyone read it.

events.name: The glimmer in the deep
events.text: A {golden|silver|pale blue} glimmer far below the clear water. A diver could reach it, if they are quick and brave.
events.twist: It is a merfolk child's lost bracelet, and her family will give a good reward.
events.check: Athletics DC 15

events.name: The far-off music
events.text: Music drifts from somewhere nobody can find. It is a dance tune, and everyone's feet keep wanting to follow the beat.
events.check: Wisdom DC 12 not to dance
events.failText: the party dances half the afternoon away

events.name: A spirit coin rain
events.text: For a few minutes, iron spirit coins rain from a clear sky, pinging off packs and helmets. Then they stop.
events.twist: A sky ship's purser has dropped the payroll, and the crew is on its way down.

events.name: The gift from the tide
events.text: The tide goes out much further than it should, leaving a mile of wet sand, pools full of fish, and a sunken skiff with its cargo still lashed down.

events.name: The pleasure flight
events.text: A sky ship is offering pleasure flights for a bronze coin a head. From above, the land looks small and the road ahead looks short.

events.name: The young admirer
events.text: A young would-be adventurer has heard of the party and follows them, asking questions. They want to know how to reach Iron rank.
events.twist: Their parents would rather they didn't. Their parents are on their way.

events.name: The matchmaker
events.text: A determined matchmaker has decided a party member is perfect for her {nephew|niece|very shy neighbour}. She has a portrait, a list, and no plans to give up.

events.name: The face from a wanted poster
events.text: A stranger stares at one of the party, then pulls a poster from a pocket. It is a drawing of someone who looks exactly like them, wanted in {Vitesse|Rimaros|Yaresh}.

events.name: The lookalike
events.text: The party meets the person from the poster. They look exactly like a party member, and they would like to swap places, just for one day.
events.twist: They are not an imposter. They are a Church of Disguise priest learning a new face.

events.name: The surveyor
events.text: A Magic Society surveyor asks the party to stand very still while she measures the magic around them. She takes a lot of notes, and one look of alarm.
events.twist: Her instruments say one party member is reading as a much higher rank.

events.name: The lost outworlder
events.nod: Newly arrived outworlder: everyday Earth comforts and culture shock
events.text: A lost outworlder, very new, asks the party which way is 'the nearest town with indoor plumbing'. Everything amazes them.

events.name: The outworlder chef
events.nod: An outworlder introducing pizza
events.text: An outworlder is selling something called 'pizza' from a stall. Nobody has bought one, and he is very upset about that.
events.twist: It is delicious. The first person to try one becomes his best customer, and he will not stop sending them pizza.

events.name: The outworlder with a towel
events.nod: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy: always know where your towel is
events.text: An outworlder with a towel over one shoulder explains, at length, why a towel is the most useful thing a traveller can carry.

events.name: The face from the past
events.text: Someone the party knew long ago is coming the other way. They are now {a priest|wealthy|a Bronze-ranker}, and keen to talk about old times.
events.twist: They remember the party owing them money.

events.name: The fan club
events.text: A small group of fans of the party have made badges with the party's faces on. They want autographs, locks of hair, and a speech.
events.twist: One of them is a spy for a rival team, and not a very good one.

events.name: The memoir writer
events.text: A retired Silver-rank adventurer is writing her memoir and wants to read the party a chapter about a surge. It takes {an hour|two hours|the whole evening}.
events.twist: The chapter mentions a hidden cache. She has forgotten she wrote it down.

events.name: The saint's relic
events.text: A Church of the Hero priest stops the party and asks to borrow a party member's weapon to bless it. He says the god pointed it out.

events.name: The relic returned
events.text: The priest returns the weapon, glowing faintly, with a parchment of blessing. The weapon now sheds light on command.

events.name: The portrait painter
events.text: A painter offers to paint the party's portrait for free, but only if they let her paint them exactly as they are. Her last portrait made a {duke|Gold-ranker|whole regiment} cry.

events.name: The runaway noble
events.text: A young noble in borrowed clothes begs to travel with the party for a day. A house steward is searching the roads behind them.
events.twist: The noble is running from an arranged marriage to someone the party knows.

events.name: The petition
events.text: A Church of Truth priest is collecting signatures on a petition to {close the local tavern|honour a dead adventurer|tell the truth about the last surge}.

events.name: The glass of wine
events.text: A stranger raises a glass to the party in an inn, then drops dead before drinking. The wine was poisoned, and he drank someone else's.

events.name: The poisoner's mistake
events.text: A woman stops the party and asks, very politely, who was sitting in the dead man's chair. She is the poisoner, and she is still looking.

events.name: The six-fingered man
events.nod: The Princess Bride: the six-fingered man
events.text: A man with six fingers on his right hand asks the party if they know a swordsman whose father he killed. He seems sorry, but not very.

events.name: The black spot
events.nod: Treasure Island: the black spot
events.text: A sailor with a wooden leg offers a party member a black spot on a scrap of paper, then runs. The crew go silent.

events.name: The old knight's quest
events.nod: Don Quixote: tilting at windmills
events.text: An elderly knight on a tired horse asks the party to help him fight a giant. The giant is a windmill, and the party can decide how to handle it.

events.name: The ghost ship's toast
events.nod: Folklore: the Flying Dutchman
events.text: A ship sails close with all lamps lit and music playing. Its crew raise their glasses to the party. Nobody aboard has a shadow.

events.name: The nervous courier
events.text: A Society courier with a sealed bag asks to travel with the party for safety. He is very nervous, and very bad at hiding it.

events.name: The courier's delivery
events.text: The courier delivers his bag safely and comes back with a reward: a small purse of bronze coins from the grateful Society.

events.name: The fisherman's tall tale
events.text: An old fisherman tells the party about the one that got away. It was {as long as a ship|a talking fish|a merfolk queen}, and it still owes him money.

events.name: The flying carpet ride
events.nod: Arabian Nights: the flying carpet
events.text: A merchant offers rides on his flying carpet for a silver coin. The carpet is real, and it is very old, and it {tilts|sneezes|has opinions}.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 12 to stay on

events.name: The bard who wants a muse
events.nod: D&D: the bard who must be inspired
events.text: A bard needs a muse for his next song and has chosen a party member. He follows them everywhere, writing down everything they say.
events.twist: His song becomes popular, and people start quoting the party's worst moments back at them.

events.name: The hidden prince
events.text: A stable boy confides he is a lost heir to a noble house, and shows a ring to prove it. He wants help getting home.
events.twist: He really is. The reward is a lifetime friend in a noble house.

events.name: The speed-reader
events.text: A Church of Knowledge scholar asks to read every book the party is carrying. She reads them all in {an hour|a minute|one breath}, then asks for more.
events.twist: She has a knowledge essence and remembers everything, including the party's private letters.

events.name: The goblin poet
events.text: A goblin poet asks the party for one {word|secret|colour} each, then writes a poem using them all. It is beautiful, and she gives it away free.

events.name: The debt collector
events.text: A Church of Trade debt collector is taking a widow's {cart|loom|goats} for her dead husband's debts, all quite legal. She asks if the party can spare anything.
events.twist: The husband is not dead. He is two towns away, under a new name.

events.name: Titans fighting
events.text: Two large monsters fighting in the distance.
events.twist: The winner turns toward the road.

events.name: A sky ship
events.text: A sky ship passing low overhead, trailing smoke.

events.name: A Host on the move
events.text: A line of walking houses on the horizon: a Host following the Tide.

events.name: A surge building
events.text: More spawn marks than there should be, animals moving out, the air heavy with magic.

events.name: Cult marks
events.text: A symbol scratched on a milestone, repeated on the next one, and the next.

events.name: Smoke
events.text: Smoke rising from a farmstead over the next rise.

events.name: A god's sign
events.text: A sudden calm, a flock moving in a pattern, and any priest in the party feels watched.

events.name: A thin sky
events.text: For a moment the sky flickers, and something vast seems to look through it.

events.name: Stars in the wrong shape
events.text: For one night, the stars rearrange themselves into the shapes of the party's essences.

events.name: Scarecrows facing the road
events.text: Every scarecrow for three farms has been turned to face the road.

events.name: A comet
events.text: A comet with a green tail. Priests along the road argue about what it means.

events.name: Birds flying the wrong way
events.text: Every bird in the sky is flying the same way, away from where the party is going.

events.name: The burning village
events.text: Smoke on the horizon, far too much for a cookfire. Whatever happened, it's over by the time anyone could get there.

events.name: A greatback on the horizon
events.text: A greatback, a beast the size of a hill, walks slowly along the skyline, a whole town riding on its back.

events.name: A rain of fish
events.text: It rains fish for ten minutes, all of them alive and all of them annoyed.

events.name: Lightning without a storm
events.text: A single bolt of lightning from a clear sky, striking the same tree three times.

events.name: A wonder from afar
events.text: On the horizon, one of the world's wonders is visible for a single hour, impossibly large and impossibly far away.

events.name: A white stag
events.text: A white stag stands in the path, watching the party, then walks into the trees. Anyone who follows finds a shortcut.

events.name: The dark sun
events.text: The sun dims to a dull red disc for an hour at midday, and all the animals go quiet.

events.name: A fleet of sky ships
events.text: A whole fleet of sky ships flying in formation, flying the banners of a noble house at war.

events.name: The wild hunt
events.nod: Folklore: the Wild Hunt
events.text: Riders across the sky at midnight, horns blowing, with hounds of smoke. Anyone who looks up too long hears their own name called.

events.name: Waves without wind
events.text: The sea goes flat as glass, then rises in a long, slow swell with no wind behind it. Something very big has passed underneath.

events.name: The broken moon
events.text: A shadow crosses the moon, and for a moment it looks cracked down the middle.

events.name: Smoke signals
events.text: Smoke signals on the hills, passing a message along a line of peaks. Someone in the party might be able to read them.
events.check: History DC 14 to read them

events.name: The weeping sky
events.text: Grey ash falling like snow. Far away, something is burning that shouldn't be.

events.name: A herd stampedes
events.text: A herd of animals stampedes past the party at a distance, fleeing something in the hills.

events.name: An aurora
events.text: A shimmering green and gold aurora fills the sky. Everyone who watches it sleeps well.

events.name: The vanishing road
events.text: The road ahead fades into fog and comes back a moment later, with a slightly different milestone than before.

events.name: The second sun
events.text: A second, smaller sun rises in the {west|north|south} at noon, crosses half the sky and sets. By evening nobody on the road can agree how long it was there.
events.twist: A Magic Society sky-watcher passing through is furious she missed it.

events.name: A star comes down
events.text: A shooting star falls {just over the next hill|in a field off the road|into the shallows nearby}, still glowing. Whatever landed is warm, heavy and humming.
events.twist: Two Iron-rank teams saw it fall too, and they are already running.

events.name: Stars going out
events.text: One by one, a line of stars winks out across the sky, as if something {long and dark|vast and slow|with wings} is crossing in front of them. They come back an hour later.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to guess what it is
events.twist: When they come back, one of them is missing for good.

events.name: A ring round the moon
events.text: A pale ring round the moon tonight. Every farmer and sailor in earshot says the same thing: bad weather within three days.

events.name: The counting stars
events.text: The stars blink in turn, slowly, like someone counting. Anyone who counts along stops at a number they can't shake off: {seven|thirteen|one hundred and one}.
events.twist: Whoever counted dreams that night of a door with that number on it.

events.name: Red sky at night
events.text: The sunset turns the whole sky a deep, warm red. Any shepherd or sailor will tell the party what that means: a fair day tomorrow. Advantage on tomorrow's Survival check.
events.nod: Folklore: red sky at night, shepherd's delight

events.name: Writing in the clouds
events.text: High clouds form neat lines of script across the sky. Before the wind smears them, someone might make out {a name|a date|half a warning}.
events.check: Arcana or History DC 15 to read it
events.twist: The name is one of the party's, spelt the way their mother says it.

events.name: Lightning, no thunder
events.text: Lightning flickers along the horizon all afternoon, without a single roll of thunder. The storm never arrives, and the {birds stay on the ground|dogs won't stop whining|cows lie down} all day.
events.twist: Where it struck, the grass is fused into a glass flower.

events.name: Stars at noon
events.text: At noon, for a few breaths, the stars show through the blue, sharp and bright. Every essence user in the party feels their mana stir like a held breath.
events.twist: Spells cast in that moment come out stronger than they should, just once.

events.name: The blood moon
events.text: The moon rises huge and red. Locals {bar their doors|bring in the children|nail charms to the gateposts} and say that under a blood moon, everything killed this season walks again.
events.nod: Video games: the Blood Moon from Breath of the Wild
events.twist: Spawn marks along the road look fresh by morning.

events.name: The grimacing moon
events.text: The moon looks bigger tonight, and its craters have settled into a scowling face. Nobody else on the road seems to have noticed.
events.nod: Video games: the falling moon of Majora's Mask
events.twist: An old woman on the road says it happens every hundred years, and the last time, the harvest failed.

events.name: The moon draws closer
events.text: The scowling moon is enormous now, filling a quarter of the sky. At midnight it shrinks back to normal size all at once, as if it has made its point.

events.name: The star that follows
events.text: One bright star stays exactly above the party wherever they go, even when they double back. A priest of the Journey would call it a blessing.
events.twist: It vanishes the moment anyone in the party tells a lie.

events.name: A moonbow
events.text: A pale silver rainbow arches over the road by moonlight. Children in the next village swear it means someone nearby is about to fall in love.
events.twist: Someone in the party gets a love letter at the next inn, unsigned.

events.name: Sunset in the east
events.text: Tonight the sun sets in the east. It rises in the east tomorrow, as normal. Nobody else on the road noticed anything wrong.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to tell which way north really is
events.failText: the party's sense of direction is shaken until morning

events.name: A sky ship burning
events.text: A sky ship burns high overhead, drifting as it falls. It comes down {miles off|beyond the far ridge|far out over the water}, too far to reach in time.
events.twist: Something small and bright breaks away just before the crash: an escape skiff.

events.name: A wish on a falling star
events.text: An outworlder riding with a caravan sees a shooting star and makes everyone stop and wish on it, as people do back home. The guards find this baffling, then lovely.
events.nod: Real-world custom: wishing on a shooting star

events.name: Shapes in the stars
events.text: A lonely outworlder by the fire is naming the strange constellations after things from home. That one is a teapot. That one is a 'motorbike'. He wants the party's help with the rest.
events.nod: Real-world constellations and everyday objects

events.name: The comet's second tail
events.text: A comet has hung low in the sky all week, and overnight it has grown a second tail, pointing the other way. Priests of Knowledge and Truth are already writing furious letters.
events.check: Religion DC 13 to guess which church is right

events.name: Cloud furniture adrift
events.text: A whole set of cloud-built furniture drifts overhead: {a sofa, two chairs and a wardrobe|a four-poster bed|a dining table laid for twelve}, slowly losing shape. Someone in a city is having a very bad day.
events.twist: The wardrobe drifts low enough to open. There's a coat inside, with coins in the pocket.

events.name: The green flash
events.text: As the sun sets, a bright green spark flashes on the horizon for a heartbeat. Sailors say it means a safe crossing.

events.name: Spawn marks in a ring
events.text: Scorched spawn marks form a ring round a milestone, each a day fresher than the last. Tomorrow's will be in the middle.
events.twist: The ring has been growing inwards for twelve days. Day thirteen is today.

events.name: Animals leaving together
events.text: {Deer, foxes and a pair of badgers|Rabbits, stoats and a wild boar|A whole village's cats} cross the road side by side, ignoring each other, all heading out of the region. The magic here is building.
events.twist: A fox stops, looks straight at the party, and seems to wait for them to follow.

events.name: A hail of cores
events.text: A patter of tiny Iron-rank monster cores falls like hail across the road. Something high above has died, or burst.

events.name: The Tide's leavings
events.text: Waist-high grass, glossy and faintly glowing, and the bones of a dozen monsters. The Wandering Tide left this valley days ago. The question is where it went.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to read which way the Tide moved

events.name: The beacon on the hill
events.text: A Society warning beacon blazes on a {hill|tower|clifftop} ahead: a surge is rising nearby. Every village on the road is shuttering its windows.
events.twist: The beacon keeper is missing, and the fire was lit by someone else.

events.name: The monitor stone
events.text: A Magic Society monitoring pillar stands by the road, its glass eye glowing {amber|deep red|a colour nobody has a name for}. A clerk's note is nailed beneath it.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to read what it is measuring
events.twist: The note reads: 'If red, send word. If any other colour, run.'

events.name: Watching a spawn
events.text: Across a field the air shimmers, thickens and folds into a {wolf|boar|long-legged bird}, newborn and blinking. It shakes itself and trots away without noticing the party.

events.name: Birds that won't land
events.text: Thousands of birds circle a patch of woodland, and none will land in it. The trees below are perfectly still, even in the wind.
events.twist: That patch is a natural array, and it is close to spawning something big.

events.name: A shape on the skyline
events.text: Far off, something the size of a hill rolls over in its sleep, throwing up dust and a cloud of birds. Locals call it a legend. It is very, very far away.
events.nod: D&D: the tarrasque

events.name: The beckoning arm
events.text: A single tentacle, thick as a ship's mast, rises from the water a mile off. It curls once, like a beckoning finger, and sinks without a ripple.
events.nod: Myth: the kraken

events.name: Monsters walking past
events.text: A long line of Bronze-rank monsters plods {north|towards the coast|uphill}, ignoring the party completely. Whatever they are walking to, they want it more than food.
events.twist: At the head of the line walks a single human child, perfectly calm.

events.name: Cocoons on the wall
events.text: Pale sacs hang from {the trees|a rock face|a ruined wall}, each with something curled inside and twitching. Burning them takes an hour. Leaving them means someone else meets what hatches.
events.twist: One of the cocoons holds a person, still breathing.

events.name: The singing glass
events.text: Dunes fused into glass ring like bells when the wind crosses them, playing the same {three notes|sad little tune|rising scale} over and over. It is getting faster.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to hear which dunes are hollow

events.name: Children on the carcass
events.text: A huge dead monster lies across a field, and the village children are climbing all over it. A Society clerk is trying to shoo them off and measure it at the same time.

events.name: Gold-rankers at work
events.text: Light flashes beyond the horizon and, seconds later, the ground shivers. Somewhere miles off, Gold-rankers are fighting something. Anyone sensible gives it a wide berth.
events.twist: By evening a column of smoke marks the spot, and the Society wants witnesses.

events.name: Glowing puddles
events.text: Every puddle along the road glows faintly {blue|green|violet}, and the frogs in them are twice the size they should be. An old farmer is counting on her fingers and muttering about the last surge.

events.name: The quiet spawn field
events.text: A meadow pitted with old, cold spawn marks. Whatever this field used to make, the Society cleared it long ago, and the grass has grown back.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to find what the Society missed

events.name: The leviathan's back
events.text: What looked like an island rises, sheds a waterfall, and sinks again. The sailors fall silent, and the oldest one throws a silver spirit coin over the side.

events.name: Feathers on the wind
events.text: Bright red feathers as long as a man's arm drift down all morning. Each one is warm to the touch and smells faintly of cinnamon.
events.twist: A Magic Society buyer in the next town pays well for them, and asks where they fell.

events.name: The sated monster
events.text: A Silver-rank {bear-thing|great lizard|six-legged cat} sleeps belly-up in the sun beside the road, snoring, surrounded by the bones of its last meal. A sign propped against it says 'do not'.
events.twist: The sign is signed by a Society clerk, and the monster is wearing a collar.

events.name: The Tide-reader's warning
events.text: A Hostfolk tide-reader, riding alone, stops to warn the party that the Tide is pooling {ahead|behind them|right here} and will turn into a surge if it lingers.

events.name: The snuffed candles
events.text: Every candle in a roadside shrine of Death has gone out at once, and the smoke hangs in the air without drifting. Someone nearby is about to die.
events.twist: It is the shrine's keeper, who is very calm about it and asks for company.

events.name: The white flame
events.text: A white flame inside a ring is painted fresh on every door in the next hamlet. Purity's preachers came through last week. Two houses have no doors at all now.

events.name: The Healer's leaf
events.text: A green leaf drifts down and settles on the most badly hurt member of the party. Their wounds ache a little less all day. Nobody can see a tree nearby.
events.twist: Anyone who keeps the leaf finds it still fresh a month later.

events.name: A flock in the shape of a road
events.text: Starlings wheel overhead and, for a breath, form a winding road beneath a star: the Journey's sign. The way ahead feels easier. Advantage on tomorrow's Survival check.

events.name: The shrine that sweats
events.text: A stone shrine of the {church} is beaded with water on a dry day. The droplets run upwards.
events.check: Religion DC 13 to read the sign
events.failText: it means nothing to the party

events.name: Scales in the sky
events.text: Two clouds hang perfectly level, like the pans of a balance, with a thin line between them. A passing priest of Justice turns pale and turns back the way she came.

events.name: The broken shackle
events.text: Someone has hammered a broken shackle to a signpost, Liberty's sign, with a note in chalk: 'Safe house, two miles, knock twice.' The chalk is fresh.
events.twist: The sign is a trap set by slavers, or it isn't. Only a visit will tell.

events.name: The Storm god's anvil
events.text: A single great cloud towers over the sea, flat-topped like an anvil, lit from within. Sailors {touch their foreheads|pour out a cup of rum|tie a knot in a rope} and say the Storm is watching today.
events.twist: By evening the cloud has drifted after the ship, all on its own.

events.name: Spears in the field
events.text: Hundreds of old spears stand point-down in a field, rusted and wreathed in poppies. A priest of War tends them, one by one, and asks the party's names.

events.name: The overflowing cup
events.text: A {fountain|village pump|holy well} in a crossroads village has started flowing with wine instead of water. The Revels' priest is delighted. The village elders are not.

events.name: The god's eye opens
events.text: An open book with an eye on its page is carved into a cliff face, and the eye was closed yesterday, according to the carter behind the party.
events.check: Religion DC 13 to know what Knowledge's eye means
events.twist: Yesterday it was closed because nobody was coming. Today, the carter says, someone is.

events.name: The hearth smoke
events.text: Smoke from every chimney in the valley rises and leans the same way, towards one small farmhouse. A Hearth priest would say someone there needs visitors.

events.name: The ground hums
events.text: The ground underfoot hums a low note, like a hand on a great drum. Priests of the Earth say the land sings when it is pleased, or when it is about to move.
events.twist: By dusk, a new spring has opened beside the road.

events.name: The hero's crown
events.text: A crown of leaves sits on a stone at the roadside, untouched by weather, with a sword-shaped gap in the moss before it. Whoever wears it for a day feels braver.
events.twist: A Hero priest arrives at dusk, looking for whoever took it.

events.name: The coins that land upright
events.text: Every spirit coin the party {pays out|drops|tosses} today lands on its edge. A Trade priest in the next town takes it very seriously and asks to see the party's accounts.

events.name: A tide that comes in wrong
events.text: The tide comes in fast, far further than it should, and stops at a line of {shells|bones|old spirit coins} laid on the sand. The Ocean is drawing a boundary.
events.twist: Something has been buried inside the line of shells, and the sea is guarding it.

events.name: The ruined temple glows
events.text: At dusk the empty windows of a ruined temple fill with light, and {a choir sings|a bell tolls|someone laughs} inside. Anyone who goes in finds bare stone and silence.
events.twist: The singing starts again the moment they leave.

events.name: Faces in the crowd
events.text: Three times today the party sees the same stranger in different places, wearing a different face each time. Disguise's faithful leave a mark like this when someone is being watched.

events.name: A skull with a flower
events.text: A skull crowned with a living flower sits on a fence post, Undeath's sign, in country where that church is hunted. The flower is still blooming.
events.twist: Locals pretend not to see it, and lower their voices when the party asks.

events.name: The shattered statue
events.text: A statue of a {noble|saint|forgotten hero} has been smashed overnight, the pieces arranged in a neat circle. Destruction's faithful do this when they think something should end.

events.name: The sky goes still
events.text: A sudden calm. Every bird lands at once, the wind drops, and a priest in the party hears their god clear their throat, as if about to speak, and then not.
events.twist: Whatever the god meant to say, the next temple's priest says it to them instead.

events.name: An avatar passing
events.text: A figure of light walks across the far hills, as tall as the trees, and is gone. Priests of the {church} spend the next week arguing about whether it was theirs.

events.name: A crack in the air
events.text: A hairline crack hangs in the air at head height, a hand's width long. Behind it is dark, and stars, and something that blinks.
events.twist: By the next morning the crack is gone, and so are the stars behind it.

events.name: A scent of springtime
events.text: The air smells of fresh flowers and spring rain, though it is {midwinter|the dead of summer|raining mud}. Someone has arrived from another world nearby.

events.name: The new arrival
events.text: The smell of spring leads to a frightened outworlder hiding in a {barn|hollow tree|beached boat}. They speak no local language and have never seen magic before.

events.name: The phoenix wing
events.text: At dawn, a wing of fire the width of the sky sweeps once across the horizon and fades. Sailors and adventurers alike say a word to the World-Phoenix, just in case.

events.name: A door on the hillside
events.text: A door frame stands alone on a {hillside|beach|patch of scrub}, no wall, no house. Through it, the view is of somewhere else entirely, at night.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to tell it is an astral space entrance
events.twist: The Society has no record of it, so whoever reports it first claims it.

events.name: The second shadow
events.text: In the late afternoon light, everyone in the party casts two shadows. The second one is {a little slow to follow|facing the wrong way|holding something}.
events.twist: It fades by sunset, except for one person's, which fades at midnight.

events.name: Things the Builder left
events.text: Tiny, perfect cubes of grey stone are scattered across the {road|beach|scrub}, each one etched with lines like a city plan. The Magic Society tells people to break them.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to know what they are

events.name: The sky is thin
events.text: Patches of the sky look like old cloth, worn thin. Through the thinnest patch, very faintly, the party can see the bottom of a sea that isn't there.
events.twist: A shadow of something enormous swims across that faraway sea floor.

events.name: The light on the water
events.text: A column of soft light stands on the {road|water|hillside} ahead, rising straight into the sky, and is gone by the time anyone gets there. Something useful lies where it stood.
events.nod: Video games: loot beams marking a drop

events.name: The ticking hour
events.text: For an hour, everyone in the party hears a clock ticking, though nobody carries one. Some say the Keeper of Moments counts time out loud before it does something to it.
events.twist: When the ticking stops, everyone's water flask is a little emptier than it should be.

events.name: A Messenger's feather
events.text: A long white feather lies on the road, too clean, and it sings very quietly when touched. Anyone who knows the stories knows what a Messenger is, and that it wants something.

events.name: The star with an echo
events.text: A new star has appeared, low on the horizon. An outworlder in the party's last inn said, crossly, that it was 'just a satellite', and nobody has stopped asking what that means.

events.name: Rain falling up
events.text: A light rain falls upwards from the {grass|road|riverbank} for ten minutes, soaking everyone from the boots up.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to trace the magic
events.twist: Overhead, the raindrops collect into a little cloud that follows the party home.

events.name: The broken horizon
events.text: Out at sea, the horizon is cut clean in two: on one side, a calm noon; on the other, a storm-lit night. The ship sails along the seam for an hour.
events.check: Navigation DC 15 to ride the seam

events.name: The astral bloom
events.text: Flowers the colour of starlight open all at once along the roadside, chime softly, then close. The local children call them door-flowers and won't touch them.
events.twist: Where they grow thickest, an astral space has a door that nobody has found.

events.name: The tired outworlder
events.text: An outworlder sits by a milestone, glaring at the night sky. 'Nope,' they say, to nobody. 'Still none I know.' They have checked every night for a year, just in case.

events.name: Footprints of light
events.text: Glowing {footprints|hoofprints|claw marks} cross the road, each one bigger than a cart, and fade within minutes. They come from nowhere and go nowhere.

events.name: The Celestine's halo
events.text: A Celestine shepherd stands in a field, and for a moment a faint light rings her head. She looks embarrassed. 'It does that before bad weather,' she says.

events.name: A rip in the fog
events.text: The fog tears open like a curtain, showing a glimpse of a place with a {purple sky|green sun|sky full of moons} and very tall, thin people looking back. Then it closes.

events.name: Eye of the sky
events.text: Clouds swirl into a vast, slow spiral directly overhead, with a dark pupil at the centre. Nobody on the road will look at it, and dogs howl until it clears.
events.twist: Scholars name a being that only consumes. The Magic Society would want to hear about this.

events.name: The glow of the Thunderveil
events.text: Far off, a glow rises above the hills all night: the mist of a great waterfall, so thick with magic it shines. Travellers who see it say their dreams are clearer.

events.name: A greatback herd
events.text: A herd of wild greatbacks crosses the {plain|valley|dry riverbed}, each the size of a barn. Any Hostfolk would pay well to know where they went.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to note their path and numbers

events.name: The Red Heart at sunset
events.text: On the far horizon a red stone monolith catches the last light and glows like an ember. The whole desert goes quiet while it burns.

events.name: The mirror lake
events.text: A salt lake so still it reflects the sky exactly. The reflection is {a few minutes behind|a few minutes ahead|of a different season}, and nobody can stop staring.
events.twist: In the reflection, the party is one person larger.

events.name: Sky ships in a race
events.text: Three sky ships race overhead, close enough to hear the crews shouting insults. One drops a bottle of wine, which lands, unbroken, at the party's feet.

events.name: A wandering island
events.text: An island with a lighthouse sits where the charts show open water. By evening it has drifted a mile further {north|east|out to sea}.
events.check: Navigation or Survival DC 13 to fix the ship's position against it

events.name: Condors over the peaks
events.text: Huge condor-like birds circle the peaks, and one carries a rider who waves. Cloud Clan riders only wave at people they think are worth knowing.

events.name: Smoke from the fire mountain
events.text: A mountain on the horizon wears a crown of storm cloud, lit red from beneath. Ash speckles everything by noon, and the water tastes of sulphur.
events.twist: Locals say the mountain is restless this year, and the fish have gone deep.

events.name: The walking town
events.text: A Host is on the move: a line of greatbacks with round tents on their backs, stretching to the horizon, riders flanking them like dust devils.
events.twist: A Khan's herald rides over to ask the party's ranks, and judges the answer.

events.name: The canyon's breath
events.text: Warm wind rises out of a deep red canyon in long, slow breaths, in and out, {every minute|in time with the party's walking|faster when anyone shouts}. Nobody has seen its lungs.
events.twist: On the in-breath, very faintly, there is a voice.

events.name: A storm cloud for a mountain
events.text: Clouds stack themselves into a peak taller than any mountain, with a Cloud Clan village clinging to its side. By the time anyone points, the wind has taken it.

events.name: The flying whales
events.text: A pod of sky-whales swims through the clouds, singing low enough to rattle teeth. Some sailors say good luck. Others say they are fleeing something.
events.twist: Hours later, the clouds behind them turn dark and move against the wind.

events.name: A battle on the horizon
events.text: Banners on the skyline: two noble houses' levies drawn up across a valley, too far off to hear. By the time the party is near, it will be over one way or another.

events.name: The reef from above
events.text: The water turns clear as glass over a reef bright with coral and fish of every colour. {The crew stop work to look|A merfolk family waves from below|A turtle the size of a boat drifts past}.

events.name: A wonder in the mirage
events.text: The heat shimmer pulls a far-off wonder close: {a waterfall a mile wide|a forest of flattened trees round a crater|a black island of towers}, hanging above the horizon for an hour.

events.name: The glacier's voice
events.text: Somewhere ahead, ice groans like an animal in pain, for minutes at a time. The guides go quiet and walk faster.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to stay off the bad ice

events.name: A floating village
events.text: A fishing village floats on rafts in a bay of limestone islands, and the whole village is slowly rowing itself {north|out to sea|towards the party}.

events.name: The heidel stampede
events.text: A herd of {heidels|wild goats|horses} thunders past at a distance, dust rising behind them. Whatever spooked them is behind the next ridge.

events.name: The banners of a war fleet
events.text: Sails crowd the horizon: a Storm Kingdom war fleet heading {south|for the islands|towards the coast}. Merchants in the next port would pay for the news.
events.check: Insight or History DC 13 to recognise the flagship

events.name: The fox that waits
events.text: A red fox sits at every fork in the road, always the same fox, always looking down the right path. Following it saves time.

events.name: Crows counting the party
events.text: A line of crows on a fence turn their heads, one by one, to follow each member of the party. When the last one has passed, they fly away together.
events.twist: A pair of them follows the party for days, always within sight.

events.name: Magpies in sevens
events.text: Seven magpies line the road. An old woman by her gate starts the counting rhyme and stops at seven, refusing to say what it means.

events.name: Apple blossom in winter
events.text: {An orchard|An old hedge|A village green} has burst into blossom out of season, every branch white and humming with bees. The farmer has no idea why and is handing out cider.

events.name: The fish swim upstream all at once
events.text: The river is suddenly thick with fish, packed shoulder to shoulder, all swimming upstream {in total silence|in perfect rows|on their backs}.

events.name: Flowers that face the party
events.text: Every {flower in the meadow|sunflower in the field|weed along the verge} turns to face the party as they pass, and turns back after.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to tell it's a dryad's doing
events.twist: One flower bows. It is in the party's way, and it will not be picked.

events.name: The dead tree in bloom
events.text: A tree struck dead by lightning years ago is covered in flowers made of pale blue fire. They don't burn. A child at the next farm says they come every hundred days.

events.name: Frogs in chorus
events.text: The marsh frogs sing, in clear and perfect harmony, {the same short tune|a hymn of the Revels|a sailor's song} over and over. Someone will be humming it for a week.

events.name: A white hart at dusk
events.text: A white hart stands in the mist at dusk, then lowers its antlers to one member of the party and is gone. Old tales say it chooses a hero, or a quarry.
events.nod: Arthurian legend: the white hart

events.name: A path of mushrooms
events.text: A ring of mushrooms has grown overnight around the camp, and a second ring outside that, and a third. Someone should count them before breakfast.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to tell whether it's safe to step out

events.name: The bees swarm the party
events.text: A swarm of bees settles on the party's {tallest member|loudest member|least favourite pack mule} and refuses to leave. They don't sting. They simply live there now, until dusk.

events.name: The mountain goat's path
events.text: A mountain goat skips up a cliff the party were about to walk round. Its path is just about passable for anyone with sense and a rope.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to follow it

events.name: Grass growing in the road
events.text: {Grass|Wildflowers|Young saplings} grow thick and green down the middle of a road that saw carts this morning. The ruts are already gone.
events.twist: In the middle of the new grass, somebody's lost boot, still warm.

events.name: The stones moved
events.text: A row of standing stones by the road has moved since anyone last looked: the locals swear they used to be on the other side of the hill.
events.check: History DC 15 to know where they used to stand
events.twist: The stones are walking towards the nearest town, about a yard a year.

events.name: Snakes in a line
events.text: Dozens of {snakes|lizards|giant centipedes} cross the path in single file, nose to tail, in a line that takes ten minutes to pass. They don't look at anyone.
events.check: Nature DC 15 to know what they are fleeing

events.name: The singing well
events.text: A village well is {singing|humming|whistling}, softly, a lullaby nobody in the village knows. The children sleep better than they have in years.

events.name: The weeping willow
events.text: A willow on the bank drips red sap into the water, and the water downstream runs pink for a mile.
events.twist: The roots wrap round an old Iron-rank badge, and a name scratched into it.

events.name: The cactus flowers
events.text: Every cactus for a mile has flowered at once, and the flowers are full of sweet water. Nobody goes thirsty today, and the packs fill up.

events.name: Rain of petals
events.text: A warm wind brings a shower of {pink petals|golden leaves|white blossom} from a forest nobody can see. Everyone on the road stops to laugh at it.

events.name: Wolves howling in daylight
events.text: {Wolves|Hounds|Something that sounds like wolves} howl from every direction at midday, all at once, and then go silent. No animal is seen all day.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to tell they were calling, not hunting
events.twist: That night, one wolf sits at the edge of the firelight and simply watches.

events.name: The beetle procession
events.text: A procession of large {black beetles|red ants|glass-winged crickets} crosses the road carrying a single bright gemstone between them. They will not be distracted.
events.check: Sleight of Hand DC 15 to take the gem without starting a war

events.name: Gulls following the ship
events.text: A cloud of {gulls|terns|black-headed skuas} follows the ship, diving at the wake. Where they go, there are fish: the cook is delighted.

events.name: Seals watching
events.text: A dozen {seals|otters|dolphins} bob in the water, watching the party with dark, human eyes. One of them waves, very slowly.
events.nod: Folklore: selkies

events.name: Ravens and a feast
