events.text: Ravens over a hillside, hundreds of them. Something big died up there, or something small died in great numbers.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to tell which, from a safe distance
events.twist: It was a Silver-rank monster, and its core is still in it. Something else wants it too.

events.name: Ribbons on every branch
events.text: Thousands of {red|black|white} ribbons hang from every branch and rope for a mile, tied in the same knot. Nobody saw who tied them.
events.check: History or Religion DC 13 to know what the knot means
events.failText: the knot means nothing to anyone

events.name: The lit beacons
events.text: Beacons flare one after another along a line of peaks, passing a call for help faster than any rider. Somebody, somewhere, is calling for aid.
events.nod: The Lord of the Rings: the beacons calling for aid
events.check: History DC 13 to know which way the call is going

events.name: Bells without ringers
events.text: Every bell for miles rings once at the same moment: {temple bells|cowbells|a ship's bell far off}. Then silence.
events.check: Religion DC 13 to know what a single stroke means
events.failText: nobody can agree, and everyone sleeps badly

events.name: The keening
events.text: A woman's wail rises from {the reeds|an empty cottage|the rocks below the cliff}, long and high, and there is no woman there. Old folk say someone nearby has hours left.
events.nod: Irish folklore: the banshee
events.check: Medicine or Insight DC 13 to work out who

events.name: A ghost ship
events.text: A ship under full sail glides past against the wind, crew on deck, lamps lit, without a sound. It passes straight through a sandbar.
events.nod: Folklore: the Flying Dutchman

events.name: The ghost ship returns
events.text: The silent ship comes back alongside, close enough to touch. Its captain lifts a hand and points the way to a safe current.

events.name: A one-eyed traveller
events.text: An old man with one eye, a broad hat and a staff watches the party pass. He asks one hard question, and nods at the answer either way.
events.nod: Norse myth: the one-eyed wanderer
events.check: Insight DC 15 to see he is more than he seems

events.name: Lanterns in the marsh
events.text: Little blue lights bob over the marsh, always a few yards ahead, always leading off the path. Following them is a very bad idea.
events.nod: Folklore: will-o'-the-wisps
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 save to resist following
events.failText: someone wanders off and the party loses an hour fetching them back

events.name: A black dog at the crossroads
events.text: A huge black dog with eyes like coals sits at a crossroads and watches the party go by. Every local spits and makes a sign.
events.nod: English folklore: the black dog of the crossroads

events.name: The black dog again
events.text: The black dog is waiting again. This time it walks with the party all day, and nothing comes near. At dusk it simply isn't there.

events.name: A red banner in the dark
events.text: A banner of some noble house hangs from nothing over the road, rippling in a wind that isn't blowing. It shows a house that died out a century ago.
events.check: History DC 15 to name the house

events.name: The dead house's heir
events.text: A {farmer|tinker|ferry-woman} at the next town has the dead house's crest tattooed on their wrist and very much does not want to talk about it.

events.name: The weather vane points
events.text: Every {weather vane|cockerel|church spire's flag} in a village points straight at the party as they pass, and swings back after.
events.check: Insight DC 10 to notice the villagers aren't surprised

events.name: Chalk marks by the door
events.text: Chalk signs on doorposts all through a village: {a circle|a cross|two lines}. Travellers' cant, if anyone can read it.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to read the cant

events.name: The milestone counts down
events.text: The milestones go 10, 9, 8, all the way down, but there is no town marked on the map. Something is at zero.
events.check: History DC 13 to know what used to be there

events.name: Milestone zero
events.text: Milestone zero stands in an empty meadow. When the party touches it, a whole town flickers into being for one breath, full of people looking up, then fades.

events.name: The sea goes red
events.text: The water around the ship turns red as far as the eye can see. It is only a bloom of tiny creatures, probably.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to know it is harmless
events.failText: nobody aboard eats fish for a week

events.name: The singing on the rocks
events.text: Sweet singing drifts from a rocky island. The sailors stuff wax in their ears without being asked, and look at the party to see if they will.
events.nod: Greek myth: the sirens
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 save for anyone listening
events.failText: someone has to be held back from the rail

events.name: Fog with faces
events.text: The fog thickens and, for a moment, a face as big as a house forms in it, looks at {the party|the youngest of them|the party's pack animals}, and drifts on.
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 save or be frightened until the fog lifts
events.twist: Whoever it looked at has a nosebleed at sunset.

events.name: St Elmo's fire
events.text: Blue fire flickers along the {mast|spear tips|tent poles}, harmless and cold. Sailors cheer: a sign the storm will spare them.

events.name: The magic squall's colours
events.text: The loose magic in the air paints the sky in bands of {violet|green|gold}. Every spell the party casts today leaves a trail of that colour.

events.name: A storm that stays put
events.text: One small storm cloud hangs over a single field, raining on it all day. The farmer, dry three yards away, has started charging to look.
events.cost: 1 iron spirit coin a head to look
events.twist: The farmer swears the cloud followed him home from a fair.

events.name: Hailstones with something inside
events.text: Hail as big as eggs. Each one, when it melts, leaves a tiny {fish|key|seed} behind.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to work out where it came from

events.name: Snow in summer
events.text: Fat snowflakes fall from a clear summer sky and melt on contact. Each one tastes faintly of {mint|honey|woodsmoke}.
events.twist: A Hearth priest in the next village says it means a birth, and she is right.

events.name: The whirlwind's dance
events.text: A dust devil dances alongside the party for a mile, picking up {leaves|sand|someone's hat} and putting them down very carefully.

events.name: The storm in a bottle
events.text: Lightning hits the sea beside the boat, and a glass float bobs up with a tiny storm swirling inside it. The Magic Society would want this.

events.name: Ball lightning
events.text: A ball of lightning the size of a head drifts gently down the road towards the party, pauses to inspect someone's sword, and floats away.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 save to stay calm and still
events.failText: it zaps the first person who flinches for 1d6 lightning

events.name: A wind that whispers names
events.text: The wind through the reeds and rigging carries whispers, and on every gust someone hears their own name. By dusk, they're sure it's coming from ahead.
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 save to shake it off
events.failText: that person has disadvantage on Perception until they sleep

events.name: Rainbow pool
events.text: At the foot of a bright double rainbow, a little pool of oily colours sits on the ground. It's raw mana, and anyone with a vial can collect some.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to bottle it safely

events.name: Green lightning
events.text: Lightning comes down {green|gold|white as milk}, and wherever it strikes, grass and flowers spring up in seconds.
events.twist: One strike leaves a ring of flowers around a buried chest.

events.name: The calm before
events.text: The air goes heavy and still, the birds stop and the light turns yellow. Anyone who has lived outside knows: shelter now, or get soaked within the hour.
events.check: Survival DC 10 to find shelter in time
events.failText: everyone is soaked through and miserable

events.name: The water rings
events.text: Perfect rings spread across the water from a point where nothing has fallen, one every few heartbeats, like a {slow pulse|clock|knock at a door}.
events.check: Perception DC 15 to see what's below
events.twist: It is a sleeping merfolk sentinel's heartbeat, magnified. She wakes as the party passes.

events.name: Cold breath in the heat
events.text: In the middle of the hottest hour, everyone's breath fogs. The cold lasts a minute and leaves frost on one person's shoulder, shaped like a hand.
events.check: Religion DC 13 to recognise a Death omen

events.name: The upside-down reflection
events.text: In every puddle and pond today, the party's reflections are upside down, and a beat late.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to find the source
events.twist: The source is a cursed coin in someone's purse, picked up as change last week.

events.name: Sails on the horizon at dawn
events.text: At dawn, the sails of {a merfolk trading convoy|a pirate squadron|a Church of the Ocean pilgrim ship} sit on the horizon, holding still as if waiting for someone.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to make out who they are

events.name: Thunder like words
events.text: The thunder rolls in long, deliberate phrases, almost speech. A Storm priest in the party, if there is one, understands three words: 'not yet, child.'
events.check: Religion DC 15 to understand any of it

events.name: The thunderbird
events.text: A bird with wings like thunderheads crosses the sky, lightning crackling between its feathers. It doesn't land, and the rain follows wherever it flies.
events.nod: Native American myth: the thunderbird

events.name: Fireflies spelling
events.text: Fireflies gather into glowing shapes over the grass. They are definitely spelling something, but very badly. It might be a warning, or a rude word.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to work it out
events.twist: It's a rude word, aimed at the party's least popular member.

events.name: Frost flowers
events.text: Frost forms ferns and roses on every surface overnight, so perfect that the whole camp stops to look before packing up.

events.name: Hot rain
events.text: Rain falls warm as bathwater all morning. The road steams, the locals strip to their shirts, and {someone sets up a laundry line|the children dance in it|a Revels priest starts a party}.
events.twist: Anyone with a cold or a cough is cured of it by noon.

events.name: Sunbeams in a row
events.text: Through a break in the clouds, sunbeams stand in a long row like pillars, lighting the way ahead. It's easier to keep the right road.

events.name: The wind turns round
events.text: The wind swings round and blows exactly the opposite way for an hour, then back. Sailors call it the Storm's breath and hold the sails still.
events.check: Navigation or Athletics DC 13 to use the turn

events.name: Dust in the shape of riders
events.text: A dust storm on the horizon shapes itself into galloping riders, a whole Host of them, {and then falls apart into ordinary sand|and charges straight at the party before falling apart|and bows once before it scatters}.
events.check: History DC 13 to recall the Host that died here

events.name: A cairn of coins
events.text: A roadside cairn bristles with iron spirit coins pushed into its cracks, a traveller's offering for luck. A note invites anyone in need to take one and leave a story.

events.name: The cairn keeper
events.text: {A goblin|A Leonid|An elderly elf} in a Journey priest's robe catches up, panting, and wants to know whether the party left a story at the cairn, and whether it was a good one.

events.name: A swollen crossing
events.text: A river or channel in flood. Cross with a DC 13 Athletics check, or lose half a day going around.

events.name: The way is blocked
events.text: A rockslide, a fallen bridge or a washed-out road. Clearing it or finding a way round costs half a day.

events.name: A breakdown
events.text: A lame mount, a broken wheel or a holed boat. Fix it with the right tools or a DC 12 check, or lose the day.

events.name: Spoiled stores
events.text: Bad water or spoiled food. Everyone who ate makes a DC 12 Constitution save or is poisoned until the next long rest.

events.name: Thieving pests
events.text: Something small and fast gets into the packs overnight.

events.name: Sinking ground
events.text: Sinking mud, quicksand or a hidden crevasse. The front of the line makes a DC 13 Dexterity save.

events.name: Supplies lost
events.text: A pack animal bolts, or a bag goes over the side, with food in it.

events.name: Exposure
events.text: Extreme heat or cold. Anyone unprepared makes a DC 12 Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.

events.name: A hornet nest
events.text: Somebody's pack knocks a monster hornet nest out of a tree. Everyone runs, and each person makes a DC 12 Dexterity save or takes 1d6 poison damage.

events.name: A rotten bridge
events.text: Planks are missing from the middle of the only bridge, and the rest creak. A DC 13 Acrobatics check gets each person over; otherwise it's half a day to find a ford.

events.name: Biting insects
events.text: A cloud of biting flies follows the party all day. Everyone has disadvantage on Concentration checks until nightfall.

events.name: Rockfall
events.text: Rocks come down from above. DC 13 Dexterity save or take 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

events.name: The ghost fire
events.text: The campfire burns blue and gives no heat. Nobody warms up until dawn, and the morning starts with a DC 11 Constitution save against a level of exhaustion.

events.name: A spoiled pack
events.text: Rot in the food pack. Half the rations are ruined.

events.name: The mirage lake
events.text: A shimmering lake on the horizon that stays exactly as far away all day. Anyone who follows it loses the way: disadvantage on tomorrow's Survival check unless someone makes a DC 13 Wisdom save.

events.name: Thin ice
events.text: A frozen lake to cross. DC 12 Survival to find the safe path, or someone goes through the ice.

events.name: Squall
events.text: A sudden squall hits the boat. DC 13 Athletics to keep the sails, or lose half a day's distance.

events.name: Wild magic field
events.text: Leftover magic from an old battle. Any spell cast here rolls on a wild magic table.

events.name: A landslide in the rain
events.text: The rain loosens a whole slope. The road ahead is buried, and the way round costs half a day.

events.name: Slipping cargo
events.text: A badly tied load slips at the worst possible moment. Somebody has to chase a rolling barrel down a hill.

events.name: Sandstorm
events.text: A sandstorm blows in. Hunker down for half a day, or press on at disadvantage on Survival.

events.name: Poison thorns
events.text: The path runs through thorn bushes with a mild poison. Everyone makes a DC 11 Constitution save or is poisoned for an hour.

events.name: Lost in the reeds
events.text: Every channel in the reeds looks the same, and the sun is hidden. Make the next Survival check at disadvantage.

events.name: A sprained ankle
events.text: A hidden hole, a twisted ankle. One party member moves at half speed until they rest, unless healed.

events.name: Stinging jellyfish
events.text: The shallows are full of jellyfish. Wading through costs 1d4 poison damage each, or half a day going round.

events.name: A flash flood
events.text: A wall of brown water roars down a dry gully. DC 14 Athletics to get the packs clear, or lose a day of food.

events.name: The road that loops
events.text: The road is enchanted and comes back to the same milestone three times. Breaking the loop takes a DC 14 Arcana check, or half a day.
events.check: Arcana DC 14
events.failText: the party walks the loop until sunset

events.name: Monster-shed spines
events.text: A monster's moulted spines carpet the path, still sharp. Someone treads on one and hops for the rest of the day.

events.name: The washed-out road
events.text: Last night's rain has carried away a stretch of road, leaving a muddy gully {waist-deep|chest-deep|full of floating fence posts}. Wade it, or lose half a day going round.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: someone slips and the party has to fish out a pack, then go round anyway

events.name: A cracked ledge
events.text: The mountain path narrows to a ledge with a long crack along it, and {a goat's skull|a snapped rope|a Society warning flag} sits at the near end. It might hold. It might not.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 for each person crossing
events.failText: the ledge gives way under someone: 2d6 bludgeoning damage and a long climb back up

events.name: The rope bridge
events.text: A Cloud Clan rope bridge across a gorge, with three planks missing and a fresh notch in one rope. A dropped boot lies on the near side.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13, or an hour making it safe
events.failText: a plank snaps, and someone dangles over the drop until hauled up

events.name: Scree slope
events.text: Loose stone the size of {fists|heads|cartwheels} covers the slope. Every step slides. Someone is going to reach the bottom faster than they planned.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save for each person
events.failText: they ride the scree down for 1d6 bludgeoning damage and a lot of bruises

events.name: The bog road
events.text: The causeway through the marsh has sunk overnight, and the planks now lie {a foot|knee-deep|waist-deep} under black water. Feel the way with a pole, or wait for the water to drop.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to find the planks
events.failText: the party waits half a day on a hummock

events.name: The ground opens
events.text: With a soft sigh, a sinkhole opens a few yards ahead, perfectly round. Far below, something glints. The edges are still crumbling.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 save for the front of the line
events.failText: they go in up to the waist and have to be hauled out, losing a pack

events.name: The landslide's leftovers
events.text: A fresh landslide has buried the road, and a hand sticks out of the rubble. It is cold. There was a cart here.
events.twist: Under the cart is a strongbox and a ledger that names its owner.

events.name: A frozen pass
events.text: Ice glazes the pass from wall to wall. Cut steps, rope up, and go slowly, or turn back and try the long way.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 for the leader to cut the steps
events.failText: the party gives up and goes the long way round

events.name: Ankle-breaker field
events.text: A meadow riddled with {burrow holes|old post holes|monster tunnels}, hidden in long grass. Walk slowly or risk an ankle.
events.check: Perception DC 12 to pick a path
events.failText: one person twists an ankle and moves at half speed until healed

events.name: The bridge of three questions
events.text: A narrow bridge over a gorge, guarded by an old man who asks each traveller three questions. Wrong answers mean a swim. He is very particular about birds.
events.nod: Monty Python and the Holy Grail: the Bridge of Death
events.check: Intelligence DC 13 for each crosser
events.failText: that traveller is pitched into the river below and fished out downstream, soaked
events.twist: Anyone who answers all three gets told the bridge keeper's real name, and a secret.

events.name: Lightning sand
events.text: A patch of fine white sand looks firm, then swallows {a rock|a thrown boot|a curious dog's stick} without a sound. More patches lie scattered along the trail.
events.nod: The Princess Bride: lightning sand in the Fire Swamp
events.check: Perception DC 13 to spot the next one
events.failText: someone goes under and has to be pulled out on a rope, losing their pack

events.name: The floor is lava
events.text: A stretch of ground glows dull red and smoulders: a hot spring vent under a crust of rock. The only way across is hopping from boulder to boulder.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 12 for each person
events.failText: a foot goes through the crust: 1d6 fire damage and a ruined boot

events.name: Rolling boulder
events.text: Someone treads on a loose stone in an old ruin's doorway, and a round boulder starts rolling down the passage behind them. {Run.|Run faster.|Somebody grab the idol and run.}
events.nod: Raiders of the Lost Ark: the rolling boulder
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 save for everyone
events.failText: 2d6 bludgeoning damage and a badly squashed hat

events.name: A quaking hillside
events.text: The ground shudders, once, twice. Up the slope, a stand of trees leans and starts to slide. There are seconds to move.
events.check: Dexterity DC 14 save for everyone
events.failText: 3d6 bludgeoning damage, half on a near miss

events.name: Thin crust
events.text: {Salt flats|A crusted mudflat|A dry lakebed} lies over brine. The crust holds a person, mostly. It does not hold a laden mule.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to pick a route
events.failText: the mule goes through and half the day is spent getting it out

events.name: Old mine workings
events.text: The road crosses ground hollowed by old {mine shafts|Builder tunnels|goblin diggings}. It booms underfoot, and somewhere below, something knocks back.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 to cross quietly
events.failText: the knocking follows the party for a mile, and the night's encounter check is at disadvantage

events.name: The fallen giant tree
events.text: A forest giant has come down across the path, trunk taller than a person, branches tangled for fifty yards either way.
events.twist: In the hollow of the trunk, a nest of something young and hungry.

events.name: A river that moved
events.text: The river has moved a {quarter mile|whole mile|hundred yards uphill} in a night, and taken the ford with it. The ferryman sits outside his hut on dry land, baffled.
events.twist: Where the river used to run, the riverbed is full of things people lost in it.

events.name: The sand sea
events.text: Dunes as far as the eye can see, each one a slog up and a slide down. Today's going is slow, and the water goes faster than planned.

events.name: Steppe fire
events.text: A line of grass fire races across the steppe on the wind, faster than a horse can trot. Get to bare ground or burn a firebreak, now.
events.check: Survival DC 14 to find safety
events.failText: the party outruns it, but loses half a day and a day of food

events.name: Avalanche
events.text: A crack like a thunderclap far above, and a white wave pours down the mountainside towards {the path|the party|the village below}.
events.check: Dexterity DC 15 save for everyone
events.failText: buried: 2d10 cold damage and an hour of digging out

events.name: Driving rain
events.text: Rain comes sideways all day, finding every gap in every coat. Camp tonight will be wet and miserable.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to keep the gear dry
events.failText: the bedrolls are soaked: no benefit from a short rest tonight

events.name: Heatstroke
events.text: The heat climbs past bearable by mid-morning. Anyone in {heavy armour|dark clothes|a bad mood} or with too little water is in trouble.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save for anyone in medium or heavy armour
events.failText: one level of exhaustion

events.name: Whiteout
events.text: The snow comes down so thick that the person ahead is a shadow, then gone. Rope together, or lose someone.
events.check: Survival DC 14 to keep the way
events.failText: the party walks in a circle for hours

events.name: The fog bank
events.text: A wall of fog rolls in, so thick the {road|shoreline|sky} vanishes. Voices in it sound close and far at once, and some of them don't belong to the party.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to keep the road
events.failText: the party ends up somewhere else, and has to backtrack

events.name: The storm hits camp
events.text: The storm flattens the tents in the night. By morning, gear is scattered across a field and {some of it is in a tree|a cooking pot is on a cow|someone's boots are in the river}.
events.check: Investigation DC 12 to recover the rest
events.failText: a pack is lost for good

events.name: Frostbite
events.text: The wind finds every bare finger and {nose|ear|toe}. By noon, the tips have gone white and numb.
events.check: Constitution DC 12 save for anyone without proper gloves
events.failText: disadvantage on Dexterity checks until they're warmed by a fire

events.name: Cooking in armour
events.text: The sun hits the party's metal armour so hard that someone fries an egg on a breastplate, to make a point. The point is taken.
events.check: Constitution DC 12 save for anyone in metal armour
events.failText: one level of exhaustion and a lasting smell of egg

events.name: Hail like stones
events.text: Hail the size of plums hammers the road for ten minutes. Get under something.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save to find cover in time
events.failText: 1d6 bludgeoning damage and a ruined hat

events.name: Lightning on the ridge
events.text: The storm settles on the ridge, and lightning picks out the highest point: {the party's tallest member|the spear on someone's back|the pack mule's ears}.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 save, or wait out the storm for half a day
events.failText: 2d8 lightning damage

events.name: The dust storm
events.text: A brown wall of dust rolls across the plain and swallows the sun. Wrap faces and hunker down, or walk blind.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to press on safely
events.failText: someone is lost in the dust for an hour

events.name: Freezing night
events.text: The temperature drops like a stone after dark. The fire barely keeps it off, and {the water skins freeze|frost forms on the bedrolls|the mules huddle in with the party}.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save for everyone
events.failText: one level of exhaustion by morning

events.name: A magic squall's shocks
events.text: Loose magic in the air sparks off every buckle and blade. Spellcasters feel their spells straining at the leash.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save for each spellcaster when casting
events.failText: the spell goes off at a random target

events.name: A wind that steals
events.text: A gust takes {a hat|a map|a whole tent} and carries it straight up into the sky. It doesn't come down.
events.twist: A goblin village two days on is using it as a flag, and wants a fee to give it back.

events.name: Sun-blind
events.text: Sun off the snow, sand or water all day. By noon, eyes are watering and the horizon is a smear.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to rig eye-shades
events.failText: disadvantage on sight-based Perception until sunset

events.name: Rain of frogs, again
events.text: It rains {frogs|small eels|very confused snails}. Not many, but they're cold, they're angry, and they get into everything. The rations are full of them.
events.twist: One of the frogs has a tiny scroll tied to its leg.

events.name: Mud season
events.text: The road has turned to {knee-deep|thigh-deep|bottomless} mud. Every step sucks a boot off. Carts sink to the axles.
events.twist: Further on, a noble's carriage is stuck worse, and its owner offers silver for a push.

events.name: The drowned camp
events.text: The stream beside camp rises in the night. The party wakes to water at their ankles and the food pack floating away.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save to grab it
events.failText: the food is gone downstream

events.name: The cold that follows
events.text: A pocket of freezing air drifts along with the party, keeping step, and frost gathers on their packs even at noon.
events.check: Religion or Arcana DC 13 to work out what's attached to them
events.failText: a level of exhaustion for whoever it settles on tonight

events.name: Mist that makes you sleepy
events.text: A golden mist drifts over the road, smelling of {honey|warm bread|a grandmother's kitchen}. Everyone starts yawning.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save
events.failText: falls asleep on their feet; the party loses an hour
events.twist: Everyone who slept dreams the same dream, of a door under a hill.

events.name: Becalmed
events.text: The wind dies completely. The sea is glass, the sails hang slack, and the crew start rationing water.

events.name: The heat haze road
events.text: The heat haze over the road warps everything, and the party's shadows start walking a few paces ahead of them, picking the way.
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 save to ignore the shadows
events.failText: the shadows lead the party a mile off the road

events.name: A sprung plank
events.text: A plank in the hull springs a leak below the waterline. Water is coming in {slowly|steadily|alarmingly fast}.
events.check: Athletics or carpenter's tools DC 13 to patch it
events.failText: the ship limps into the nearest cove for repairs

events.name: Between rock and whirlpool
events.text: The only channel runs between a cliff where something large nests and a whirlpool that spins like a drain. Pick which to hug.
events.nod: Greek myth: Scylla and Charybdis
events.check: Navigation DC 15 to thread the middle
events.failText: the cliff side costs 2d6 damage to one sailor, the whirlpool side costs a day of stores

events.name: The bag of winds
events.text: A sailor opens a leather sack he won at dice, hoping for wine. Out howls every wind in it at once, and the ship spins round.
events.nod: Greek myth: the bag of winds
events.twist: One small breeze is left in the bag, and it blows wherever its owner asks, once.

events.name: Fouled anchor
events.text: The anchor has caught on something on the seabed and won't come up. Cut the cable, or send someone down.
events.check: Athletics DC 14 to free it underwater
events.failText: the anchor is lost, and the ship must buy another at the next port
events.twist: It is caught in the rigging of an old wreck.

events.name: A rogue wave
events.text: A wave far bigger than the rest rises out of {a calm sea|the fog|nowhere} and breaks over the deck. Anyone not holding on goes with it.
events.check: Strength DC 13 save for everyone on deck
events.failText: swept overboard: a rope, a swim and 1d6 cold damage
events.twist: The wave leaves a large, surprised fish on deck. It is wearing a ring.

events.name: Barnacle drag
events.text: The hull has grown a thick coat of barnacles in two days, which isn't possible. The ship wallows. Something is seeding them.
events.check: Arcana or Nature DC 13 to find the cause
events.twist: A merfolk hedge-witch was paid to slow this ship, and she's following it.

events.name: Fresh water gone foul
events.text: The water casks have gone {green|cloudy|thick as soup} and stinking. There's nothing to drink but what can be found ashore.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to collect rain or find a spring
events.failText: everyone gains a level of exhaustion before landfall

events.name: Seasickness
events.text: A long, greasy swell sets in. The party's {bravest fighter|loudest talker|only cook} turns green and stays green.
events.check: Constitution DC 12 save for each landsman
events.failText: poisoned until they set foot on dry land

events.name: Flooded ford
events.text: The ford is chest-deep and running fast, brown with mud and {branches|dead sheep|half a barn}. Rope across, or wait a day for it to drop.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 for the strongest swimmer to get the rope over
events.failText: the party waits for the river to drop

events.name: The sucking reeds
events.text: The reeds close in until the boat can barely move, and the water beneath grows warm. Bubbles rise. Something below is breathing.
events.check: Strength DC 13 to pole through
events.failText: the party has to back out and find another channel

events.name: Leeches
events.text: Wading through the shallows, the party comes out with {a few|a dozen|far too many} leeches each. Burning them off takes an hour, and there's always one more.
events.check: Constitution DC 11 save
events.failText: lose 1d4 hit points and itch for days

events.name: Ice in the shipping lane
events.text: Ice floes crowd the water ahead, grinding against the hull. The lookout calls {a berg off the bow|a berg off the stern|bergs on every side}, very close.
events.check: Navigation DC 14 to steer clear
events.failText: the hull is holed and the ship makes for shore

events.name: The rip current
events.text: The beach looks calm, but the water between the sandbars runs out to sea fast. Anyone swimming or wading gets dragged.
events.check: Athletics DC 13
events.failText: dragged out, and fetched back with a rope after a long, cold hour

events.name: The drowning compass
events.text: Every compass on board starts spinning, the stars smear, and the sea itself seems to slope. Ships vanish in waters like this.
events.check: Navigation DC 18, or wait for it to pass
events.failText: the ship comes out a day off course, and one crewman is simply not aboard

events.name: A ship's cat overboard
events.text: The ship's cat has fallen in, and the whole crew is shouting. Someone has to dive.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 to get it
events.failText: the cat climbs back up the anchor chain on its own, unimpressed
events.twist: Rescuing it wins the crew's undying loyalty and a better berth.

events.name: Water snakes
events.text: A school of sea snakes rises around the boat, curious and venomous. One drops into {the bilge|the galley|someone's hammock}.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 to catch it safely
events.failText: a bite: 1d6 poison damage and a nasty swelling

events.name: Oasis gone dry
events.text: The oasis on the map is cracked mud, a dead palm and {a skull|a broken bucket|a goblin's apologetic note}. The water the party planned on isn't there.
events.check: Survival DC 14 to dig for a seep
events.failText: the water runs out a day early

events.name: The mule says no
events.text: The pack mule plants its feet and refuses to go another step. It has opinions about this road.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13
events.failText: the mule wins, for an hour
events.twist: It's right. Round the next bend, the road has collapsed.

events.name: Weevils
events.text: The flour sack is crawling with weevils. A day's food is fit only for the brave.

events.name: Snapped bowstring
events.text: In the damp, every bowstring in the party has gone slack or snapped. Spares are dry, aren't they?
events.check: Survival DC 10 to have kept them dry
events.failText: ranged weapons with strings are useless until a market or a dry day

events.name: A lame horse
events.text: A {horse|mule|heidel} throws a shoe and comes up lame. Walk it, or leave it.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 12 to fix the hoof
events.failText: it has to be led the rest of the day

events.name: The rations mimic
events.text: The ration crate has teeth. It has been eating the rations from the inside for a day, and now it would like a hand.
events.nod: D&D: the mimic
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save for whoever opens it
events.failText: 1d6 piercing damage and a sticky arm

events.name: Spoiled in the heat
events.text: The heat has turned the meat. Whatever was planned for dinner is now a buzzing problem.

events.name: Monster-chewed straps
events.text: Something chewed through the {pack straps|tent ropes|saddle girths} overnight. Everything has to be lashed back together with spare rope.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to track the chewer
events.failText: it's still out there, and hungry

events.name: Wet tinder
events.text: Every scrap of tinder is soaked. No fire tonight unless someone is {clever|magical|willing to burn a book}.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to get a fire going
events.failText: a cold camp: no benefit from a short rest

events.name: Bad water skins
events.text: A seam has split in the {water skins|water barrel|only good flask}. Half the water is soaking away before anyone notices.

events.name: The runaway cart
events.text: A brake gives way on a hill, and the cart sets off without anyone. It is heading for {a duck pond|a market stall|a very expensive carriage}.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to catch it
events.failText: it gets there first, and someone wants paying for the damage

events.name: Cracked core lamp
events.text: The monster core in the party's lamp cracks, and the light it gives turns a sickly green. Monsters can smell it.
events.check: Arcana DC 12 to dampen it
events.failText: disadvantage on tonight's encounter check
events.twist: The core's last flicker shows a map, for one second, burned into the wall.

events.name: The boots give up
events.text: Someone's boots finally fall apart, sole flapping. Every step is a blister.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to patch them
events.failText: half speed for that person until a market

events.name: Theft by goats
events.text: A herd of steppe goats swarms the camp and eats {the bread|the map|a priest's prayer book}. They regret nothing.

events.name: The greatback's bad day
events.text: A Host's greatback has gone lame and sat down across the only trail, tent and family still on its back. Nobody moves a greatback that doesn't want to move.
events.check: Medicine or Animal Handling DC 15 to help
events.failText: the party waits a day with the Host

events.name: The heidel bolt
events.text: A {clap of thunder|snake|loud sneeze} spooks the pack animals, and one bolts with half the stores on its back.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to track it down
events.failText: the party never finds it

events.name: Rusted to the scabbard
events.text: Overnight a rust bloom has crept across every piece of metal in camp. Blades are stuck in scabbards and buckles crumble in hands.
events.nod: D&D: the rust monster
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to find the rust-eating thing in the grass
events.failText: one weapon or armour piece is ruined

events.name: The salt in the bread
events.text: Someone packed salt instead of sugar, and salt fish instead of dried apples. Every meal today is a punishment.
events.twist: It was a prank by the party's last innkeeper, who left a cheerful note.

events.name: Cloud cushion leak
events.text: The party's cloud-stuff {cushions|bedrolls|pack liners} are leaking, and the packs are getting lighter, floatier and harder to hold down.
events.check: Arcana DC 12 to seal them
events.failText: a pack floats off, and the party chases it across two fields

events.name: Soldiers took the stores
events.text: A noble house's levy, short of food, has emptied the last waystation's stores. There's nothing to buy, and the next market is days away.

events.name: Spirit coins gone to dust
events.text: A purse of {iron|bronze} spirit coins has crumbled to grey dust, as if something drank the magic out of them. The other purses are getting lighter too.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to find the cause
events.failText: another purse goes the same way by morning
events.twist: A tiny, fat, glowing creature is asleep in the bottom of the purse.

events.name: A lost map
events.text: The map is gone. {Dropped|Stolen|Eaten by a goat}: either way, today is guesswork.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to keep the way without it
events.failText: the party wanders half a day off course

events.name: Too much luggage
events.text: Someone has packed a {portrait of their mother|full tea service|small anvil}. It is very heavy, and nobody will carry it.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to make them leave it
events.failText: it comes along, and so does the bickering

events.name: The briar wall
events.text: A hedge of black briars, taller than a house, has grown across the {road|valley|only pass} in a night. Through the thorns, the roofs of a sleeping village.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Sleeping Beauty's hedge of thorns

events.name: The sleeping village
events.text: Beyond the briars, a whole village sleeps where it fell, smiling. Waking the first villager wakes them all, and they are very grateful, and very confused.
events.check: Arcana or Religion DC 15 to break the sleep

events.name: Ticks in the long grass
events.text: The long grass is alive with ticks, and these ones glow faintly {blue|green|pink} from the magic they've been drinking. By evening, everyone has a few.
events.check: Medicine DC 12 to pull them all
events.failText: someone runs a fever and has disadvantage on Constitution saves for a day
events.twist: A glowing tick taken to a Magic Society alchemist is worth an iron coin.

events.name: The mosquito cloud
events.text: A whining cloud of marsh mosquitoes settles on the party and doesn't lift. Folk here talk about the fever like the weather.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save for everyone
events.failText: marsh fever: poisoned until the next long rest
events.twist: A marsh herbalist sells a smoke-stick that keeps them off, for a price.

events.name: Itching ivy
events.text: Someone answered nature's call in a bed of glossy red leaves. By noon they can think of nothing but the itching.
events.twist: The only cure grows on a farm a mile back, and the farmer laughs for a full minute.
events.check: Medicine DC 12 to treat it
events.failText: disadvantage on Concentration checks until tomorrow

events.name: Strangler vines
events.text: The vines across the path move when nobody is looking at them. A dead deer hangs among them, wrapped tight.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to see the safe way through
events.failText: someone is grappled and needs a DC 13 Strength check or a blade to get free

events.name: Rats in the stores
events.text: Rats got into the stores at the waystation, and into the party's packs while they slept. Half a sack of oats is gone.

events.name: A carpet of thistles
events.text: Thistles the height of a man, purple and smelling of honey, crowd the path for a mile. A shepherd swears they weren't there last spring and wants them gone.

events.name: The bees' road
events.text: A wild hive the size of a cart hangs over the road, humming. Getting past means going slowly and quietly, but there's a fortune in comb up there.
events.check: Stealth or Nature DC 13
events.failText: 1d6 poison damage from stings each

events.name: The scavengers wait
events.text: {Vulture-like monsters|Huge black crows|Bald-headed sky-lizards} circle above all day, patient as tax collectors. Whenever the party stops, one lands a little closer.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to lose them
events.failText: disadvantage on tonight's encounter check
events.twist: They follow the party right up to a monster's lair, which is why they came.

events.name: Crab swarm
events.text: Thousands of {red|blue|glowing} crabs cross the beach towards the sea, and the party is in the way. They pinch everything, especially toes.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save
events.failText: 1d4 piercing damage and a crab that won't let go
events.twist: Crab is on the menu in every coast village tonight, and it's very cheap.

events.name: Thorn wood
events.text: The shortcut runs through a wood of iron-hard thorns. It costs blood and cloth, but the berries on the thorns sell well to the Healers.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 save for everyone
events.failText: 1d6 slashing damage and torn cloaks

events.name: Sleep poppies
events.text: A valley of {red poppies|blue lilies|white star-flowers}, swaying with no wind. The scent is heavy and sweet, and the far side seems very far away.
events.nod: The Wizard of Oz: the poppy field
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save for everyone
events.failText: falls asleep and has to be carried, and the party loses half a day
events.twist: In the middle of the field, an old Iron-ranker sleeps, smiling, his beard down to his knees.

events.name: Gremlins in the tack
events.text: Small, damp, grinning creatures have got into the tack and the cart springs. Spill water on one and there are suddenly three.
events.nod: Gremlins: don't get them wet
events.check: Animal Handling or Sleight of Hand DC 13 to catch them all
events.failText: a buckle or axle gives way at the worst moment

events.name: The spore puff
events.text: A fat grey mushroom bursts underfoot. The spores taste of copper, and everyone who breathed them starts hearing very faint whispering.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save
events.failText: the whispering lasts a day: disadvantage on Wisdom saves
events.twist: The whispers are a fungal mind trying, very politely, to ask for help.

events.name: A plague of moths
events.text: Moths in their millions blot out the sun and settle on everything. They eat {wool|leather|paper}, and only that. Cloaks, packs or books become lace in an hour.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to wrap the woollens
events.failText: everyone's warm gear is ruined, and the next cold night costs a level of exhaustion
events.twist: The moths are fleeing something, and it's coming the same way.

events.name: Snake in the boot
events.text: Someone pulls on their boot and finds it already occupied.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save
events.failText: a bite: 1d6 poison damage

events.name: The poisoned spring
events.text: A clear spring with {dead birds|a dead deer|dead fish} around it. The water smells sweet. Some animal, or someone, has fouled it.
events.check: Nature or Medicine DC 13 to know not to drink
events.failText: anyone who drank is poisoned until a long rest
events.twist: A Purity tract is nailed to a tree nearby, about cleansing the unworthy.

events.name: A colony of bats
events.text: The cave the party shelters in turns out to be home to ten thousand bats, who leave at dusk, all at once, through the party.
events.twist: The floor is deep in guano, which an alchemist in the next town will buy by the sack.

events.name: The singing frogs' venom
events.text: Bright blue frogs line the trail, singing. Touching one makes the toucher sing too, involuntarily, all day.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to know not to touch them
events.failText: that person can't cast spells with a verbal component in silence, or stop humming

events.name: Ants on the march
events.text: An army of {finger-long ants|glass-backed beetles|red army ants} is crossing the valley in a river of bodies a hundred yards wide. Everything in its path is stripped to the bone.
events.check: Survival DC 14 to get round safely
events.failText: the edge of the column catches the party: 2d6 piercing damage each

events.name: A natural array underfoot
events.text: The path crosses a natural array, a seam of pooled magic. Hair stands on end, and every spell cast within it {doubles|fizzles|comes out in the wrong colour}.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to find the edge before casting
events.twist: The array is close to spawning. Lingering for long is a very bad idea.

events.name: The fresh spawn
events.text: Mid-stride, the air beside the path folds, and a newly spawned {Iron|Bronze}-rank monster blinks into being, confused and furious.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 to get away before it gathers itself
events.failText: it attacks
events.twist: It spawned holding something it shouldn't have: half of an iron key.

events.name: Leaking astral space
events.text: The rules of an astral space are leaking out of a cracked entrance nearby. Here, for a mile, everything falls {sideways|slowly|upwards for a heartbeat first}.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to find the crack and plug it
events.failText: the party loses an hour picking up everything that fell

events.name: Wild magic ground
events.text: Old {battle-magic|ritual magic|surge leavings} still soaks this ground. Every spell cast here today has a chance to do something unasked for.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to recognise it before casting
events.failText: the first spell cast rolls on a wild magic table
events.twist: A Magic Society student is camped here on purpose, taking notes.

events.name: Surge-thick air
events.text: The magic is so thick the air tastes of metal. Monsters will come, and they will be stronger than they should be.
events.check: Survival DC 15 to find a less saturated route
events.failText: the party goes round, and the next encounter check is at disadvantage anyway

events.name: A spell that sticks
events.text: A light spell cast this morning refuses to end. It follows its caster, bobbing cheerfully, lighting them up like a beacon.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to unpick it
events.failText: no Stealth checks for the caster until dawn
events.twist: By evening it has learned to hum.

events.name: Mana sickness
events.text: The magic here is too rich. Anyone of Iron rank or less feels feverish and slow, like {drinking too fast|eating too much cake|standing too near a fire}.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save for each Normal or Iron-ranker
events.failText: one level of exhaustion until they leave the region

events.name: The quintessence bog
events.text: A shallow pool glows with raw quintessence. It's valuable to crafters, and it eats through leather in seconds.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to collect it safely
events.failText: 1d8 acid damage and a ruined pack

events.name: A time slip
events.text: The party steps through a patch of shimmering air and out the other side to find the sun much lower. Half a day has gone in three steps.

events.name: The time slip's echo
events.text: The party meets themselves on the road, half a day younger, looking terrified. The two groups pass in silence. Nobody ever talks about it.
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 save for everyone
events.failText: frightened of their own reflection until tomorrow

events.name: Glass rain
events.text: A magic squall drops a rain of tiny {glass beads|crystal needles|frozen sparks}. Pretty, until they cut.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save to get under cover
events.failText: 1d6 slashing damage
events.twist: The beads are worth a little to a glassblower, if anyone sweeps them up.

events.name: The memory fog
events.text: A grey fog that makes people forget. By the time it lifts, nobody can remember {which way they were going|why|whose turn it was to cook}.
events.check: Intelligence DC 13 save, or someone wrote it down
events.failText: the party wastes half a day working it out

events.name: Builder stones
events.text: Grey stone cubes lie scattered across the ground, and they hum. Anyone who stands near them too long feels an urge to stack them.
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 save for everyone
events.failText: that person loses an hour building, and won't stop until dragged away
events.twist: Whoever stacked them first left a tower here. It's almost finished.

events.name: The Society's warning sign
events.text: A Society sign: 'Active array. Spawn risk. Detour 6 miles.' The detour is clearly marked. The shorter path is right there.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to judge whether the short way is safe
events.failText: something spawns as the party passes, and they run back to the detour

events.name: Gravity gone wrong
events.text: For a few hundred yards, down is slightly to the {left|right|north}. Everyone walks at an angle, and loose things roll uphill.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 12 to keep on the path
events.failText: someone tumbles into a ditch for 1d4 bludgeoning damage
events.twist: At the centre, an old fallen statue is pulling everything towards it.

events.name: A cursed milestone
events.text: Whoever passes this milestone feels heavier with each step after. By noon, packs weigh double. A priest could lift it, or a sharp mind could.
events.check: Religion or Arcana DC 14
events.failText: the party crawls on and the curse wears off at dusk
events.twist: The curse was meant for a tax collector, and the milestone apologises if spoken to.

events.name: The beautiful mirage
events.text: A shimmering city of glass towers floats on the horizon, the most beautiful thing anyone has seen. It's behind them, and in front, and to the side.
events.check: Wisdom DC 14 save for the navigator
events.failText: the party chases it half a day off course
events.twist: On the way back, someone is still staring at it, and has to be led.

events.name: Monster core on the boil
events.text: A big monster core lies in the road, cracked and leaking light, hissing like a kettle. It is going to burst.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to drain it safely
events.failText: it bursts: 2d6 force damage to anyone within ten feet
events.twist: Drained, it's still worth a bronze spirit coin to the right buyer.

events.name: Animated weather
events.text: The {rain cloud|fog bank|snow cloud} overhead has gained a face and a temper. It follows the party, getting worse when they shout at it.
events.check: Persuasion or Arcana DC 14 to calm it
events.failText: everyone is drenched and miserable, and the bedrolls are soaked
events.twist: If befriended, the cloud waters the next farm it passes and the farmer is delighted.

events.name: The dead zone
events.text: Magic simply stops here. No spells, no essence abilities, no {cloud-stuff|core lamps|enchanted locks}, nothing. The sense of loss is physical.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to know how far it reaches
events.failText: the party walks right through it before working out how to go round

events.name: The essence pull
events.text: Something in the land pulls at essences. Every essence user feels their power drawn, like a tide going out.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save for each essence user
events.failText: they can't use their highest-level ability until a long rest
events.twist: The pull is coming from an awakening stone, buried just under the road.

events.name: An old pit trap
events.text: The leader's foot goes through a mat of old branches into a spiked pit. At the bottom lies a skeleton with {a full purse|a sealed letter|an Iron-rank badge}.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 save
events.failText: 1d10 piercing damage
events.twist: The pit has a second pit inside it.

events.name: The ten-foot pole
events.text: An outworlder walking with the party insists on prodding every step ahead with a ten-foot pole, 'just in case'. It is slow and maddening, and then it finds a trap.
events.nod: D&D: the ten-foot pole
events.twist: He sells spare poles. They are nine feet long.

events.name: The old battlefield
events.text: The road crosses an old battlefield, the ground still studded with rusted blades and bones. Anyone careless cuts a foot, and the dead here are not quite at rest.
events.check: Perception DC 12 to step carefully
events.failText: 1d4 piercing damage and a festering cut until healed

events.name: The battlefield wakes
events.text: That night, the party hears marching. Rusted soldiers stand in ranks round the camp, facing outward, guarding it. At dawn they are bones again.

events.name: Smugglers' caltrops
events.text: Caltrops have been scattered across the coast road to slow the excise riders. The party finds them {the painful way|with the mule's hoof|in the dark}.
events.check: Perception DC 13
events.failText: a mount or a person goes lame for the day
events.twist: The smugglers come back at dusk to collect them, and are embarrassed.

events.name: A cult's warding line
events.text: A line of salt and dried blood crosses the path. Stepping over it makes every hair stand up, and the birds go quiet.
events.check: Religion DC 13 to break it safely
events.failText: whoever crosses first is cursed: disadvantage on saves until a priest lifts it
events.twist: On the other side, a cult had something penned in. It is gone now.

events.name: The burnt bridge
events.text: The bridge has been burnt from the far side, still smoking. Someone didn't want to be followed, or didn't want {anyone|the party|the Society} coming.

events.name: Who burnt the bridge
events.text: A wounded {courier|deserter|young noble} hides in the reeds ahead. They burnt the bridge, and the people chasing them are not far behind.

events.name: The toll chain
events.text: A chain across the road, padlocked, with a bell and a sign: 'Ring for passage.' Nobody comes when it's rung. {Nobody has come for years.|Something answers from the woods.|A crow rings it back.}
events.check: Thieves' tools or Strength DC 13
events.failText: the party goes round, through the brambles
events.twist: Whoever finally comes to answer it has been waiting a very long time for company.

events.name: Abandoned coin farm
events.text: An overgrown coin farm, its wards failing. Monsters have moved into the pens, but the vault is still sealed.
events.check: Stealth DC 14 to get in and out
events.failText: the monsters wake: an encounter tonight for certain

events.name: The collapsed tunnel
events.text: The road tunnel through the hill has partly fallen in. A gap at the top is just wide enough to wriggle through, and the roof is still {dripping|creaking|whispering}.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 save for each person crawling through
events.failText: a fall of rock: 2d6 bludgeoning damage
events.twist: Halfway through, someone's voice from the other side: 'Is there anyone there?'

events.name: The fire swamp
events.text: Gouts of flame burst from the marsh without warning, the air pops, and something big and rat-like rustles in the reeds.
events.nod: The Princess Bride: the Fire Swamp
events.check: Perception DC 13 to hear the pop before each flame
events.failText: 2d6 fire damage

events.name: Snakes, of course
events.text: The ruin's floor is a carpet of snakes. The outworlder with the party groans and says it is always snakes, then refuses to move.
events.nod: Raiders of the Lost Ark: why did it have to be snakes
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to move him
events.failText: the party carries him
events.twist: One of the snakes is wearing a tiny gold crown.

events.name: The cube in the gully
events.text: The gully ahead looks oddly clean, and shiny, and slightly wobbly. There's a sword hanging in mid-air in the middle of it.
events.nod: D&D: the gelatinous cube
events.check: Perception DC 14 to see it before walking in
events.failText: engulfed: 3d6 acid damage before the others haul them out

events.name: Rotten floorboards
events.text: The waystation's upper floor gives way in the night, and someone wakes on the ground floor with the bed on top of them.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save
events.failText: 1d6 bludgeoning damage
events.twist: Under the floor, a hidden smuggler's cache.

events.name: A warded farmhouse
events.text: The only shelter for miles is a farmhouse with wards on every door and window. They let the party in, but not out again until dawn.
events.twist: The farmer is inside too, and very sorry. The wards were for something else.

events.name: Dysentery
events.text: Bad water catches up with someone. An outworlder in the party's company solemnly announces that they have died of dysentery. They have not, but they wish they had.
events.nod: The Oregon Trail: you have died of dysentery
events.check: Constitution DC 13 save
events.failText: poisoned until the next long rest
events.twist: The outworlder insists on writing a gravestone for the sufferer anyway. It's funny, mostly.

events.name: The trail of crumbs
events.text: The trail markers the party left this morning have been eaten, every one. The {birds|squirrels|goats} look fat and pleased.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Hansel and Gretel's breadcrumbs
events.check: Survival DC 14 to find the way back
events.failText: the party is lost for half a day
events.twist: Further in, a cottage that smells of gingerbread. Nobody should go in.

events.name: The stench bog
events.text: One wrong step in the bog, and the smell clings to whoever made it. It doesn't wash off. Animals flee from them, and so do innkeepers.
events.nod: Labyrinth: the Bog of Eternal Stench
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 save for everyone
events.failText: that person stinks for a week: disadvantage on Persuasion
events.twist: The smell drives off the night's monsters too. Small mercies.

events.name: The sorrow marsh
events.text: In this marsh a grey despair seeps up from the water. Mounts lie down in the mud and won't rise, and people start to wonder why they bother.
events.nod: The NeverEnding Story: the Swamps of Sadness
events.check: Wisdom DC 14 save for everyone, and the mounts
events.failText: someone has to be pulled on by the others, and the party loses half a day

events.name: Kindness in the mud
events.text: The party's cart sinks to the axles. Before anyone can curse, a dozen farmhands appear with ropes and a pair of oxen, refusing payment.
events.twist: They do expect the party to stay for supper and tell stories.

events.name: The rescue party
events.text: A flood has stranded a {Hearth family|goatherd and his goats|Society clerk} on a roof. Getting them off costs time and soaked boots, and earns a meal and a safe night.
events.check: Athletics DC 13
events.twist: The family were stranded on purpose: the flood was a neighbour's doing.

events.name: A healer's caravan
events.text: Someone in the party is hurt worse than they let on. A Church of the Healer cart, passing, stops without being asked.
events.check: Insight DC 12 for the party to admit it
events.twist: The healer is an old Silver-ranker who used to adventure, and has advice.

events.name: Lost and found
events.text: Something important was dropped yesterday. Today, a child runs up the road holding it, out of breath and proud.

events.name: A lucky fall
events.text: Someone slips down a bank into a stream, swearing, and comes up holding a fistful of {glittering stones|old coins|tiny monster cores}. The bank is full of them.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 save
events.failText: 1d6 bludgeoning damage, but they keep the stones
events.twist: The stones belong, technically, to a local noble, whose bailiff is watching.

events.name: The cave-in reveals
events.text: A rockfall blocks the path, but in the fresh face of the cliff glows a seam of crystal. Getting round costs hours. Getting some costs sweat.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to dig some out

events.name: Shelter with a price
events.text: Caught in a storm, the party finds a dry cave. It belongs to a hermit who demands one good story each, and pays the best one in herbs.
events.check: Performance DC 13

events.name: The lucky snag
events.text: A fishing line snagged on the bottom won't come free. Hauling it in takes the whole crew, and brings up {a sea chest crusted in shells|a merfolk spear|a bell from a sunken temple}.
events.check: Athletics DC 14

events.name: The broken wheel's gift
events.text: A wheel breaks outside a wheelwright's yard, as if planned. She fixes it cheaply, and tells the party of a hidden trail.

events.name: The detour's shrine
events.text: A fallen tree forces a detour past a forgotten Journey shrine. A coin left there earns a blessing: advantage on tomorrow's Survival check.

events.name: A storm-tossed find
events.text: The storm drives the boat ashore on a strange little island. Repairs take a day, but the island has a wreck on it, and the wreck has a hold.

events.name: The mocking echo
events.text: In this valley, every word comes back in a different voice, and twice. It is {unsettling|funny|deeply rude} for an hour, then infuriating.
events.check: Wisdom DC 12 save
events.failText: snaps at the party all day: disadvantage on Insight and Persuasion
events.twist: One of the echoes answers a question nobody asked.

events.name: The wrong road
events.text: The signposts here have all been turned, by {pranksters|a petty spirit|a bored goblin}. Every one points somewhere unhelpful.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to see through it
events.failText: the party walks half a day the wrong way

events.name: The sleepwalker
events.text: Someone in the party sleepwalks in the night, and wakes a mile from camp, barefoot and cold, holding a {stranger's hat|bird's nest|monster core}.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to find them

events.name: Bad luck penny
events.text: Someone has picked up a penny that brings bad luck. Today, every roll that can go wrong does. Somebody will have to give it away.
events.check: Insight DC 14 to work out which coin
events.failText: disadvantage on one check of the DM's choice
events.twist: Giving it to someone else is very tempting, and very rude.

events.name: The cursed boots
events.text: A pair of fine {boots|riding boots|dancing shoes}, found at the roadside, fit perfectly and won't come off. They walk a little faster than their wearer wants.
events.check: Arcana DC 14 to remove them
events.failText: the wearer walks ahead all day, alone, and gets into trouble
events.twist: The boots lead, eventually, to their previous owner's grave, and stop.

events.name: A misplaced wish
events.text: Someone mutters 'I wish this road were shorter'. Something hears. The road shrinks, and so does everything on it, including the party.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to reverse it
events.failText: the party is tiny until dusk, and the walk is huge
events.twist: A tiny goblin, the right size now, offers the party a lift on his beetle.

events.name: The jealous river spirit
events.text: A river spirit is in a sulk. The water rises to block every ford while the party watches.
events.check: Persuasion or Religion DC 14 to soothe it
events.failText: the party waits for the spirit to calm down
events.twist: It would love a gift: anything shiny.

events.name: The creeping campsite
events.text: The campsite has moved in the night: the tents are {fifty yards|a field away|on the other side of the stream} from the fire, and nobody felt a thing.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to find out how
events.failText: half the food is somewhere back at the fire's old spot, eaten

events.name: A hole in the world
events.text: A tear in the air, the size of a door, hangs over the road. Everything nearby is slowly sliding towards it, including the party.
events.check: Athletics DC 15 for everyone
events.failText: someone is dragged half through and comes back with a level of exhaustion and a strange new scar
events.twist: Something on the other side is pushing, and the World-Phoenix's servants will want to know.

events.name: The bargain at the pass
events.text: A {goblin|Leonid|human} trapper has the only rope across a flooded ravine and offers it, for a price. The price is a favour, unspecified.

events.name: The trapper's favour
events.text: The trapper catches up. The favour: carry a sealed letter to the next town, and don't open it. It is ticking.

events.name: Stuck in the doorway
events.text: A waystation door won't let anyone through without being told a joke. It {does not find the party funny|only likes puns|has heard that one}.
events.check: Performance DC 14
events.failText: the party sleeps outside and the door laughs at them
events.twist: The door used to belong to a Revels temple, and misses it terribly.

events.name: The leaking ship's hold
events.text: The hold is shipping water from a seam nobody can find, and there is a smell of something rotting below the cargo.
events.check: Investigation DC 14 to find the leak
events.failText: the ship puts into port a day early

events.name: What was in the hold
events.text: The leak was gnawed from inside: a stowaway young sea monster, now the size of a dog, has been eating the cargo and wants to go home.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13 to coax it overboard

events.name: The mountain's mood
events.text: A Cloud Clan herder on the path stops dead, looks at the peaks, and says the mountain doesn't want visitors today.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to know whether to listen
events.failText: the party pushes on and gets caught in a storm

events.name: The mountain relents
events.text: The herder catches up, sniffs the wind and announces the mountain is in a better mood. A cloud path opens across the gorge, clear and solid.

events.name: A child in the well
events.text: Shouting from a farmyard: a {child|lamb|very old dog} has fallen down the well, and the farmer can't fit. Somebody small, strong or clever is needed.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to get down and back

events.name: The well's thanks
events.text: The rescued family's neighbours have heard. At the next village, the party is met with bread, bunting and a free night's lodging.

events.name: A visitor at the fire
events.text: A stranger walks into the firelight and knows the party's names.

events.name: A shared dream
events.text: Two party members dream the same dream, and it points somewhere.

events.name: Night spawn
events.text: Lights among the trees where magic is pooling. By morning there will be monsters.

events.name: Sleepwalker
events.text: A party member is found walking out of camp, toward something.

events.name: Wrong stars
events.text: A clear night, and a sky that does not look quite right.

events.name: Raided stores
events.text: Something takes food from camp during the watch.

events.name: Someone else's fire
events.text: Across the valley, another campfire, exactly matching the party's. When they put theirs out, the other one goes out too.

events.name: The fox thief
events.text: A fox gets into camp and steals one specific thing from each person, always the thing they'd miss most. Its den is close by.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to track it by morning

events.name: A visitor bearing soup
events.text: An old woman from a nearby farm walks into camp with a pot of hot soup, because she 'saw the fire and thought you looked cold'.

events.name: Singing from the water
events.text: Someone is singing out on the water, sweet and sad. Anyone on watch makes a DC 13 Wisdom save or walks toward it.

events.name: The stars talk
events.text: On second watch, the person on guard hears the stars whispering, very faintly. If they listen, they learn one true thing about tomorrow.

events.name: Bad dreams
events.text: Everyone dreams of the same door, and something knocking on the other side. No one sleeps well.
events.twist: The door is real, and it is a day's travel ahead.

events.name: Glowing mushrooms
events.text: The ground around camp lights up with glowing mushrooms after dark. They are harmless, and worth a little to an alchemist.

events.name: A ghost asking for directions
events.text: A polite ghost walks into camp and asks how to get home. Its home was a village that burned down a century ago.

events.name: The snoring
events.text: The snoring from somewhere in camp is so loud that it draws a curious monster to investigate. It turns out to be the monster snoring.

events.name: A stolen watch
events.text: The person on watch nods off for a moment. When they wake, someone has gone through the packs.

events.name: Storytelling
events.text: A quiet night with good stories around the fire. Everyone gets inspiration, or a d6 to add to one roll tomorrow.

events.name: The tapping
events.text: Tapping on the tent canvas all night, from the inside.

events.name: A night herd
events.text: A herd of luminous, semi-transparent deer passes through camp in total silence, ignoring everyone.

events.name: A torch on the road
events.text: A single torch moves along the road in the dark, slowly, toward the camp. It stops just outside the firelight, and nobody is holding it.

events.name: Message in the embers
events.text: The embers of the fire rearrange themselves into words in an old language, then fall apart.
events.check: Arcana or History DC 15 to read them

events.name: The bedroll thief
events.text: A large, friendly monster crawls into camp and goes to sleep in someone's bedroll. It is very warm and refuses to move.

events.name: The nightmare
events.text: One party member wakes screaming from a dream of their own death. The details are very specific.

events.name: A camp in the ruins
events.text: The party camps in a ruin. In the dark, they hear a whole town going about its business around them, and see no one.

events.name: Phone home
events.nod: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
events.text: An outworlder child, hiding in the brush, has built a little machine out of junk and swears it will let them talk to home. They are hungry and scared.

events.name: A sleeping spirit
events.nod: My Neighbour Totoro
events.text: A huge, soft, grey forest spirit sits by the road in the rain, waiting for something. Anyone who gives it an umbrella or a cloak gets a gift of seeds in the morning.

events.name: The midnight pedlar
events.text: A pedlar with a lantern on a pole arrives at midnight, sets out a blanket of goods, and says he only trades after dark. Everything is priced in {secrets|songs|iron spirit coins}.

events.name: A Host rider at the fire
events.text: A {young|scarred|very old} Drift Host rider walks her two-headed heidel into the firelight and asks to share it. She is following the Wandering Tide and says it is coming this way.
events.twist: She is a tide-reader, and wants the party's help moving her family's greatback before dawn.

events.name: The lantern seller
events.text: A thin man in a {grey|patched|far too fine} coat sells the party a lantern that burns without oil. 'Keep it lit till you reach a town,' he says, and is gone.

events.name: The lantern goes out
events.text: On the second watch the stranger's lantern gutters and goes out. In the dark beyond the camp, something large stops moving.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to relight it before whatever it was arrives

events.name: A knock on nothing
events.text: {Three|Five|Seven} slow knocks sound in the middle of camp, as if on a door. There is no door. On the next watch, the knocks come again, closer to the fire.

events.name: Iron-rank runaways
events.text: {Two|Three} teenage Iron-rankers creep up to the fire, badges new and stomachs empty. They took a contract above their rank and ran. They are ashamed and very hungry.
events.twist: The monster they ran from followed them.

events.name: Healer on the night road
events.text: A Church of the Healer sister walking through the night stops at the fire, checks everyone's wounds without asking, and leaves a little {mint|willow-bark|honey} tea that makes for deep, clean sleep.

events.name: Watch swap
events.text: A stranger in a Society coat offers to take the party's watch for the night. He insists it is a tradition. He snores by the end of the {first hour|first song|first sentence}.

events.name: Eyes in the reeds
events.text: Dozens of small green eyes watch the camp from the reeds, unblinking. They move when nobody is looking straight at them.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to see what they are
events.twist: They are frogs. Something else is behind them, using them to watch.

events.name: The kettle raider
events.text: A monster the size of a cat makes off with the party's {cooking pot|best ladle|kettle}, then sits just outside the firelight banging it with a stick, demanding to be chased.
events.check: Athletics or Animal Handling DC 12 to get the pot back

events.name: Wolf song
events.text: A {wolf pack|pack of hill-dogs|lone monster} is howling across the hills all night, never coming closer. Nobody sleeps well, and tomorrow's watch is tired.

events.name: A heidel spooked
events.text: Something spooks the party's heidels in the dark. Both heads scream at once, and one beast pulls its tether loose and bolts.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13 to calm it
events.failText: it is found at dawn, a mile off and very sorry

events.name: Something tasting the ropes
events.text: On the second watch, something under the hull is tasting the {anchor rope|rudder|hull planks}, slowly and carefully, the way a dog sniffs a stranger's hand.
events.twist: It wants the ship's monster cores, and it knows where they are stored.

events.name: The scorpion lamp
events.text: Desert scorpions gather in a perfect ring around the fire, tails up, and stay there all night. They don't attack. They seem to be keeping something out.

events.name: Jungle chorus
events.text: At midnight the whole jungle goes silent, then every insect, frog and bird sings the same single note together. Anyone awake feels it in their {teeth|bones|spirit coins}.
events.twist: Anyone with a Life essence hears words in it.

events.name: The night grazer
events.text: A greatback, lost from its Host, wanders up to camp and lies down beside the fire like an enormous dog. Its tent platform is still strapped on, empty.

events.name: A Host comes looking
events.text: Riders of a Drift Host reach camp at dawn, looking for their greatback. When they find it safe, the Khan's daughter offers the party a guest-right among them.

events.name: The dream of the road
events.text: One party member dreams the next day's road in perfect detail: every bend, every {stream|ford|ambush spot}, every place to avoid. It is all accurate.

events.name: Borrowed nightmare
events.text: Everyone wakes from someone else's nightmare: drowning in a dark channel, a hand on the ankle. Each blames another party member. The nightmare belongs to none of them.
events.twist: It belongs to a dead Iron-ranker in the water nearby, who wants to be found.

events.name: Talking in sleep
events.text: A party member talks in their sleep all night, loudly and in great detail, about {a secret crush|where they hid their coins|an argument they lost years ago}.

events.name: A dream of rank
events.text: Each party member dreams of themselves one rank higher: stronger, older, colder. Some find it inspiring. Some don't like who they become.
events.twist: One of the dreams shows a confluence they could actually reach.

events.name: Nobody dreams
events.text: Nobody in the party dreams tonight, and everyone wakes feeling as if they lost something in the night. Small things in the packs, like {spoons|boot laces|badges}, have been moved a few inches.

events.name: The sleepless one
events.text: One party member cannot sleep at all. Every time they close their eyes, they see the face of the {last thing they killed|first person they failed|monster that got away}.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13
events.failText: no benefit from the long rest

events.name: Coin glow
events.text: In the dark, every spirit coin in the party's purses glows {softly|blue|like a heartbeat}, all pulsing in time. Out in the night, something else is pulsing with them.
events.twist: A buried coin cache lies a short walk away, still giving off the beat.

events.name: A star falls
events.text: A star falls slow and bright and lands {a mile|two hills|a long walk} away with a soft, distant chime. A pale glow rises from where it came down.

events.name: The fallen star's keeper
events.text: A Celestine in a dusty travelling coat catches up with the party. She has been chasing that falling star for a month and will pay well for word of it.

events.name: Sky ship lights
events.text: High above camp, a sky ship drifts past with its lamps out, making no sound. Someone aboard flashes a {mirror|green lamp|red lamp} three times toward the party.
events.twist: It is a smuggler's signal, and they think the party is their contact.

events.name: Aurora of the essences
events.text: Curtains of light fill the sky, and each colour matches someone's essence. For one night, everyone in camp can feel exactly where the others are.

events.name: The moon's second shadow
events.text: The moon casts two shadows tonight. Everyone's second shadow is a little late, and a little out of step, and one of them waves.

events.name: The magic thickens
events.text: On second watch, the air goes thick and {sweet|metallic|warm}. The magic is pooling around the camp. By morning, something will spawn here unless the party moves now.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to break camp and find safer ground in the dark
events.failText: the spawn catches them packing

events.name: A good night's sleep
events.text: The ground is soft, the night is warm, and everyone sleeps right through. Everyone wakes rested and with one extra Hit Die back.

events.name: Burnt supper
events.text: Supper catches fire. Then the {spoon|cook's eyebrows|ration sack} catches fire. Then, somehow, the bucket of water meant to put it out.

events.name: Watch-fire stories
events.text: Over the fire, someone asks each party member for the {worst contract they ever took|strangest monster they ever saw|worst thing they ever ate}. The stories get taller, the laughter gets louder, and the night goes quickly.
