events.twist: One story is true, and someone in the dark is listening for it.

events.name: The singing kettle
events.text: The cooking pot starts humming a tune just as the water boils. It is the same tune every night after, and nobody in the party knows it.
events.twist: An old Hearth priest would know it: it is a blessing.

events.name: Card game by the fire
events.text: A game of cards on watch gets very serious very fast. By dawn, someone owns {another's boots|the rations for a week|a promise they will regret}.

events.name: Hearth stones
events.text: The party builds the fire ring from flat stones by the path. One is carved with the flame-in-stones of the Hearth. The fire burns warm all night on a handful of sticks.

events.name: The patrol that never came back
events.text: A line of ghostly soldiers marches through camp in silence, wearing a noble house's colours from {fifty|eighty|a hundred} years ago. The last one stops and asks if the war is over.

events.name: The drowned bell
events.text: A ship's bell rings below the water, far beneath the hull, every hour on the hour. The crew say it means a wreck. They say it in whispers.
events.twist: The wreck still carries its cargo of silver spirit coins.

events.name: Grave goods
events.text: The ground the party camps on turns out to be an old burial field. In the dark, one person's hand closes on a {ring|badge|locket} in the soil.
events.twist: Death priests would want it reburied. A collector would pay well.

events.name: Footprints round the camp
events.text: In the morning there are bare footprints all the way round the camp, just outside the firelight. Nobody saw anyone. The circle is a little smaller than it should be.

events.name: The circle closes
events.text: The footprints are back, and the circle is tighter now, close enough to touch the bedrolls. Something has been walking round the sleepers all night.
events.check: Perception DC 15 on watch to see it
events.twist: It is a lost spirit trying to work out which of them is alive.

events.name: Rising water
events.text: The {tide|river|flood channel} comes in further than anyone expected. The lowest bedroll is soaked, and so are the rations in it.

events.name: Freezing night
events.text: The desert night turns bitterly cold. Without blankets or a good fire, each person makes a DC 10 Constitution save or wakes with a level of exhaustion.

events.name: Stars through a gap
events.text: A {storm|squall|rain front} passes, and for an hour the clouds open on a single patch of sky full of unfamiliar stars. A Magic Society scholar would pay to know what the party saw.

events.name: Sheltering cave
events.text: The rain drives the party into a dry cave. It is warm and sound, but the back of it is full of bones, all neatly sorted by {size|colour|species}.
events.twist: Whatever sorted them is a goblin hermit, and this is his house.

events.name: The hunt in the sky
events.text: Hounds bay in the clouds and horns blow overhead. A host of riders crosses the sky. Anyone outside a ring of firelight is invited, very politely, to join them.
events.nod: Folklore: the Wild Hunt
events.check: Wisdom save DC 15 to refuse
events.twist: Those who ride along come back at dawn a hundred miles away, with a trophy and no memory.

events.name: Lights on the marsh
events.text: Small {blue|green|white} lights bob over the marsh, just out of reach, always moving away. They look like lanterns carried by someone who knows the path.
events.nod: Folklore: will-o'-the-wisp
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13 to stay put
events.failText: the follower ends up waist-deep in black water

events.name: Bowl of cream
events.text: A farmer's wife tells the party to leave a bowl of {milk|cream|honey} out tonight. If they do, they wake to find their boots polished, their kit mended and the fire laid.
events.nod: Folklore: brownies and house spirits

events.name: Three hungry brutes
events.text: Three huge, dim monsters sit round a fire nearby, arguing about how best to cook travellers. The argument has gone on for hours, and dawn is close.
events.nod: The Hobbit: the trolls arguing until sunrise
events.check: Deception or Performance DC 13 to keep them arguing until sunrise
events.twist: Daylight doesn't turn them to stone. It just sends them to sleep.

events.name: Enemies are nearby
events.text: Every time someone lies down, a nearby monster {growls|shrieks|hoots}. When they stand up, it stops. It is a small, smug monster, and it is doing this on purpose.
events.nod: Video games: 'You cannot rest, there are monsters nearby'
events.check: Survival DC 12 to find it
events.failText: nobody gets a full rest

events.name: A thousand and one
events.text: A merchant's widow joins the fire and begins a story she refuses to finish. 'Tomorrow night,' she says. Each night she adds a little more, and the story is about the party.
events.nod: One Thousand and One Nights: Scheherazade

events.name: The lumpy bedroll
events.text: A noble's heir sharing the camp cannot sleep and complains all night about a lump in her bedroll. There is one. It is a dried pea, under six blankets.
events.nod: Fairy tale: The Princess and the Pea

events.name: The piper at the edge
events.text: A {thin|tall|faceless} piper plays outside the firelight. One by one the party's heidels pull at their tethers, trying to follow the tune into the dark.
events.nod: Folklore: the Pied Piper
events.check: Animal Handling or Performance DC 13 to drown out the tune
events.failText: one heidel slips loose and is found at dawn, far off and dazed

events.name: Hook-hand
events.text: An outworlder at the fire tells a ghost story from his world about a courting couple, a radio and a man with a hook. At the end, something scrapes the side of the wagon.
events.nod: Urban legend: The Hook
events.twist: It is a branch. Probably.

events.name: Sweets on sticks
events.text: An outworlder pulls out a bag of soft white sweets she made herself, toasts them on sticks, and squashes them between biscuits. She calls it the best thing her world ever invented.
events.nod: S'mores and campfire marshmallows

events.name: Wrong constellations
events.text: An outworlder lies by the fire naming the stars wrongly: the Hunter, the Plough, the Great Bear. He is quiet afterwards. Not one of them is up there.
events.nod: Earth constellations: Orion, the Plough

events.name: Don't get it wet
events.text: A small, furry, big-eyed monster begs at the fire, sweet as a kitten. Its keeper's note says: no bright light, never get it wet, and never feed it after midnight.
events.nod: Gremlins
events.twist: It's raining by dawn.

events.name: Dancing in the ring
events.text: A ring of mushrooms near camp lights up at midnight, and music comes from it. Anyone who steps in can dance till dawn and feel only joy.
events.nod: Folklore: fairy rings
events.twist: Each dancer wakes a day older for every hour they danced.

events.name: Light keeps them off
events.text: Every patch of dark ground near camp sprouts a small monster as the night deepens. Anywhere the firelight reaches stays clear. Keep the fires going all night.
events.nod: Minecraft: monsters spawn in the dark
events.check: Survival DC 13 to keep enough fires burning
events.failText: a fight before dawn

events.name: The selkie's skin
events.text: A sealskin lies folded on the rocks by the water, warm to the touch. Somewhere out in the dark, someone is crying.
events.nod: Folklore: selkies
events.twist: It belongs to a merfolk shapeshifter who needs it to go home, and a fisherman wants to keep it.

events.name: The sleeper by the road
events.text: An old man asleep under a tree wakes as the party camps and asks for news. He names a war, a Duke and a price of bread that are all forty years out of date.
events.nod: Rip Van Winkle

events.name: The bedroll with teeth
events.text: One bedroll is warmer and softer than it was this morning. It also has a faint pulse, and the owner's {spare boots|soap|socks} are missing.
events.nod: D&D: the mimic
events.check: Perception DC 13 before lying down
events.failText: it bites

events.name: A chicken-legged cottage
events.text: A cottage on enormous bird legs settles down beside the camp for the night and puts out a lamp. Its door swings open, inviting.
events.nod: Folklore: Baba Yaga's hut
events.twist: The old woman inside will answer one question truly for a night of honest chores.

events.name: A borrowed ember
events.text: A tiny fire spirit, barely a spark, shaped like a {mouse|moth|tiny old man}, drifts into camp and asks in a crackle to borrow an ember. Its own flame is almost out.

events.name: The ember returned
events.text: The little fire spirit returns, now a blaze the size of a {dog|barrel|heidel}, and leaves a gift of warmth: no one in the party feels cold for a week.

events.name: The lost child
events.text: A small goblin child stumbles into camp in tears, lost in the dark. She knows her village is near a {crooked tree|stone bridge|big red rock}, and not much else.

events.name: The village's thanks
events.text: The goblin child's family find the party at the next stop and won't hear of thanks: they press on the party food, a good knife and the best directions for a day's walk.

events.name: The second watch hears drums
events.text: Far off, someone is {drumming|clapping|beating a pot}. The rhythm matches the heartbeat of whoever is on watch, and speeds up when they get scared.
events.twist: It is a cult in a nearby gully, and the drumming is how they choose a sacrifice.

events.name: Watch of the deck
events.text: The night is calm, the sails are slack and the deck creaks. The watch spots a light far off to port, too low to be a star.
events.check: Perception DC 12 to make out another ship
events.twist: It is a merfolk raft carrying a sick child to the nearest healer.

events.name: Night fishing
events.text: The crew rig lines over the side after dark and haul up silver fish that glow faintly. One has {a bronze spirit coin|a merfolk ring|an iron core} in its belly.

events.name: Phosphor sea
events.text: The sea lights up blue around the ship, then forms a shape: a vast fish, longer than the ship, swimming alongside in light alone.
events.twist: It wants to be followed, and it knows a faster current.

events.name: Something on the mast
events.text: The watch looks up and sees someone sitting on top of the mast, legs swinging, looking down. By the time anyone climbs up, there are only wet footprints going down the wood.

events.name: The tide-wraith
events.text: On a dark beach, a figure walks out of the sea and up to camp, dripping, and asks for a {sailor|fisherman|ship's cook} by name. It knows when it is lied to.
events.twist: The sailor is someone the party met earlier, and the wraith is their drowned brother.

events.name: Cold sands song
events.text: As the desert cools, the dunes start to sing: a deep, slow humming as the sand settles. The song is old, and some of the notes sound like names.
events.check: History DC 13 to recognise one of the names
events.twist: The names belong to a caravan lost here a century ago.

events.name: Desert stars
events.text: No cloud, no moon, no light for a hundred miles. The stars over the desert are so thick they cast shadows. Even the grumpiest member of the party stops to look.

events.name: The sand-sleeper
events.text: In the cold of the desert night, the sand by the camp breathes in and out. A huge shape is buried there, asleep, and very warm.
events.twist: It is a monster the size of a house. The heat coming off it would keep the party warm all night.

events.name: A lantern in the dunes
events.text: A single lantern sits on top of a dune, lit, with no tracks leading to it. A note under it reads 'For the next ones.' The oil is fresh.

events.name: Cloud bed
events.text: A Cloud Clan herder shows the party how to fluff the mountain cloud into a {bed|pillow|whole mattress}. It is the softest night anyone has had in months.

events.name: Rope bridge in the dark
events.text: Across the gorge, someone is walking the rope bridge in the dark. The ropes creak with every step. The footsteps never reach the other side.
events.twist: A Clan crafter fell from it last year, and her cloud-glass tools are still on a ledge below.

events.name: Condor on the ledge
events.text: A huge condor monster lands on the ledge above the camp and spends the night watching the party's food. It is very patient.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 15 to make friends
events.twist: It is a tamed bird from the Cloud Clans, with a message tied to its leg.

events.name: Climbing vines
events.text: During the night, vines creep over the camp. By the second watch they have tied two {bedrolls|boots|heidels} together and are working on a third.
events.check: Perception DC 12 on watch
events.failText: a sleeper wakes half-wrapped and has to be cut free

events.name: Hammocks in the canopy
events.text: A jungle guide shows the party how to sling hammocks high in the trees, above the crawling things. It is the best sleep anyone has had since the jungle began.

events.name: The night bloom
events.text: A shield-sized flower near camp opens at midnight and gives off a silver pollen. Breathing it gives sweet dreams and, for one person, a glimpse of the next day.
events.twist: Its seeds sell for a lot to an alchemist.

events.name: Fever dreams
events.text: Someone wakes burning hot after a mosquito bite. By the end of the night, they are talking to people who are not there.
events.check: Medicine DC 13 to break the fever
events.failText: a level of exhaustion that lasts until a healer sees them

events.name: Owl post
events.text: A huge {owl|crow|bat} lands on a branch over the camp and drops a sealed letter in someone's lap. It waits. It clearly expects a reply, and a tip.
events.twist: The letter is for someone else entirely, and very indiscreet.

events.name: Woodcutter's lamp
events.text: A Lindover lumber camp lets the party sleep in their bunkhouse. There is stew, a dry floor and a lot of very loud opinions about trees.

events.name: A tree that sighs
events.text: The tree the party camps under sighs heavily every hour. When someone pats its bark, it stops, and drops a branch of ripe fruit.

events.name: Eel-fishers' fire
events.text: Delta eel-fishers in green-stone boats tie up beside the party and share smoked {eel|frog legs|river snail} and gossip about which channels have gone bad this season.

events.name: Mist at midnight
events.text: Mist rolls in off the channels and swallows the camp. Inside it, the person on watch hears their own voice calling their name, from further away each time.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13
events.failText: they wander off and must be found

events.name: The stilt-house light
events.text: A stilt house stands in the reeds with one lit window, and nobody lives there. Every night someone lights the lamp, according to the eel-fishers.
events.twist: It is a Rock Keeper signal, telling the marsh monster where to feed.

events.name: Barn for the night
events.text: A farmer lets the party sleep in the barn, for a price: help with the {milking|mucking out|egg collecting} before dawn. The cows are ill-tempered and the barn cat is worse.

events.name: Scarecrow on the move
events.text: The scarecrow in the next field was facing east at dusk. On the second watch, it's facing the camp. By morning, it's a field closer.

events.name: Harvest-night dance
events.text: A farming village is celebrating the {harvest|first rice|end of a monster plague} with a bonfire and a dance, and drags the party in. Church of the Revels wine flows. Nobody keeps much of a watch.
events.twist: Someone uses the noise to break into the party's packs.

events.name: Waystation bunks
events.text: A Church of the Journey waystation has two free bunks, a fire and a cook. Everyone else sleeps on the floor. It's still the best night in a week.

events.name: A carriage stopped at midnight
events.text: A fine carriage stands stopped on the road with its lamps lit and its door open. The heidels are calm. The seats are warm. There is no one in it.
events.twist: The owner is hiding in the ditch, terrified of whatever stopped the carriage.

events.name: The milestone talks
events.text: The milestone by the camp is carved with a face. After midnight it complains, at great length, that nobody {ever reads its distances correctly|cleans its moss|says good night}.

events.name: Grass waves at night
events.text: The steppe grass glows faintly, in waves running north. The tide-readers would say the Wandering Tide is moving, and moving fast.
events.check: Survival or Arcana DC 13 to read which way to go tomorrow

events.name: Watch over the herd
events.text: The Host the party travels with asks them to take a watch over the heidel herd. Nothing happens, until something does: a pair of eyes in the grass.
events.check: Perception DC 13
events.failText: a heidel is taken in the night

events.name: Khan's fire
events.text: A Bronze-rank {Leonid|Draconian|human} Khan invites the party to her fire and asks each of them their rank. She is quietly working out whether they are worth following, or fighting.

events.name: Old camp ring
events.text: The party camps in the ring of an old Host camp. At midnight, the grass inside the ring flattens as if a whole town was lying down to sleep.
events.twist: Every ruin on the steppe is a town that tried. This one is still trying.

events.name: Dream of a door
events.text: A party member dreams of a door at the bottom of a {lake|well|canal}, with their name on it. In the morning, there is mud under their fingernails.
events.twist: The lake is real, and the door is an astral space entrance.

events.name: Sleep-walk to the water
events.text: The person on second watch finds another party member sleepwalking toward the water, eyes open, saying a name that isn't theirs.

events.name: The shared snore
events.text: The whole party snores in unison. It's oddly beautiful. A passing {bard|owl|Revels priest} writes it down.

events.name: The dead mentor
events.text: A party member dreams of someone they lost, who tells them they did well. They wake with tears and inspiration.

events.name: Dream of the god
events.text: One party member dreams of a vast presence watching them through the eyes of their church's symbol. It says one word, and the word is a name.
events.twist: The name belongs to someone the god wants found, alive.

events.name: Insomnia
events.text: Nobody can sleep. The night is too hot, the ground too hard and the {insects|frogs|heidels} too loud. Everyone starts tomorrow tired.

events.name: The ghost who wants a duel
events.text: A ghostly Iron-ranker challenges the strongest party member to a duel. He is very bad at it. He just wanted someone to finally say he fought well.

events.name: The widow's lamp
events.text: An old woman walks the road at night with a lamp, looking for her {son|daughter|husband}. The Society listed him dead in the last surge. She checks every face at every fire.

events.name: A Society runner
events.text: An exhausted Adventure Society runner stumbles into camp with a sealed satchel and a {crossbow bolt|claw wound|burn} in her shoulder. She begs the party to deliver the satchel.
events.twist: It holds surge readings that someone powerful wants kept quiet.

events.name: Bargain at the fire
events.text: A stranger in a blank mask sits at the fire and offers to trade one good thing for a small promise. He doesn't say what the promise is until it's made.

events.name: The promise called in
events.text: The masked stranger is back at the fire, and the promise is due: carry a small, heavy box to the next town without opening it.
events.twist: The box is warm, and something in it is breathing.

events.name: Pilgrim snorer
events.text: A Church of the Journey pilgrim, {very old|very young|very large}, asks to share the fire, then sleeps like a felled tree. Every so often he mutters directions to places that don't exist.

events.name: A priest of Death
events.text: A Death priest with a black candle passes in the night, nods at the party, and says he will not be needed here after all. He seems relieved.
events.twist: He was walking toward a village half a mile on.

events.name: The cold guest
events.text: A thin girl sits down at the fire and holds out her hands. The flames lean away from her. She says she is warming up, and never does.

events.name: Ants in the bedding
events.text: The party has camped on {an ant nest|a scorpion burrow|a beetle nest}. By midnight, everyone knows it.
events.check: Survival DC 10 to spot it before bed
events.failText: a miserable night and no proper rest

events.name: Embers in the wind
events.text: The wind picks up and blows embers into the dry grass. A small fire starts, fast, just as everyone gets to sleep.
events.check: Athletics or Survival DC 12 to beat it out
events.failText: the party loses a pack to the flames

events.name: Storm watch
events.text: A storm hammers the camp all night. The tent rips, the fire dies and everyone is soaked. Anyone without shelter makes a DC 12 Constitution save or wakes with exhaustion.

events.name: Cave echoes
events.text: The cave the party shelters in carries voices from deeper in. They are having the party's exact conversation, a few minutes later.

events.name: Unexpected visitors to the larder
events.text: Something raids the food. In the morning, the culprits are found asleep in the ration sack: a family of very full, very round {hedgehog-like|toad-like|furry} small monsters.

events.name: Essence sparks
events.text: As everyone drifts off, small sparks rise from each sleeper in the colour of their essences and dance together above the fire, forming the shape of a {key|crown|wheel}.
events.twist: The shape is the sign of a confluence one of them could form.

events.name: Spirit-coin moths
events.text: Pale moths gather around the purse of spirit coins and drink from them. The coins dim slightly. The moths glow bright enough to read by.
events.twist: Caught in a jar, they make a lamp that lasts a month.

events.name: The walking stars
events.text: Three stars come down out of the sky and walk across the {hills|dunes|water} on long legs of light, then climb back up before dawn.
events.twist: Wherever they stepped, the ground is now a natural array.

events.name: A moon in the water
events.text: There are two moons in the water tonight, though only one in the sky. The second one is closer, and swimming.

events.name: Night of the wisp-wind
events.text: A warm wind blows through camp carrying tiny motes of light, and every wound in the party knits a little. By morning, everyone has regained an extra {1d4|1d6|1d8} hit points.

events.name: A glowing awakening stone
events.text: In the dark, something in the {roots of a tree|rocks by the path|bilge water} gives off a steady glow. It is an awakening stone nobody has noticed in years.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to tell what it does

events.name: The astral aperture
events.text: A thin crack of light opens in the air beside the camp for one hour. Through it, the party can see {a silver forest|a city of glass|an endless library}.
events.twist: Something on the other side sees them back, and waves.

events.name: The snow that rises
events.text: On a cold night, {snow|frost|ash} falls upward from the ground into the sky, slowly and silently. The ground underneath is warm.

events.name: Phoenix ember
events.text: A single feather of fire drifts down out of the night and lands in the campfire. The fire burns gold all night, and nobody has bad dreams.
events.twist: The feather does not burn away. It is still in the ashes at dawn.

events.name: The fire speaks
events.text: The campfire talks, in a crackling voice, about the things it has seen while burning in other camps. It knows {one secret about a rival|where a cache is buried|a monster's weakness}.

events.name: Stars spell a name
events.text: The stars swing into letters for a moment and spell out {npc}. Then they slide back as if nothing happened.
events.twist: The Magic Society would very much like a written record of this.

events.name: Light in the bones
events.text: The bones of a huge old monster near camp start to glow as the night deepens. By midnight, the outline of the living beast stands over them, grazing.

events.name: Shared rations
events.text: Another traveller's party camps nearby and has run out of food. If the party shares, they wake to find {their kit cleaned|their heidels groomed|a hand-drawn map of the road ahead} by way of thanks.

events.name: Fireside music
events.text: A wandering musician with a {lute|drum|pipe made from a monster bone} plays at the fire until late. The songs are sad and lovely, and everyone sleeps soundly afterwards.

events.name: The night-heron
events.text: A wounded heron limps into camp and lets the party bandage its wing. It sleeps by the fire. At dawn it flies, circles twice, and leads them toward the best path.

events.name: Honest watchmen
events.text: The party camps outside a hamlet and the local Iron-rank watch insists on taking a shift for them. They are serious, proud and very bad at whispering.

events.name: Letters home
events.text: In the quiet of the second watch, someone writes a letter to {family|an old friend|a rival}. The others offer to add a line. It turns into the funniest letter ever written.

events.name: The kids' fireflies
events.text: Children from a nearby farm creep out to watch the party's fire and catch fireflies in jars. They want to hear about {monsters|astral spaces|the biggest city in the world}.

events.name: Warm hands
events.text: A Smoulder {pedlar|pilgrim|soldier}, warm as a stove, offers to sit by the coldest party member all night. It's the warmest anyone has been in weeks.

events.name: Merfolk lullaby
events.text: Merfolk sing far off in the dark water, a slow lullaby that drifts over the deck. Even the sailors stop to listen, and nobody has bad dreams.

events.name: A Hearth blessing
events.text: A Hearth priest walking late blesses the party's fire with a pinch of salt. It burns all night on almost nothing, and the stew tastes like {home|a feast|a grandmother's cooking}.

events.name: The guest list
events.text: In the morning, someone has written the party's names in the {ashes|dew|sand} of the fire. There is one more name than there are people in the party.
events.twist: It is the name of someone who travelled with them before.

events.name: The extra breath
events.text: Lying in the dark, the person on watch counts the sleepers' breathing. There is one breath too many, and it is coming from {under the wagon|above them|right behind them}.

events.name: Faces in the smoke
events.text: The smoke from the fire forms faces as it rises. Each face looks at a different party member, mouths something, and blows away.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to make out the words

events.name: The camp left behind
events.text: The party finds a camp that matches their own: same bedrolls, same packs, still warm. Nobody is in it. Then they look back, and their own camp is empty.
events.twist: It is an astral space that has swallowed the night, and it will let them go at dawn.

events.name: A call for help
events.text: Somewhere in the dark, a child is crying for help. It is always the same distance away, whichever way the party walks.
events.check: Insight DC 15 to realise it is a lure
events.failText: the searchers come back hours later, cold and lost

events.name: The hanging lights
events.text: Lanterns hang from the trees all round the camp, lit, when the party wakes on second watch. Nobody hung them. They are all {facing inward|slowly turning|swinging in no wind}.

events.name: Coded fire
events.text: From the hilltop, the watch sees signal fires flickering on {three peaks|the coast|the far side of the valley}, passing a message along a line. Someone is coming.
events.check: History DC 13 to read the code
events.twist: The signal belongs to a noble house moving soldiers at night.

events.name: Night traffic
events.text: A line of {six|ten|twenty} carts passes on the road in the dark, unlit, wheels wrapped in cloth. The drivers nod at the party and don't say a word.
events.twist: They are smuggling Church of Liberty runaways out of reach of their buyers.

events.name: Lights under the water
events.text: Lights move under the water at night, in rows, like a street. Something down there is busy.
events.twist: It is a merfolk market, and they take visitors who can hold their breath.

events.name: A meeting in the dark
events.text: From a hiding place, the watch sees two cloaked figures meet nearby. One hands over a crate of monster cores. The other pays in {bronze coins|a sealed letter|nothing at all}.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 to get close enough to hear names

events.name: The open grave
events.text: A fresh grave stands open near camp, the earth piled neatly beside it and a shovel stuck upright. The headstone has no name yet.

events.name: A courteous burglar
events.text: The watch catches {a goblin|an elf|a very small} burglar in the packs, who apologises, puts everything back, and asks if there's anything the party wants taken from someone else.

events.name: The overnight clerk
events.text: A Society clerk arrives at midnight with a lamp and a ledger and asks to record the party's camp location 'for the survey'. He has walked here from {the nearest town|three valleys away|nowhere he will name}.

events.name: The night ferry
events.text: A ferryman rows up out of the dark and offers to carry the party across the water now, at night, for half price. He refuses to explain why.
events.twist: He rows them across a river that isn't on any map.

events.name: A cook in the night
events.text: Someone has cooked breakfast for the party while they slept: {eggs, bread and tea|fried fish|porridge with honey}, still hot. There are no tracks and no note.

events.name: Counting sheep
events.text: A shepherd's whole flock of {sheep|goats|tiny heidels} files past the camp at midnight, in perfect single file, with no shepherd. Each sheep pauses to look at the fire.

events.name: The sleep-talker's map
events.text: A party member draws a map in their sleep, in the dirt, with a stick. It is precise and labelled. They have never been to the place it shows.

events.name: Upside-down rain
events.text: Rain falls at night, but it lands on the camp from below, beading up out of the ground and dripping upward into the dark.

events.name: A clock in the trees
events.text: A loud ticking comes from the trees all night. In the morning, the party finds a grandfather clock standing among the trunks, perfectly on time.

events.name: The tent moves
events.text: Everyone wakes in the same places, but the tent is facing a different direction. It is also on the far side of the {stream|road|dune} from where they pitched it.

events.name: Shadow swap
events.text: Two party members' shadows swap in the night. Nobody notices until morning, when one shadow is clearly taller than its owner.
events.twist: It lasts until someone with a Dark essence asks them nicely to swap back.

events.name: Cheese moon
events.text: The moon tonight is a strange yellow and smells faintly, unmistakably, of cheese. Every {monster|dog|heidel} within ten miles is howling at it.

events.name: The upside-down tree
events.text: There is a tree nearby that grows down from the sky. Its roots hang in the air above camp, and its leaves brush the ground at dusk.
events.twist: Its fruit tastes of {lightning|mint|nothing at all}.

events.name: Dancing tools
events.text: In the dark, the party's tools clatter out of the packs and dance a slow, polite reel by the dying fire. They stop the moment anyone sits up.

events.name: The watch finds a thief's cache
events.text: On second watch, a shifting light leads the watch to a loose stone. Behind it: a thief's bag of {iron spirit coins|a Bronze monster core|forged Society badges}.

events.name: Shore treasures
events.text: The night tide leaves the beach strewn with shells, and among them a sealed {bottle|jar|lantern} and a chest the size of a loaf.
events.twist: The chest's owner is a merfolk merchant, and she will pay a finder's fee to get it back.

events.name: A friendly spirit's gift
events.text: A small spirit of the place visits the fire, accepts a scrap of food, and in return tells the party where the {spring|safe path|monster lair} is.

events.name: The night trade
events.text: A Drift Host trader camps nearby and wants to trade before dawn: cores, hides and steppe salt for anything shiny. The prices are good if the party haggles.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 for a good bargain

events.name: Spare provisions
events.text: A {supply cart|pedlar's wagon|Society cart} broke an axle near the camp and its driver has left. A note says 'Take what you need, the rest will spoil.' There is plenty.
events.twist: The driver comes back, and is very relieved somebody ate it.

events.name: Cores in the ash
events.text: The party's fire burns hotter than it should. In the ashes in the morning lie {two|three|four} tiny Iron monster cores, as if something burned up there in the night.

events.name: The last ration
events.text: The food is nearly gone. Someone has to go without {tonight|their share|supper}, or someone has to hunt in the dark.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to hunt at night
events.failText: everyone goes hungry

events.name: Watch of the stars
events.text: On the second watch, the stars slowly arrange themselves into a picture of {a tower|a monster|a face the party knows}. It lasts an hour.

events.name: The tower in the stars
events.text: The party reaches a hilltop and sees, far off, exactly the picture the stars drew. It is real.
events.twist: It is a Magic Society observatory, abandoned during the last surge.

events.name: The dawn chorus
events.text: The party wakes before dawn to birdsong so loud and joyful it is impossible to stay grumpy. Even the heidels seem to be humming.

events.name: A checkpoint
events.text: A checkpoint run by a noble house, charging a toll in spirit coins.

events.name: A Society call-up
events.text: A nearby region is surging. Every licensed adventurer passing through is ordered to help, and refusal is misconduct.

events.name: Purity zealots
events.text: Church of Purity zealots questioning travellers about cults, and sometimes the wrong travellers.

events.name: A fugitive hunt
events.text: An Adventure Society discipline officer tracking a fugitive adventurer.

events.name: Inspection
events.text: A tax collector, border patrol or harbour inspector who wants to see what the party carries.

events.name: A noble's census
events.text: A noble house's clerks are counting everyone on the road, with names, ranks and destinations, and they write it all down.

events.name: Bridge closed by order
events.text: A bridge closed by order of the local lord, with guards turning back everyone. A bribe or a good reason gets the party through.
events.check: Persuasion or Deception DC 13
events.failText: the long way round

events.name: Society inspection
events.text: An Adventure Society inspector checks everyone's badge and rank, and finds a clerical error on one of them.

events.name: The quarantine
events.text: A village under quarantine after a monster-borne plague. Soldiers turn everyone back, and nobody is allowed out.

events.name: Hunting the outlaw
events.text: A sheriff and his posse are hunting a dangerous outlaw and want to deputise the party. The outlaw may be innocent.

events.name: The new tax
events.text: A brand-new tax on 'travelling with too many swords'. The collector is making it up as he goes.

events.name: Requisitioned
events.text: Soldiers requisition one of the party's mounts or wagons for the war effort. Arguing is possible, but expensive.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15

events.name: Magic Society seal
events.text: Magic Society officials have sealed off a whole valley. Nobody will say why, and they want to search the party's packs for 'artefacts'.

events.name: Inquisitors of Truth
events.text: Church of Truth inquisitors stop the party and ask a single question each. They can tell when someone lies.

events.name: The duke's messenger
events.text: A messenger with the ducal seal, delivering a summons or an invitation to the party.

events.name: Border dispute
events.text: Two noble houses claim the same stretch of road and have each built a checkpoint, fifty feet apart, charging separate tolls.

events.name: A royal procession
events.text: A royal procession takes the whole road. Everyone must kneel at the roadside until it passes, which takes an hour.

events.name: The wanted poster
events.text: A wanted poster with a crude drawing of the party. The reward is insultingly small.

events.name: Guards in trouble
events.text: A patrol of town guards pinned down by monsters, asking the party for help. They'll owe a favour.

events.name: Customs search
events.text: Customs officers at a port searching every bag for smuggled cores and essences.

events.name: The corrupt magistrate
events.text: A magistrate charging travellers with crimes they didn't commit, then fining them.

events.name: Conscription
events.text: A surge has hit nearby, and the Adventure Society is conscripting everyone of the party's rank for a week.

events.name: The tired guard
events.nod: Skyrim: 'I used to be an adventurer like you, then I took an arrow in the knee'
events.text: An old checkpoint guard tells the party he was an adventurer once, until he took a {spear|crossbow bolt|very determined goose} to the knee.

events.name: Show your papers
events.nod: Bureaucracy humour and passport control
events.text: An outworlder runs a checkpoint with forms in triplicate, a rubber stamp he made himself, and a sign reading 'Please take a number'. It works horribly well.

events.name: A friendly patrol
events.text: A cavalry patrol escorts the party for the rest of the day. No encounter check tomorrow.

events.name: Badge check at the ford
events.text: Two Adventure Society wardens at the ford check every badge against a list. Anyone unlicensed carrying {weapons|monster parts|cores} is fined on the spot.
events.cost: 5 iron spirit coins per unlicensed person

events.name: Rank reassessment
events.text: A Society assessor on the road insists one party member's rank looks wrong and wants to test them here, now, against a caged {monster|training dummy|very bored Iron-ranker}.
events.check: Athletics or Arcana DC 13
events.failText: a note goes on their file

events.name: The overdue contract
events.text: A Society clerk stops the party with a list of contracts that went unfinished this season. One {Iron|Bronze} team on it is missing, last seen on this road.
events.twist: Their badges turn up on a market stall in the next town.

events.name: Contract board on a cart
events.text: A Society wagon with a contract board nailed to its side is posting local work as it goes. Most are small. One, to {clear a nest|find a lost child|guard a coin farm}, pays well and wants Iron-rankers today.
events.twist: The client is the Society wagon's driver, who has posted it himself.

events.name: Misconduct hearing
events.text: A Society discipline officer asks the party to witness a roadside misconduct hearing: an Iron-rank team accused of abandoning a {village|client|wounded teammate}.
events.twist: The team is telling the truth. Their client lied to the Society.

events.name: Marked as witnesses
events.text: The party saw a {fight|duel|shouting match} between two adventuring teams on the road. A Society officer takes their names as witnesses and says they will be called.

events.name: Called to testify
events.text: A Society rider catches up with the party: they are wanted at a hearing in the next town. One team will lose its licences on their word.
events.twist: A noble house offers a purse to remember things differently.

events.name: The licence fee
events.text: A Society clerk insists that the party's heidels need adventuring licences too, because they 'took part in combat'. He has the forms, and a little stamp shaped like a {heidel|heidel's left head|heidel's right head}.

events.name: Society recruiter
events.text: A cheerful Society recruiter is signing up {farmhands|fishermen|anyone with a pulse} as Iron-rankers, though most of them have one essence or none. He is paid by the name.

events.name: Quiet word from the director
events.text: A branch director rides out with {two guards|a hooded clerk|nobody at all} to speak to the party in private. She has a job that can't go on the board, and won't say why.
events.twist: The job is to quietly arrest one of her own officers.

events.name: Artefact registry
events.text: Magic Society clerks at a waystation are registering every magic item carried past. Registration is free. Refusing costs {a fine|a search|a night in the cells}.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to skip the queue
events.failText: a long wait in line

events.name: The confiscated core
events.text: Magic Society officers seize one of the party's monster cores 'for study', on the grounds that it is {unusual|the wrong colour|still warm}. They issue a receipt.

events.name: Return of property
events.text: A young Magic Society researcher finds the party with their seized core, a written apology, and a small purse of {iron|bronze} spirit coins. The core was very unusual indeed.
events.twist: She wants to know exactly where it came from, and will pay more.

events.name: Ritual in progress
events.text: Magic Society ritualists have closed the road while they seal a crack in the air. The crack hums. Anyone with {Arcana|a magical essence|a spare spirit coin} can help.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to help

events.name: Sample collectors
events.text: Two Magic Society researchers ask, very politely, for a lock of everyone's hair and a few drops of blood 'for the essence survey'. They pay an iron coin each.
events.twist: The survey is real. The second researcher is selling the samples on.

events.name: An array marked off
events.text: Ropes and Magic Society seals ring a natural array beside the path. A tired guard warns everyone off. The air above it glitters with drifting light.
events.twist: At midnight the array is unguarded, and it would charge any spirit coin left in it.

events.name: Purity questioning
events.text: Church of Purity zealots stop the party and walk round each person in silence, sniffing at them. They want to know who has {a Dark essence|absorbed a core|met an outworlder}.
events.check: Deception or Persuasion DC 15
events.failText: they take names and follow at a distance

events.name: Purity's second visit
events.text: The Purity zealots are back, with a priest whose eyes burn white. He knows exactly which party member they want, and asks them to come quietly.
events.twist: A Liberty priest has been watching too, and offers a way out.

events.name: A Justice tribunal
events.text: A Church of Justice priest is holding a court at a crossroads, with a gallows already built. The accused is a teenage {goblin|Smoulder|elf}. The evidence is thin.
events.check: Investigation or Persuasion DC 15 to prove him innocent
events.twist: The real culprit is in the crowd, cheering.

events.name: Truth at the gate
events.text: A Church of Truth priest stands at the town gate with an unshuttered lantern, asking each traveller one question. Today's question is {where are you going|who do you serve|what did you take}.

events.name: Healer quarantine
events.text: Church of the Healer priests have closed a village with a red cord. A {fever|rash|coughing sickness} is spreading. They need someone outside to fetch medicine from the next town.
events.twist: The fever was brought in on purpose by a rival village.

events.name: Dominion slave-takers
events.text: Men with Church of Dominion badges and a contract stamped in Rimaros are taking a {debtor|farmer's son|runaway sailor} in chains. The contract is legal there. Here, it may not be.
events.check: Persuasion or Intimidation DC 15
events.twist: The debtor's debt was bought up by a noble house to silence him.

events.name: Liberty's runaways
events.text: A Church of Liberty priest asks the party to say nothing about the family hidden in her cart. Riders are coming up the road behind them.
events.twist: One of the family is carrying something that belongs to the riders' master.

events.name: Hero's honour guard
events.text: A Church of the Hero honour guard stops the party, salutes, and asks to hear about their {last fight|worst wound|proudest moment}. They write it into a big book of deeds.

events.name: War church muster
events.text: A Church of War recruiting sergeant is counting anyone of fighting age on the road and offering a {bounty|new sword|hot meal} to sign up. He takes no for an answer, eventually.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12
events.failText: a long recruiting speech

events.name: The Journey's road wardens
events.text: Road wardens of the Church of the Journey are mending the road and handing out water. They tell the party which stretch ahead has turned dangerous.

events.name: House colours at the bridge
events.text: Guards in a noble house's colours hold the only bridge for miles. Anyone not on their list pays a toll in {iron coins|news|a song for the captain}.

events.name: The heir's escort
events.text: A noble heir on her first contract, {fifteen|nineteen|forty} years old, has her family's guards ordering travellers off the road so she can pass. She is mortified and wants to apologise to each of them.

events.name: A noble's lost signet
events.text: A house guard is searching the roadside for a signet {ring|seal|brooch} his lord dropped. If the party finds it first, they hold something a great house badly wants.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to find it
events.twist: The ring opens a vault, and the lord did not drop it. It was stolen.

events.name: The house remembers
events.text: A rider in house colours finds the party with a sealed letter. The family is grateful for the ring, and the letter is a promise of one favour.
events.twist: Another house has already heard about it.

events.name: Feuding patrols
events.text: Two patrols from feuding houses face each other across the road, {swords half drawn|crossbows cocked|insults flying}. Both demand the party say who started it.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to see who is lying
events.twist: Neither started it. A third house paid for the first stone.

events.name: The hunting party
events.text: A noble hunting party after {a stag|a rare monster|a lost bet} has closed the forest road for the day. Anyone who goes round loses time. Anyone who goes through risks being mistaken for the quarry.

events.name: Estate guards
events.text: The road crosses a walled estate's grounds. The guards let travellers through, but only after a search, and only on foot.
events.twist: One guard slips the party a note asking for help getting out.

events.name: Riders from the desert estate
events.text: Riders from a desert estate pass at dusk, hooded and silent, and stop to look long at the party's {youngest|healthiest|largest} member. Then they ride on.

events.name: The new bridge toll
events.text: A toll-keeper has put a chain across a bridge and charges by the leg: one coin for a person, two for a heidel. He has never seen a centipede monster, and is about to.

events.name: Harbour master's ledger
events.text: A harbour master boards the ship and goes through every {crate|barrel|hammock}. The ledger and the cargo don't match, and the captain looks at the party.
events.check: Deception or Persuasion DC 13
events.twist: The extra cargo is a crate of stolen cores, and the captain knew.

events.name: Salt tax
events.text: Tax collectors on the salt road weigh every pack and charge for any salt found. They are thorough, slow and {bored|hungry|suspicious of sugar}.

events.name: Counting the cores
events.text: A tax clerk insists on counting every monster core the party carries, then charges a tenth. He weighs each one on a tiny brass scale and writes its {colour|smell|mood} down.
events.cost: a tenth of the party's cores

events.name: Coin purity test
events.text: A Church of Trade assayer at the market gate tests travellers' spirit coins. One of the party's {iron|bronze} coins is a fake, and the assayer wants to know where they got it.
events.twist: The fake came from a Society payout.

events.name: A toll in rumours
events.text: A Cloud Clan chieftain's warden at the bridge takes no coin. The toll is news from below. Good news gets the party a guide for the next day.

events.name: Rumour of a new toll
events.text: Travellers say the lord of the next valley has started charging a toll for each {sword|boot|beard} carried on his road. The lord on this side has started charging for each shield.

events.name: The toll war
events.text: Both lords now charge tolls on every item: swords, shields, spoons. Their collectors stand side by side, glaring. Whoever the party pays first, the other is outraged.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to talk their way through both
events.failText: the full tolls, twice

events.name: Wanted for questioning
events.text: A town's notice board has a fresh poster for {theft|arson|unpaid tolls}, showing someone who looks a lot like a party member. Two watchmen are already walking over.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to sort it out
events.failText: a night in the cells

events.name: The posse
events.text: A sheriff and eight farmers with pitchforks ask the party to help catch whatever killed their {sheep|watchman|reeve} last night. They are frightened and well armed.

events.name: Hanging day
events.text: A town is holding a public hanging, and the road through the square is packed. The condemned {man|woman|goblin} shouts that he has proof hidden on the road the party just walked.
events.twist: The proof is real, and someone else is looking for it.

events.name: Curfew
events.text: A town is under curfew after dark. Anyone caught on the streets is fined, searched and sent back to their inn.
events.twist: The curfew is to hide what moves through the streets at night.

events.name: The sheriff's men
events.text: The local sheriff's men are taxing the poor down to their last copper. A cheerful archer in green is robbing the sheriff's tax cart in return, and asks the party to keep watch.
events.nod: Robin Hood and the Sheriff of Nottingham

events.name: Three questions at the bridge
events.text: An old bridge-keeper will let the party cross only if each of them answers three questions. The third question is always {impossible|about swallows|their favourite colour}.
events.nod: Monty Python and the Holy Grail: the Bridge of Death
events.check: Wisdom or Intelligence DC 12 each
events.failText: a very wet detour

events.name: Bread thief
events.text: A grim inspector of the watch has followed one ex-convict for nineteen years over a stolen loaf. He asks the party if they have seen the man. They have: he runs the orphanage they passed.
events.nod: Les Misérables: Javert and Valjean

events.name: The unnamed charge
events.text: Two clerks in grey arrest one party member on a charge they will not name. They are courteous. The trial will be held soon. Nobody can say where.
events.nod: Franz Kafka, The Trial
events.twist: The charge is real, and the clerks themselves don't know what it is.

events.name: Stop right there
events.text: A town guard shouts 'Stop right there, criminal scum!' at a party member who picked up a {loaf|cabbage|dropped spoon} in the market. He is very proud of the line.
events.nod: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion guards
events.cost: 1 iron spirit coin fine, or a chase

events.name: The magnificent robe
events.text: A lord rides through town in a robe so finely enchanted that 'only the worthy can see it'. His guards insist everyone admires it. He is wearing his {underclothes|nightshirt|socks}.
events.nod: Fairy tale: The Emperor's New Clothes
events.check: Persuasion or Deception DC 13 to admire it convincingly
events.failText: the party is thrown out of town

events.name: The tide-ordering lord
events.text: A coastal lord sits on a chair on the beach with his court, ordering the tide to stay back from his new {harbour|summer house|statue of himself}. The tide is not listening.
events.nod: The legend of King Canute and the tide
events.twist: He has spent the town's surge funds on the harbour.

events.name: The paladin who cannot lie
events.text: A young Justice paladin stops the party to report that one of them broke a minor rule {three towns ago|this morning|in their sleep}. He wants to arrest himself for not noticing sooner.
events.nod: D&D: the 'lawful stupid' paladin

events.name: Parking warden
events.text: An outworlder has painted lines on the road outside a market town and is fining heidel carts for stopping on them. He has a tiny notebook, a {peaked cap|whistle|clipboard} and no authority at all.
events.nod: Traffic wardens and parking tickets

events.name: Objection
events.text: An outworlder lawyer bursts into a roadside trial pointing and shouting 'Objection!' He wins the case with a contradiction nobody else spotted, and wants a fee of {five coins|a pie|the defendant's hat}.
events.nod: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney

events.name: Anything to declare
events.text: An outworlder customs officer at the harbour asks everyone if they packed their own bags and whether they are carrying {liquids|fruit|sharp objects}. She says it is how things are done properly.
events.nod: Airport security

events.name: Form A38
events.text: To pass, the party needs a permit from the clerk on the third floor, who sends them to the clerk on the first, who needs a form from the third.
events.nod: Asterix: the place that sends you mad (Permit A38)
events.check: Intelligence DC 15 to beat the system
events.failText: a lost half day

events.name: The unpaid piper
events.text: A town council refuses to pay the adventurers who cleared its {rat-monster|bat-monster|beetle} plague. The leader of the team, a thin man with a flute, says they will regret it.
events.nod: The Pied Piper of Hamelin

events.name: Not the ones
events.text: A cloaked woman at a checkpoint waves her hand at the guards and says these are not the travellers they are looking for. The guards agree, and wave the party on.
events.nod: Star Wars: 'These aren't the droids you're looking for'
events.twist: She wants a favour later.

events.name: Too sane to leave
events.text: The Adventure Society call-up excuses anyone too mad to fight. Anyone who asks to be excused is clearly sane, and so not excused.
events.nod: Catch-22
events.check: Persuasion DC 18 to talk round the clerk
events.failText: a day of drilling with the levies

events.name: Notice of demolition
events.text: Workmen are about to knock down the bridge ahead to build a faster bridge. The notice was on display for a year, in a locked {cellar|cupboard|privy} in a town office.
events.nod: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy: the bypass notice

events.name: None shall pass
events.text: A knight in rusted armour holds a narrow bridge and won't yield. He keeps fighting after every wound, insisting each one is only a scratch.
events.nod: Monty Python and the Holy Grail: the Black Knight
events.check: Athletics DC 13 to shove him aside, or Persuasion DC 15 to talk him down

events.name: The census of souls
events.text: An outworlder clerk is counting every traveller for a {duke|lord|church} 'so that everyone can be taxed', and he says his world did the same once, long ago, with famous results.
events.nod: The census in the Nativity story

events.name: Storm Kingdom envoys
events.text: Envoys from the Storm Kingdom travel the road in a fine coach, asking questions about the strongest people the party has met. They tip very well for names.
events.twist: They are also asking about the party.

events.name: A royal on contract
events.text: A young Celestine with metallic hair is on a contract with two bored guards in sapphire blue. He wants the party to tell him what adventuring is really like.
events.twist: Someone wants him dead before he gets home.

events.name: Yaresh harbour closed
events.text: The harbour is closed to ships from one realm, overnight and without warning. The party's ship flies the wrong flag.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15 to get a pass
events.twist: The harbour master would take a bribe, but someone is watching him.

events.name: Naval boarding
events.text: A {warship|coastguard cutter|merfolk patrol} comes alongside and orders the party's ship to heave to. Marines board and check papers, cargo and passengers.
events.check: Persuasion or Deception DC 13
events.failText: the whole day lost

events.name: Pirate-hunters
events.text: A privateer captain with a letter from a crown stops the ship and declares the party's {cargo|ship|lunch} enemy goods. The letter is real. The war is not.
events.check: History DC 13 to spot the war ended years ago
events.twist: He is a pirate himself, and the letter is stolen.

events.name: The Khan's tally
events.text: Riders of a Drift Host stop the party and ask their {ranks|names|essences}. A Khan's tally-keeper writes them down and says the Khan will want to meet the strongest.
events.twist: The Khan's rival will want to meet them too.

events.name: Greatback crossing
events.text: A whole Drift Host is crossing the party's path. The Khan's riders say nobody crosses the line of walking houses until the last one passes.

events.name: A chieftain's bridge
events.text: {A young|An one-eyed|A Silver-rank} Cloud Clan chieftain meets the party on a narrow rope bridge and asks what they can do for her village. The answer decides the rest of the climb.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13
events.failText: the long way round

events.name: Vitesse escort rules
events.text: Silver-rank wardens are keeping Iron and Bronze travellers in supervised groups, by order of the city. The party is assigned a chaperone, who is very strict about {lunch|posture|singing}.

events.name: Foreign coin refused
events.text: A {border town|fishing port|market village} refuses every coin the party carries, saying spirit coins are fine but these spirit coins are foreign. They are the same coins.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12
events.failText: a terrible exchange rate

events.name: Evacuation column
events.text: A whole {village|fishing town|mining camp} is walking the road the other way under Society guard, carrying what they can. A surge is rising behind them, and the guards want help bringing up the rear.

events.name: Road closed for the surge
events.text: Society wardens have closed the road ahead: the surge is flooding. Only teams of Bronze rank or above may pass.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15 to be let through

events.name: Monitors' camp
events.text: A Magic Society monitor team has a camp of brass instruments by the road. Every needle is pointing at the party.
events.twist: One of the party is carrying something that is feeding the surge.

events.name: Levies at drill
events.text: Every able-bodied farmer in the district has been called up to drill with spears on the green. The sergeant asks the party to show them how it's done.
events.check: Performance or Intimidation DC 12

events.name: Refugees at the gate
events.text: A town has shut its gates on refugees from a surge. The guards let in adventurers only. The refugees watch the party go in.
events.twist: A child slips in under the party's cloaks.

events.name: Society beacons
events.text: The Society has lit warning beacons along the hills. Every town is on alert, and travellers are searched for {monster parts|fever|cores} at every gate.

events.name: The plague cart
events.text: Healer priests are burning a cart of bedding from a fever village, and searching everyone who passed through it. The party did.
events.check: Constitution save DC 12
events.failText: a night in quarantine

events.name: The ghost tax collector
events.text: A ghost in an old tax collector's coat stops the party and demands a tax that was abolished {a century|two centuries|three hundred years} ago. He accepts payment in old coins only.

events.name: Construct at the gate
events.text: A brass construct guards a town gate and asks every traveller the same question, '{Why?|Whose?|How many?}', then stamps their hand. Nobody in town remembers who built it or what the stamp means.

events.name: A monster sheriff
events.text: The sheriff of this valley is an intelligent bear-like monster wearing a tin star. The villagers elected him. He takes the job very seriously and smells of {honey|fish|wet dog}.

events.name: The walking checkpoint
events.text: A checkpoint hut on chicken legs strolls along the road, stopping travellers at random. Its guard leans out of the window, bored, and asks for papers.

events.name: Self-writing warrant
events.text: A warrant nailed to a tree is rewriting itself as the party reads it. The name of the wanted person keeps changing, and settles on {one of the party|{npc}|the reader's mother}.

events.name: Bureaucrat in a jar
events.text: A Magic Society official's head speaks from a glass jar on a cart, issuing travel permits. His body, he explains, is back at the office, doing {the filing|lunch|its exercises}.

events.name: The oath-stones
events.text: Every traveller crossing into the valley must lay a hand on a standing stone and swear to keep the peace. The stone {hums|grows warm|laughs} if anyone lies.

events.name: The upside-down court
events.text: A court of law sits in a roadside meadow, and everyone in it, judge included, is standing on their head. 'Local custom,' says the bailiff. The accused is a goat.

events.name: A fish for a magistrate
events.text: The delta village's magistrate is a huge, ancient carp in the village pond. Disputes are shouted at the water, and the carp decides with bubbles.

events.name: Mirror sentry
events.text: A tall mirror on a post guards the pass. Each traveller's reflection steps out, checks their bags, and steps back in. The reflections are stricter than the people.

events.name: Astral permit
events.text: The Society has licensed an astral space entrance by the path. A warden with a ledger stands at its glowing door, selling a day's entry to teams of the right rank.
events.twist: Today the door shows {a frozen forest|a sunken city|a cloud palace}.

events.name: Divine seal
events.text: A village has been sealed by {a Purity|a Healer|an Earth} priest's divine power: a dome of pale light that nobody can cross. Inside, the villagers wave cheerfully. They do not know.
events.twist: The priest sealed them in to protect them from something outside.

events.name: The light-writ
events.text: A Church of Knowledge courier hands the party a writ written in light. It grants them free passage on the next {ferry|bridge|toll road}, but fades at sunset.

events.name: Summons by sending
events.text: Everyone in the party hears the same calm voice in their head: a Society director summoning them to the nearest branch {at once|within three days|after supper}.

events.name: The hearing
events.text: The Society branch director the party was summoned to see has a file on them, very thick, and a question. Someone has accused them of breaking the rules of a contract.
events.twist: The accuser is a rival team who took the contract instead.

events.name: Storm envoy's sky ship
events.text: A Storm Kingdom sky ship hangs over the road, its hull crackling with lightning. Officials lower a basket and ask the party to put any sealed letters in it.
events.twist: One of the party's letters vanishes and is never seen again.

events.name: Sea-judge
events.text: A Church of the Ocean judge rises out of the waves on a throne of water and asks the captain to account for a broken oath to the sea: {an unpaid offering|a drowned crewman|a stolen pearl}.
events.check: Persuasion or Religion DC 15
events.failText: the ship is becalmed for a day

events.name: Friendly reeve
events.text: The reeve of a small village meets the party at the boundary with {bread and salt|plum cake|a jug of beer} and a list of the village's troubles, in case they have time.

events.name: The fair magistrate
events.text: A magistrate in a roadside court throws out a farmer's case against a hungry boy, then pays for the boy's dinner out of her own purse.

events.name: Sheriff's thanks
events.text: The sheriff of the last town rides after the party to thank them for the help and hands them a {brass token|carved whistle|signed letter}. Any watchman in the district will see them right.

events.name: Watchmen with tea
events.text: Two old watchmen at the town gate have {a kettle|a pot of soup|a griddle of cakes} on and insist the party has a cup before anyone looks at their papers.

events.name: Pardon
events.text: A herald reads out a general pardon in the square to mark a noble {wedding|birth|recovery from illness}. Every unpaid fine on the road is forgiven, including the party's.

events.name: The patrol's guide
events.text: A delta patrol in green-stone boats offers to pole the party through the channels to their road, to save them the walk.

events.name: The watchers in white
events.text: Church of Purity faithful in white stand silent at every crossroad for a day's walk, watching the party pass. None of them speaks. All of them write something down, and {nod|frown|smile}.

events.name: The magistrate's smile
events.text: A smiling magistrate invites the party to dine with him. His staff never speak, never blink and serve the food very slowly.
events.twist: He is a cultist, and the staff are his dead.

events.name: The census of the dead
events.text: A Church of Death clerk is counting graves in the village churchyard and asks the party to count with him. There are {three|six|twelve} more graves this year than people who died.
events.twist: Someone is burying people who have only gone missing.

events.name: Faceless guards
events.text: The guards at this checkpoint all wear blank masks and speak in turn, one word each. They want to know where the party has been.
events.twist: They serve the Church of Disguise, and are looking for one of their own.

events.name: Bounty paid early
events.text: A Society bounty officer recognises a monster the party killed earlier from their description and pays the bounty on the spot, in {iron coins|a cheque on the branch|a good sword}.

events.name: The deputy's badge
events.text: A sheriff deputises the party for a day. The badge lets them requisition fresh heidels from any stable in the district.

events.name: Reward for the fugitive
events.text: A Society discipline officer is offering a fat reward for a missing adventurer. The party saw him, yesterday, going the other way.
events.twist: He is not a criminal. He is running from someone powerful.

events.name: Seized goods sale
events.text: A magistrate's bailiffs are auctioning seized smuggled goods by the road. Cores, essences and {odd gear|a cursed teapot|a crate of boots} go cheap, if the party bids sharply.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to spot the bargain

events.name: Grateful garrison
events.text: A border fort short on {food|salt|good cheer} buys the party's spare rations at three times the price and lets them sleep in the barracks.

events.name: Forms in triplicate
events.text: A town clerk needs the party to fill in a form saying they are not monsters. There is a box for each limb. Someone has ticked 'tentacles' on the example.

events.name: The polite arrest
events.text: A watchman arrests a party member for {humming in public|wearing the wrong colour|walking too quickly}, then apologises, lets them go, and asks for an autograph.

events.name: A sheriff on holiday
events.text: The local sheriff is on holiday. He has left his {eight|nine|ten}-year-old daughter in charge, with his badge and a very serious face.

events.name: Lord of the hamlet
events.text: A hamlet of six houses has its own lord, its own flag, its own army of one and its own customs post. They are very proud of all four.

events.name: The inspector of hats
events.text: An inspector stops every traveller to check their hat. Something about a law against {green feathers|tall hats|hats indoors}. Nobody has hats indoors on the road.

events.name: Sworn to silence
events.text: The guards at this fort have sworn a vow of silence for {Death|the Earth|Knowledge}. They wave the party through with very expressive eyebrows.

events.name: Interrupted wedding
events.text: A magistrate is marrying a couple at the roadside and needs two witnesses, right now. The bride's family is very large. The groom's family is a single goose.

events.name: The overzealous bailiff
events.text: A bailiff is seizing everything in a debtor's house, including his cat, which disagrees. He asks the party to hold the cat.

events.name: Letters of passage
events.text: A {courier office|town clerk|harbour master} will only stamp the party's letters of passage if they can prove where they were born. One of the party is an outworlder, and cannot.
events.check: Deception or Persuasion DC 13
events.failText: a wasted morning

events.name: Census of the trees
events.text: Two Lindover clerks are counting and tagging every tree in the forest. They want the party to stop leaning on the inventory.

events.name: Jungle fort
events.text: A Society fort on the jungle river charges a toll for safe passage upriver, and searches boats for {monster eggs|live samples|stolen relics}.

events.name: The river warden
events.text: A Leonid warden of the jungle river stops the party and asks them to carry a sealed report to the coast. It is about something climbing out of the deep jungle.
events.twist: The report is a lie meant to start a panic.

events.name: Tree-top tribunal
events.text: Jungle villagers have tied a {thief|liar|stranger} to a tree for the monsters, by order of their elders. He swears he was framed.
events.check: Insight DC 13
events.twist: He was framed by the elder's son.

events.name: Jungle permits
events.text: A Magic Society station at the jungle edge issues collecting permits for plants and monster parts. Anything collected without one is confiscated on the way out.

events.name: Papers at the river mouth
events.text: Guards on a {customs barge|stilt platform|green-stone tower} at the river mouth check every boat's papers and its passengers' names against a list.
events.twist: One name on their list is a party member's.

events.name: Mounted patrol
events.text: A mounted patrol of {six|ten|a dozen} heidel riders stops the party, asks where they are headed, and warns them off the {low road|eastern track|old bridge}.

events.name: Toll by weight
events.text: A toll-keeper weighs the party's packs on a great scale and charges by the pound. Whatever the party is carrying, it is too much.
events.twist: He has a thumb on the scale.

events.name: The search
events.text: Soldiers stop the party and search every pack. They are looking for {a stolen core|a runaway|forbidden books}, and they make a mess.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12 to hurry them along
events.failText: half a day repacking

events.name: Ferry inspection
events.text: The ferry won't leave until a Society warden has checked every passenger for monster bites. It takes {an hour|all morning|until the tide turns}. Nobody is bitten, except the warden.

events.name: A guard post at dusk
events.text: A lonely guard post on the edge of the {desert|marsh|steppe} wants to know the party's business. The two guards are glad of company and full of rumours.
events.twist: One of the rumours is about the party.

events.name: Fined for camping
events.text: A ranger fines the party for last night's camp: it was on a lord's hunting ground. The fine is small, but the ranger is writing names.

events.name: Ship's papers
events.text: A harbour clerk refuses to let the party land until the ship's captain pays a fee nobody has heard of. The captain looks to the party to help.
events.check: Persuasion or Intimidation DC 13

events.name: Desert well-wardens
events.text: The wardens of the only well for a day's walk charge {a coin|a song|a day's labour} for water. They are not open to argument.
events.twist: The well belongs to a house that is collecting debts in water.

events.name: Checking the brands
events.text: A Drift Host patrol checks every heidel the party has for the brand of a stolen herd. Horse thieves are hanged on the steppe. Heidel thieves are worse.
events.check: Animal Handling or Persuasion DC 13
events.twist: One of the party's heidels was sold to them stolen.

events.name: Society rank queue
events.text: A Society checkpoint lets Bronze-rankers straight through and makes Iron-rankers queue. The queue is long, and full of {people complaining|a pedlar selling pies|a bard}.

events.name: Gallows by the road
events.text: A gallows at the roadside holds {two|three|five} bodies, with a sign naming their crime: 'Cult'. One of them wears a Society badge.
events.twist: The badge belongs to someone the party has met.

events.name: The press gang
events.text: Sailors with clubs are taking men from the docks to crew a warship. They try to take a party member who looks like {a sailor|a deserter|an easy mark}.
events.check: Athletics or Intimidation DC 13

events.name: Burned village
events.text: A noble house's soldiers have burned a village they say harboured a cult. The villagers say they only harboured their own children.
events.twist: One survivor saw who really gave the order.

events.name: Debtors in chains
events.text: A line of {six|twelve|twenty} chained debtors is being walked to the coast to be sold, under a contract from Rimaros. One of them calls a party member by name.
events.twist: They were taken in Greenstone, where it is illegal.

events.name: The confession
events.text: A Church of Truth priest is hearing confessions at a crossroads. A Silver-ranker kneels and confesses to a murder, then walks away. Nobody stops him.

events.name: Sentence of exile
events.text: A town is driving a woman out under sentence of exile, with nothing. She was an Iron-ranker until she lost her badge. She asks to walk with the party.
events.twist: She was exiled for telling the truth about a noble.

events.name: A deputised escort
events.text: A sheriff deputises the party to take a prisoner to the next town for trial. The prisoner is a quiet, polite Runic who says he did it.

events.name: Delivering the prisoner
events.text: The town gallows are ready before the party arrives with their prisoner. The magistrate doesn't want a trial. The prisoner asks the party for a last kindness.
events.twist: He was confessing to protect someone.

events.name: Executions at sea
events.text: A naval ship is hanging pirates from its yardarm as the party's ship passes. The captain makes everyone watch, as is the custom.
events.twist: One of the pirates signals the party with his eyes, toward a hidden cargo.

events.name: The quarantine line
events.text: A cord of red rope runs for miles across the marsh. Beyond it, Healer priests and the sick. On this side, soldiers who shoot anyone crossing.

events.name: Dead inspector
events.text: A customs inspector lies dead in his hut at the border, with his ledger open. The last entry is the party's own description.
events.twist: Whoever killed him wanted the party blamed, and the watch is on its way.

events.name: Two rival sheriffs
events.text: Two sheriffs both claim this town. They split the badge between them, one wearing the star and the other the pin, and argue over every arrest.

events.name: Taxing the dead
events.text: A tax collector is charging a village for its dead, because the dead are 'still living on the land'. The village {Death priest|Hearth priest|elder} is furious.

events.name: The very old guard
events.text: The guard at this post is an elf who has stood here for four hundred years. He remembers when the road was a river. He has stamped every traveller since.

events.name: A goat's toll
events.text: The toll at this bridge is paid to a goat in a hat, by order of a long-dead lord's will. The goat takes {turnips|apples|hats}.

events.name: Banned colour
events.text: The local lord has banned the colour {blue|orange|green} for a week, to mourn his wife. His guards confiscate any found, including dyed hair.

events.name: Lost lord
events.text: A lord's hunting party is lost in the {jungle|marsh|desert}. The lord insists on giving the party orders, as if they work for him, while asking the way.

events.name: Society survey
events.text: A Society surveyor asks the party to rate their last contract from one to five, and to name the monster. She has a lot of forms.

events.name: The secret tax
events.text: A village pays a tax to a lord nobody has ever seen, collected by a hooded rider every new moon. He is due tonight.
events.twist: The lord is a monster the village feeds instead of reporting.

events.name: The rival investigator
events.text: A Church of Justice Avenger is investigating the same crime as the {Society|town watch|party}, and suspects the wrong person entirely.

events.name: Flag of truce
events.text: Two noble houses are holding peace talks under a tent by the road, and need a neutral party to carry messages between the tents.
events.check: Insight DC 15 to spot which side is stalling

events.name: Seized sky ship
events.text: A sky ship has been grounded by the town watch and chained to the field. The crew swear they are innocent. The captain offers passage if the party frees it.
events.check: Persuasion or Investigation DC 15 to clear them
events.twist: The crew are innocent of smuggling, and guilty of something worse.

events.name: Claims office
events.text: A Society claims office records who found which astral space first. Two teams are arguing over the same entrance, and want the party to settle it.
events.twist: Both teams forged their claims.

events.name: The disputed entrance
events.text: The disputed astral entrance is a door in a hillside, and it has a lock with a name carved in it. The name belongs to neither team.
events.twist: It belongs to someone who disappeared inside it fifty years ago.

events.name: The confused herald
events.text: A herald reads a royal proclamation to the empty road. It is {six|eleven|twenty} years old. He has been lost for most of them.

events.name: Sheriff's nephew
events.text: The new deputy is the sheriff's nephew, and he arrests the party for {loitering|existing loudly|looking suspicious} three times before lunch.

events.name: Tax on monsters
events.text: A collector tries to charge the party tax on the monster they just killed, as 'imported livestock'. He wants to see its papers.

events.name: Checkpoint cat
events.text: The checkpoint's real authority is a fat cat on the barrier. If it doesn't like a traveller, the guards won't let them through.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 12
events.failText: a long wait while the cat decides

events.name: Old soldiers
events.text: Retired soldiers from a {long-ago war|surge nobody talks about|border fight} keep a free shelter at the border for travellers. The party is welcome, and so are their stories.

events.name: Village thanks the watch
events.text: A village throws a small feast for its watchmen, who survived a monster attack, and invites the party to join. The watch captain toasts the adventurers who taught her to fight.

events.name: Healers' passage
events.text: Healer priests wave the party through a closed road ahead of the queue, because they saw {a wounded person|a limping heidel|blood} among them.

events.name: The silent checkpoint
events.text: A checkpoint at the edge of a ruin is fully staffed, the lamps lit and the barrier down. The guards are all asleep, and cannot be woken.
