events.twist: They have slept for a week, and are not getting any older.

events.name: The whispering warrant
events.text: A Society warrant for a dark-essence user is passed hand to hand along the road. When anyone reads it, they hear the fugitive whispering.
events.twist: The fugitive is close, and asking for help.

events.name: Contraband reward
events.text: Customs officers paid by the haul offer the party a cut if they point out smugglers on the ship. One of the passengers is clearly sweating.
events.check: Insight DC 13

events.name: A royal courier's charter
events.text: A courier carrying a royal charter needs company to {the coast|the next city|a noble estate}. Anyone escorting a royal courier travels toll-free and fed.

events.name: Society blessing
events.text: A Society director of Gold rank, passing the party, nods to them in greeting, and the weight of that much power in one person makes everyone feel very small.

events.name: The noble's ball
events.text: A herald invites the party to a noble ball tonight, on behalf of a house that wants to be seen with adventurers. Formal clothes are not optional.
events.twist: Another house wants the party there for a different reason.

events.name: A game trail
events.text: A game trail cuts through the rough ground in the right direction.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to follow it
events.failText: it peters out in a thicket

events.name: A shallow ford
events.text: The river is low enough to wade here instead of walking to the bridge.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: someone is swept downstream and has to be fished out, and the packs are soaked

events.name: A farmer's directions
events.text: A farmer swears there is a quicker way, if you know which hedge to turn at.
events.check: Persuasion DC 10 to get the real directions

events.name: Old waystones
events.text: Moss-grown waystones from an older road, straighter than the new one.
events.check: Investigation DC 14 to read them
events.failText: they lead to a ruin and stop

events.name: The scree slide
events.text: A long slope of loose scree, a fast way down for anyone sure-footed.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 14 for everyone
events.failText: 2d6 bludgeoning damage to whoever falls, but the party still gets down

events.name: Low tide
events.text: The tide is out, and the flats offer a straight line where the channels usually wind.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to judge the tide
events.failText: the water comes back early and the party wades back to land

events.name: Forced march
events.text: The ground is good and the party could push on into the night.
events.check: Constitution save DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: anyone who fails gains a level of exhaustion

events.name: A cleared path
events.text: Another team cleared monsters along this route a few days ago, and the going is easy.

events.name: A favourable wind
events.text: The wind is behind the party all day.

events.name: A ferry
events.text: A ferryman offers to take the party across a lake rather than around it.

events.name: A smugglers' tunnel
events.text: A tunnel through the hillside, marked with smugglers' scratches.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 to get through without meeting the smugglers
events.failText: the smugglers are home, and want a toll or a fight

events.name: A mapmaker's copy
events.text: A traveller sells a hand-drawn map of the region.
events.check: History DC 15 to tell whether it's any good
events.failText: it's a forgery and sends them the long way

events.name: A hidden goat path
events.text: Goats are using a path along the cliff that isn't on any map.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: someone slips and the party has to climb down to get them

events.name: The dry riverbed
events.text: A dry riverbed runs straight in the right direction, flat and easy.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to be sure it won't flood
events.failText: it floods, and they scramble out with soaked packs

events.name: A ferryman
events.text: A ferryman offers a crossing that saves the long walk round the lake.

events.name: A miller's lane
events.text: A miller lets the party cut through his property, if they help unload a cart first.

events.name: The old tunnel
events.text: An old mining tunnel goes straight through the hill. It's dark, cold and not quite empty.
events.check: Perception DC 14 to spot the danger
events.failText: they meet the thing living in the tunnel and run the long way round

events.name: Follow the river
events.text: Where the hills get steep, the party drops down to the riverbank and walks the flat ground beside the water instead.

events.name: A rope bridge
events.text: A rope bridge across a gorge saves a whole day's walk.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: the bridge gives way and they have to climb back

events.name: The tide road
events.text: At low tide, a causeway appears across the bay.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to time the tide
events.failText: the tide comes in fast, and everyone swims back

events.name: A cut through a crop
events.text: A straight line through a farmer's field. The farmer is less happy about it than the party.
events.check: Stealth DC 11 or Persuasion DC 13

events.name: A stone stairway
events.text: An ancient stairway carved straight up the cliff, glowing faintly. It shortens the climb impossibly.

events.name: A shortcut from a sprite
events.text: A tiny spirit offers to show the party a 'shorter way' in exchange for a song.
events.check: Performance DC 12
events.failText: the spirit didn't like the song, and the 'shortcut' leads into a bog

events.name: A beaver dam
events.text: A huge monster-beaver dam makes a walkable bridge over the marsh.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 11

events.name: A hunter's trail
events.text: A local hunter shows the party a trail she uses.
events.check: Persuasion DC 11

events.name: The forced march
events.text: The party can march through the night. Everyone gains a level of exhaustion, but they gain a day.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 for everyone, or gain a level of exhaustion

events.name: Wind at your back
events.text: A strong, steady wind at the party's back all day.

events.name: The pass is open
events.text: The snow has melted early on a high pass that is usually closed.
events.check: Survival DC 14
events.failText: the snow comes back, and they turn around

events.name: The hollow tree
events.nod: Fairy tales: a door in a tree to elsewhere
events.text: A door in a huge hollow tree opens onto the far side of the forest.

events.name: The underground river
events.text: A river vanishes into a cave mouth. A raft could take the party straight through the mountain.
events.check: Survival or Athletics DC 14
events.failText: the raft breaks up, and they wash out at the wrong side

events.name: A smuggler's signal
events.text: A lantern code from a hilltop: smugglers telling their friends the patrols are away. Someone who can read it learns the patrol road is clear.
events.check: Investigation DC 14 to work out the code

events.name: A shortcut that isn't
events.text: A sign reads 'SHORTCUT', with an arrow. It is a lie painted by an innkeeper on the long road.
events.check: Insight DC 12 to see through it
events.failText: they follow it straight to the innkeeper's door, the long way round

events.name: A goatherd's whistle
events.text: A goatherd {girl|boy|grandmother} whistles the party over and points out the ledge path her flock uses every day.
events.check: Persuasion DC 10
events.twist: Her goats insist on coming too, and eat anything left unattended.

events.name: The postrider's cut
events.text: A Society courier on a lean heidel shouts that the {hill|ridge|river} road is faster than the {valley|main|toll} road, then is gone in a cloud of dust.

events.name: Children who know the way
events.text: Village children race the party to the edge of the fields and insist on showing them the 'secret path' behind the {mill|chapel|pig sheds}. It is real.

events.name: A fisher's channel
events.text: An old fisher in a green-stone boat says the reeds part in a straight line if you know where to push. She will pole the party through for a {song|coin|good joke}.
events.cost: 2 iron spirit coins, or a song

events.name: The pilgrim's route
events.text: {An elderly|A barefoot|A singing} pilgrim of the Church of the Journey walks a route marked only by star-and-road symbols scratched into stones. She says it is older and straighter than the road.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to keep up with her
events.failText: they lose her marks at dusk and backtrack

events.name: The honest liar
events.text: Two {shepherds|sisters|drunks} give opposite directions, each swearing the other has never left the village. One of them is right.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to pick the right one
events.failText: they pick wrong and meet the other local's cousin, who laughs at them
events.twist: They are twins, and swap places when nobody is looking.

events.name: A Drift Host track
events.text: Deep, round prints the size of cart wheels: a greatback line passed here, flattening the grass for miles in the party's direction.
events.twist: The Host is still in sight ahead, and its outriders want to know who is following them.

events.name: A Cloud Clan runner
events.text: A Cloud Clan {runner|herder|child} steps off the path onto a patch of thickened cloud and beckons. The cloud holds, just, for anyone who walks lightly.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: someone sinks to the knee and the runner has to haul them back, tutting

events.name: The drover's lane
events.text: A wide, trampled drove lane runs between the hedges, used to move heidel herds to market. It is {muddy|dusty|cratered}, smelly and straight.

events.name: Ask the toll-keeper
events.text: A toll-keeper admits, for a coin, that the road loops round for no reason except that his grandfather owned the loop.
events.twist: The grandson wants the party's help selling the loop to someone else.

events.name: A merfolk pilot
events.text: A merfolk pilot surfaces beside the {boat|ship} and offers to lead it through the shoals by the fast channel, for a fair fee.
events.check: Insight DC 12 to judge her honest
events.failText: she takes the fee and leads them the long way, laughing

events.name: The tide-reader's word
events.text: A Drift Host tide-reader says the Wandering Tide is pooling to the {west|north|south}. The ground to the east is safe and quick, for now.

events.name: The ranger's blazes
events.text: Fresh {axe blazes|paint marks|knotted ribbons} on the trees mark a path cut by a Society ranger team last week.
events.check: Survival DC 11 to follow them
events.twist: The last blaze is fresh blood, not paint.

events.name: Grandmother's mule track
events.text: A grandmother on a two-headed heidel says she has taken the hill track to market for sixty years and will show the party, if they carry her {eggs|cheeses|very angry goose}.

events.name: The smuggler's boy
events.text: A boy offers to show the party 'the way the customs men don't know about', for a price, and is very keen they don't tell his uncle.
events.check: Stealth DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: they walk straight into his uncle's crew, who are not pleased

events.name: A guide who talks
events.text: A local guide knows a quick route and cannot stop talking about his {divorce|bunions|theory that the moon is hollow}. The route is good. The company is not.
events.check: Wisdom DC 12 to listen politely all day
events.failText: someone snaps at him and he sulks, so they lose an hour finding the last turn

events.name: A drowned road
events.text: An old paved road runs under a shallow {lake|flood|mere}, its stones clear beneath the water. Something keeps pace with the party just below the surface.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: something tugs an ankle and they flounder back to shore
events.twist: It is a drowned village's lord, still walking his road.

events.name: The aqueduct walk
events.text: A broken aqueduct strides across the valley, its channel dry and wide enough to walk along, high above the rough ground.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 12 at the gaps
events.failText: a span is missing and they climb down the long way
events.twist: Water starts to trickle along the channel behind them.

events.name: A legion road
events.text: Under the grass lies an old {military|imperial|pilgrim} road, ruler-straight. Find the edge stones and follow them.
events.check: Investigation DC 12
events.failText: the stones fade into the turf

events.name: The empty town
events.text: The road runs through a town abandoned in the last {surge|plague|war}. Its streets are a straight line, if the party can stand walking past the open doors.
events.twist: One door is closed, with a fresh meal on the table.

events.name: A collapsed bridge
events.text: A stone bridge has {fallen|been washed out|been smashed by something big}, but its piers still stand in the river like stepping stones.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: someone falls in and the packs need drying
events.twist: A troll is sitting under the last pier, looking for work.

events.name: The quarry railway
events.text: A rusting cart-rail from an old green-marble quarry runs downhill in the party's direction. One cart still rolls.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 to brake it
events.failText: the cart jumps the rails at the bottom, spilling everyone into a gorse bush, but still ahead
events.twist: The cart is full of green marble, and the quarry wants it back.

events.name: A watchtower line
events.text: A chain of ruined watchtowers runs along the {ridge|coast|old border}. From the top of each, the next is in sight.
events.check: Perception DC 11

events.name: The stair of kings
events.text: A stair of {green marble|white stone|black glass} climbs the cliff in a single sweep, each step worn by a thousand years of feet that are no longer here.
events.twist: Halfway up, a stone throne faces the view. Something is sitting in it.

events.name: The tunnel of names
events.text: A road tunnel through the ridge. Its walls are covered in names scratched by everyone who passed. Some names are the party's.
events.twist: The names are in each party member's own handwriting, dated next year.

events.name: Paving under the sand
events.text: The wind has scoured a dune away, showing old {paving stones|marble slabs|glazed tiles} heading straight across the desert.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to follow it before the sand returns
events.failText: the sand covers it by noon and they wander
events.twist: The road leads past a half-buried statue with a fresh flower in its hand.

events.name: A road of milestones
events.text: Every milestone on this old road gives a different {distance|name|date} to the same town. One of them is accurate.
events.check: History or Investigation DC 13
events.failText: they trust the wrong one

events.name: The sunken causeway
events.text: A causeway of green stone lies a hand's depth under the marsh water. Probe ahead with a pole and walk.
events.check: Survival DC 12
events.failText: they step off the edge into black water and climb out filthy

events.name: A temple path
events.text: A ruined Church of the Earth temple has a pilgrim path straight through the hills, still marked with carved stones that {hum|glow faintly|feel warm} underfoot.

events.name: The dead road
events.text: A straight road no one uses. Locals say it was built for {funeral carts|plague carts|a dead king's procession}. The party has it to themselves, and the crows.

events.name: A coin farm road
events.text: A paved service road to {an abandoned|a bankrupt|a monster-wrecked} spirit coin farm. Hard-packed, well drained and empty.
events.twist: The farm's last iron coins are still in a hopper by the gate.

events.name: The ruined lighthouse stair
events.text: A ruined lighthouse on the point has an inner stair down to the beach, cutting off the long walk round the headland.
events.check: Athletics DC 11

events.name: Speak and pass
events.text: A sealed door in the mountainside, carved with the words 'Speak, friend, and pass'. Beyond it, a dry road runs straight through the rock.
events.check: Intelligence DC 14 to see the answer
events.failText: they argue about riddles until dusk and go round
events.nod: The Lord of the Rings: the doors of Moria
events.twist: Something on the far side answers too.

events.name: A road of yellow brick
events.text: A road of glazed yellow bricks appears in the grass, running straight to the horizon. It is warm underfoot and nobody local has seen it before.
events.nod: The Wizard of Oz: the yellow brick road

events.name: The green pipe
events.text: A huge green pipe pokes out of the hillside, wide enough to climb into. A hollow 'bloop' sounds whenever a stone is dropped in.
events.check: Wisdom DC 12 to dare it
events.failText: nobody is brave enough today
events.nod: Super Mario: warp pipes
events.twist: Whoever goes first pops out of a pipe miles ahead, wearing a stranger's red cap.

events.name: Do not take the mines
events.text: A map left on a cairn by another team. Someone has written 'TAKE THE MINES' and someone else 'DO NOT TAKE THE MINES'. They both signed it.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to work out who was right
events.failText: they take the mines
events.nod: The Lord of the Rings: the fellowship arguing over the pass and the mines

events.name: Rabbit with a watch
events.text: A white hare in a waistcoat checks a tiny watch, mutters that it is late and bolts into a hedge. There is a tunnel behind the hedge.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 to keep up
events.failText: they get stuck in the tunnel and back out, scratched
events.nod: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland: the White Rabbit
events.twist: The hare is late for a tea party, and it wants company.

events.name: Seven-stride boots
events.text: A pedlar rents boots that cover a mile with every seven steps. They only work for the day and they pinch terribly.
events.cost: 1 bronze spirit coin for the party
events.nod: Fairy tales: seven-league boots
events.twist: Someone goes seven strides too far and has to walk back an hour.

events.name: The rainbow bridge
events.text: After the rain, a rainbow arches over the gorge and stays solid enough to walk on. It is fading fast.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 for everyone, and hurry
events.failText: it fades mid-span and they scramble back
events.nod: Norse myth: Bifrost, the rainbow bridge

events.name: The ferryman's coin
events.text: A silent, hooded ferryman waits at a dark river and holds out a hand. He wants one coin for each of them, placed on the tongue.
events.nod: Greek myth: Charon, ferryman of the dead
events.twist: On the far bank, the party's reflections are a moment late.

events.name: Breadcrumbs
events.text: A trail of breadcrumbs runs through the trees in a perfectly straight line. Birds have eaten most of it.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to follow what is left
events.failText: the trail ends at a gingerbread-scented clearing that the party decides to leave at once
events.nod: Hansel and Gretel

events.name: A barge going downstream
events.text: A {grain|timber|monster-hide} barge is heading the party's way and the bargemaster wants extra hands on the poles.

events.name: The green-stone raft
events.text: A half-sunk green-stone boat lies in the {reeds|mud|mangroves}. Bail it out and it floats, as the stone always does.
events.check: Athletics DC 11 to bail and pole it

events.name: The cable ferry
events.text: An unmanned {ferry raft|basket|rowboat} hangs on a cable across the river. Haul yourselves over.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for two of the party
events.failText: the cable sticks halfway and it takes an hour to free it
events.twist: The ferry's owner turns up on the far bank and wants paying.

events.name: A frozen river
events.text: The river has frozen hard enough to walk along, a flat white road between the trees.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to read the ice
events.failText: someone goes through to the waist and they need a fire

events.name: A canal lock
events.text: A Church of Trade lock-keeper will let the party through on the canal barge, but only if they can recite the {lock fee schedule|seven lock blessings|names of her cats} back to her.
events.check: Intelligence DC 12
events.failText: she makes them wait for the next barge, which takes hours

events.name: Riding the flood
events.text: Last night's flood carries wreckage downstream at speed. A {roof|barn door|hay wagon} floats past. So does a body.
events.check: Athletics DC 14 to ride the roof
events.failText: the roof breaks up and they swim for the bank
events.twist: The body is alive, and very grateful.

events.name: An eel-pond dyke
events.text: The dykes between the eel ponds make narrow, raised paths straight across the wet ground.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 10

events.name: The river spirit's ford
events.text: A river spirit, shaped like a heron of water, offers to hold back the current while the party crosses. It wants a story it hasn't heard.
events.check: Performance or Persuasion DC 13
events.failText: it has heard that one, and lets the current go mid-crossing

events.name: A log jam
events.text: {Logs|Drowned trees|Monster bones} have jammed across the river from bank to bank. They look solid.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: the jam shifts and someone takes a cold swim

events.name: The flats at dawn
events.text: At dawn the delta mist lies flat on the mudflats. A line of posts shows a crossing that only exists at the lowest tide.
events.check: Nature DC 13
events.failText: the tide turns early and they wade back through the mist
events.twist: One post is a person, standing perfectly still in the mist.

events.name: Swim the strait
events.text: The ferry {sank|was eaten|went on strike} last week. The strait is narrow and cold, and swimming it saves a day round the bay.
events.check: Athletics DC 14 for everyone
events.failText: someone has to be dragged back, half-drowned, and they take the long road

events.name: The warm current
events.text: The water turns {warm and blue|green and clear|dark and quick}, and the ship picks up speed: a current running the right way.
events.check: Nature or navigator's tools DC 13 to stay in it
events.failText: they slip out of it by noon
events.twist: It is warm because something huge sleeps beneath it.

events.name: A reef gap
events.text: A gap in the {reef|sandbar|rocks} saves sailing round it, if the helm is steady.
events.check: Dexterity with vehicles (water) DC 14
events.failText: the hull scrapes, and they spend the afternoon on repairs

events.name: The night wind
events.text: A steady {land breeze|warm wind|cold wind} rises after dark. Sailing through the night uses it, at the cost of sleep.
events.check: Constitution DC 12 for the crew

events.name: Following the whales
events.text: A pod of island-sized {whales|turtles|rays} passes, riding a deep current. A ship in their wake is carried along with them.
events.check: Nature DC 13 to keep the right distance
events.failText: a tail-slap throws the ship off course
events.twist: One whale has a hut on its back, and someone waves.

events.name: The tide race
events.text: The tide is running hard through the channel between two {islands|headlands|rocks}, and it is running the party's way.
events.check: Nature DC 12 to time it
events.failText: they hit it at the turn and fight it for hours

events.name: A channel through the islands
events.text: A fisherman's chart shows a channel between the islands that the big ships can't use. A small one can, just.
events.check: Dexterity with vehicles (water) DC 13
events.failText: they run aground and wait for the tide
events.twist: Someone has strung a toll chain across the narrowest point.

events.name: The storm's edge
events.text: A storm is passing to the {south|north|east}. Sailing its edge gives a howling, fast wind and a very wet crew.
events.check: Constitution DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: the crew are exhausted, and the ship has to heave to

events.name: The merfolk road
events.text: Merfolk buoys of carved {coral|driftwood|whalebone} bob in a line across the sea. Merfolk use them to mark a fast current, and they don't mind ships following.
events.twist: The buoys warn of something too, in merfolk script.

events.name: Kelp lanes
events.text: A field of giant kelp has grown in perfectly straight rows, as if someone planted it. The open water between the rows is calm and fast.
events.twist: Someone did plant it, and their sea-farmers want a word about the trespass.

events.name: A sea-spirit's dare
events.text: A laughing {sea-spirit|water elemental|spray-shaped child} races the ship, and promises a fair wind if the crew can outsail it for an hour.
events.check: Dexterity with vehicles (water) DC 14
events.failText: the spirit wins, and sulks off with the wind

events.name: The trade wind
events.text: The ship finds the trade wind at last. It blows steady from behind, day and night.

events.name: Through the fog bank
events.text: A fog bank lies across the course. Going round costs half a day. Going through means sailing blind, listening for {breakers|bells|gulls}.
events.check: Perception DC 14
events.failText: they hear bells in the fog where there is no land, and turn back
events.twist: A ghost ship sails beside them for an hour, then turns away.

events.name: The Storm Kingdom lanes
events.text: A Storm Kingdom patrol ship signals the party to follow it down a cleared shipping lane, swept of sea monsters this week.

events.name: Wind-knots
events.text: A sea-witch on the dock sells a cord with three knots. Untie one for a breeze, two for a gale. Never untie the third.
events.nod: Northern sea folklore: wind sold in knotted cords
events.twist: Someone in the crew is very curious about the third knot.

events.name: The tow
events.text: A merchant ship with a giant {sea turtle|eel|crab} in harness is happy to throw the party a line, for a share of the work keeping the turtle fed.
events.twist: The turtle eats a third of the ship's stores by evening.

events.name: The current under the ice
events.text: A floe field shows one clear streak of black water through it, moving fast. Something under the ice keeps it open.
events.check: Nature DC 14
events.failText: the streak closes behind them and they break free the hard way

events.name: Becalmed, then not
events.text: The ship is becalmed by morning. Rowing out of the dead air reaches a breeze by afternoon.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for everyone at the oars
events.failText: they row all day and get nowhere

events.name: Gulls over the shoal
events.text: Gulls wheel over a patch of water: a shoal of fish, and beneath it a fast cold current running {north|south|east}.
events.check: Survival DC 11
events.twist: The fish are fleeing something.

events.name: Ride the bore
events.text: The tide is coming up the estuary as a single wave. A boat that catches it right surfs inland at a gallop, and everyone screams.
events.check: Dexterity with vehicles (water) DC 13
events.failText: they catch it wrong and spin in circles for an hour
events.twist: A merfolk surfer is already riding it, and is cross about sharing.

events.name: The sky ship's wake
events.text: A sky ship passes low over the sea, and its wind-arrays leave a long trail of following breeze behind it.

events.name: Sail by the stars
events.text: Clear skies all night. A good navigator can hold a straighter course by the {stars|moon|Celestine Lantern constellation} than by the coast.
events.check: Survival or navigator's tools DC 13

events.name: A shoal of glowing jellies
events.text: At night the sea lights up {blue|green|gold} with jellyfish drifting the same way, all marking the same current.

events.name: The dead calm channel
events.text: A channel through the rocks where the water is glass-flat and no birds fly. It is quick. It is also silent.
events.twist: At the far end, every sailor's reflection is one breath behind.

events.name: The fisher fleet
events.text: A {fishing fleet|whaling fleet|merfolk family} heading home invites the ship into the middle of their convoy, safe from sea beasts, along the fast current they use.

events.name: A storm-priest's blessing
events.text: A Church of the Storm priest aboard calls a hard wind into the sails, {grinning|singing|cackling}. The crew is less happy.
events.check: Dexterity with vehicles (water) DC 13 to handle it
events.failText: the wind tears a sail, and they limp on slower
events.twist: She has called more storm than she meant.

events.name: The Ocean's road
events.text: A Church of the Ocean shrine buoy rings as the ship passes. The priest aboard says the god's road runs this way today.
events.twist: The road leads past a merfolk shrine that wants an offering.

events.name: The whirlpool slingshot
events.text: A {whirlpool|maelstrom|spinning eddy} turns slowly on the course. Skimming its edge can throw the ship out the far side at speed.
events.check: Dexterity with vehicles (water) DC 15
events.failText: it spins them round twice and spits them out backwards

events.name: Outworlder at the ford
events.text: An outworlder at a river crossing gravely warns the party to 'ford the river' and never caulk the wagon. He also asks if anyone has dysentery.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for everyone to wade it
events.failText: someone is swept away and the packs float off
events.nod: The Oregon Trail: fording the river and 'you have died of dysentery'

events.name: An astral fold
events.text: The air ahead ripples like heat haze: a fold where an astral space brushes the world. Step through and the far side is miles on.
events.check: Arcana DC 14 to find the edge
events.failText: they step into the wrong fold and walk out where they started, an hour later
events.twist: Someone steps through and comes out a day younger, slightly.

events.name: A natural array
events.text: {Standing stones|Old trees|Rock pillars} form a natural array that hums when the party stands in it. Anyone who walks its line feels lighter, faster and slightly sick.
events.check: Constitution DC 11 or spend the evening queasy

events.name: The Journey's waystone
events.text: A waystone of the Church of the Journey glows with a winding road beneath a star. A traveller who prays there knows the straightest way for a day.
events.check: Religion DC 12

events.name: A borrowed blessing
events.text: A travelling Journey priest shares Swift Feet with the party for the morning. The miles fly by under them.
events.twist: She asks them to carry a sealed letter to her sister at the next town.

events.name: The misty step stone
events.text: An awakening stone of misty step lies in a {shrine bowl|hollow tree|niche}, with a note: 'For the road. Put back.' Using its power for a day saves the climbs and ditches.
events.check: Arcana DC 13 to use it without absorbing it
events.failText: nobody can make it work, and they put it back sheepishly
events.twist: The note's author is waiting to make sure they do put it back.

events.name: Surge-quickened ground
events.text: The magic is so thick here that the ground seems to slide under the party's feet. Every step goes a little further than it should.
events.twist: So do the monsters' steps.

events.name: A lost spirit's path
events.text: A pale spirit of a long-dead {traveller|pedlar|courier} walks ahead, beckoning. It knows a quicker way and has been waiting a long time to show someone.
events.check: Wisdom DC 13 to keep following without fear
events.failText: someone panics and they lose the spirit in the dark
events.twist: At the end, the spirit asks the party to bury the bones it shows them.

events.name: The compass that points ahead
events.text: A battered compass found by the way does not point north. It points, firmly, at the party's destination.
events.twist: It started pointing somewhere else at midnight.

events.name: A bargain with the wind
events.text: A wind spirit circles the party, curious. It will push them along all day in return for a {name|song|secret} it can keep.
events.check: Persuasion DC 14
events.failText: it takes offence at the name offered and leaves
events.twist: Whoever gave the name hears it whispered on every breeze for a week.

events.name: The lantern of the way
events.text: A Church of Truth lantern hangs from a branch, unshuttered. Its light shows only true paths and makes false ones vanish.
events.twist: Held up to a party member, it shows a false path in them.

events.name: A sky ship's ladder
events.text: A sky ship drifts low, and a rope ladder drops. The captain will give them an afternoon's lift if they pay the {crew|cook|navigator}.
events.twist: The captain is changing course for {place}, and wants company.

events.name: A cloud skiff for hire
events.text: A {cheerful|nervous|very young} pilot with a cloud skiff, a raft of thickened cloud, offers to float the party over the worst of the ground.
events.cost: 1 bronze spirit coin for the party
events.twist: The pilot is new, and the skiff has a slow leak.

events.name: The confluence trick
events.text: One party member's essences hum in this place, and their confluence power works twice as well. The others just have to keep up.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for everyone else

events.name: A shrine of the Revels
events.text: A Church of the Revels shrine promises 'a quick way to the next party'. A painted arrow points down a hill. There is a {wheelbarrow|tea tray|large cheese wheel}.
events.check: Dexterity DC 13 to steer
events.failText: the wheelbarrow wins

events.name: A teleport gate, broken
events.text: A broken teleport array stands in a ruin. It still works, a little. It moves anyone who stands in it exactly one mile, in a random direction.
events.check: Arcana DC 15 to aim it
events.failText: it drops them in a pond a mile the wrong way
events.twist: It moves a cow in from somewhere, every time.

events.name: A Celestine's sense
events.text: A Celestine traveller with eyes like {brass coins|silver mirrors|polished copper} says she can feel the astral currents. She points out the way they run, which is the party's way.

events.name: The road that walks
events.text: A stretch of old road has come loose from the land and is crawling slowly forward like a stone snake. It's faster than walking.
events.twist: It is going somewhere, and is very determined.

events.name: Through the astral space
events.text: An Adventure Society-licensed astral space has two doors, miles apart. The clerk on duty will let the party cross through for a fee and a signature.
events.twist: The inside rule today: nobody can speak above a whisper.

events.name: A witch's broom loan
events.text: A {hedge-witch|retired cleaner|Hearth priest} lends the party her spare brooms. They do not fly. They do sweep the path clear of brambles at remarkable speed.
events.twist: The brooms keep sweeping after she takes them back.

events.name: The fast-travel stone
events.text: A Journey priest at a waystone can send the party ahead in a flash, but grumbles that he 'can't do it while enemies are nearby'.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to find the monster sulking in the bushes
events.failText: they can't find it, and walk
events.nod: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, 'You cannot fast travel when enemies are nearby'

events.name: The wardrobe
events.text: A wardrobe stands alone in a ruined inn. Inside, past the moth-eaten coats, there is snow, and a lamp-post, and a path that comes out miles on.
events.nod: The Chronicles of Narnia: the wardrobe

events.name: The invisible bridge
events.text: A chasm, and on the far side a carved hand pointing down. A pinch of thrown dust shows the stone bridge nobody can see.
events.check: Wisdom DC 14 for whoever steps first
events.failText: nobody will trust it today
events.nod: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade: the leap of faith

events.name: A speedrunner
events.text: An outworlder in strange shoes insists the party can 'clip through' the hillside if they walk into one exact crack backwards. She calls it a sequence break.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 15
events.failText: three people get stuck in the crack and need pulling out
events.nod: Speedrunning culture: sequence breaks and clipping through walls

events.name: Just ride the birds
events.text: An outworlder is furious that nobody here ever just rides the giant condors over the mountains, 'like in Lord of the Rings'. A Cloud Clan tamer hears him and shrugs.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 15
events.failText: the condor declines, and so does the tamer
events.nod: The Lord of the Rings: 'why didn't they just fly the eagles?'

events.name: The door that opens one way
events.text: A heavy gate in a cliff wall, locked from the far side. Climb round, open it, and the next traveller has a shortcut forever.
events.check: Athletics DC 14
events.failText: the climb is too much, and they go the long way
events.nod: Dark Souls: one-way doors and shortcuts opened from the other side

events.name: A greatback's wake
events.text: A lone wild greatback has been walking ahead, flattening a path of {grass|scrub|young wheat} wide enough for a cart.

events.name: The heidel herd
events.text: A herd of wild heidels is migrating the same way. Their trail cuts straight through the scrub.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 12 not to spook them
events.failText: they stampede and scatter the party's packs
events.twist: A calf has lost its herd and adopts the party.

events.name: A burrower's tunnel
events.text: A round tunnel, perfectly smooth, bores into the hillside: a giant {worm's|beetle's|mole's} old tunnel, going the party's way.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to tell whether it is really old
events.failText: it is not old, and they run

events.name: Monster-cleared ground
events.text: A Silver-rank monster passed through last night. It flattened the {forest|undergrowth|trees} and scared everything else off. The going is easy and very quiet.

events.name: The ant highway
events.text: Giant {ants|beetles|termites} have cut a road through the jungle, smooth and clear. They are very busy, and they do not care about the party as long as nobody stops.
events.check: Dexterity DC 12 not to get in their way
events.failText: someone treads on one, and the column turns to chase them out
events.twist: The ants are carrying a person, wrapped and alive.

events.name: Riding the turtle
events.text: A huge, slow river turtle is crossing the lake and doesn't seem to mind passengers. It does mind {singing|boots|anyone called Gerald}.

events.name: A tamed sand-lizard
events.text: A desert trader's sand-lizards need exercise, and he'll let the party ride them to the next {well|oasis|town}.

events.name: Follow the goats
events.text: Wild mountain goats file along a cliff in the right direction, never putting a hoof wrong.
events.check: Athletics DC 14 for everyone
events.failText: the goats can do it and the party can't

events.name: The condor's path
events.text: A giant condor circles low, then flies in a straight line down a valley the map doesn't show. Cloud Clan folk say to follow where the birds go.

events.name: Dolphins at the bow
events.text: Dolphins ride the bow wave and pull ahead, then wait, as if leading the way. They are, into a fast current.

events.name: A monster bridge
events.text: The skeleton of a huge {monster|serpent|Gold-rank beast} lies across the ravine, its spine a bridge. Its bones are still being picked clean.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 13
events.failText: the bone-pickers object
events.twist: There is a core still lodged in one of the vertebrae.

events.name: The sea serpent's trail
events.text: A wide band of smooth water stretches ahead, where something long swims just under the surface. It is going the same way.
events.check: Wisdom DC 14 to follow it calmly
events.failText: it notices them, and they veer away fast
events.twist: It is a mother, and she has young nearby.

events.name: A fox who knows
events.text: The same {red|white|three-tailed} fox appears ahead of the party three times, each time looking back. A local says foxes on this road always know the quick way.
events.check: Survival DC 12 to follow it

events.name: The wyvern's thermals
events.text: Wyverns are riding a thermal off the cliffs. The wind that lifts them is perfect for a cloud skiff or a sky ship.
events.twist: One wyvern decides to race them.

events.name: The uncle's toll
events.text: The smuggler boy's uncle catches up, furious, then admits the boy chose well and offers his own route for a bigger fee.

events.name: The sky ship again
events.text: The sky ship from before drops its ladder once more. The captain needs an escort past {faction} waters and will carry the party free for it.

events.name: The Tide turns
events.text: The tide-reader was right. {Smoke|Dust|Monster-light} rises to the west where the Tide pooled, and the party's road east is quiet and fast.

events.name: The pilot's cousin
events.text: The merfolk pilot's cousin finds the ship and says she was sent to lead it through the next stretch, at family rates.

events.name: The pilgrim's last mark
events.text: The pilgrim's star-and-road marks lead to a shrine where the path folds on itself. A prayer there carries the party a full mile in a step.
events.check: Religion DC 12

events.name: The heron returns
events.text: The water-heron spirit finds the party again. It liked their story so much it wants another, and offers a quick path through the reeds.

events.name: The third knot
events.text: Someone has untied the third knot. The gale is tremendous. The ship goes very fast in a direction that is almost the right one.
events.check: Dexterity with vehicles (water) DC 15
events.failText: they are blown wildly off course

events.name: The guide's wife
events.text: The talkative guide's wife catches up on a heidel, with a quicker route, and her own side of the story.

events.name: Push on through the rain
events.text: The rain has kept every other traveller off the road. Pushing on through it gets the party there sooner, {soaked to the bone|miserable|steaming}.
events.check: Constitution DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: anyone who fails catches a chill and has disadvantage on Perception tomorrow

events.name: No stopping for lunch
events.text: The party could skip the midday rest and eat on the move.
events.check: Constitution DC 10 for everyone, or gain a level of exhaustion

events.name: Straight up the gully
events.text: A gully climbs straight up the hill. It's steep and loose, but it cuts out three switchbacks.
events.check: Athletics DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: a rockslide sends them back down, bruised

events.name: Cutting through the bramble
events.text: A thicket of {thorny bramble|rope-vine|razor-grass} blocks the direct way. Hacking through is faster than going round, and bloodier.
events.check: Constitution DC 11 or take 1d4 piercing damage

events.name: Night sailing
events.text: A {full|bright|half} moon and a steady wind: the crew could sail on all night instead of anchoring.
events.check: Constitution DC 12 for the crew
events.failText: the tired crew make mistakes, and the ship drifts

events.name: The dune ridge
events.text: Walking the crest of the dunes is faster than slogging through the hollows, but it's hot and exposed.
events.check: Constitution DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: anyone who fails gains a level of exhaustion from the heat

events.name: The burnt forest
events.text: A {wildfire|Smoulder's bad temper|monster's breath} has burnt the undergrowth away, and the party can walk straight through the ash. Nothing is alive. The smell stays for days.

events.name: Coin surge sprint
events.text: A party member could eat a spirit coin a rank above their own and carry everyone's packs at a run for an hour. They'll pay for it later.
events.cost: 1 spirit coin one rank above the eater's
events.failText: the eater gains a level of exhaustion

events.name: The cold crossing
events.text: The pass is open, just, under a lowering sky. It's a day saved or a night spent in a snow hole.
events.check: Survival DC 15
events.failText: the cold drives them back down, frostbitten and slower

events.name: Bog hopping
events.text: Tussocks of {firm grass|old stumps|sleeping turtles} dot the bog in a rough line. With a running jump, they lead straight across.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: someone misses and is pulled out of the bog by the ankles, with a wet pop

events.name: Rowing in shifts
events.text: No wind at all. Rowing in shifts all day moves the ship slowly, but it moves.
events.check: Athletics DC 11 for everyone, or disadvantage on Strength checks tomorrow

events.name: A clean corridor
events.text: A cave passage through the hill, spotless and polished as glass. No dust, no bones, no moss. Something has been keeping it very clean.
events.check: Perception DC 14 to spot the clear, wobbling wall before it moves
events.failText: the wall moves, and they flee back the way they came, minus a boot
events.nod: Dungeons and Dragons: the gelatinous cube

events.name: Descend by rope
events.text: A sheer {drop|cliff|sea wall} instead of the long winding path. With enough rope, it's a quarter of an hour.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 for everyone
events.failText: whoever fails takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage at the bottom

events.name: The deep jungle river
events.text: A slow brown river runs straight through the jungle. A raft would be quick. The ripples suggest the party wouldn't be alone.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to build a raft and keep to the middle
events.failText: something grabs the raft, and they swim for the bank
events.twist: A drowned Society team's raft is jammed in the roots downstream.

events.name: A noble's private road
events.text: A gated road across a {house|lord|baron}'s estate. The gatekeeper will let travellers through if they compliment the {house's hounds|lord's portrait|topiary}.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12
events.failText: the compliments are not sincere enough
events.twist: The lord is out with his hounds, and wants news of the road.

events.name: The Society permit route
events.text: An Adventure Society checkpoint opens a guarded {road|sea lane|river route} to licensed adventurers on contract. The clerk wants to see the party's badges.
events.check: Persuasion DC 11, or automatic for a team with an active contract
events.failText: the permits are in order but the clerk is having a bad day
events.twist: The clerk wants them to carry the week's reports.

events.name: A bribe at the gate
events.text: A guard will open the closed quick road for a bribe. Refugees sleep against the wall, unable to pay.
events.twist: Paying for the refugees too costs twice as much, and the guard pretends not to count them.

events.name: The Trade caravan lane
events.text: A Church of Trade caravan has a licence for the fast inland road. They'll add the party as guards, unpaid, if they want the speed.

events.name: A hermit's gate
events.text: A hermit owns the only gap in a long cliff. He asks no toll. He wants each traveller to tell him one {secret|joke|true thing}.
events.check: Deception or Persuasion DC 11

events.name: Pay the barge
events.text: A barge-owner will carry the party past the {rapids|falls|monster nests} and the long portage.

events.name: The ducal fast road
events.text: A ducal messenger road, closed to commoners, runs straight towards {place}. The party could pass as couriers.
events.check: Deception DC 14
events.failText: a real courier challenges them, and they leave fast

events.name: A Liberty smuggler's way
events.text: A Church of Liberty sister says her road-wardens know the paths borders try to hide. She'll show the party one if they carry a sealed parcel.
events.twist: The parcel is breathing.

events.name: The convoy berth
events.text: A harbour master offers the ship a berth in an escorted convoy leaving at {dawn|noon|dusk} on the fast outer route.

events.name: Shared oars
events.text: A ship full of Leonid rowers is going the same way and offers a tow, if the party will join the evening singing.

events.name: A gambler's map
events.text: A gambler wagers a hand-drawn map against the party's best {dagger|boots|cheese}, on a single roll of the dice.
events.check: Sleight of Hand or a straight d20 over 11
events.failText: they lose the dagger and keep walking the long way
events.twist: The map is real. The gambler is a Church of Disguise priest.

events.name: The Hero's challenge road
events.text: A Church of the Hero shrine marks a dangerous quick {path|passage|crossing} 'for heroes only'. A board lists everyone who took it. Half the names are crossed out.
events.check: Athletics DC 14 for everyone
events.failText: the party joins the half that came back the long way
events.twist: A Hero priest asks the party to add their names, either way.

events.name: The cartographer's error
events.text: The Magic Society's official map shows a {lake|forest|mountain} here. There is no lake. There is a lovely flat meadow, straight across.
events.twist: The lake comes back at full moon.

events.name: A deal with goblins
events.text: A goblin trading family has built a rope-and-pulley line over the ravine. One iron coin a ride, and they will tell you every story about every rope.

events.name: A Dominion highway
events.text: A smooth road built by slave labour for the Church of Dominion. It is fast, safe and patrolled, and the party will see the workers.
events.twist: A worker slips the party a note asking for help.

events.name: The ship's own trick
events.text: The ship's old mate knows a current most captains have forgotten. He'll use it if the party buys the crew a cask at the next port.

events.name: The salt-road guild
events.text: A {salt|spice|glass} caravan's leader offers to share the paths her guild keeps clear across the flats.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12

events.name: A Death priest's path
events.text: A Church of Death priest walks the old corpse road to a graveyard over the hill, and lets the living follow if they keep quiet.

events.name: An honest tip
events.text: A crier at the last town shouted the news: the bridge ahead has been repaired a season early.

events.name: The weather-wise
events.text: An old {sailor|cook|cabin boy} taps her nose: the wind will back to the south by noon. Wait for it, and it carries the ship half a day further.
events.check: Nature DC 12 to judge her right

events.name: A cook's shortcut
events.text: A camp cook offers to cook all the party's meals on the move so they never stop. Her {stew|porridge|everything} is terrible. Nobody stops.

events.name: A navigator's notebook
events.text: A retired {navigator|guide|courier} shares a notebook of shortcuts gathered over forty years, and refuses payment. She asks only that the party add one of their own.

events.name: A lift from a family
events.text: A {Leonid|Draconian|Runic} family travelling the same way insists the party share their {wagon|boat} for the afternoon, and feeds them too.

events.name: Word from a friend
events.text: A message reaches the party from {npc}, who heard where they were going and sends a quicker route with a fond, badly spelled note.
events.twist: The route passes somewhere {npc} badly wants news from.

events.name: The man who measures
events.text: A Magic Society surveyor with chains, stakes and a very long face is measuring the world in straight lines. He knows the straightest one ahead.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12 to get him to share it
events.twist: He thinks the world is getting smaller, and has the numbers.

events.name: The Society notice
events.text: A notice from the Adventure Society says {a Bronze|an Iron|a Silver}-rank team has cleared the quick route ahead this week, and lists it.

events.name: A day of good guesses
events.text: The party's navigator has one of those days when every guess is right and every turn is the good one.
events.check: Survival DC 14
events.failText: the luck runs out by noon

events.name: A barge going their way
events.text: A cargo barge heading the same way has room on deck.

events.name: Green-stone boats
events.text: Delta folk will lend the party floating green-stone boats to pole through the channels.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12, or a favour done for the village

events.name: A sky ship berth
events.text: A sky ship has put down to take on water, and its captain will sell passage.

events.name: Spare heidels
events.text: Riders of a Host offer to lend the party fast steppe heidels, for a price or a contest.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13, or win their contest

events.name: A cloud skiff
events.text: Clan crafters can thicken a cloud into a skiff that rides the mountain winds.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15, or a task for the chieftain

events.name: A grounded flier
events.text: A wounded flying monster, the kind tamers pay well for, is grounded nearby.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 16 to calm it and ride it
events.failText: it lashes out and flies off

events.name: A summoner's mounts
events.text: A friendly essence user offers to summon spirit mounts for the party for a couple of days.
events.cost: a favour, or 5 iron spirit coins each

events.name: A fast current
events.text: A strong current running the right way.
events.check: Survival or Nature DC 13 to find it

events.name: An astral shortcut
events.text: An astral space whose two entrances open many miles apart, and the far one is the right way.
events.check: clear the space, or sneak through it (Stealth DC 15 for everyone)
events.failText: they have to fight their way out the way they came

events.name: A caravan of greatbacks
events.text: A merchant caravan travelling day and night on huge greatbacks offers the party a place.
events.cost: 2 iron spirit coins a head a day

events.name: A whale-drawn barge
events.text: A barge pulled by a tame sea monster, heading along the coast.

events.name: A sand skiff
events.text: A sand skiff with sails, skimming the dunes, has room for passengers.

events.name: A caravan of heidels
events.text: A caravan of heidels with spare mounts for hire.
events.cost: 2 iron spirit coins a head a day

events.name: A river ferry going downstream
events.text: A big river ferry going downstream, packed with farmers and livestock.

events.name: A friendly giant
events.text: An enormous, gentle monster lets the party ride on its back, if they scratch the spot it can't reach.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13

events.name: A Cloud Clan lift
events.text: A Cloud Clan cloud-ship drops a rope ladder and offers a lift, in exchange for news from the ground.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13

events.name: A Journey priest's blessing
events.text: A Church of the Journey priest blesses the party's feet. For two days they travel like the wind.
events.cost: a donation of 5 iron spirit coins

events.name: A mail coach
events.text: A fast mail coach with two seats free.

events.name: A hired dhow
events.text: A coastal trader with a fast dhow is heading the same way.

events.name: The flying carpet
events.nod: Arabian Nights / Aladdin: a flying carpet
events.text: A merchant demonstrating a flying carpet needs volunteers to prove it is safe. It mostly is.
events.check: Acrobatics DC 12 to stay on

events.name: A shortcut
events.text: A shortcut through easy ground: half a day's extra progress.

events.name: A hospitable farmstead
events.text: A real bed, a hot meal, and a local's warning about the road ahead.

events.name: Perfect weather
events.text: Fine weather tomorrow: advantage on the next Survival check.

events.name: Rich ground
events.text: Land where the magic has just drained away, rich enough to forage several days of food.

events.name: Good company
events.text: A friendly patrol or caravan to travel with; no encounter check tomorrow.

events.name: A kind farmer's cart
events.text: A farmer gives the party a lift on his hay cart for the afternoon and won't take payment.

events.name: An honest map
events.text: A Church of the Journey waystation gives out maps of the road ahead, freshly corrected. Advantage on tomorrow's Survival check.

events.name: A blessed spring
events.text: A spring blessed by the Healer. Anyone who drinks regains one Hit Die.

events.name: A shepherd's dogs
events.text: A shepherd's huge, scarred dogs adopt the party for the night and sit guard round the fire. No night events tonight, and nothing creeps up on them.

events.name: A hunter's gift
events.text: A hunter with too much meat shares it. Nobody needs to eat from their own supplies for two days.

events.name: Gratitude
events.text: A family the party helped earlier, or someone who has heard of them, gives them a bag of supplies and a warm hug.

events.name: A lost purse
events.text: A purse of spirit coins in the road, with no name on it.
events.twist: Its owner is a day ahead and would be very grateful to have it back.

events.name: A favourable wind
events.text: A perfect wind fills the sails all day.

events.name: A secret hot spring
events.text: A hot spring hidden among the rocks. A long soak counts as a short rest and cures one level of exhaustion.

events.name: Lessons from a veteran
events.text: A veteran adventurer walks with the party for a day, sharing tricks. Each character can reroll one ability check before the next long rest.

events.name: A message from home
events.text: A courier catches up with a letter for one of the party, from someone who misses them.

events.name: A shrine of the Journey
events.text: A wayside shrine of the Church of the Journey. Anyone who prays there won't get lost tomorrow.

events.name: A free meal
events.text: A tavern holding an eating contest. Whoever eats most wins free board for the night, and the party's appetite is legendary.
events.check: Constitution DC 13

events.name: A well-stocked hut
events.text: A hunting hut, stocked by the local lord for travellers: firewood, dry beds and preserved food.

events.name: The luck of the road
events.text: A black cat crosses the path from left to right, which in this region is extraordinarily lucky. Everyone gains inspiration.

events.name: A healer's rest
events.text: A travelling healer offers to tend everyone's hurts for free. Everyone regains all their hit points.

events.name: A borrowed tent
events.text: A family lends the party a big, dry tent for the night. A full night's rest guaranteed, whatever the weather.

events.name: A favour repaid
events.text: Someone from {faction} recognises the party and pays for their next night's lodging and a meal.

events.name: A towel
events.nod: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy: always know where your towel is
events.text: A traveller insists the party take a towel, 'the most useful thing a traveller can carry'. It is, oddly, magical, and dries anything instantly.

events.name: It's dangerous to go alone
events.nod: The Legend of Zelda: 'It's dangerous to go alone! Take this.'
events.text: An old hermit in a roadside cave presses a battered sword into the youngest party member's hands. 'It's dangerous out there. Take this.' The sword is junk, and the hermit is sincere.

events.name: A Hearth shrine welcome
events.text: A Hearth shrine at a {farmhouse|mill|crossroads inn} keeps a pot on the fire for any traveller. The widow who tends it will not hear of payment.
events.twist: She asks the party to carry her son's letter on to the next town.

events.name: A Drift Host guest-right
events.text: A Drift Host camp grants the party guest-right for the night. They sleep in a round tent on a greatback's back, warm, fed on {mare's milk|roast heidel|spiced flatbread} and safe.
events.twist: The Host's strongest rider wants to test one of the party at dawn, as a friendly custom.

events.name: The fisher's table
events.text: A fishing family pulls the party in out of the weather and feeds them {grilled eel|crab stew|fried squid} until nobody can move.

events.name: A wedding feast
events.text: A village wedding spills onto the road, and the party are dragged in as honoured guests. There is dancing, too much food and a {fight|proposal|small fire} by midnight.
events.twist: The bride's family wants the party to stand as witnesses, which comes with obligations.

events.name: A rich merchant's hospitality
events.text: A merchant of {Yaresh|Vitesse|Rimaros} travelling with servants invites the party to dine. Silver plates, soft cushions, and a gift of road wine.
events.twist: She is fishing for adventurers to hire, and the party just passed the interview.

events.name: A Cloud Clan terrace
events.text: A Cloud Clan family lets the party sleep in a room built of thickened cloud. It is {softer|cooler|quieter} than any bed in the world.

events.name: An inn with a spare room
events.text: The only inn for miles has exactly one room left, and it's the {good one|bridal suite|one with the bath}.
events.twist: The usual occupant arrives at midnight, a Silver-ranker, and is very polite about it.

events.name: The ship's captain's table
events.text: The {grizzled|young|one-eyed} captain invites the party to dine at her table, shares her charts and tells them where the sea monsters were last seen.
events.twist: She is short a mate, and offers the job to one of the party.

events.name: A goblin homestead
events.text: A goblin {family|grandmother|gang of cousins} takes the party in for the night. Everything in their burrow is tiny, borrowed and labelled with the name of its original owner.
events.twist: One label has the name of a party member's lost item on it.

events.name: A Leonid smithy
events.text: A Leonid smith at a roadside forge offers to sharpen, mend and oil everything the party owns while they eat her {husband's stew|daughter's pies|own terrible soup}.
events.twist: Her apprentice is an outworlder who has never seen a heidel before.

events.name: A shepherd's bothy
events.text: A dry stone bothy on the hillside, with a peat fire laid ready and a tin of {biscuits|tea|toffee} on the shelf.

events.name: The open door
events.text: A sign on a cottage door says 'Travellers welcome. Soup on the stove. Shut the gate.' Nobody is home. The {soup|stew|curry} is excellent.
events.twist: The owner left a note: 'Please feed the cat.' There is no cat.

events.name: A barge family
events.text: A barge family moors beside the party's camp and shares their fire, their {fiddle|drum|accordion} and their gossip.

events.name: A merfolk welcome
events.text: Merfolk surface around the ship and toss up gifts of {pearl-shells|sea fruit|cold fresh fish}, curious about the strangers.

events.name: A night in a temple
events.text: A {Church of the Healer|Church of the Hearth|Church of the Journey} temple offers the party a dormitory for the night, clean sheets and a bell for breakfast.

events.name: The friendly tollhouse
events.text: A tollkeeper so bored he waives the toll, cooks them dinner and tells the same {joke|story|riddle} six times.

events.name: The noble's hunting lodge
events.text: A {Mercer|Cavendish|Geller} steward opens the house's hunting lodge to adventurers on the road: hot baths, real beds and a full larder.
events.twist: The steward asks a small favour: a monster has been taking the lodge's deer.

events.name: The oasis camp
events.text: A trading caravan has camped at an oasis and makes room for the party in the shade. Fresh {dates|figs|melon} and cold water all round.

events.name: A watch-post's coffee
events.text: A lonely Society watch-post on the ridge has hot {coffee|tea|spiced milk}, a warm stove and a guard happy to talk to someone new.

events.name: Shelter in a hollow hill
events.text: A hill opens like a door in the rain. Inside, a hall lit by glowing roots, a fire, and a table set for exactly the party's number.
events.twist: Nobody comes, but the plates are cleared by morning.

events.name: A ferry family's floor
events.text: The ferry family lets the party sleep on their floor by the {fire|stove|hearth} for the price of the crossing.

events.name: A shrine of Trade
events.text: A Church of Trade waystation sells supplies at honest prices, and the clerk gives the party first look at {faction}'s new stock.

events.name: A Healer's travelling clinic
events.text: A Church of the Healer cart has set up a clinic by the {road|well|bridge}. Anyone treated regains all their Hit Dice.
events.twist: The priest asks for a donation, and mentions which noble house funds the cart.

events.name: The warm pool
events.text: A warm pool below a {waterfall|cliff|ruined bathhouse}. A long soak and everyone feels new: one level of exhaustion gone.
events.twist: A Silver-rank monster bathes here too, at dusk.

events.name: A herbalist's poultice
events.text: An old herbalist dresses the party's cuts with a green poultice that stings and smells of {mint|pine|old socks}. Everyone regains 2d4 hit points and sleeps soundly.

events.name: The Healer's spring
events.text: Water bubbles from a stone carved with an open hand holding a leaf. Anyone who drinks is cured of one disease or poison.

events.name: A good night's sleep
events.text: For once, nobody snores, nothing {howls|rains|bites} and the ground is soft. Everyone wakes rested and gains inspiration.

events.name: A sea-bath
events.text: The sea is {warm and calm|green and clear|full of friendly dolphins}. Swimming off the ship washes away a week of salt-crust and sweat, and lifts everyone's mood.

events.name: Mud that mends
events.text: A bubbling mud spring that locals swear by. It works: bruises fade, aches go, and everyone smells of {eggs|cabbage|drains} for two days.

events.name: A masseur from Vitesse
events.text: A travelling masseur from {Vitesse|Yaresh|Rimaros} insists on working on the party's knots. It is agony, and afterwards everyone moves like a cat.

events.name: A Death priest's vigil
events.text: A Church of Death priest offers to sit up all night by the party's fire, so the dead in this place stay where they are. They do.
events.twist: In the morning she leaves a black candle and the name of someone she buried here.

events.name: A day of rest
events.text: The rain sets in and the party sit it out in a snug barn until noon. Everyone counts as having finished a short rest, and nobody is wet.

events.name: A troupe of healers
events.text: A band of novice healers on their pilgrimage begs to practise on the party. Their work is clumsy but kind, and everyone regains half their hit points.
events.twist: One novice has real talent and wants to join a team.

events.name: The Hearth's sanctuary
events.text: A Hearth {priest|grandmother|novice} touches the party's campfire and calls it sanctuary. Nothing hostile comes near, and everyone regains an extra Hit Die.

events.name: A cot on the ship
events.text: The ship's {purser|cook|bosun} finds the party proper hammocks in a dry part of the hold. Nobody rolls off.

events.name: The old soldier's remedy
events.text: An old soldier swears by his hangover cure, and the party needs it. It works, and tastes of {boots|pond|regret}.

events.name: A Celestine's touch
events.text: A Celestine healer, travelling alone, lays a hand on each of them. The light is warm and gold, and old scars fade.
events.twist: She is looking for her outworlder parents, and wants to know if the party has met any.

events.name: Clean water
events.text: A clear, cold {spring|well|rain barrel}, after days of bad water. Everyone drinks and refills, and nobody gets sick.

events.name: A bathhouse of the Revels
events.text: A Church of the Revels bathhouse on the road: hot water, scented oils, music, and far too many questions about the party's love lives.

events.name: The sleep of the just
events.text: A Justice shrine in a ruined court. Anyone with a clear conscience who sleeps there wakes with advantage on their first saving throw tomorrow.
events.twist: Anyone without one dreams of a scales-bearing judge, and wakes sweating.

events.name: Rest in a coin farm
events.text: The caretaker of a mothballed spirit coin farm lets the party sleep in the warm hall. The thick magic makes everyone dream of numbers.

events.name: A swordsmith's whetstone
events.text: A whetstone left on a {milestone|stump|shrine} with a sign: 'Free. Bring back.' Every blade in the party gets a fine edge.

events.name: A cache of the Society
events.text: An Adventure Society supply cache, its lock opened by any badge. Dried food, rope, torches and a note asking finders to restock what they can.
events.twist: The last entry in the log is a team the party knows, a week overdue.

events.name: A fallen monster
events.text: A monster killed by something bigger lies by the {path|shore|river}. Its core is still in it.
events.twist: The bigger thing comes back for it at dusk.

events.name: Windfall fruit
events.text: An orchard gone wild, the ground thick with ripe {apples|pears|plums}. Enough to eat well for three days.

events.name: Spirit coins in the stream
events.text: Iron spirit coins glint in the stream bed, washed down from somewhere upstream. A patient hour gathers {1d6|2d6|3d6} of them.
events.twist: Upstream, a coin farm's broken hopper is still leaking, and its owners are coming.

events.name: A drifting crate
events.text: A sealed crate bobs past the ship, stamped with a {Yaresh|Rimaros|Greenstone} trading mark. Hauling it in takes a hook and some swearing.

events.name: A fishing net full
events.text: The ship's net comes up heaving with {fish|squid|lobsters}. The cook is overjoyed and the crew eats like kings for two days.

events.name: The Tide's leavings
events.text: The Wandering Tide has just drained from this valley. The grass is waist-high and monsters killed at its edge have left cores and hides everywhere.

events.name: Forager's luck
events.text: {Mushrooms|Hazelnuts|Wild leeks}, wild garlic and a beehive in a hollow log. The party eats well without touching their supplies.
events.twist: The beehive's owner, a very large bear, returns.

events.name: A dead adventurer's pack
events.text: A Bronze-rank adventurer died here, alone. Her pack is intact: food, gear, and a pouch of coins. Her badge says Tilda Rook.
events.twist: The Society would pay to know how she died, and her family would pay more.

events.name: A pedlar's surplus
events.text: A pedlar closing up shop for the {season|winter|wedding} sells everything at half price, then gives the rest away.
events.twist: The pedlar is retiring to become a Church of the Journey pilgrim, and wants a blessing.

events.name: The awakening stone on the wall
events.text: An awakening stone sits in a niche in a ruined wall, mossed over, overlooked for years.
events.twist: It is a stone of an essence nobody in the party has seen before.

events.name: A wrecked supply wagon
events.text: A supply wagon lies on its side, its heidels gone, its driver buried in a shallow grave by someone kind. The {stores|water barrels|medical chest} are untouched.

events.name: Salvage on the beach
events.text: A storm has thrown a wreck's cargo up on the beach: barrels, rope, a chest. Nobody else has found it yet.
events.twist: The ship's merfolk crew are camped in the surf, waiting to see who takes it.

events.name: A bird's hoard
events.text: A giant magpie's nest in a low tree is stuffed with shiny things: spoons, buttons, two spirit coins and a signet ring.
events.twist: The ring belongs to a house that will want it back.

events.name: A full waterskin
events.text: Just when the water ran low, a {desert cistern|rock tank|hidden well} full of cold, clean rain.

events.name: The free sample
events.text: An alchemist's apprentice is handing out free potion samples to drum up trade. Most are fine.
events.twist: One sample turns someone's hair green for a week.

events.name: A ten-foot pole
events.text: A pedlar's single item for sale is a ten-foot pole. He swears every adventurer needs one. He is going to be {right|insufferable about it}.
events.nod: Dungeons and Dragons: the classic ten-foot pole

events.name: A chest that is just a chest
events.text: A wooden chest sits alone on the {road|beach|deck of a wreck}. Everyone braces for it to bite. It is a chest, full of supplies.
events.nod: Dungeons and Dragons and video games: mimics

events.name: Open, cave
events.text: A rock face with a carved door and no handle. Saying the old word for 'open' in the right tongue rumbles it aside to a cave of forgotten trade goods.
events.check: History or Arcana DC 15
events.nod: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves: 'open sesame'
events.twist: The forty owners have not forgotten about it.

events.name: Elven way-bread
events.text: An elf {ranger|pilgrim|merchant} shares a packet of thin, leaf-wrapped wafers. One bite fills a grown adult for a whole day.
events.nod: The Lord of the Rings: lembas

events.name: A goose that lays coins
events.text: A farmer is trying to sell a goose that lays one iron spirit coin a day. It is true. The goose is {also|unfortunately} the most violent animal in the region.
events.nod: Fairy tales: the goose that laid the golden eggs

events.name: A warning in time
events.text: A frightened traveller coming the other way warns that {bandits|a monster|a flood} has closed the main road ahead, and shows the way round.

events.name: The Society board
events.text: A waystation's Society board has fresh contracts on it, including one the party could do on the way.
events.twist: The contract's issuer is someone the party already knows.

events.name: A local's map
events.text: A {villager|shepherd|child} sketches a map of the next day's ground in the dirt, with every bog, ford and grumpy farmer marked.

events.name: The sailor's almanac
events.text: A sailor sells an almanac of winds and currents for this sea, with the dangerous waters marked in {red|blood|very bad handwriting}.

events.name: A scholar on the road
events.text: A Church of Knowledge scholar walking to {place} tells the party a piece of history about where they are going, and it is useful.

events.name: The whisper
events.text: A traveller leans in and whispers one true thing about the party's destination, then walks on. Nobody saw her face.
events.twist: It will be true. The DM chooses what.

events.name: A rival's notes
events.text: Another team's {camp|boat|tent}, hastily abandoned. Their notes on the region are still there, and very good.
events.twist: The notes end mid-sentence.

events.name: Tide tables
events.text: A harbour {clerk|master|urchin} hands over this month's tide tables, and points out the dangerous days.

events.name: A truthful dog
events.text: {A scruffy|A three-legged|An enormous} dog follows the party all day and growls at every wrong turn. It is never wrong.
events.twist: It is somebody's familiar, and they are looking for it.

events.name: A Magic Society bulletin
events.text: A Magic Society courier is posting bulletins: the local magic is running {high|low|strangely}, and here is what to expect.

events.name: A song with directions
events.text: Children are singing a {skipping|clapping|counting} song that is, the party realises, a list of turns to the next town.

events.name: An oracle's guess
events.text: A blind seer at a crossroads tells each party member one thing they will see tomorrow. Each one happens.
events.twist: One prophecy is for someone not in the party, and she asks them to deliver it.

events.name: A poacher's confession
events.text: A poacher caught by the party trades what he knows for his freedom: where the monsters lie in this {forest|marsh|valley} and how to slip past.

events.name: The ship's rat
events.text: The ship's cat drops a live rat at a party member's feet each morning. The crew says this is the luckiest sign there is.
events.twist: The rat is someone's familiar, and they want it back.

events.name: Outworlder card night
events.text: An outworlder teaches the party a card game called Uno, with a hand-painted deck. Whoever wins the long game by the fire gains inspiration.
events.nod: Uno, the card game
events.twist: Nobody can agree on whether you can stack the draw cards.

events.name: A second breakfast
events.text: A halfling outworlder, the only one anyone has seen, insists the party join her for second breakfast, as is only civilised. It is {magnificent|enormous|mostly mushrooms}.
events.nod: The Lord of the Rings: hobbits and second breakfast

events.name: A clear morning
events.text: The rain stops overnight and the morning is {clear and cool|bright and dry|crisp and still}. The going is easy.

events.name: A fair current
events.text: The ship picks up a friendly current at dawn and rides it until dusk.

events.name: A herd of deer
events.text: {Deer|Wild heidels|Antelope} grazing at the forest edge, unafraid. A hunter in the party could feed everyone for days.
events.check: Survival DC 12
events.twist: One deer is pure white, and the local Church of the Earth forbids hunting it.

events.name: The fish run
events.text: Silver {fish|eels|salmon} are running up the river in thousands. Anyone can catch dinner with their hands.

events.name: Rainbow over the camp
events.text: A double rainbow spans the camp at sunset. Everyone stops talking for a while, and the next day starts well.

events.name: Wild honey
events.text: A wild hive in a dead tree, its bees drowsy in the cold. Enough honey for the whole party, and a {few|great many} stings.

events.name: A cool day in the desert
events.text: A high haze takes the edge off the sun all day. Nobody needs to check for heat, and the water lasts longer.

events.name: Whales at dawn
events.text: A pod of whales surfaces around the ship at dawn, singing. The crew swears it means safe waters.
events.twist: One whale has a barnacled message tube on its fin.

events.name: A grove of ripe mangoes
events.text: A grove of {mango|fig|breadfruit} trees heavy with fruit. The monkeys are furious about the competition.

events.name: Moss beds
events.text: A clearing of thick, dry {moss|pine needles|heather}, soft as a mattress. Everyone sleeps deeply.

events.name: Fresh snow
events.text: A light {snow|frost|dust storm} falls in the night and covers every track for miles. Nothing can follow the party today.

events.name: The night-blooming field
events.text: A field of flowers opens at moonrise, glowing faintly {blue|silver|pink}. Their scent soothes, and everyone wakes with a clear head.
events.twist: Something comes to drink the nectar at midnight.

events.name: A rich tide pool
events.text: Low tide leaves pools full of {crabs|prawns|oysters}, mussels and edible weed. Dinner is free.

events.name: Drained ground
events.text: The magic has drained from this ground recently, and it is bursting with growth: berries, roots and fat game.

events.name: A strong tailwind
events.text: The {wind|breeze} swings behind the party and stays there all day.

events.name: Flying fish
events.text: A school of flying fish crosses the deck in a silver spray. Dozens land in the boat, and one lands in the {captain's hat|cook's pot|bosun's shirt}.

events.name: The calm after
events.text: After the storm, the sky goes pink and gold, the sea lies flat, and the whole crew sits out on deck to dry.

events.name: Kindly fog
events.text: A thick fog hides the party from everything on the road. Shapes move past them in the white, and none of them notice the party.
events.twist: One shape stops, sniffs, and moves on.

events.name: A water-tree
events.text: A fat-trunked desert tree. Cut the bark and clear, {sweet|bitter|cold} water runs out. Enough for everyone, and the tree heals by morning.
events.twist: A Desert tribe tends it, and they want to know who cut it.

events.name: Seabirds point the way
