events.text: Seabirds flying home at dusk show where the land is, and the navigator corrects their course.

events.name: A warm stone
events.text: A big {boulder|standing stone|fallen statue} by the camp stays warm all night, as if it had been in an oven. Nobody can explain it. Everyone sleeps against it.
events.twist: In the morning, it has moved a foot closer to the fire.

events.name: Snow-melt stream
events.text: A snow-melt stream runs clean and ice-cold beside the path. Nobody needs to ration water today.

events.name: A blessing of the Journey
events.text: A Church of the Journey priest blesses the party's {boots|packs|feet}. Nobody gets a blister for a week and the road seems shorter.

events.name: The Storm's favour
events.text: Lightning strikes the mast and leaves it glowing blue all night. The crew cheers: a Church of the Storm sign of favour.
events.twist: The priest aboard insists someone owes the god a gift now.

events.name: Earth's gift
events.text: A Church of the Earth shrine stone splits open at a touch, revealing {a clear crystal|a lump of raw silver|a perfect geode}.

events.name: A natural array's glow
events.text: The camp is inside a natural array. The magic is thick and warm, and everyone's spells and powers recharge with ease.
events.twist: Monsters like it too, and one is on the way.

events.name: A friendly spirit
events.text: A small glowing spirit follows the camp all night, lighting the way to the latrine and warning of anything that creeps up.

events.name: A shrine of the Hero
events.text: A Hero shrine with a bowl of {water|wine|blood}. Whoever drinks and swears an oath to protect someone gains inspiration, and the god is listening.

events.name: Coins to the fountain
events.text: A fountain at a crossroads full of thrown iron coins. A sign says take one if you need it, leave one if you can.
events.twist: A Church of Trade official is watching who takes.

events.name: An awakening stone's hum
events.text: An awakening stone hums in a party member's pack all day. By night, they understand one new word in every language they hear.
events.twist: The stone is not theirs. Someone slipped it in their pack at the last town.

events.name: The Ocean's calm
events.text: A Church of the Ocean priest pours a jar of seawater over the bow. The sea goes flat and blue for a day.

events.name: The horseshoe charm
events.text: A heidel shoe is nailed above a ruined {doorway|barn|chapel}, points up to keep the luck in. Whoever sleeps beneath it gains inspiration.
events.nod: Folklore: the lucky horseshoe hung points up

events.name: The fairy fountain
events.text: A spring in a cave, ringed with laughing lights. Anyone who steps in regains all their hit points, and a light follows them for a minute, giggling.
events.nod: The Legend of Zelda: the great fairy fountains

events.name: A Liberty blessing
events.text: A Church of Liberty priest cuts a frayed cord off a party member's wrist and calls it the last chain they'll wear. Everyone feels lighter.
events.twist: She is being followed by Dominion slave-takers.

events.name: Truth's lantern
events.text: A Church of Truth lantern keeper offers to light the party's way for {one evening|a night}. Under its light, every lie they hear tonight is obvious.

events.name: A Celestine's gift
events.text: A Celestine {child|pilgrim|grandmother} gives each of the party a smooth pebble that glows faintly in the dark. They never need a torch on this journey.

events.name: Surge-luck
events.text: The rising magic makes everything a little more of itself. The party's food stays fresh longer, their fire burns hotter and their boots dry in a minute.

events.name: A shrine to the Revels
events.text: A Revels shrine with a barrel of wine and a sign: 'Drink, or the god will be offended.' The god would be offended.
events.twist: The barrel never empties, and someone is going to try.

events.name: The Knowledge library-cart
events.text: A Church of Knowledge library-cart lends the party a book on the region. It has a {pressed flower|love letter|recipe} and a map tucked inside.

events.name: A Destruction priest's gift
events.text: A Church of Destruction priest burns the party's damaged gear in a white flame and hands them replacements from his own pack, without a word.
events.twist: Each item is engraved with the name of someone who died carrying it.

events.name: A spirit coin in the bread
events.text: The {baker|innkeeper|priest} at the last village has baked an iron spirit coin into one of the loaves, as is the custom here. It's lucky to find it.

events.name: An astral glimmer
events.text: An astral space's door hangs open, just for tonight. Through it, the party can see a field of silver grass and hear a night song.
events.twist: Anyone who steps through and back gains inspiration. The gods can't see them in there.

events.name: The Earth's long sleep
events.text: The ground under the camp is so solid and still that nothing below can rise tonight. A Church of the Earth pilgrim would call it blessed rock.

events.name: The novice catches up
events.text: The talented novice healer catches up, pack on her back, and asks to walk with the party for a few days. Her healing is free.

events.name: The merchant's offer
events.text: A runner brings a letter from the merchant who dined the party: a guard contract, well paid, starting at {place}.

events.name: The whale's message
events.text: The message tube from the whale's fin holds a merfolk chart, marking a safe channel and a sunken wreck nobody has looted.

events.name: A bonus from the board
events.text: A Society runner finds the party: the contract they noticed has a bonus for any team passing that way, and they qualify.

events.name: The wedding gift
events.text: A boy runs up the road after the party with a gift from the newly-weds: a cloth-wrapped cake and a carved charm for luck.

events.name: Tilda's brother
events.text: A grey-faced man catches up: Tilda Rook's brother. He wants to hear how they found her, and gives the party her spare spirit coins.

events.name: The spirit returns
events.text: The little glowing spirit is back at the camp, brighter now. It has brought friends, and they ring the camp like lanterns.

events.name: News of the parents
events.text: A letter reaches the party from the Celestine healer. She found a trace of her outworlder parents and wants the party's help to follow it.

events.name: A Society escort
events.text: A {Bronze|Silver}-rank team heading the same way invites the party to travel with them. Nothing on this road wants to try it.

events.name: The herd dogs
events.text: A pair of shaggy {herd dogs|wolfhounds|heidel-herders} decide the party is their flock and guard the camp all night, growling at every shadow.

events.name: A convoy of pilgrims
events.text: A big column of pilgrims heading for a shrine takes the party in. Slow, safe and very, very cheerful.
events.twist: One pilgrim keeps asking the party to bless things.

events.name: A merfolk escort
events.text: A merfolk {patrol|hunting party|family} shadows the ship through the dangerous waters, waving off anything that comes near.

events.name: A patrol of the Sapphire Crown
events.text: A Storm Kingdom warship flying Sapphire Crown colours sails beside the party's ship for a day. Nothing comes close.

events.name: The cloud-bird
events.text: A Cloud Clan tamer's giant condor perches over the camp all night. Every predator on the mountain gives it a wide berth.

events.name: The walking house
events.text: A Drift Host {family|elder|tide-reader} invites the party to ride on their greatback for a day. The view is magnificent and the progress is good.

events.name: A sky ship's watch
events.text: A sky ship anchors overhead for the night, its lookouts sweeping the ground with lanterns. Nothing creeps up on anyone.
events.twist: In the morning, the captain sends down a message for {npc}.

events.name: A mercenary's day off
events.text: A {Draconian|Leonid|Smoulder} mercenary on leave walks with the party for a day and insists on paying for everything. He is bored, and rich.
events.twist: He is hiding from his own guild.

events.name: The guard goose
events.text: A farmer lends the party her guard {goose|llama|hound} for the night. Nothing gets past it, including the party.
events.twist: The goose follows them when they leave.

events.name: A Smoulder's fire
events.text: A Smoulder traveller lights the party's fire with a snap of her fingers, keeps it going all night in the rain, and tells excellent stories.

events.name: Travellers with music
events.text: A troupe of musicians shares the road and the camp. The night is loud, warm and fun.
events.twist: One of the songs is about the party, and it's not flattering.

events.name: A lighthouse keeper's signal
events.text: A lighthouse keeper flashes a lamp code to the ship, warning of {rocks|a sea monster|pirates} ahead and pointing out the safe channel.

events.name: A Runic's ward
events.text: A Runic traveller traces a glowing ward around the camp with one finger, the runes on her arms flaring. Nothing hostile crosses it.

events.name: The bear that walks along
events.text: A big {bear|boar|stag} walks beside the party all afternoon, minding its own business, and nothing else on the road comes near them.

events.name: A War church column
events.text: A Church of War column marching to a border offers the party a place in its camp. It is safe, disciplined and full of people who expect to die soon.

events.name: A free drink
events.text: An innkeeper recognises the party from {a contract|a song|a wanted poster} and stands them a round. Everyone is smiling.
events.twist: A rival team in the corner is not happy about it.

events.name: The badge opens doors
events.text: A local official sees the party's Society badges and waves them past the queue, the toll and the paperwork.
events.twist: The queue they skipped includes someone important.

events.name: A grateful village
events.text: Word of the party has run ahead of them. At the next {hamlet|farm|crossroads}, a cart of food and a basket of clean {socks|bread|honey} waits with their names chalked on it.

events.name: Thanks from a noble house
events.text: A rider in {Mercer|Remore|Vane} colours brings a sealed letter of thanks for some past deed, and a purse.
events.twist: The letter also asks a small favour.

events.name: Your money's no good here
events.text: A shopkeeper refuses to take the party's money because they once saved her cousin. She will not say which cousin.
events.twist: The cousin is coming to say thanks in person.

events.name: A rumour of the party
events.text: The party hear a wildly exaggerated tale of their own deeds told in a tavern. The teller has never met them, and offers to buy them a drink for listening.

events.name: The Society's thanks
events.text: An Adventure Society clerk has a bonus for the party, for a {report|core|map} they filed weeks ago that turned out to matter.

events.name: A free ferry
events.text: The ferryman's daughter was saved by adventurers once. He takes the party across for free, and gives them {lunch|a bag of apples|his brother's address}.

events.name: A captain's welcome
events.text: The captain of the next ship knows the party's reputation and offers them the best cabin for nothing, if they'll guard the hold.

events.name: A smith's gift
events.text: A Leonid smith who heard of the party gives them a fine {blade|shield|set of arrowheads}, 'for the next one you save'.

events.name: The shoemaker's helpers
events.text: The party leaves their worn boots by the fire. In the morning they are mended, oiled and stitched with tiny, perfect stitches.
events.nod: Grimm fairy tale: the elves and the shoemaker
events.twist: Tiny muddy footprints lead away to a mouse hole.

events.name: Stone soup
events.text: A {traveller|soldier|beggar} boils a stone in a pot and says it makes fine soup with a little help. Everyone adds something. It does.
events.nod: Folk tale: stone soup

events.name: The umbrella at the stop
events.text: At a roadside shelter in the rain, a huge furry forest spirit stands waiting, soaked. Lending it a cloak earns a gift of seeds that sprout by morning.
events.nod: My Neighbour Totoro: the bus stop in the rain

events.name: The clinic chime
events.text: A cheerful Healer nurse heals the whole party at once, plays a little chime, and says she hopes to see them again. She does not mean it as a threat.
events.nod: Pokemon: the Pokemon Centre nurse and healing jingle
events.twist: She asks if they have a pet that needs healing too.

events.name: The hooded stranger
events.text: A hooded figure sits in the darkest corner of the inn, watching the party. Eventually he comes over. He {just wants|is a lonely farmer who wants} to buy them dinner.
events.nod: Dungeons and Dragons: 'you all meet in a tavern' and the mysterious hooded stranger

events.name: The jug that never empties
events.text: A poor old couple share their last meal with the party. Their single jug of milk keeps pouring, however many cups are filled.
events.nod: Greek myth: Baucis and Philemon
events.twist: The couple don't seem surprised.

events.name: Happy little trees
events.text: An outworlder with a magnificent beard is painting the view by the road, talking softly about happy little trees. He gives the party a painting.
events.nod: Bob Ross and The Joy of Painting
events.twist: The painting shows the party's next camp, before they see it.

events.name: The cat in the pack
events.text: {A stray|A ginger|An one-eyed} cat climbs into a party member's pack and will not leave. Sailors and farmers both say a cat that chooses you is luck.
events.nod: Internet memes: 'if it fits, I sits'
events.twist: The cat belongs to a Church of Disguise priest, and is a spy.

events.name: As you wish
events.text: A farmhand hired for a day says 'as you wish' to every request, carries everything, and gazes at one party member a great deal.
events.nod: The Princess Bride: 'As you wish'
events.twist: He is a disguised noble heir, running from an arranged marriage.

events.name: The woman who never blinks
events.text: A pleasant woman shares her supper by the {road|rail|fire}: fresh bread, hot stew, good wine. She never blinks, and never eats.
events.twist: In the morning she is gone, and so are the party's bad dreams.

events.name: Someone tidied the camp
events.text: In the morning the fire is banked, the boots are dry, and a dead monster lies neatly beside the camp. There are no tracks.
events.twist: The same thing happens the next night, a little closer.

events.name: Wet footprints on deck
events.text: At dawn there is a pile of fresh fish and a {pearl|silver ring|bronze spirit coin} on the deck, and a line of wet bare footprints from the rail.

events.name: Lucky bones
events.text: A bone-reader at a crossroads casts knucklebones and gives each of the party a lucky bone. Carrying it grants inspiration. The bones are human.
events.twist: The bone-reader asks for one of the party's bones in return, one day.

events.name: The empty storehouse
events.text: A burned village's storehouse stands intact. The villagers will not be back. Their {grain|salt fish|cheese} would feed the party for a week.

events.name: A soldier's grave goods
events.text: On an old battlefield, the Church of War has left weapons on the graves for anyone who will carry on the fight. A note asks them to be used well.
events.twist: Someone is watching from the trees to see who takes them.

events.name: A dying man's map
events.text: A dying {Iron|Bronze}-rank adventurer presses his map into a party member's hand and asks them to finish his contract. The map is very good.
events.twist: The contract is against a noble house.

events.name: The polite monster
events.text: An Iron-rank monster leaves a dead rabbit at the edge of camp every morning, bows its head, and goes. Nobody knows why.
events.twist: It wants something killed, and has chosen the party for it.

events.name: Upside-down rain
events.text: The rain falls upward around the camp, leaving a dry circle for everyone to sleep in.

events.name: A signpost that argues
events.text: A signpost argues with itself in two voices about which way is quickest. Eventually one voice wins, and it is right.
events.twist: The losing voice follows them, sulking.

events.name: An old acquaintance
events.text: {npc} is on the road, going the other way.

events.name: A hook resurfaces
events.text: A loose thread catches up with the party: {hook}

events.name: Someone remembers
events.text: Someone sent by {faction} has been looking for the party.

events.name: News from home
events.text: A traveller brings news from {place} that concerns the party.

events.name: A letter catches up
events.text: A courier has been chasing the party for a week with a letter from {npc}.

events.name: A face in the crowd
events.text: At a market, one party member sees someone who should be dead, or far away. They're gone before anyone can reach them.

events.name: A familiar face
events.text: {npc} is at the same inn tonight, and buys the first round.

events.name: The rumour has grown
events.text: A bard is singing about the party's last adventure, and has got all of it wrong. In this version, they won.

events.name: The hook resurfaces
events.text: News from the road brings the party back to something they let slip: {hook}

events.name: The thank-you feast
events.text: A town the party once helped has heard they're passing, and has laid out a feast with banners.

events.name: A debt called in
events.text: Someone who did the party a favour has come to collect, with a request they can't easily refuse.

events.name: The church remembers
events.text: A priest of {church} has heard of the party and wants a word, privately.

events.name: The witness
events.text: A stranger describes something the party did, in detail, from a place where no one should have been watching.

events.name: The second meeting
events.text: {npc} is here too, on this road, at this exact moment. It's not a coincidence.

events.name: A gift from a friend
events.text: A package left at a waystation for the party, from {npc}, with a note and something useful.

events.name: Reputation
events.text: People in this town have heard of the party. Prices drop by a tenth, and nobody wants to fight them.

events.name: A poster for a friend
events.text: A missing poster for {npc}, posted on a waystation board.

events.name: Someone took credit
events.text: A team of adventurers in a tavern is boasting about something the party did, and getting free drinks for it.

events.name: The child they saved
events.text: Someone the party helped long ago has grown up, and wants to say thank you.

events.name: The forged contract
events.text: A forged Adventure Society contract with the party's names on it is going around the region.

events.name: The watchers
events.text: The party realises they've been followed for days by someone working for {faction}.

events.name: The innkeeper remembers
events.text: An innkeeper remembers the party from {place}, and keeps a room for them free of charge.

events.name: The old rival
events.text: A rival from the party's past is on the road with a team of her own, going the same way.

events.name: The outworlder's return
events.text: An outworlder the party met before has made a name for themselves, and wants to thank them for the help that started it.

events.name: Word left at the waystation
events.text: The waystation keeper has a message for the party, left two days ago by {npc}. It says only: {wait here|turn back|trust nobody from the east}.
events.twist: The keeper was paid to read it first, and has told someone else too.

events.name: A seat kept warm
events.text: At the next inn, the landlord says {npc} passed through recently and paid for the party's {supper|rooms|horses' feed} in advance, should they come this way.

events.name: The same road, the other way
events.text: {npc} is coming the other way with {a heavy pack|a lame horse|a new companion} and a tired face, and stops to trade news.
events.twist: They have just come from where the party is going, and advise against it.

events.name: A familiar seal
events.text: A sealed letter in a dead {courier's satchel|pedlar's coat|sailor's boot} bears the name of {npc}. It was meant for someone else entirely.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to open and reseal it unnoticed
events.failText: the wax cracks, and anyone who sees it will know

events.name: Trouble finds an old ally
events.text: {Smoke|Shouting|Crows circling} ahead. The burning wagon belongs to {npc}, and whoever did this is still close.
events.twist: It was staged to draw the party in, and the attackers know their names.

events.name: Asked after
events.text: Everyone at the {ferry|toll gate|well} says the same thing: a stranger was here yesterday asking, on behalf of {npc}, whether the party had passed, and describing them perfectly.
events.twist: The stranger left a tip for whoever passed the answer on.

events.name: A borrowed thing returned
events.text: A carter waves the party down. {npc} asked him to return {a cloak|a cooking pot|a book} the party lent long ago, and he has carried it for a month.
events.twist: Something has been added to it, wrapped in oilcloth.

events.name: The favour in writing
events.text: A {Society runner|Journey courier|grubby street child} brings a sealed note from {npc}. It asks a favour, offers a fair price, and gives a deadline.

events.name: Fresh tracks, known boots
events.text: A party member recognises the bootprints in the mud. They belong to someone they last saw in {place}, and they are following the same route.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to read how old they are
events.failText: the tracks vanish where they should not

events.name: The one who got away
events.text: A traveller describes {a scarred|a smiling|an one-eyed} stranger who robbed them last week. It sounds exactly like someone the party let go near {place}.
events.twist: The stranger has been using the party's names.

events.name: A rival's camp
events.text: Up ahead is the camp of a rival team the party has crossed before. Their fire is still warm, and their {map|contract|ledger of cores} is drying on a rock.
events.check: Stealth DC 13 to read it
events.failText: the rivals come back for it, and words get sharp

events.name: An unpaid grudge
events.text: A well-dressed stranger names the party. Their testimony sent him to an island prison years ago. He escaped, grew rich, and has come to settle it.
events.twist: He has already bought the inn they plan to sleep at.
events.nod: The Count of Monte Cristo

events.name: The mocking note
events.text: Pinned to a tree in the party's path: a rude drawing of the party and the words '{Too slow again|Better luck next time|We got here first}'. Their old rival's mark is in the corner.
events.twist: The rivals have taken the contract the party was heading for.

events.name: A shared enemy
events.text: Someone the party once fought sits alone at the roadside, {beaten and robbed|stripped of their rank badge|half-drowned}. They ask, stiffly, for help against the people who did it, who wear the colours of {faction}.

events.name: The rival in trouble
events.text: The rival team the party loves to hate is stuck by the road, their wagon {missing a wheel|axle-deep in mud|on its side}. They pretend not to need help.
events.check: Athletics DC 12 to lift the wagon
events.failText: it slides back in, and the rivals laugh

events.name: Old blades, new owner
events.text: A pedlar is selling a weapon the party took from a foe near {place} and later sold. He claims it is haunted by its first owner's temper.
events.twist: The first owner is alive, and wants it back.

events.name: The grudge-keeper's ledger
events.text: A dropped notebook lists every inn the party has stayed at this year, with dates, under two columns marked 'naughty' and 'nice'. The last line is today's road.
events.nod: Father Christmas and his list of who has been naughty or nice

events.name: A face from the fight
events.text: A beggar at the crossroads has a scar a party member gave him {in a tavern brawl|on a contract|in an ambush}. He is not angry. He just wants to know why.

events.name: Respect between enemies
events.text: A rider from {faction} delivers a gift of {good wine|a fine knife|a cured ham} and a short note: 'For the trouble last time. No hard feelings, yet.'

events.name: They kept score
events.text: A rival team has painted a tally board on a barn wall: their wins against the party's. The party is losing, according to the board, by a great deal.
events.twist: The rivals are hiding behind the barn, waiting to see the party's faces.

events.name: The road companion again
events.text: {npc} is resting at the same spring, and says it is good luck to share water with someone you know on a long road.

events.name: A message by bird
events.text: A small bird made of folded paper and faint light lands on a party member's shoulder and recites a message from {npc} in their voice, then falls apart.

events.name: Old allies, older debts
events.text: A team the party fought beside at {place} now owes the Society a fine, and asks the party to vouch for them at the {next branch|hearing in Greenstone|branch in Rimaros}.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 later, at the branch
events.twist: One of them did exactly what the fine says.

events.name: The rival's sister
events.text: A young adventurer introduces themselves as the {sister|cousin|apprentice} of someone the party beat in a contest. They seem thrilled, not angry, and want tips.

events.name: Ambush, but polite
events.text: A former enemy waits at the bridge with {two friends|a hired Bronze-ranker|their grandmother}. They announce, very formally, that they will attack at noon, and it is now eleven.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to talk them into lunch instead
events.failText: the fight starts at noon, sharp

events.name: The grudge goes quiet
events.text: The enemy who has hounded the party for weeks is sitting by the road, staring at nothing. They do not react to their own name.
events.twist: Something drained them in an astral space, and it might not have finished.

events.name: Help from an odd quarter
events.text: A one-time foe from {place} tells the party where the bandits ahead are waiting, then leaves without explaining why.

events.name: The rival's apology
events.text: A rival from {place} catches up on a tired horse just to say sorry for {a cheap shot at the guild hall|a stolen contract|a rude song}. It has clearly cost them a lot of pride.

events.name: Paying for the fight
events.text: A farmer recognises the party. His fence was smashed in their last brawl near here, and he wants {5|10|15} iron spirit coins for it.
events.cost: the fence money, or a few hours of fence-mending

events.name: Two old enemies meet
events.text: Two people the party has wronged at different times have found each other, and are drinking together at the {inn|bathhouse|dog fights} tonight.

events.name: The enemies' proposal
events.text: The two old grudges are waiting at the roadside, sober. They offer a deal: one job together, and all is forgiven.
events.twist: One of them means it. The other is selling the party to {faction}.

events.name: The old rival's wedding
events.text: A wedding party fills the road. The groom is a rival the party once humiliated, and he insists they attend so they see how well he is doing.
events.check: Performance DC 12 for a toast that does not start a fight
events.failText: the toast starts a fight

events.name: A ghost of an old fight
events.text: Near {place}, where they once fought for their lives, the party hears the clash of weapons, faint and exact, like a memory playing aloud.

events.name: Someone repaid
events.text: An Iron-ranker the party once saved from a monster runs up the road with a pouch of {spirit coins|dried meat|monster cores}. 'I said I'd pay you back.'

events.name: Too familiar a smile
events.text: The ferryman greets one party member by a childhood nickname that nobody here should know, then adds that {npc} sends regards.
events.twist: He was paid to say it, by someone who has been studying them.

events.name: Letters from the front
events.text: A bundle of letters washes up in an oilskin. They are from {npc}, and they describe trouble that may already be over.

events.name: A friend's new rank
events.text: Word comes that {npc} has {come into money|reached a new rank|been honoured by their town}, and wants the party at the celebration when they pass back through {place}.

events.name: The marked map
events.text: A map found in the road has the party's route drawn on it in red, and a cross at {a ford|a ruin|an inn} two days ahead.
events.twist: The map belongs to a bounty hunter who wants it back, badly.

events.name: Not the same person
events.text: {npc} waves from across a river, but the voice, the walk and the laugh are all slightly wrong.
events.twist: It is a twin, or a shapeshifter, and both would be news.

events.name: The insult in song
events.text: A street singer performs a song about the party's rival. It is rude and catchy, and the rival is sitting in the front row.

events.name: The deck of names
events.text: A fortune teller turns three cards and each one shows a face the party knows: {npc}, a stranger, and one of the party.
events.twist: The stranger will be on the road tomorrow.

events.name: A long wave
events.text: From a passing ship's rail, {npc} waves and shouts something lost on the wind.

events.name: Enemy at the hearth
events.text: The only shelter for miles is a farmhouse, and the family inside lost a {son|daughter|brother} in a fight the party was part of.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15 to be let in
events.failText: the party sleeps cold in the barn

events.name: The thank-you that hurts
events.text: A grieving traveller thanks the party for avenging their {husband|wife|brother}. The party did not. They were paid to stay out of it.

events.name: The wanted poster
events.text: A wanted poster for the party is nailed to the waystation. The drawings are terrible, and the reward is insultingly {small|specific|paid in turnips}.
events.twist: Someone has been doing crimes in their name.

events.name: Children playing heroes
events.text: Village children are acting out the party's last adventure with sticks and {a sheet|a goat|a cart} for a monster. They argue over who gets to be which party member.

events.name: The tale has teeth
events.text: In this town the story of the party's last fight is told as a warning. Parents use their names to frighten children {into bed|away from the river|into eating greens}.
events.twist: Something did happen here after the party left, and the town blames them.

events.name: The impostors
events.text: Three adventurers at the inn are calling themselves by the party's names and running up a tab they say {faction} will pay.
events.check: Insight DC 12 to catch them out in front of the room
events.failText: the crowd sides with the impostors, who are more charming

events.name: Free drinks, conditions apply
events.text: A tavern offers the party free drinks for a night if they tell the story of {their last contract|their worst defeat|how they met}. The crowd heckles every detail.

events.name: A statue, of sorts
events.text: Someone has carved the party in wood at a crossroads. The likeness is uncanny, and the statues have moved a few feet closer to the road since the last traveller saw them.

events.name: Hearsay at the toll
events.text: The toll keeper waves the party through for nothing. 'Heard what you did at {place}. Go on.'

events.name: The minstrel who follows
events.text: A minstrel has started trailing the party, singing a verse about each brave thing they do, and a longer verse about each time they ran away.
events.nod: Monty Python and the Holy Grail: Brave Sir Robin's minstrels

events.name: The rumour of a death
events.text: Everyone in {place} believes one of the party died last month. There is a memorial stone, flowers, and a grieving {friend|sweetheart|debt collector}.
events.nod: Mark Twain: reports of his death were exaggerated

events.name: The broadsheet
events.text: A Greenstone broadsheet has a column about the party, with details only someone close could know. The writer thanks {npc} for their help.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to work out the real source
events.failText: the party suspects the wrong friend

events.name: The fan
events.text: A young {farmhand|cook|goatherd} has copied one party member exactly: the clothes, the walk, the catchphrase. He wants to join.

events.name: A legend, misplaced
events.text: A village insists the party slew a dragon here years ago. They have never been here, and there are no dragons nearby, and the village has the bones to prove it.
events.twist: The bones are real, and the dragon's mate has just heard who killed it.

events.name: Weighed and found wanting
events.text: A Society branch clerk reads the party's file aloud at the counter, including every {failed contract|unpaid fine|complaint from a farmer}, while the queue listens.

events.name: Big in the Drift Hosts
events.text: A Drift Host walking house stops beside the party. Its riders have heard of them and want the full story over {roast heidel|fermented milk|a very long meal}.
events.check: Performance DC 13 to tell it well
events.failText: the riders wander off, bored

events.name: The ballad gets a new verse
events.text: A singer at the fire adds a verse about the party that describes something that has not happened yet.
events.twist: It happens within the week, in some form.

events.name: A sign of welcome
events.text: A painted sign outside {place} now reads 'Friends of this town are friends of the party' with their names misspelled.

events.name: Sea shanty
events.text: The crew of a passing ship are hauling lines to a shanty about the party. The chorus rhymes one of their names with something rude.

events.name: Cloud Clan honour
events.text: A Cloud Clan scout recognises the party's names from a tale told in the mountains, and offers safe passage through clan skies.

events.name: The tavern where it began
events.text: The party passes a tavern with a new plaque: 'A band of heroes met here'. It is not where they met, and the owner will not hear otherwise.
events.nod: D&D: every party meets in a tavern

events.name: Fame, misread
events.text: Pilgrims bow to the party and leave offerings at their feet. A shrine in the next village says they are minor saints of {church}.

events.name: What the river town says
events.text: Delta boatmen recognise the party and charge them the local rate, which is {half the price|a third of the price|free, for a story}.

events.name: Home again, changed
events.text: The party reaches a familiar stretch near {place} and finds {new walls|a burned barn|a new shrine} where they remember none.

events.name: News from the old town
events.text: A traveller from {place} brings news: someone the party knew there has died, and left them something.
events.twist: The something is a debt.

events.name: The inn that kept the room
events.text: A coaching inn on the road still has the party's names chalked over a door. 'You never came back for your room. It's paid till {spring|the solstice|next year}.'

events.name: The town that blames them
events.text: The people of {place} have put the party on their list of people who did not help when it mattered. The list is carved into the town gate.

events.name: Postcards from nowhere
events.text: A letter addressed to the party in their own handwriting is waiting at the post house in {place}. It is dated next month.
events.twist: It warns them about something on this very road.

events.name: A change at the crossroads
events.text: The crossroads shrine the party prayed at on their way out has been smashed, and nobody here will say who did it.

events.name: The shrine-breakers
events.text: Ahead, the party finds the shrine-breakers: young zealots of the Church of Purity, scrubbing another roadside altar clean.
events.check: Persuasion or Intimidation DC 13 to stop them without a fight
events.failText: they shout heresy, and the next town will hear of it

events.name: The dog remembers
events.text: An old, grey {dog|goat|mule} at the roadside staggers up and greets one party member like family. It was a stray they fed once, long ago.
events.nod: Homer's Odyssey: Argos the old dog recognising Odysseus

events.name: Market day, again
events.text: The party reaches {place} on market day, just as last time. The same stallholders remember what they bought, and have opinions about it.

events.name: The healer's clinic
events.text: A Church of the Healer clinic on this road treated the party once. The healer insists on checking old wounds, free.

events.name: The bridge they broke
events.text: The bridge the party wrecked in a fight months ago has been rebuilt, with a small carved warning: 'No heroes on the bridge'.
events.twist: The bridge-builder is waiting at the far end with the bill.

events.name: A harbour that remembers
events.text: The harbourmaster of {place} has a crate waiting for the party. Nobody signed for it, and it {ticks|hums|is warm}.

events.name: The sleeper in the hollow
events.text: A man wakes from a long sleep in an astral space and asks the party for news. He insists the last thing he remembers is the party themselves walking past, years ago.
events.nod: Rip Van Winkle
events.twist: He describes them perfectly, but older.

events.name: The bloodstain message
events.text: Scratched into the ground where a party member nearly died, in their own handwriting: 'try rolling'. Nobody remembers writing it.
events.nod: Dark Souls: player messages left on the ground

events.name: Same greeting, word for word
events.text: The innkeeper greets the party with the exact words, joke and wink they used last time, and the time before that.
events.nod: Groundhog Day: the same morning repeating
events.twist: She does it to everyone. She thinks it is charming.

events.name: An envoy on the road
events.text: A {rider|carriage|walking courier} bearing the colours of {faction} pulls alongside. The envoy has been sent to find the party, and has a question.
events.twist: The envoy is lost too, and would love directions.

events.name: The faction's price
events.text: A clerk for {faction} presents a bill: damages from the party's last job, itemised, with interest. Payment is expected {today|by the next town|in favours}.
events.twist: Half the items on the bill are for things the party did not do.

events.name: Watched by the faithful
events.text: Every shrine of {church} on this road has a fresh candle burning, and someone has scratched the party's names beneath each one.
events.twist: The candles are prayers for their safety, from someone they once helped.

events.name: A blessing waiting
events.text: At a wayside altar of {church}, the offering bowl fills with clear water as the party approaches, and a party member hears their name spoken kindly.

events.name: The priest's request
events.text: A travelling priest of {church} remembers the party's help and asks one more: carry a {relic|letter|sealed jar} to the next temple, without opening it.
events.twist: The faction that wants it will try to buy it off them on the way.

events.name: A sermon about them
events.text: A priest of {church} is preaching from a cart. His lesson for today is the party, and they are the bad example of {pride|gluttony|reckless spending}.
events.check: Performance or Persuasion DC 13 to win the crowd back
events.failText: the crowd jeers them out of town

events.name: Invited to dinner
events.text: Riders from {faction} bring an invitation: dinner at their lodge tonight, in honour of past help. The food is real, and so are the questions after it.
events.twist: The dinner is also a job interview.

events.name: Sent to test them
events.text: A young member of {faction} challenges the party to a {duel|riddle game|race to the next milestone}. It is clearly an assignment.
events.check: the contest's skill, DC 13
events.failText: the youngster reports back that the party is overrated

events.name: A tithe remembered
events.text: A collector for {church} stops the party: they promised a donation last time they passed a temple. It was a polite promise. He has it written down.
events.cost: 2 iron spirit coins, or an awkward refusal
events.twist: He is not a real collector, and the temple has never heard of him.

events.name: A faction's apology
events.text: A messenger from {faction} delivers a purse and an apology for a past slight. It is the most money the party has seen this month.

events.name: Shadowed by grey cloaks
events.text: For two days, a pair in plain grey cloaks has stayed exactly a mile behind. When challenged, they show the token of {faction} and say nothing.
events.check: Stealth DC 15 to lose them
events.failText: they are back by evening
events.twist: They are bodyguards. Someone is paying to keep the party alive.

events.name: Sanctuary offered
events.text: Rain hammers the road. A small temple of {church} flings its door open and calls the party in by name.

events.name: The faction's map
events.text: A member of {faction} who owes the party a favour sends a marked map: a quicker route, and a {safe camp|hidden cache|friendly farm} on the way.
events.twist: The map also marks where the faction's rivals camp.

events.name: The church remembers wrongly
events.text: A temple of {church} has written the party into its records as saints, heretics and benefactors, in three different hands.
events.twist: For a donation they can read the records, and some of it is news to them.

events.name: A loose thread pulls
events.text: A stranger at the inn mentions something in passing that makes one party member go cold. It ties back to something old: {hook}

events.name: A paper trail
events.text: A Society notice board carries a fresh contract that sounds familiar. Read closely, it is linked to this: {hook}

events.name: Someone else is working it
events.text: Another team asks the party for directions, and the place they are looking for is part of a lead the party dropped: {hook}

events.name: The thread tightens
events.text: The party finds a {body|burned cart|ransacked camp} by the road, and a note nearby. It shows they waited too long on this: {hook}

events.name: A dream about the hook
events.text: Three party members wake from the same dream. In it, a voice keeps returning to one thing: {hook}

events.name: Clue on the wind
events.text: A loose page blows into a party member's face and sticks. It is a page torn from a ledger, and it relates to this: {hook}

events.name: The hook, but sooner
events.text: A rider gallops past shouting news. The party realises it changes the timing of something they have been putting off: {hook}

events.name: The witness to the hook
events.text: An old {drover|fisherwoman|retired guard} by the fire saw something years ago and never told anyone. With a drink in them, they mention it, and it bears on this: {hook}
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to get the whole story
events.failText: they clam up, and only give half

events.name: Bought by someone else
events.text: A broker in the market has sold information about a lead the party was keeping quiet, to a rival team. The lead was this: {hook}

events.name: A price on the thread
events.text: A hooded figure offers {10|20|50} iron spirit coins to forget something the party knows: {hook}
events.twist: Refusing marks them. Accepting does too.

events.name: Gifts from the road church
events.text: A Church of the Journey shrine has a small bag left on the altar with the party's names: dried fruit, clean socks and a blessing.

events.name: Called before the Society
events.text: A Society runner catches up with a summons: the party is wanted at the nearest branch to explain the {paperwork|damages|missing core} on their last contract.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to get the hearing put off
events.failText: the runner insists, and the party must call in at the branch

events.name: The Magic Society's interest
events.text: A Magic Society researcher has been studying a {core|weapon|potion} the party sold. She has questions about where they got it, and pays for answers.
events.twist: She thinks it came from something that should not exist.

events.name: A house flag at the inn
events.text: The inn is flying the banner of a noble house the party once crossed. Inside, all the staff are wearing the house colours, as if by order.
events.twist: The house has bought the inn, and raised the prices.

events.name: A crown of storms
events.text: An envoy of the Storm Kingdom's crown has heard of the party, and wants to {hire|bribe|warn} them, in that order.

events.name: The church's spy
events.text: A {pilgrim|pedlar|chatty widow} who has walked beside the party all day turns out to be keeping notes for {church}.
events.check: Insight DC 14 to notice before nightfall
events.failText: the notes are already sent

events.name: Old cult, new face
events.text: A smiling charity worker hands out bread at a crossroads. A party member recognises the symbol on the bread basket from a cult they once disrupted.
events.twist: The cult recognises them too, and is very polite about it.

events.name: A gift for a gift
events.text: A Church of the Hearth priest gives the party a loaf of bread in return for help they gave another hearth, long ago. It is still warm, though the temple is miles back.

events.name: Owed by the house
events.text: A steward of a noble house stops the party with a {letter of credit|purse|cask of wine}. The house pays its debts, even small ones, even late.

events.name: Church against church
events.text: Two priests, one from {church} and one from its rival, both ask the party to back their side in a roadside dispute. Both remember them as allies.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15 to keep both happy
events.failText: one of the churches holds a grudge

events.name: A faction's banner, torn
events.text: The party finds a torn banner of {faction} staked in the ground, with fresh blood on the pole and the party's camp sign beside it.

events.name: The archive copy
events.text: A Church of Knowledge scribe is following the party, writing down everything they say for the archive. Everything. Including the {snoring|swearing|singing}.
events.twist: He sells copies on the side, and they are popular.

events.name: A god's attention
events.text: For one moment, the road falls silent and the party feels the attention of the god of {church}, warm and curious, then gone.
events.twist: Their next prayer to that god is answered, briefly and personally.

events.name: The returned favour
events.text: A clerk from {faction} waves the party through a checkpoint and quietly tears up a fine with their name on it.

events.name: The sealed order
events.text: A rider of {faction} hands the party a sealed order with their names on it, then rides off before they can refuse.

events.name: The order opens itself
events.text: The unopened order from {faction} splits its own wax and unfolds at dawn. It contains instructions and a deadline of tonight.
events.twist: The instructions are for someone else. The party got it by mistake.

events.name: The core remembers
events.text: A monster core the party harvested long ago glows in a pack, and shows a flicker of the {fight|forest|astral space} it came from.
events.twist: It points, faintly, toward another of its kind.

events.name: A spirit's thanks
events.text: A spirit the party once freed rises from a {stream|well|tide pool} as they pass and leaves a gift on the bank: a smooth stone that hums.

events.name: Footprints of light
events.text: Glowing footprints run ahead along the route, the same size as those of {npc}. They fade a few minutes after the party steps in them.
events.twist: They lead to a camp spot that is perfectly safe tonight.

events.name: Ghost of the road past
events.text: A pale figure falls into step beside one party member and shows them, like a window in the air, a choice they made a year ago, and who it hurt.
events.nod: A Christmas Carol: the Ghost of Christmas Past

events.name: The confluence answers
events.text: One party member's essences stir in recognition of a place they have never been. A natural array here once touched someone they knew: {npc}.
events.twist: Standing in it for an hour grants advantage on one check tomorrow.

events.name: The pedlar who is everywhere
events.text: The same cheerful pedlar the party met three towns back is set up at the next crossroads, ahead of them again, with the same stock and the same wink.
events.nod: Resident Evil 4: the merchant who turns up everywhere

events.name: A letter in a fish
events.text: A fish caught for supper has a sealed letter in its belly, dry and addressed to the party, from {npc}.

events.name: Their own luggage
events.text: The party finds a pack by the road. It is one of theirs, lost months ago, and it has been carefully repacked by someone with very neat habits.
events.twist: There is a thank-you note inside, for the use of the {blanket|knife|lucky sock}.

events.name: The talking milestone
events.text: A milestone speaks up as the party passes and reads out a message from {npc}, in a flat stone voice, with all the punctuation.

events.name: An old bounty pays out
events.text: A Society branch clerk chases the party down the street: a bounty they claimed months ago was underpaid, and here is the rest, {5|10|15} bronze spirit coins.

events.name: Salvage rights
events.text: A wreck the party reported off {place} months ago has been raised. As the reporters, they are owed a share, and the salvage master is honest.

events.name: The stashed loot
events.text: The party passes the hiding place where they stashed {spare cores|a bag of coins|a spare sword} on their last trip. It is still there.
events.check: Perception DC 13 to find it again
events.failText: someone found it first, and left a thank-you rock

events.name: A grateful village
events.text: The village the party saved from {a monster surge|a fire|a flood} has a cart of supplies ready for them. The kids hand over the food, solemnly.

events.name: A guide from before
events.text: A guide the party once hired in {place} falls in with them for a day, free, and shows them a way only locals know.

events.name: The appraisal comes back
events.text: A Magic Society messenger finds the party: an item they left for appraisal is worth {much more|much less|something entirely different} than they hoped.

events.name: Your own grave
events.text: A roadside grave carries a party member's name and a date from last year. The flowers on it are fresh.

events.name: The mourner
events.text: A veiled stranger stands at the roadside, weeping. They say they buried a party member last year, and want to know who walks in that face.
events.twist: A shapeshifter died wearing that face, and the mourner loved them.

events.name: The letters stop
events.text: At every waystation for a week, there has been a letter from {npc}. Today there is not, and the keeper says someone collected it already.
events.check: Investigation DC 13 to learn who collected it
events.failText: the keeper cannot describe them at all, which is strange in itself

events.name: A familiar voice in the fog
events.text: In the fog, someone calls for help in the voice of {npc}. It moves when the party moves.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13 to resist following it
events.failText: whoever follows wanders an hour off the route

events.name: The trophy wall
events.text: An abandoned hunting lodge has a wall of trophies. One is the helm of someone the party fought beside, and it is labelled.

events.name: The old wound aches
events.text: An old wound on one party member starts to ache, sharply, whenever they face {north|the coast|the next town}. It never has before.

events.name: Someone is collecting them
events.text: A collector's catalogue in a dead man's pack lists each party member by name, rank and essences, with a price beside each one and the buyer's mark of {faction}.

events.name: Their names on a ship
events.text: A new fishing boat in the harbour has been named after the party. The owner is very proud. The boat is very leaky.
events.twist: The owner wants the party to bless it, properly, before it sinks.

events.name: The biographer
events.text: An outworlder with ink-stained fingers is writing the party's life story. He calls the rude bits 'fan fiction' and asks if they mind.
events.nod: Internet culture: fan fiction

events.name: Mistaken for each other
events.text: Travellers from {place} greet two party members by each other's names, and refuse to be corrected. Whatever happened here last time, it is their version now.

events.name: The detective's last question
events.text: A rumpled investigator from the Society stops the party, apologises, walks away, then turns back with {one more thing|just a small question|a tiny detail} about an old contract.
events.nod: Columbo: 'just one more thing'

events.name: The old enemy's tutor
events.text: A dignified old woman says she tutored someone the party defeated, and asks politely what they did wrong. She is taking notes for her other students.

events.name: Mail at the next town
events.text: The postmaster at {place} has a small stack of letters for the party, some of them very old.
events.twist: One is in a hand none of them knows, sent from the Storm Kingdom.

events.name: Back on familiar ground
events.text: The party recognises this stretch of road from a past journey, and makes good time without stopping to check the way.

events.name: The bill catches up
events.text: A bailiff with a very long scroll has followed the party through three towns. The scroll is their bar tab from {place}.

events.name: Their monster, stuffed
events.text: A taxidermist's shop proudly displays the head of a monster the party killed. The plaque credits a local {noble|priest|baker}, who has never left town.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13 to get the plaque changed
events.failText: the owner has them thrown out

events.name: We meet again
events.text: An old foe leaps onto a rock and begins a speech: 'So, we meet again.' He has clearly rehearsed. It goes on for some time.
events.nod: Cliche villain line from countless films and cartoons
events.twist: If interrupted, he gets flustered and starts again from the top.

events.name: The cursed souvenir
events.text: A street seller offers 'genuine relics of the party', including a sock, a tooth and a lock of hair. None of it is theirs. Some of it is from a goat.
events.twist: One item really is theirs, and it is hard to explain how he got it.

events.name: Hello, my name is
events.text: A young swordsman steps into the road, bows, and recites a speech about someone the party once worked for, who wronged his family. He wants directions, then revenge.
events.nod: The Princess Bride: Inigo Montoya's revenge speech

events.name: Where everyone knows them
events.text: The whole inn in {place} raises a cheer and calls out the party's names as they walk in. Someone has already poured their drinks.
events.nod: Cheers: the bar where everybody knows your name

events.name: A wedding invitation
events.text: The couple the party once helped meet are getting married in {place}, and have saved them {a seat at the front|a dance|a speech}.

events.name: A song for them
events.text: Merfolk surface beside the boat and sing a short, wordless song. It is the one they sang when the party helped them last.

events.name: The healed child
events.text: A child the party carried to a Church of the Healer clinic runs up the road on two good legs to say thank you.

events.name: They kept the fire going
events.text: A camp the party built on their last trip is still in use. Travellers have kept the fire ring, added a bench, and carved a {thank-you|map|joke} into it.

events.name: A Celestine's gift
events.text: A Celestine courier the party once sheltered lands lightly on the road and leaves a sprig of something that glows faintly blue. It keeps one night's camp warm.

events.name: The rookies grew up
events.text: The scared Iron-rank team the party once rescued is now Bronze, and they insist on {buying dinner|taking first watch|carrying the packs} for a day.

events.name: The old map, updated
events.text: A Leonid caravan master the party once helped presses an updated map on them, with all the new washouts marked.

events.name: The debt collector
events.text: A quiet clerk of {faction} has a contract with a party member's signature on it, for a loan they swear they never took.
events.twist: The signature is real, from a night they cannot remember.
events.check: Insight DC 15 to tell if the clerk knows more
events.failText: the clerk leaves, promising to come back

events.name: The ones they could not save
events.text: A memorial stone at {place} lists the dead of a disaster the party arrived too late to stop. People nod to them as they pass, and do not smile.

events.name: A second copy of the key
events.text: A locksmith returns a key the party left with him. He kept a copy, and someone paid him well for it last week.
events.twist: The buyer wore the badge of a noble house.

events.name: The rival's offer
events.text: A rival team proposes a truce and a joint contract against {faction}. They are serious, and they bring a map.

events.name: The old contract reopens
events.text: The Society has reopened a contract the party closed months ago. The monster they killed has been seen again.
events.twist: It was never the same monster. There were two.

events.name: A passenger from the past
events.text: A passenger aboard ship knows the party from somewhere, but will not say where, and asks to share their table every night.

events.name: A letter with no sender
events.text: A letter waits at the post house in {place}: one party member's name, a time and a place, and the words 'come alone'.

events.name: The empty meeting place
events.text: At the meeting place the party finds a lantern, a chair and a second letter: 'You were followed. I could not risk it. Look behind you.'
events.twist: Someone is behind them, and seems just as surprised.

events.name: The small man's bargain
events.text: A small, sharp-faced man stops the party. Someone they once helped made a bargain with him to save their lives, and now cannot pay. He wants the party to cover it.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Rumpelstiltskin

events.name: The name game
events.text: The small man returns for his due, and offers one way out: guess his true name by sundown.
events.check: Investigation DC 15 to learn it from the last village
events.failText: he takes what he is owed, and laughs all the way down the road

events.name: The thank-you drawing
events.text: A child at the waystation hands over a drawing: the party, fighting the monster that once troubled {place}. The whole town has heard they are coming.

events.name: The welcome committee
events.text: The party is met on the road by half a town: a cart of food, a brass band of three, and a very small parade.
events.twist: The band knows only one tune, and plays it all day.

events.name: The third-act warning
events.text: An outworlder grips a party member's arm. 'I've seen this film. The trusted friend betrays the heroes in the third act.' He means {npc}.
events.nod: Films in general: the third-act betrayal

events.name: Proof, or not
events.text: A messenger brings a letter that seems to bear out the outworlder's warning. It is in a familiar hand, and addressed to an enemy.
events.check: Investigation DC 15 to tell whether it is forged
events.failText: the party cannot tell, and must decide anyway

events.name: The cub
events.text: A wounded monster cub, harmless now, that will grow into something dangerous.

events.name: The thief
events.text: A thief caught taking the party's food, starving, with children waiting.

events.name: Two cries for help
events.text: Two groups begging for help in opposite directions, and time to help only one.

events.name: The fugitive
events.text: A village hiding a fugitive the Adventure Society has a bounty on, who seems to be innocent.

events.name: The dying stranger
events.text: A dying stranger offers their essence or awakening stone to whoever promises to finish their task.

events.name: Lawful captives
events.text: Captives the party could free, but doing it breaks a lawful contract or starts a feud with a house.

events.name: The deserter
events.text: A young deserter begs the party not to turn her in. The reward for her is high, and her unit is a day away.

events.name: A wounded rival
events.text: A rival team lies wounded after a monster attack. Helping them costs a day, and they are heading for the same contract.

events.name: The core thief
events.text: A starving child steals a monster core from the party. It's worth more than his family earns in a year.

events.name: The wrong bounty
events.text: The bounty the party has been hunting turns out to be a scared old woman who did nothing wrong. The client wants proof of death.

events.name: The last healing potion
events.text: A dying traveller and one healing potion left. There is a long road ahead.

events.name: The caged monster
events.text: Merchants have a caged intelligent monster that begs to be freed. They bought it legally.

events.name: A false confession
events.text: A village has caught the 'killer'. The party is fairly sure he didn't do it, and the hanging is at dawn.

events.name: Pay the toll or fight
events.text: Starving villagers have blocked the road and demand a toll. They are not bandits, just desperate.

events.name: Leave the slow one
events.text: A refugee caravan is fleeing a surge. The party can stay with them and go slowly, or go on at their own speed.

events.name: The lost heir's secret
events.text: The party learns that a noble heir is an outworlder in disguise. Revealing it would make them rich, and ruin her.

events.name: The cult child
events.text: A child raised in a cult, now free, with nowhere to go. The cult will come looking.

events.name: The essence
events.text: A dying adventurer offers the party an essence, in exchange for a promise to deliver a message to someone very dangerous.

events.name: The honest thief
events.text: A thief returns something she stole from the party, with an apology. She wants to stop stealing, and her boss won't let her.

events.name: Fire in the forest
events.text: A forest fire is coming. The party can stop and help evacuate a village, or outrun it.

events.name: A monster mother
events.text: A monster mother caught in a trap, her young crying nearby. The trapper will be back soon.

events.name: The rich man's horse
events.text: A noble offers the party good money to find his lost horse. The horse has escaped to a farm, where it is clearly much happier.

events.name: Bandits with a cause
events.text: Bandits rob only the noble house that taxed their village to ruin. They offer the party a share to look away.

events.name: Truth or comfort
events.text: A widow asks how her husband died. The party knows, and it was not heroic.

events.name: The hungry pilgrims
events.text: Pilgrims who have run out of food. Feeding them costs the party a day of supplies, and earns the Church of the Journey's goodwill.

events.name: The trolley problem
events.nod: Philosophy: the trolley problem
events.text: A runaway ore cart is heading for five trapped miners. A lever would send it down the other track, where one miner is working, unaware.

events.name: The poacher's family
events.text: A {gamekeeper|house steward|Society warden} has caught a poacher on noble land. The penalty is a hand. His children are watching from the hedge.
events.twist: The gamekeeper would take a bribe, and the poacher would rather lose the hand than owe the party.

events.name: The escaped servant
events.text: A runaway from a Storm Kingdom slave gang hides {under the party's cart|in their tent|behind a waystation wall}. The slaver's riders will be at the ford by noon, and their papers are legal there.
events.check: Deception DC 15 to hide her
events.failText: the riders find her, and remember the party's faces
events.twist: She has a brand on her shoulder, and the riders have a painting of her.

events.name: The honest smuggler
events.text: A smuggler is running cheap {healing potions|lamp oil|grain} past a Church of Trade tariff post. The tariff is legal. The village he sells to cannot afford the taxed price.
events.twist: The tariff officer is his sister, and she is looking the other way, for now.

events.name: A thief who stole back
events.text: A thief is fleeing a noble's guards with a {necklace|ledger|sealed box}. She swears it was stolen from her mother first, and the party half believes her.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to judge her story
events.failText: the party cannot tell, and must choose blind

events.name: The confessing bandit
events.text: A wounded bandit confesses to the party before he dies, and names a respected {Iron-rank adventurer|village reeve|temple deacon} as the one who planned the raids.
events.twist: The adventurer is standing in the crowd at the next town, being thanked.

events.name: The village secret
events.text: A village has been quietly paying a monster in {livestock|grain|cheese} to leave them alone. The Society would order it killed, and the village would lose its protection.
events.twist: The monster is getting old, and something worse waits for it to die.

events.name: The underage adventurer
events.text: A fourteen-year-old with a stolen Iron-rank badge is trying to sign up for contracts at the waystation. She is very bad at lying and very good with {a sling|a spear|her fists}.
events.twist: Her mother is a Silver-ranker, and is looking for her.

events.name: The bribe-taking guard
events.text: A gate guard takes a small bribe from every traveller. He gives every coin to {an orphanage|the Church of the Healer|his sick neighbours}, and the party saw him do it.

events.name: Turning in a friend
events.text: The Society has posted a bounty on a hedge-{witch|wizard|healer} the party bought charms from. Her charms worked. The charge is selling unlicensed magic.

events.name: The rigged trial
events.text: A roadside court of a noble house is trying a farmer for {theft|poaching|insulting the family}. The judge is the house's cousin, and the evidence is thin.
events.check: Persuasion DC 15 to speak for the farmer
events.failText: the court fines the party for interrupting
events.twist: The farmer did steal, to feed the judge's own unpaid servants.

events.name: Lost and found coins
events.text: A purse of spirit coins lies in the road with a name sewn in it. The owner's farm is half a day off the route.
events.twist: The owner calls it a trick, and accuses the party of taking some.

events.name: Mercy for a cultist
events.text: A young cultist, wounded and abandoned by her group, begs the party, weeping, {in the road|from a ditch|at their campfire}, not to hand her to the Church of Purity. She knows where the others went.

events.name: The forger's offer
events.text: A forger offers to fake the party a Bronze-rank {Society seal|guild licence|noble pass} for half the usual cost. It would open doors. It would also be fraud.
events.cost: 10 bronze spirit coins, if they accept
events.twist: The Society is running a sting, and the forger works for them.

events.name: The goat on trial
events.text: A village has put a goat on trial for eating the reeve's {hat|tax records|wedding cake}. The goat's owner begs the party to act as counsel, and the hearing is right now.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12 to win the goat's acquittal
events.failText: the goat is sentenced to a week of public shame, and so is its lawyer

events.name: Two claims, one stone
events.text: Two prospectors each swear they found the awakening stone first. Both ask the party to judge, and both have offered them a share.
events.nod: The judgement of Solomon
events.twist: Suggest splitting the stone, and watch which one flinches.

events.name: Stealing from thieves
events.text: The party finds a bandit camp empty, with the loot of {a dozen|twenty|countless} robberies piled in a tent. Returning it would take weeks. Keeping it would be easy.

events.name: The fleeing groom
events.text: A young man in wedding clothes sprints past and begs the party to say they never saw him. {Thirty angry relatives|The bride, with a cudgel,|A furious priest} arrive a minute later.

events.name: The informant
events.text: A soft-spoken man offers names: everyone in the next town who has sheltered {outworlders|dark essence users|deserters}. He says the Church of Purity pays well, and asks the party to carry the list.
events.twist: His list includes one of the party.

events.name: The returned prisoner
events.text: An old prisoner has finished his sentence in a Storm Kingdom mine and is walking home. He asks the party to read him the letter from his family, because he never learned.
events.twist: The letter says his family moved, and did not leave an address.

events.name: Bounty on a beast-friend
events.text: A Society contract offers good coin for a 'dangerous monster' near this road. The party finds it living peacefully with a hermit who feeds it.

events.name: The hunters arrive
events.text: Another team arrives to claim the beast-friend's bounty, armed and impatient. The hermit stands in front of his monster with a frying pan.
events.check: Persuasion or Intimidation DC 15 to turn them away
events.failText: it comes to blows, or to the hermit losing his friend

events.name: The egg clutch
events.text: A nest of {six|ten|two dozen} monster eggs, warm and unguarded, sits by the road. A Magic Society buyer would pay for them. Left alone, they will hatch into a problem for the next village.
events.twist: One egg is already hatching, and the chick thinks the party is its mother.

events.name: The talking monster's plea
events.text: An intelligent monster with {a broken leg|a crushed wing|an arrow in its side} asks the party, politely, to kill it quickly rather than leave it for the scavengers. Its core would be worth a lot.

events.name: The pet that grew
events.text: A farmer has raised a monster from a pup as a guard dog. It is now the size of a barn, adores children, and is technically illegal.
events.twist: It has already eaten two tax collectors, and the farmer swears that was a misunderstanding.

events.name: The mother's bargain
events.text: A huge monster blocks the road and speaks. It will let the party pass in peace, if they bring back its stolen young from the camp ahead.
events.twist: The camp ahead is a Church of the Healer clinic, and the young is very sick.

events.name: The greatback in the bog
events.text: A greatback is stuck in a bog, sinking slowly, with a caravan's {whole stock|silk and spices|family heirlooms} on its back. Saving the animal means losing the cargo, and the cargo is the caravan's future.
events.check: Athletics DC 15 for everyone to save both
events.failText: there is only time to save one

events.name: The surge refugees
events.text: A small band of weak monsters is fleeing a surge, and they are heading straight for {a village|a farm|a pilgrim camp}. They do not seem hostile, just terrified.

events.name: The last of its kind
events.text: A Magic Society hunter is closing in on a glowing, deer-like monster that may be the last of its kind. Its core is priceless. It looks the party in the eye.

events.name: Cores for the clinic
events.text: A village healer will trade three days of healing for the core of the monster that lives in the old {well|millpond|chapel crypt}. The monster is shy, and seems to keep the water clean.

events.name: The kraken's ransom
events.text: A large, polite sea monster has the captain's {hat|parrot|logbook}, and will return it only if the ship's cook stays with it. The cook seems quite keen.

events.name: The scorpion and the ferry
events.text: An intelligent monster with a stinger asks to ride the ferry across, swearing on its core it will not sting anyone.
events.nod: Aesop: the scorpion and the frog
events.twist: It means it, today.

events.name: Goblin children
events.text: The party clears a goblin raiders' camp and finds the raiders' young hiding in a cooking pit, frightened and armed with {spoons|sticks|very sharp teeth}.
events.nod: D&D's classic table argument: what to do with the goblin babies
events.twist: Their mother is still alive, and listening from the rocks.

events.name: The tamer's whip
events.text: A monster tamer is beating a cowering, intelligent beast to train it for a noble's arena. It is his property, under the law, and he is within his rights.

events.name: Lure of the core farm
events.text: A coin farm owner offers good pay to help bait monsters into his array. It is legal, but the bait is a live goat with a name tag reading '{Biscuit|Lady Esmerelda|Gerald}'.

events.name: The merfolk's net
events.text: A merfolk youth is tangled in a fishing net, and the fishermen want to sell him to a collector. He offers the party a pearl to cut him free.
events.twist: His mother is watching, and her thanks would be worth far more than a pearl.

events.name: The grateful monster
events.text: A monster the party spared once is waiting by the road, carrying a smaller, wounded {monster|child|Celestine} in its mouth. It lays it at their feet, and waits.

events.name: The rogue elemental
events.text: A small fire elemental, lost and dimming, begs to be carried in a lantern to a volcano vent two days off the road. It cannot survive the rain otherwise.
events.twist: If it lives, it promises to keep the party's fires lit for a year.

events.name: The hydra's heads
events.text: A small hydra stands at a crossroads, and its three heads are arguing. Each head offers the party a different deal, {gold|secrets|safe passage}, for cutting off the other two.

events.name: The pack mule's secret
events.text: A mule the party bought turns out to be a monster in disguise, very sweet, very good at carrying, and {growing|hungry for iron|learning to talk}. The Society would want it reported.

events.name: The siren who stopped
events.text: A siren on a rock has stopped singing ships to their deaths. She begs passage to somewhere no one knows her, and the sailors want her dead.
events.twist: If she is taken aboard, the sea goes very still and the crew stops rowing.

events.name: Monster on the altar
events.text: Villagers are bringing {goats|bread|their best fish} to a monster they think is a god. It keeps the other monsters away. It is also getting bigger.
events.nod: Folklore: offerings to a dragon or sea serpent to spare a town

events.name: The arena champion
events.text: An intelligent monster champion of a fighting pit asks the party to buy its freedom. The pit master names a price, {20 bronze coins|a fight|a favour}, the party can just afford.
events.cost: 20 bronze spirit coins, if they pay

events.name: The miscounted pay
events.text: The Society clerk has paid the party {twice|three times|ten times} what the contract was worth. Nobody else has noticed.

events.name: The drowned man's purse
events.text: A body on the shore still wears a fat purse and a ring with a {family crest|guild seal|church mark}. The family is a week's travel away.
events.twist: He did not drown. Someone held him under.

events.name: The cheap cores
events.text: A trader is selling monster cores at {a third|a quarter|half} of the market price, no questions asked. The cores still have Society tags, from a team posted missing.
events.twist: The trader is the missing team's last survivor, and is not well.

events.name: Buy the whole stall
events.text: A widow is selling her late husband's adventuring gear at the roadside, far too cheaply, because she needs the money today. A fair price would cost the party {10|15|20} iron spirit coins more.

events.name: The rich fool
events.text: A wealthy young noble wants to hire the party as 'guides' and is willing to pay a fortune. He wants to fight a monster. He has never held a sword.
events.twist: His mother is paying twice as much to make sure he never reaches one.

events.name: The rigged game
events.text: A card sharp is cheating a farmer out of his {harvest money|cow|daughter's dowry}. The farmer is winning anyway, through sheer luck, and the card sharp is close to tears.
events.check: Sleight of Hand DC 14 to fix the game for one side
events.failText: both of them notice

events.name: Blood money
events.text: A noble's agent offers the party a heavy purse to swear they saw {a rival heir|a merchant|a priest} at the scene of a murder. They did not.

events.name: The finder's fee
events.text: The party finds a lost child's dog, and the child's family is very rich. The reward poster says 'generous'. The child just wants a hug from the dog.
events.twist: The parents offer far less than the poster promised, and the child is mortified.

events.name: A cut of the haul
events.text: A sky ship crew offers the party a share of salvage from a wrecked {merchant ship|noble's yacht|Society supply barge}, if they help strip it before the owners arrive.

events.name: The awakening stone tithe
events.text: A priest of {church} asks the party to donate their newest {awakening stone|monster core|essence-touched blade} to the temple. In return, he promises a blessing that may or may not be real.

events.name: Paid to lose
events.text: The organiser of a village wrestling match offers the party's strongest member good money to lose to the reeve's {son|daughter|nephew}, who has a fragile ego.
events.check: Performance DC 13 to lose convincingly
events.failText: everyone can tell, and the reeve's son is even angrier

events.name: The debt sale
events.text: A merchant is selling a family's {farm|fishing boat|mill} to pay their debts, and the family is standing in the yard watching. The party could buy the debt, for most of what they have.

events.name: Coins on a grave
events.text: Travellers leave spirit coins on a roadside grave for luck. There is a small fortune there. The locals say whoever takes it is never lucky again.
events.twist: The grave is empty, and the priest of {church} who collects the coins is very much alive.

events.name: Selling the map
events.text: A rival team offers a good price for the party's map of a newly found {astral space|ruin|core seam}. They would get there first, and they are good at what they do.

events.name: The generous mistake
events.text: A shopkeeper gives the party {twice the change|a silver coin instead of iron|a whole purse by mistake}, and is clearly having a terrible day. Handing it back might make it better.

events.name: The tax collector's satchel
events.text: The party finds a tax collector's satchel in a ditch, full of coin taken from the villages they passed. The collector is nowhere to be seen.

events.name: The collector turns up
events.text: The tax collector staggers up, robbed and beaten, and begs for his satchel. Without it, he hangs. With it, the villages starve this winter.

events.name: The magic ring of no one
events.text: A plain {ring|cloak|button} turns its wearer invisible. The party knows nobody saw them find it, and nobody would ever know what they did with it.
events.nod: Plato's Ring of Gyges

events.name: Sold as a slave
events.text: A Storm Kingdom trader offers to buy a captured {bandit|cultist|pirate} from the party. The price is high, the sale is legal there, and the bandit tried to kill them yesterday.

events.name: A crate of potions
