events.text: A crate of healing potions has fallen off a {cart|barge|sky ship} and is lying unbroken. It is stamped with the mark of the Church of the Healer, for a clinic three days away.

events.name: Bought off
events.text: {faction} offers the party {20|50|100} bronze spirit coins to forget a contract and go home. It is more than the contract pays.
events.twist: The contract was a trap set for the party all along.

events.name: The cursed coin
events.text: A beggar asks the party to take a single silver spirit coin from him. He says it is cursed to return to whoever gives it away, and he desperately wants rid of it.
events.twist: It is cursed, but only to make its owner a very bad singer.

events.name: The stuck carriage
events.text: A carriage is stuck axle-deep in mud, and its driver is far too {old|drunk|pregnant} to dig it out alone. Helping costs the morning.

events.name: The long way round
events.text: The quick route runs through a village under quarantine for a {fever|curse|blight}. The long way costs two days. The villagers beg for medicine at the barricade.

events.name: The lame horse
events.text: One of the party's {horses|mules|heidels} has gone lame. Pushing on will ruin the animal for good. Resting costs half a day.

events.name: The wedding needs a priest
events.text: A wedding party on the road has lost its priest to {a twisted ankle|food poisoning|cold feet}, and asks if anyone in the party can say the words. It would take the afternoon.
events.check: Religion DC 12 to get the words right
events.failText: the couple are married anyway, though one vow is about turnips

events.name: Search party
events.text: A village is gathering a search party for a missing child, lost in the {woods|marsh|hills} since yesterday. The party's tracker could find her, but it will cost a day.
events.check: Survival DC 13 to find her before dark
events.failText: they find her at dawn, cold but alive

events.name: The slow pilgrims
events.text: An elderly pilgrim of {church} asks to walk with the party for safety. She walks at exactly half their speed, and talks the whole time.

events.name: The flood is coming
events.text: A dam above a valley farm is failing. The party can spend the day shoring it up, or warn the farm and keep going.
events.check: Athletics DC 15 for everyone to hold it
events.failText: the dam breaks anyway, but the family is out

events.name: The sinking boat
events.text: A {fishing boat|merfolk raft|pilgrim barge} is sinking in rough water. Turning the ship to help means losing the wind and a day of travel. The captain says it is the party's call.
events.twist: The fishermen are smugglers, and their cargo is worth more than the voyage.

events.name: Help with the harvest
events.text: A farming family has lost its eldest son to the Society's levy, and the {wheat|rice|apple} harvest is rotting. Two days of work would save it.
events.twist: The son's last letter asked someone, anyone, to help.

events.name: The courier's broken leg
events.text: A Society courier has broken a leg and begs the party to deliver his sealed packet on time. It is in the opposite direction.
events.twist: The packet holds the party's own names, and the deadline is not a coincidence.

events.name: A detour for a funeral
events.text: Villagers ask the party to carry a stranger's coffin. Nobody else can lift a Silver-ranker's, which weighs {as much as an ox|nearly nothing|a little more each mile}.

events.name: The stranded Celestine
events.text: A Celestine has torn a wing and cannot fly home. She asks to be carried to the nearest high peak, a day off the route.
events.twist: From the peak, she shows them a faster way.

events.name: Escort duty
events.text: A caravan of Runic craftsmen has lost its guards and asks the party to escort it. They pay well, but travel at half the party's pace.

events.name: A day of rest for the sick
events.text: A party member's fever is not getting worse, but it is not getting better either. A healer in the next town could help, a day out of the way.

events.name: Teach the village
events.text: A village with no Society branch asks the party to stay a day and teach its young how to fight off {weak monsters|bandits|giant rats}.

events.name: Two villages, one warning
events.text: Scouts report a monster surge coming. There is time to warn one village, not both. One is larger. The other is where {npc} lives.

events.name: The cat in the tree
events.text: A crying child begs the party to rescue her {cat|lizard|very old ferret} from a very tall tree. The cat has no intention of being rescued, and is armed.
events.check: Athletics DC 13
events.failText: the cat wins, decisively, and the child cries harder

events.name: The broken waystation
events.text: The waystation's {well rope|roof beam|signal bell} has snapped and the bucket is at the bottom. Fixing it takes hours. The next travellers will need it.

events.name: The sunken sky ship
events.text: A sky ship has crashed into a lake, and its crew is clinging to the wreck. Saving them means diving, and the lake is home to something large.
events.check: Athletics DC 15
events.failText: the something large notices

events.name: The fake relic
events.text: A shrine's holy {bone|tooth|finger} draws hundreds of pilgrims and feeds a whole village. A party member can tell it came from a pig.
events.check: Medicine or Nature DC 12 to be sure
events.failText: the party is not certain either way

events.name: The dying wish
events.text: A dying {soldier|sailor|old adventurer} asks whether they died well, and whether their team got away. The party saw the team flee and leave them.

events.name: The parents' hope
events.text: A couple ask whether the party has seen their son, an Iron-ranker who went into an astral space {a year|two years|a season} ago. The party found his badge inside one, last month.

events.name: The love letter
events.text: A shy young {sailor|guard|baker} asks the party to read his love letter aloud to the one he loves, because he cannot. It is very, very bad.
events.check: Performance DC 13 to make it sound good
events.failText: it is received with polite, terrible silence

events.name: A false prophet's good work
events.text: A self-proclaimed prophet of {church} is obviously a fraud, but his followers have stopped drinking, fixed the bridge and fed the poor.
events.twist: The real church is sending investigators, and they are not gentle.

events.name: The outworlder's secret
events.text: A cheerful travelling {cook|tinker|musician} is clearly an outworlder: odd words, odd tools, odd songs. She begs the party not to tell anyone. Collectors pay well for outworlders.

events.name: The forged pedigree
events.text: A noble heir confides that his whole bloodline is made up. His grandfather was a pig farmer. The heir is the best ruler the region has had in years.
events.twist: His cousin, a real noble and a monster, would inherit if anyone found out.

events.name: The cheating husband
events.text: A wife asks the party whether her husband is truly guarding caravans on the road, as he claims. The party knows he is. He is guarding them very badly.

events.name: The bad map
events.text: A proud old mapmaker gives the party a gift: his map of the region. It is beautiful, and {almost completely wrong|upside down|full of invented towns}.
events.check: Persuasion DC 12 to point out the errors kindly
events.failText: he is hurt, and the party leaves with the map anyway
events.twist: One mark is right: a ruin no one else knows about.

events.name: The miracle cure
events.text: A travelling seller's 'cure' is just coloured water, but a dying woman believes it is working, and is smiling for the first time in weeks.

events.name: The hero's statue
events.text: A town's founding hero, whose statue stands in the square, was {a bandit|a coward|a Storm Kingdom spy}. The party has found the proof in a ruin nearby. The town is very proud of him.

events.name: The lie that saved a town
events.text: A town believes it is protected by a god's blessing, so the monsters stay away. It is actually a natural array, and it is fading.
events.twist: Telling them would start a panic. Not telling them might be worse.

events.name: Who stole the pie
events.text: A baker accuses a party member of stealing a {pie|whole cheese|tray of buns} from her windowsill. The party member did not. Another party member did, and is still chewing.
events.check: Deception DC 13 to bluff it out
events.failText: the crumbs give it away, and the baker wants double

events.name: The spy's confession
events.text: A party member's new travelling companion admits she is a spy for {faction}, sent to watch them. She is also the best cook they have ever met.

events.name: The unwritten letter
events.text: A dying soldier asks the party to write to his mother, saying he is safe and happy. The party can lie, or tell her the truth.
events.twist: His mother has already guessed. She writes back thanking them for the kindness.

events.name: The rival churches' feud
events.text: Priests of {church} and a rival faith both claim a roadside {spring|oak tree|standing stone} as holy, and have nearly come to blows. Each asks the party to bear witness for them.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to find a fair answer
events.failText: one church feels cheated, and remembers
events.twist: The spring belongs to a third god, who is getting annoyed.

events.name: The Purity raid
events.text: Church of Purity zealots are about to burn the herb store of a village healer who uses death essence magic. She has saved half the village.

events.name: The healer's request
events.text: The death-essence healer from the raided village finds the party at camp. She asks them to carry her books to safety, and to tell no one.
events.twist: One book holds a cure. Another holds something the Church of Purity was right to fear.

events.name: The Society's order
events.text: The Adventure Society orders the party to stop and bring in a deserter from their contract. The deserter is fleeing to warn a {village|monastery|mining camp} the Society has written off.

events.name: The house's request
events.text: A noble house asks the party to carry a sealed message to its rival. It pays well. The party suspects the seal hides {a poison|a curse|an insult}.
events.check: Investigation DC 15 to check without breaking it
events.failText: the seal cracks, and the house will know
events.twist: The message is a marriage proposal. The poison is for the bearer.

events.name: A crisis of faith
events.text: A young priest of {church} has lost her faith on the road and is going home. She asks the party whether they think the gods really care.
events.twist: Her god is listening, and gently sends a sign while the party talks.

events.name: The forbidden shrine
events.text: A hidden shrine to the outlawed Church of Undeath, with fresh offerings. Reporting it would earn a reward. The worshippers are an old couple who lost their {son|daughter|grandchildren}.

events.name: Society or house
events.text: A Society contract and a noble house's order point the party to the same village, for opposite reasons. One wants a man arrested, the other wants him protected.

events.name: The man in the middle
events.text: The man everyone wants turns out to be a beekeeper with no idea why. His bees, however, have an awakening stone in the hive.

events.name: The Hero's challenge
events.text: A priest of the Church of the Hero demands the party prove their worth with a deed of glory before he will bless them. The only deed nearby is a lost {goat|cat|grandmother}.

events.name: Choosing a god
events.text: Two avatar messengers, one from {church} and one from its rival, appear on the road and each offer one party member a blessing, but only if they refuse the other.
events.twist: Refusing both earns quiet respect from a third god.

events.name: The Revels' feast
events.text: A Church of the Revels festival blocks the road. The party can join and lose a day to wine and dancing, or push through and be cursed with bad hangovers anyway.

events.name: The cult's good works
events.text: A cult runs the only clinic on this road. It is clean, kind and free. Every patient leaves with a small {tattoo|scar|new habit} they do not remember getting.
events.nod: Folklore and fiction: the charity that hides a cult

events.name: The Journey's rule
events.text: A Church of the Journey custom says travellers must share their fire with anyone who asks. Tonight, {a known thief|an old enemy|a Church of Purity inquisitor} has asked.

events.name: The Hearth's guest right
events.text: A family invites the party in under Hearth guest right. Then the party sees the bounty poster: their host is wanted for murder.
events.twist: Breaking guest right would be a sin. Waiting for morning might be too late.

events.name: The Justice priest's verdict
events.text: A priest of Justice has sentenced a thief to lose a hand. The thief is the priest's own brother. The priest asks the party to carry out the sentence.

events.name: The Liberty smugglers
events.text: Church of Liberty priests are smuggling escaped slaves across the border. They ask the party to carry {two|three|five} of them as their servants, past the checkpoint.
events.check: Deception DC 14 at the checkpoint
events.failText: the guards are suspicious, and want everyone's names

events.name: The Knowledge archive
events.text: A Church of Knowledge scholar will pay well for the party's notes on a cult they fought. The notes name people who have since left the cult.
events.twist: One of those names is now a priest of the Church of Purity.

events.name: The War chaplain
events.text: A Church of War chaplain is recruiting {farm boys|fishermen|miners' sons} for a noble's levy, with promises of glory. He asks the party to say a few words about the adventuring life.

events.name: The Ocean's due
events.text: Sailors say the Church of the Ocean's god demands one thing from each ship that crosses here. The sea has gone glass-flat, and is waiting for the party's offering.
events.twist: It wants something that matters. Coins will not do.

events.name: The Earth priest's mountain
events.text: A Church of the Earth priest begs the party not to let miners open a new {seam|tunnel|quarry face}. The mountain, he says, is sleeping. The miners' families are starving.

events.name: The Disguise priest
events.text: A priest of the Church of Disguise asks to borrow one party member's face for a day. They promise to return it, and to do nothing wicked with it.
events.twist: They give it back with a much nicer complexion.

events.name: The honest reward
events.text: A merchant offers the party a choice: a fat purse now, or a small favour from his patron, a powerful {mage|Gold-ranker|priest}, some day.

events.name: Keep or share
events.text: The party finds a rich cache of monster cores in a ruined camp. Another team nearby, beaten and broke, saw them find it.
events.twist: Sharing earns friends who will be Silver-rank one day.

events.name: The essence offer
events.text: A rival team has a spare {fire|shadow|swift} essence that would suit one party member perfectly. They will trade it, in return for the party's share of a contract they both want.

events.name: Treasure for a song
events.text: A dying old adventurer offers his last awakening stone to the party member who sings him the best {song|joke|lie}. The others in the room are also singing, loudly.
events.check: Performance DC 14
events.failText: a goatherd with a lovely voice wins it

events.name: The Trade wager
events.text: A Church of Trade priest offers a simple deal: put up {5|10|20} iron spirit coins, and if the party reaches the next town by sundown, he doubles it.
events.check: Athletics or Survival DC 13 for everyone
events.failText: they arrive after dark, and the priest is gracious about it

events.name: The withered paw
events.text: A pedlar sells a shrivelled monster paw that grants three wishes. He looks exhausted, and only wants it gone. 'Wish carefully,' he says, 'or better, not at all.'
events.nod: W. W. Jacobs: The Monkey's Paw
events.twist: Each wish comes true in the worst way that still counts.

events.name: The spirit in the lamp
events.text: A bound spirit in a brass lamp offers the party three favours. When asked what it wants, it whispers: freedom, which would cost the last favour.
events.nod: Arabian Nights: Aladdin and the genie

events.name: The sealed box
events.text: A dying courier presses a sealed box into the party's hands and makes them swear never to open it. It is very light, and it {hums|whispers|is warm}.
events.nod: Greek myth: Pandora's box

events.name: The box speaks
events.text: The sealed box starts talking in the night, offering a party member their heart's desire if they let it out. It sounds sincere. It sounds lonely.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 14 to resist peeking
events.failText: the lid lifts an inch, and something small and bright escapes into the dark

events.name: The two prisoners
events.text: Two captured {bandits|smugglers|cultists} are held apart. Each offers to name the other as the killer in exchange for freedom. Only one of them can be telling the truth.
events.nod: Game theory: the prisoner's dilemma
events.check: Insight DC 15 to tell which
events.failText: both stories sound true

events.name: The happy town's cellar
events.text: A town of perfect happiness and wonderful weather. Beneath the shrine, a monster child is chained in the dark, and the townsfolk say the blessing depends on it.
events.nod: Ursula K. Le Guin: The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas

events.name: The mayor's old crime
events.text: A bounty hunter is tracking a man who stole bread twenty years ago and broke parole. That man is now a beloved mayor who built an orphanage.
events.nod: Victor Hugo: Les Miserables
events.twist: The bounty hunter is his son, who does not know it.

events.name: Two doors
events.text: A ruin has two doors and a riddle. Behind one is a treasure, behind the other a hungry monster. The princess who set the riddle is smiling at one of them.
events.nod: Frank Stockton: The Lady, or the Tiger?
events.check: Insight DC 15 to read her smile
events.failText: the party has to choose blind

events.name: Save or harvest
events.text: A small glowing spirit is carrying an awakening stone inside itself. Taking it would kill the spirit and give a fine stone. Freeing it gives a smaller gift, and its thanks.
events.nod: BioShock: rescue or harvest
events.twist: The spirit's thanks pay off later, in a way the stone never could.

events.name: The town on the sleeping beast
events.text: A village is built on the back of a dormant giant {turtle|serpent|crab}. A Magic Society agent pays well for anyone willing to wake it, to harvest its core.
events.nod: Fallout 3: the town built around an unexploded bomb

events.name: The unwinnable test
events.text: An outworlder officer of a mercenary company sets the party a test she designed to have no winning answer. She wants to see how they lose.
events.nod: Star Trek: the Kobayashi Maru
events.twist: There is an answer: refuse to take the test. She will not say so.

events.name: The prime directive
events.text: An outworlder healer refuses to show a village how to cure its blight. 'Back home we call it the Prime Directive.' The party knows the cure too.
events.nod: Star Trek: the Prime Directive

events.name: Ford the river
events.text: The caravan leader stares at the swollen river and asks the party: ford it, caulk the wagons and float, or wait for a ferry that may not come?
events.nod: The Oregon Trail video game
events.check: Survival DC 13 to choose well
events.failText: a wagon is lost, and someone gets dysentery

events.name: The crossroads deal
events.text: At a crossroads at midnight, a well-dressed stranger offers a party member the skill they most want, at once, for a price named later.
events.nod: Folklore: the deal with the devil at the crossroads
events.twist: He keeps very good books.

events.name: The honest mirror
events.text: A hand mirror shows each person who they will be in {ten|twenty|forty} years if they keep going as they are. The current owner asks the party to smash it. It is worth a fortune.

events.name: The swapped faces
events.text: Two travellers have swapped faces in an astral space accident and want the party to decide whose face is whose. Both lie, and both are very convincing.
events.check: Insight DC 14
events.failText: the party picks wrong, and nobody may ever know

events.name: The duplicate
events.text: A perfect copy of one party member steps out of a natural array. It is kind, frightened and has all their memories. Only one of them can keep the name.

events.name: The weight of a promise
events.text: Every promise the party has broken this year appears as a small stone in their packs. A shrine offers to take the stones, if they make one more promise.

events.name: The talking sword
events.text: A sentient sword stuck in a tree offers itself to whoever pulls it out. It is very powerful and talks constantly about {its feelings|its ex-wielders|food it cannot eat}.
events.check: Athletics DC 15
events.failText: it will not budge, and is offended
events.twist: Its last wielder is still holding the other end, deep inside the tree.

events.name: The memory merchant
events.text: A Magic Society mage offers to buy one bad memory from a party member, for good coin. It would be gone for good, along with what it taught them.

events.name: Last slice of pie
events.text: One slice of {apple pie|honey cake|meat pie} left, and a hungry stray child at the camp's edge watching it. The party member who earned it is also very hungry.

events.name: The wedding gift
events.text: {Newly-weds|An eloping couple|Two old sweethearts} on the road are so poor they have no wedding feast. The party has just enough supplies to give them one, and go hungry tomorrow.

events.name: The runaway's choice
events.text: A girl has run from home to join the Adventure Society. She is brave and clever and twelve. Her worried father is a day behind.
events.twist: She will join one day, and remember who was kind to her.

events.name: The old horse
events.text: A farmer is about to put down his old {horse|ox|donkey}, who can no longer work. The horse looks at the party with soft eyes. Taking it would slow them down.

events.name: Share the fire
events.text: A family of goblins asks to share the party's fire on a freezing night. The next village shoots goblins on sight, and would ask questions.
events.twist: The goblins know a warmer cave, and share it in the morning.

events.name: A gift returned
events.text: A poor fisherwoman insists the party take her finest {fish|crab|eel} in thanks for directions. It is clearly her family's dinner.

events.name: The orphan's blessing
events.text: An orphanage run by {church} asks the party to sponsor one child's training at the Society. It would cost a real share of their savings.
events.cost: 5 bronze spirit coins, if they agree

events.name: Lend the cloak
events.text: A shivering old man asks to borrow a party member's warm cloak for the night. He promises to return it at dawn. He has very honest eyes, and a lot of other people's cloaks.

events.name: The stowaway
events.text: A stowaway is found in the ship's hold. Ship's law says throw her overboard or sell her at the next port. She claims to be a noble heir in hiding.
events.twist: She is, and the people hunting her are on board.

events.name: The hunters on deck
events.text: Two passengers corner the party at night. They know about the stowaway, and offer a share of a large reward to hand her over quietly.

events.name: The cursed village gold
events.text: A village sits on a rich vein of {spirit coin ore|awakening stones|cloud crystal}. Telling the Magic Society would make them rich, and bring every noble house running.

events.name: The lost astral key
events.text: The party finds a key to a sealed astral space, and the Society's records say a team went in and never came out. Opening it might rescue them, or let something out.

events.name: The mercy cut
events.text: A man bitten by a cursed monster begs to be killed before he turns. The nearest Church of the Healer clinic is two days away. He might last that long.

events.name: The ration line
events.text: Supplies are short. One party member has been secretly {eating more|drinking more|feeding a stray from} than their share. They are also the one doing the most fighting.
events.twist: They are pregnant, and have not told anyone.

events.name: The rope
events.text: Two climbers dangle from one rope over a gorge, and the anchor is slipping. The party can hold them both for a moment, but not for long.
events.check: Athletics DC 18 to save both
events.failText: one of them makes the choice for the party, and lets go

events.name: The neighbours' fence
events.text: Two farmers have argued over a fence line for forty years and ask the party to settle it. Both are clearly in love with each other, and neither will admit it.
events.check: Insight DC 13 to see it
events.failText: the party settles the fence, and both farmers look disappointed

events.name: The hermit's rent
events.text: A hermit charges the party one honest answer as rent for camping by his {spring|cave|ancient tree}. He asks the hardest question he can think of.

events.name: The volunteer
events.text: A cheerful man offers to take a punishment owed by someone else, for a fee. He has done it nine times. He would like the party to hire him for a tenth.
events.twist: He is a priest of the Church of Disguise, and wears the faces of the guilty.

events.name: The tidy thief
events.text: Someone has been sneaking into the party's camp each night and tidying it. Nothing is stolen. One small thing is always added: {a button|a feather|a polished pebble}.

events.name: Meeting the tidy thief
events.text: The party catches the night-time tidier: a very small, very neat Runic who wants to come along as a camp steward. She is wanted for theft in three towns.
events.twist: She only steals mess, she says. The towns disagree.

events.name: The broken cart
events.text: A merchant's cart has broken an axle. The party has a spare {axle|wheel|harness}. They also have a long road ahead, and only one spare.

events.name: Water for the stranger
events.text: A parched traveller asks for water in the dry country. The party has just enough to reach the next well, if nothing goes wrong.

events.name: The lost glove
events.text: A child dropped a mitten in the snow a mile back, and is crying about it. Going back costs an hour. It is a very small mitten.

events.name: The fading array
events.text: A natural array that has healed travellers for {centuries|a thousand years|longer than anyone knows} is dying. The party can feed it a monster core to keep it going, or harvest what is left.

events.name: The wishing well's price
events.text: A wishing well grants one wish a year. A village child has saved her wish for her sick grandmother, but gives the party first go, because they look tired.
events.twist: The well whispers to the party: only one wish will come true today.

events.name: The star that fell
events.text: A fallen star lies glowing in a crater, alive and in pain. A Magic Society buyer will pay a fortune. The star asks only to be carried back to the sky.

events.name: Back to the sky
events.text: On the highest hill around, the fallen star asks to be thrown upward with all the party's strength, and promises to remember them.
events.check: Athletics DC 15, with help
events.failText: it falls back, dims a little, and asks to try again tomorrow

events.name: The race to the stone
events.text: Two teams spot a bright awakening stone glinting in a riverbed at the same moment. The other team's youngest is closest, and slipping.
events.twist: Help the youngster, and the other team gives up its claim.

events.name: Ask for payment
events.text: A village the party saved can just afford to pay them, if it sells its {seed grain|plough oxen|church bell}. The reeve brings the purse anyway.

events.name: Wrong time
events.text: Ground where time runs wrong: an hour passes in a minute, or the reverse.

events.name: Astral bleed
events.text: The astral bleeds through, and for a moment another world is visible.

events.name: A messenger
events.text: A messenger of an astral power watches the party, then leaves without a word.

events.name: A wandering entrance
events.text: An astral space entrance that moves a little every hour.

events.name: Out of place
events.text: Monsters that should not exist in this terrain, spawned from magic out of place.

events.name: Resonance
events.text: Essences in the party resonate with something nearby, pulling them toward it.

events.name: The repeating hour
events.text: The same hour happens twice. Everyone notices except the people they meet, who do and say exactly the same things again.

events.name: Gravity takes a break
events.text: For a minute, everything floats a few inches off the ground: people, rocks, puddles.

events.name: The colour drain
events.text: Colour drains out of the world for an hour, then floods back all at once.

events.name: Talking animals
events.text: Every animal the party meets today can talk, and every one of them is rude.

events.name: The astral window
events.text: A window into an astral space hangs in the air, showing a room full of treasure. It closes in ten minutes.

events.name: Swapped voices
events.text: Two party members wake up with each other's voices. It wears off by sundown.

events.name: A second shadow
events.text: One party member's shadow is a step behind them, and it has started to wave.

events.name: The magic garden
events.text: Plants grow while the party watches, flowering and fruiting in a minute, then rotting just as fast.

events.name: Upside-down rain
events.text: It rains upward for an hour, from the puddles into the sky.

events.name: The memory flower
events.text: A flower that, when smelled, brings back one forgotten memory in perfect detail.

events.name: The essence echo
events.text: One party member's essence powers flare on their own for a moment, showing a glimpse of what they might become.

events.name: The house that wasn't
events.text: A house stands where none was on the map. The door is open, dinner is on the table, and the chairs are still warm.

events.name: The time slip
events.text: The party walks around a bend and finds themselves an hour back down the road.

events.name: The magic storm
events.text: A storm of pure magic rolls across the sky, coloured lights and no rain. Anyone touched by it feels a shiver of power.

events.name: The weight of names
events.text: For a day, saying anyone's name aloud makes the speaker forget it for an hour.

events.name: The bigger-inside shrine
events.nod: Doctor Who: the TARDIS
events.text: A tall blue wooden shrine of the Church of the Journey stands at a crossroads, and the room inside is far too big. A tired priest asks if anyone has seen 'the Doctor of Roads'.

events.name: The chicken-legged house
events.nod: Slavic folklore: Baba Yaga's hut on chicken legs
events.text: A cottage on enormous bird legs crouches beside the road. Its owner offers one question, answered truthfully, in exchange for a day's chores.

events.name: Back in the morning
events.nod: Dark Souls: resting at a bonfire respawns enemies
events.text: A shrine with a fire that never goes out. Anyone who rests here wakes fully healed, but the monsters the party killed yesterday are back where they fell, and angry.

events.name: The frozen moment
events.text: Everything stops: birds in the air, a falling leaf, a raindrop. For the party, it lasts one minute.

events.name: A mirror path
events.text: The path splits into two identical roads. Each one has the party already walking on it, far ahead.

events.name: No gods past this point
events.text: A {church} priest has nailed a sign beside an astral space entrance: beyond here, you are on your own. Someone has scrawled underneath: so bring snacks.

events.name: The upside-down entrance
events.text: An astral space entrance hangs upside down in the sky, thirty feet up. A {rope|chain|knotted bedsheet} dangles from it. Someone inside is yelling for help.
events.check: Athletics DC 13
events.failText: the rope snaps and the entrance drifts away before anyone reaches it

events.name: Essence weather
events.text: For an hour, each person's essences show in the air around them: {embers|mist|drifting leaves|tiny sparks}. Normal-rankers watching are very impressed.

events.name: The jealous essence
events.text: One party member's essence trait cantrip refuses to work until they {compliment it|sing to it|apologise to it} out loud. Sincerely. In front of everyone.
events.check: Performance DC 10
events.failText: it sulks until dawn and the cantrip will not cast

events.name: A core that hums
events.text: A monster core lies in the road, humming {a lullaby|a marching song|a tune nobody can place}. Any party member who hums along finds their essences hum back.
events.twist: The core is from a monster none of them killed. Its owner may want it back.

events.name: Pulled by a stone
events.text: One essence user feels a tug, like a hook in the ribs. It leads to a hollow tree, and an awakening stone in a nest of {feathers|glass|old coins}.
events.check: Survival DC 13
events.failText: the tug fades before they find it

events.name: Confluence chorus
events.text: Two people in the party hear their confluences sing to each other, a low chord only they can hear. For the day, they can feel where the other is.
events.twist: The chord grows louder near danger. It hums a warning before the next fight.

events.name: The swapped traits
events.text: Two party members wake with each other's essence traits. The Fire-user is suddenly good at {swimming|stealth|masonry} and very unhappy about it.
events.twist: It swaps back after a sneeze. Anyone who wants it back sooner needs pepper.

events.name: The essence thief bird
events.text: A {magpie|crow|small green parrot} with glowing eyes follows the party, stealing tiny sparks of essence power. Each spark it steals makes it slightly larger.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13
events.failText: by nightfall it is the size of a dog and stole someone's cantrip for the day
events.twist: Befriend it and it brings back a gift: a shiny awakening stone fragment.

events.name: Divine static
events.text: Near this old battlefield, divine essences crackle like wool in winter. Priests in the party get small shocks whenever they touch metal.
events.check: Constitution save DC 10
events.failText: a priest drops their weapon twice and has disadvantage on attack rolls until noon

events.name: The tasting stone
events.text: A smooth rock that tells anyone who licks it the name of their confluence, {loudly|in rhyme|in a terrible accent}. Someone has scratched a long list of results on its side.

events.name: A spirit coin spring
events.text: A small spring bubbles up cloudy blue water. In the basin below, {a dozen|twenty|three} iron spirit coins have formed like pebbles.
events.twist: A coin farm three miles away has noticed its output dropping.

events.name: Essence echo in stone
events.text: An outcrop is carved with the shapes of a thousand hands. Press a palm to it and the stone glows the colour of your essences, then remembers you.
events.twist: The stone remembers a dead Bronze-ranker's hand that matches one party member's exactly.

events.name: The unwanted gift
events.text: A beggar offers the party an essence for one iron spirit coin. The essence is real. The beggar will not say where it came from, and will not stop smiling.
events.twist: It is a Sin essence. Its last owner is the beggar's shadow.

events.name: Cores in bloom
events.text: Monster cores lie in a field like seeds, and small {pale|bright red|star-shaped} flowers are growing out of them. Each flower is a different shape of magic.

events.name: The rank pressure
events.text: The ground shudders and the sky flashes from somewhere miles away: a Gold-ranker fighting at full strength. Normal-rank animals lie flat. Whatever caused it is {very angry|grieving|fighting something}, and very far off.
events.check: Constitution save DC 13
events.failText: someone gains a level of exhaustion from the pressure

events.name: The stone that asks
events.text: An awakening stone sits on a fence post. When picked up, it asks politely which essence it should go to. It has opinions about each.
events.twist: It refuses the obvious choice.

events.name: Resonant chimes
events.text: Wind chimes made of shed {monster scales|old spirit coins|seashells} hang from a roadside tree. When an essence user passes, they play a short tune just for them.

events.name: Quintessence frost
events.text: Every leaf and stone in a little hollow is rimed with a glittering frost that is not cold. Crafters would call it quintessence.
events.check: Arcana DC 13
events.failText: it melts to nothing in the hand before anyone works out how to keep it

events.name: Overcharged
events.text: Mana runs so thick here that every spell or power used today goes off twice as bright and twice as loud. Stealth with magic is impossible.

events.name: Dry ground
events.text: A mile of land so empty of magic that essence powers fizzle and cantrips sputter. A Normal-rank farmer here says it is the most peaceful place in the world.

events.name: The bargaining core
events.text: A cracked monster core starts talking: it wants to be sold to {the Magic Society|a nice family|a collector}, not eaten, and it is willing to negotiate.

events.name: Rainbow rain
events.text: The rain falls in colours, each drop a different shade. Clothes come out of it {striped|spotted|a fetching purple} and stay that way for a week.

events.name: The upward snow
events.text: Snow rises from the ground into the clouds. The {fields|slopes|rooftops} are left bare and warm, and the clouds look very full.
events.twist: By evening the clouds give it all back in one go.

events.name: A thunderclap that talks
events.text: Thunder rolls overhead, and inside it is a voice saying one party member's name. Just once.
events.twist: A priest of the Storm would say that is a compliment. Probably.

events.name: Lightning in a jar
events.text: A bolt of lightning strikes a {jar|bottle|teapot} left on a fencepost and stays inside it, crackling. Its owner has left a note: finders keepers.
events.twist: Thrown, it deals 3d6 lightning damage once. Opened, it deals that to the opener.

events.name: The wind with an opinion
events.text: The wind blows only in the direction the party is not going. When they turn round, it turns round too. When they give up, it sighs and stops.
events.check: Survival DC 13
events.failText: half a day is lost arguing with the weather

events.name: Fog that keeps faces
events.text: The fog holds the faces of people who walked through it before. Some look {lost|angry|peaceful}. One looks exactly like a party member.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13
events.failText: someone follows the familiar face off the path, and tomorrow's Survival check has disadvantage

events.name: Mana aurora
events.text: Green and gold curtains of light ripple overhead in daylight. The Magic Society calls it a mana aurora. Spells cast under it are a little stronger.

events.name: The rain cloud pet
events.text: A small rain cloud, the size of a {sheep|pony|large dog}, attaches itself to the party. It waters anything they plant and cries when they leave.

events.name: The cloud returns
events.text: The little rain cloud is back, proud, with a friend: a small storm cloud. They have brought {a fish|a frog|someone's washing}.

events.name: Heat that sings
events.text: The heat shimmer hums in a long, low chord. Anyone who hums the same note feels cool all day and ignores the heat.
events.check: Performance DC 10

events.name: Hail of glass
events.text: Hail of clear glass beads falls for a minute, sharp and cold. Anyone caught in the open makes a DC 12 Dexterity save or takes 1d6 slashing damage.

events.name: The sky ship ghost
events.text: A sky ship sails overhead, all lamps lit, every sail full. It casts no shadow. Its crew wave, then the ship is gone.
events.twist: The ship was lost over the Drowning Compass twenty years ago. A captain's widow in port would give a lot to hear this.

events.name: Stars at noon
events.text: The sky darkens at noon and the stars come out for one minute. One of them {winks|spells a name|falls, very slowly}.

events.name: Weather jar seller
events.text: A woman with a cart of corked jars sells weather: {one sunny afternoon|a light breeze|a small fog for hiding}, each labelled in crayon.
events.twist: One jar is labelled do not open. It is a storm. She would like it gone.

events.name: The tame squall
events.text: A magic squall rolls up, sniffs the party like a dog, and rolls away again. Something on the wind smelled of the Storm's favour.

events.name: The sunbeam path
events.text: A single sunbeam breaks through the cloud and lies along the way like a carpet. Walking in it, nobody tires.

events.name: Moonlight that pools
events.text: Moonlight gathers in hollows like {milk|silver water|thin honey}. Scoop it up and it glows in a cup until dawn, bright as a lantern.

events.name: The slow puddle
events.text: A puddle by the road shows ripples from rain that fell {an hour|a day|a week} ago. Drop a stone in and the splash takes a full minute to rise.

events.name: Yesterday on the road
events.text: The party passes themselves going the other way, looking a day younger and arguing about {breakfast|the map|whose turn it is to cook}. Their past selves do not notice them.
events.twist: One past self drops something. It is still on the road, and it was never lost.

events.name: The borrowed hour
events.text: Time pools in a dip in the land. Rest there for ten minutes and it counts as an hour: anyone can take a short rest without losing travel time.

events.name: The ageing stretch
events.text: For a mile, every step makes hair and nails grow. By the end, {beards reach belts|plaits reach knees|nails curl like claws}. It all falls out by morning.

events.name: A minute too late
events.text: Every sound the party makes arrives a few seconds late today: footsteps, speech, the clink of a cup. Stealth checks have advantage, and conversations are hard work.

events.name: The stopped mill
events.text: A watermill frozen mid-turn, its water hanging in the air like glass. A miller stands inside with {flour|a mug of ale|a startled cat} halfway to the floor.
events.check: Arcana DC 15
events.twist: Restart the moment and the miller finishes his sentence: a warning about the road ahead. Advantage on tomorrow's Survival check.

events.name: Hourglass sand
events.text: Fine silver sand drifts across the road in a line, flowing uphill. Scholars say it marks where the Keeper of Moments smoothed a ripple in time.
events.twist: A pinch kept in a vial lets one person reroll an initiative roll, once.

events.name: A day remembered twice
events.text: Everyone wakes certain that today already happened. They remember the weather, the food, a small accident. Then the small accident starts to happen.
events.check: Perception DC 13
events.failText: the accident happens anyway, and a day of rations ends up in the mud

events.name: The echo of a battle
events.text: A battle replays itself across a field: {Iron|Bronze}-rank adventurers holding a line against a surge, decades ago. They fall where they fell. The grass there grows red.

events.name: Lost minutes
events.text: Everyone checks the sun at once. An hour has gone missing, and every pack is {neatly repacked|full of wildflowers|tied shut with ribbon} by someone with very tidy habits.

events.name: The quick sunset
events.text: The sun sets in a minute, rises again a minute later, and carries on as if embarrassed. Every {rooster|dog|owl} within a mile loses its mind.

events.name: The forgotten word
events.text: For a day, nobody in the party can remember the word for {spoon|horse|left}. Everyone they meet has forgotten it too.

events.name: The clock tree
events.text: An old oak with rings that tick. Hold an ear to the bark and hear one moment from its long life: a lovers' quarrel, a Messenger passing, a child laughing.

events.name: Slow arrows
events.text: A patch of air where thrown things drift. A thrown {stone|knife|apple} takes half a minute to land. Ranged attacks inside it are useless, which is worth knowing.
events.twist: Something left a crossbow bolt hanging there, long ago. It is still on its way to whoever it was meant for.

events.name: The memory fog
events.text: A pale fog that smells of {home|baking bread|a lost friend}. Inside it, each person relives their happiest memory, and has to choose to leave it.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13
events.failText: someone lingers half a day, smiling

events.name: Remembering a stranger
events.text: A {woman|young Leonid|grey-haired Runic} on the road greets the party by name and thanks them for saving their life next year. They will not say more.
events.twist: She is a Normal-rank farmer and has no idea how she knows.

events.name: The skipping stone road
events.text: The road skips like a scratched record. Every few minutes the party finds themselves a hundred yards further on, with no memory of walking it.

events.name: The unending afternoon
events.text: The afternoon lasts as long as two. The sun hangs still until everyone is sick of it.

events.name: Echo of a prayer
events.text: At a ruined shrine of the {church}, the party hears a prayer said here a hundred years ago: someone asking that travellers on this road come home safe.

events.name: A letter from tomorrow
events.text: A sealed letter lies on a milestone, addressed to one party member in their own handwriting. It says only: {take the left fork|trust the goat|do not eat the soup}.

events.name: The letter makes sense
events.text: The moment from the letter arrives exactly as written. Anyone who followed the advice gains inspiration. Anyone who ignored it finds out why.

events.name: The keeper of sands
events.text: An hourglass the height of a person stands alone in the {grass|sand|snow}, emptying sideways. Nobody touches it. Everyone feels watched by something very patient.
events.twist: When the last grain falls, the party's next day of travel takes no time at all.

events.name: A door in the wind
events.text: A plain wooden door stands in the {field|dune|surf}, attached to nothing. Behind it is a sunny room with a bowl of fruit and a sign: please wipe your feet.
events.twist: It is an astral space entrance. The fruit is real and heals 1d4 hit points per piece.

events.name: The sealed entrance
events.text: A ring of Adventure Society warning posts around a shimmering {rock face|tree stump|pool}. A notice reads: astral space, unopened, do not knock. Something on the other side is knocking.
events.twist: The knock follows a pattern. Anyone with Arcana DC 15 recognises it as a request to be let out.

events.name: The space with a queue
events.text: An astral space entrance has opened by the road, and {twenty|forty|a dozen very tired} Iron-rankers have formed an orderly queue. A Society clerk is selling numbered tickets.
events.twist: The space only lets one team in a day. Number one has been camped here for a week.

events.name: The breathing doorway
events.text: A cave mouth that breathes. Warm air out, cold air in, slow as sleep. The Society has not charted it. The breath smells faintly of {rain|copper|spice}.
events.check: Survival DC 13
events.failText: someone wanders too close and comes back with frost on their eyelashes and no memory of the last hour

events.name: Astral weather
events.text: For an hour the sky turns the deep violet of the astral, scattered with distant lights that are worlds. Then the blue comes back, slightly embarrassed.
events.twist: One of the distant lights blinks out while the party watches.

events.name: A crack in the air
events.text: A hairline crack hangs in the air at head height. Through it: darkness, and a sound like {a crowd holding its breath|distant bells|someone snoring}.
events.check: Arcana DC 15
events.twist: It is a failing astral space boundary. The Magic Society would pay to hear of it.

events.name: Leftovers of a cleared space
events.text: Where an astral space collapsed, odd things lie scattered on the ground: {a glass apple|a key with no teeth|a bronze feather}, still warm.

events.name: The tidy dungeon
events.text: An astral space entrance has a welcome mat, a boot scraper and a polite note: closed for cleaning, monsters back on Fourday.

events.name: The silent shrine
events.text: A priest of the {church} sits outside an astral space entrance, praying hard. Her team went in three days ago, and her god cannot follow them.
events.twist: She will pay well for anyone who goes in and brings them out.

events.name: The made space
events.text: An astral space entrance with straight edges, like a door frame cut by a tool. A sigil of gears is {scratched into the rock|painted in blood|burnt into a tree} beside it.
events.twist: Builder cultists are feeding this space. Fresh spirit coin dust on the ground says they were here this morning.

events.name: Leaking light
events.text: A shaft of light from a sky that is not this one falls across the path, gold and warm. Anyone who stands in it has advantage on one saving throw before nightfall.

events.name: The astral tide
events.text: The ground goes briefly see-through, showing a great dark ocean beneath with lights drifting in it. Then it is soil again. Everyone walks a little more carefully.
events.twist: For a moment, something large in the dark ocean turned to look up.

events.name: Lost from a space
events.text: A confused monster is sitting by the road: a {flower-headed hound|stone owl|small polite crab}. It spawned inside an astral space and came out of the wrong door.
events.twist: Return it to its space and the space rewards the party on their way out.

events.name: A Messenger feather
events.text: A single white feather taller than a person, lying in a {scorched ring|frozen puddle|circle of dead grass}. Birds will not land near it. Old stories say Messengers came once before.
events.twist: The feather is still warm, and it points north.

events.name: Two skies
events.text: Look up and there are two skies, one over the other: this one, and a {red|green|starless black} one with three suns. They drift apart by noon.

events.name: The astral market stall
events.text: A stall stands in the {road|reeds|dunes} where an entrance flickers. A cloaked trader sells goods from the space behind her: odd, cheap, and only today.
events.twist: The coins she takes turn to sand once she is gone. Nobody is cheated, but the economy is confused.

events.name: A window on the sea floor
events.text: Under the hull, the sea goes clear as glass for a mile, showing a drowned astral space entrance glowing on the bottom.
events.check: Athletics DC 15
events.failText: the dive is too deep, and the glow fades

events.name: The door that follows
events.text: A door-shaped shimmer has been following the party since dawn, always a hundred yards behind. When they stop, it stops. When they {wave|shout|run}, it does nothing.

events.name: The door catches up
events.text: The shimmering door is beside the camp this morning, open. Inside is a small astral space shaped like the party's own camp, with one extra tent.
events.twist: The extra tent holds a gift and a note: thank you for not running.

events.name: The walking stones
events.text: A line of standing stones has moved since the map was drawn. Today they are {crossing the road|standing in a lake|lined up as if queuing}.

events.name: A natural array
events.text: Rocks, trees and a stream form a perfect pattern, a natural array humming with power. Anyone who sleeps inside it wakes with one spent spell slot or power back.
events.check: Arcana DC 15
events.failText: nobody can find the centre, and the hum just gives everyone a headache

events.name: The sulking forest
events.text: The trees lean away from the party as they pass, rustling disapprovingly. Somebody here once {lit a very large fire|carved their name in everything|sold firewood}.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13
events.failText: the branches drop pine cones on everyone all day

events.name: The singing dunes
events.text: The dunes sing as the wind crosses them, each one a different note. At dusk they sing together, and the party can follow the tune to water.

events.name: Glass footprints
events.text: A line of footprints fused into glass crosses the sand, each one still warm. They are {huge|bare and small|clawed}, and they lead toward the Glass Sea.
events.twist: At the end of the trail, a Smoulder pilgrim sits meditating. She made them, walking barefoot.

events.name: The river that changes its mind
events.text: The river flows {upstream|in a circle|straight up a waterfall} for an hour, then goes back to normal. The fish look exhausted.

events.name: The thirsty field
events.text: A field of {wheat|barley|tall rice} turns its heads to follow the party, as sunflowers follow the sun. At the far edge, every stalk points at the same person.
events.twist: The field belongs to a hedge-witch who wants to meet whoever it chose.

events.name: The mangrove that gives
events.text: A mangrove tree lowers a root like a hand and offers the party a basket of fruit someone left in its branches years ago. It is still fresh.

events.name: Sea glass shallows
events.text: The sea runs shallow over a reef of {green|blue|amber} sea glass that glows from beneath. Sailors call it lucky to trail a hand in it.
events.twist: Anyone who does has advantage on their next saving throw against drowning or the sea.

events.name: The whirlpool garden
events.text: A ring of small calm whirlpools spins on the open sea, each with a single flower turning at its centre. Merfolk tend it, and they do not like visitors.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13
events.failText: the merfolk splash the deck and send the ship the long way round

events.name: The cliff of faces
events.text: A cliff shows the faces of everyone who has ever fallen from it, carved by no hand. A new one is forming, and it looks {familiar|surprised|like it is laughing}.

events.name: Moss that maps
events.text: Glowing moss on the north side of every tree spells out the route ahead in plain lines, like a map someone grew.
events.check: Survival DC 10

events.name: The breathing mountain
events.text: The mountain breathes: a slow wind out of every crevice at dawn, a slow wind in at dusk. Cloud Clan folk set their day by it.

events.name: The polite bog
events.text: A bog that burps loudly whenever someone steps wrong, then apologises in a {deep, wet|tiny, squeaky|very posh} voice.

events.name: Thorn hedge of sleep
events.text: A wall of briars blocks the old road. Beyond it, a manor sleeps, with servants asleep at the gate and dust on their shoulders.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Sleeping Beauty and the briar hedge
events.check: Athletics DC 15
events.failText: the thorns cause a deep drowsiness, and someone sleeps through the afternoon

events.name: The pocket valley
events.text: A narrow gap in the rocks opens on a green valley far too large to fit, with its own warm sun and {a herd of white deer|an orchard|a silent village}. It closes at dusk.
events.twist: The Drift Hosts know it, and leave an offering of salt at the gap.

events.name: The heidel stones
events.text: Round grey stones lie in the grass like sleeping heidels, and every few hours one of them {rolls over|sighs|trots a few feet and stops}.

events.name: The giant beanstalk
events.text: A beanstalk as thick as a tower climbs out of a farmer's plot and disappears into the clouds. The farmer insists it is a perfectly normal size for this time of year.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Jack and the Beanstalk
events.twist: A cloud castle sits at the top. The Cloud Clans want a word about who built it.

events.name: The reflecting salt
events.text: The salt flat reflects the sky so perfectly that the party walks among clouds. Their reflections walk half a step ahead.
events.twist: The reflections know the way. Follow them for advantage on tomorrow's Survival check.

events.name: The tide that stays out
events.text: The sea draws back a mile and simply stays there, leaving fish flapping and an old wreck in plain view. Locals are already scavenging.
events.check: Perception DC 13
events.failText: the tide comes back all at once, and someone loses a day of rations to it

events.name: Green lightning forest
events.text: A grove struck by a mana storm long ago. The trees are stone, and the {birds|squirrels|deer} in them are stone too, still mid-song or mid-leap.

events.name: The fairy ring
events.text: A ring of white mushrooms with dancing music faintly inside. Step in and the party loses a day, or so it seems to them.
events.nod: Folklore: fairy rings and lost time, as in Rip Van Winkle
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13
events.failText: whoever stepped in comes out convinced a year has passed, and is shaky until tomorrow

events.name: Reflections out of step
events.text: In every pool, blade and window, the party's reflections run a few seconds late. In one of them, someone extra is {waving|weeping|pointing at the road}.
events.twist: The waving reflection wants to warn them about something at the next water they cross.

events.name: The heavy shadow
events.text: One party member's shadow has become heavy. It drags behind them like a sack, and they walk at half speed until it is fed some lamplight.
events.check: Arcana DC 13
events.failText: the party loses half a day carrying a shadow

events.name: Borrowed eyes
events.text: For an hour, each person sees through the eyes of the person to their {left|right}. Walking is hard. Holding hands helps.

events.name: Feather hair
events.text: One party member's hair turns to {feathers|leaves|fine copper wire} overnight. It is warm, and birds love it.
events.twist: It changes back after a kind word from a stranger.

events.name: The lightness
events.text: Everyone weighs a quarter of what they should for a day. {Long jumps|Stair climbing|Running downhill} is glorious. Strong wind is terrifying.

events.name: Taste of colour
events.text: For the morning, everyone can taste colours. Grass tastes of mint, the sky of cold water, and one party member's {cloak|boots|hair} tastes absolutely awful.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 10
events.failText: someone is so distracted by the taste of the sky that they walk into a ditch

events.name: The truthful tongue
events.text: Water from a roadside well makes the drinker unable to lie for an hour. A merchant from {faction} has just drunk a bucketful, and he is very upset.

events.name: Night eyes
events.text: Everyone wakes with eyes that glow faintly gold. They have darkvision out to 60 feet until the next dawn.

events.name: The quiet voice
events.text: One party member speaks, and no sound comes out. Instead, the nearest {crow|goat|parrot} repeats their words, perfectly, a moment later.
events.check: Arcana DC 13
events.failText: the crow keeps their voice until sunset and will not stop talking

events.name: Glowing footsteps
events.text: The party leaves glowing {gold|green|pink} footprints all day. Children in the next village follow the trail, delighted, and bring the party a cake.

events.name: The twin
events.text: Someone who looks exactly like one party member is on the road ahead, waving. When they meet, the twin shrugs and walks into a tree, and is gone.
events.twist: The twin left a single footprint, facing back the way the party came.

events.name: The ache of a wound
events.text: Old wounds ache together across the party, all at the same moment. Something nearby remembers violence. A grave cairn stands on the next rise.
events.twist: Leave it alone, or disturb an Iron-rank team's resting place.

events.name: Lucky itch
events.text: One party member's palm itches all day. Local wisdom says money is coming. Later, they find {a spirit coin in a boot|an iron coin in bread|a bronze spirit coin in a bird's nest}.

events.name: The tiny curse
events.text: A hedge-witch at a crossroads, insulted by something the party said, curses them to sneeze whenever someone says the word {road|horse|lunch}.
events.check: Persuasion DC 13
events.failText: the curse lasts the rest of the journey

events.name: The lingering scent
events.text: One party member suddenly smells of springtime, faintly, like an outworlder. Dogs follow them. A Magic Society clerk on the road asks a lot of questions.
events.twist: It is a passing whiff of astral air, and it fades. The clerk does not believe that.

events.name: Old hands
events.text: For an hour, each person's hands know a skill they never learned. The party briefly includes a {weaver|lute player|surgeon|stonemason}, and the knowledge fades with a sigh.

events.name: The cold hand
events.text: Someone in the party feels a cold hand slip into theirs as they walk. It squeezes once, and lets go at the next milestone.

events.name: The drink me bottle
events.text: A small bottle on a tree stump with a paper tag: drink me. Anyone who does shrinks to the size of a cat for an hour.
events.nod: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland: the drink me bottle
events.twist: A second bottle, labelled eat me, sits behind the first.

events.name: Sea legs
events.text: Everyone on board can walk on the water for an hour, as long as they do not look down. Several sailors have already looked down.
events.check: Wisdom save DC 10
events.failText: someone looks down and has to be fished out

events.name: A spawn in slow motion
events.text: Magic gathers in the air ahead, swirling into the shape of a monster over an hour. The party can watch it form, or leave before it finishes.
events.check: Arcana DC 13
events.twist: Strike the swirl at the right moment and it collapses into a monster core instead.

events.name: The wrong spawn
events.text: A monster spawns right in front of the party: {a fearsome|an enormous|a very confused} rabbit made entirely of {cheese|bread|soap}. It is as surprised as they are.

events.name: Spawn in the wake
events.text: The ship's wake glows, and small {fish-like|crab-like|eel-like} monsters form in it, swimming after the ship like ducklings. Nobody has the heart to stop them.

events.name: The ducklings grow
events.text: The glowing fish in the wake have grown to the size of dogs overnight. They still follow the ship. They are getting hungry.
events.check: Animal Handling DC 13
events.failText: they snap at the oars and someone takes 1d6 piercing damage

events.name: The counting old man
events.text: An old man sits on his porch counting spawns on his fingers. He has reached {nine|ten|eleven} today. He says the last surge started at twelve.

events.name: Surge-thick air
events.text: The air feels thick enough to chew. Small monsters blink into being at the edge of sight and blink out again before anyone can turn.
events.twist: Pay attention to the pattern: it points away from where the next real spawn will come.

events.name: The abandoned village
events.text: A village emptied for the surge. Doors left open, dinners left out, a child's drawing of a monster pinned to a door: go away.
events.twist: One house is still lived in. An old woman refuses to leave her cat.

events.name: Tide-readers' warning
events.text: A Drift Host tide-reader rides up on a heidel and warns the party that the Wandering Tide is pooling in the valley ahead. Go round, or go through fast.
events.check: Survival DC 13
events.failText: the party goes the long way and loses half a day

events.name: Monster egg
events.text: A monster has spawned as an egg, which is not supposed to happen. It sits by the road, {warm|ice cold|faintly glowing}, and it is wobbling.

events.name: The egg hatches
events.text: The strange egg hatches overnight. The small monster inside looks at the nearest party member and decides they are its mother.

events.name: The core rain
events.text: Something huge died high in the air, and tiny monster cores patter down like {hail|seeds|warm rain}. A few are worth keeping.

events.name: The spawning pond
events.text: A still pond where monsters rise from the bottom like bubbles. Each one is smaller than the last. The water is getting lower.
events.twist: Something at the bottom is drinking the magic. It has noticed the party.

events.name: Monsters that wait
events.text: Freshly spawned monsters stand in a line along the ridge, perfectly still, watching the party pass. They do not attack. They are waiting for something else.

events.name: Spawn tax
events.text: A Society checkpoint asks each traveller to declare any monsters that spawned on them in the last day. The clerk has a form for it. It is {very long|in triplicate|written in verse}.

events.name: The crossroads bargain
events.text: At midnight, at the crossroads, a figure in a black hat offers to teach one party member any skill in exchange for {a memory|their shadow|their middle name}.
events.nod: Folklore: the deal at the crossroads at midnight
events.twist: The skill is real: proficiency in one skill for the rest of the journey.

events.name: The piper
events.text: Music from a reed pipe drifts over the hill, and every animal the party owns turns to follow it. So does one party member, a little.
events.nod: Folklore: the Pied Piper of Hamelin
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13
events.failText: animals and one person wander off, and the party loses half a day bringing them back

events.name: Guess the name
events.text: A small grumpy spirit sits on the party's pack and will not get off until someone guesses its name. It gives one clue every hour, and none of them help.
events.nod: Fairy tale: Rumpelstiltskin and the name-guessing game
events.check: Insight DC 15
events.failText: it gets bored at sunset and leaves, taking the cheese

events.name: The wishing well
events.text: A well with a sign: one wish, one iron spirit coin. Drop a coin and the well grants a small wish exactly as worded, and no more.
events.twist: Previous wishes are carved on the stones. Some were badly worded.

events.name: The hungry lantern
events.text: A paper lantern floats beside the path, lit from inside by nothing. It leads the way if fed a spirit coin, and {sulks|sings|flickers rudely} if refused.

events.name: A spirit at the hearth
events.text: A small house spirit climbs out of the campfire and warms its hands beside the party. It asks for a story and leaves a blessing of the Hearth in return.

events.name: The cursed boot
events.text: A single {boot|glove|hat} lies by the road. Whoever picks it up cannot put it down: it hops after them, faithful as a dog.
events.twist: Its pair is a day ahead, hopping after a very tired Silver-ranker.

events.name: Wandering lights
events.text: Small blue lights dance over the marsh, and every map-reader in the party is suddenly sure they lead the right way. They do not.
events.nod: Folklore: the will-o'-the-wisp
events.check: Wisdom save DC 13
events.failText: the party follows the lights, and tomorrow's Survival check has disadvantage

events.name: The coin that comes back
events.text: An iron spirit coin turns up in the party's purse no matter how many times it is spent. Traders it was paid to look puzzled and then furious.
events.twist: A coin farm stamped it wrong. The farm wants it back very badly.

events.name: The sword in the rock
events.text: A sword stands in a boulder at a market cross, with a queue of hopefuls, a pie stall and a Society clerk taking names. Every hour, someone tries.
events.nod: Arthurian legend: the sword in the stone
events.check: Athletics DC 18
events.twist: It comes out for whoever is not trying. It is a very ordinary sword.

events.name: The mimic shrine
events.text: A small shrine to the {church} with a full offering bowl. When someone reaches for a coin, the shrine yawns, shows a lot of teeth, and goes back to sleep.
events.nod: D&D: the mimic
events.twist: Feed it a monster core and it spits out a better one.

events.name: The lonely scarecrow
events.text: A scarecrow waves to the party, and keeps waving until they wave back. Then it does a little {dance|bow|cartwheel}.

events.name: The wishing paw
events.text: A dried monster paw hangs from a dead tree, three of its five claws curled shut. A note beneath it reads: please, do not.
events.nod: The Monkey's Paw: wishes with a terrible price
events.twist: It grants one more wish, exactly. It always takes something of the same weight.

events.name: Sparks on metal
events.text: The air is charged. Every buckle and blade sparks when touched, and anyone in metal armour makes a DC 10 Constitution save or has disadvantage on attack rolls until noon.

events.name: A patch of wild magic
events.text: Loose mana hangs over this stretch. The first spell or essence power used today has a strange side effect: {flowers bloom|hair turns blue|a small rain cloud appears|everyone hiccups}.
events.nod: D&D: the wild magic surge table

events.name: The quiet waystone
events.text: An old waystone soaks up magic. Light spells and glowing essence effects go dark within ten feet of it. Good for hiding, bad for reading.

events.name: Glowing stream
events.text: A stream runs faintly blue with dissolved mana. A DC 10 Medicine or Arcana check shows it is safe to drink, and it tastes of mint.

events.name: Mana sickness
events.text: The magic here is thick enough to turn stomachs. Everyone makes a DC 12 Constitution save or is poisoned for an hour.

events.name: An old ward post
events.text: A carved ward post from some long-gone village still glows faintly. Monsters steer around it. Camp here and nothing troubles the night.

events.name: Floating stones
events.text: Rocks hang knee-high across the path, bobbing gently. Crossing quickly takes a DC 10 Acrobatics check.
events.failText: someone trips, and picking a slow way through costs half a day

events.name: Cold fire
events.text: A patch of ground where fire will not catch. Tinder smokes and dies. It is {a cold supper|raw fish|stale bread} tonight unless someone has a magical flame.

events.name: A cracked circle
events.text: A broken teleport circle lies in the grass, its runes half scrubbed away. A DC 15 Arcana check reads where it once sent travellers, and points the way.

events.name: Coin moths
events.text: Pale moths that feed on loose magic cover a dead tree. Their old cocoons, split and empty, each hold a single cloudy iron spirit coin.

events.name: A page of the Book
events.text: A single page of glowing script drifts down from a clear sky. Whoever reads it understands magic a little better: proficiency in Arcana for a week.
events.twist: Scholars who venerate the Celestial Book would pay anything for it. Reading it makes it blank.

events.name: The ship that asks for letters
events.text: A grey ship pulls alongside in the mist. Its crew hand over a bundle of letters to deliver ashore. Every name on them is a hundred years dead.
events.nod: Sea folklore: the Flying Dutchman and its letters home

events.name: The winged shadow
events.text: A vast winged shadow sweeps across the land from a cloudless sky. Every animal goes silent. Old priests on the road begin to pray.
events.twist: Something in the astral has looked at this world. The Magic Society will want every detail.

events.name: The rainy roadside spirit
events.text: A large, soft, grey spirit stands at a roadside stop in the rain, holding a leaf over its head. Offer it shelter and it gives a gift of seeds.
events.nod: My Neighbour Totoro: the bus stop in the rain

events.name: This is fine
events.text: An outworlder sits drinking tea while a small magic squall sets the grass around him gently alight. He says it is fine, then explains a picture of a dog from his world.
events.nod: Meme: the This is fine dog in a burning room

events.name: The wall-clipper
events.text: An outworlder keeps running into the corner of a ruined wall, again and again. He says in his world, gamers call it speedrunning, and one day he will clip through.
events.nod: Video games: speedrunning and clipping through walls
events.twist: Today, thanks to a strange astral flicker, he does. He reappears a mile ahead, delighted.

events.name: The loop expert
events.text: An outworlder stops the party to ask what day it is. On hearing it, she groans. She says this is the sixth time, like a film called Groundhog Day, and asks for help.
events.nod: Groundhog Day (1993 film)
events.twist: She is wrong. She is just very bad at calendars. The party may never convince her.

events.name: The wardrobe in the ruin
events.text: A wardrobe stands upright in a burnt-out {manor|inn|farmhouse}. Behind the coats is snow, a pine forest and a single lit lamp post.
events.nod: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe: the wardrobe and the lamp post
events.twist: It is a small astral space. The snow is warm, and somebody has built a snowman with an Adventure Society badge.

events.name: The singing stone
events.text: A stone by the road sings one verse of a song nobody knows, about {a lost crown|a drowned bell|a road that never ends}, and stops mid-line.

events.name: The last verse
events.text: Another stone, many miles on, sings the last verse of the song. It names a {hill|ruin|well} nearby where something old is buried.

events.name: A seed from the sky
events.text: A glowing seed the size of a fist falls from the clouds and lands at the party's feet, warm as a heartbeat.

events.name: The sky tree
events.text: Where the seed was dropped or planted, a sapling of {silver|gold|glass-clear} leaves has grown overnight. Each leaf, chewed, heals 1d4 hit points.

events.name: The shadow walks off
events.text: At noon, one party member's shadow peels off the ground and wanders away into the {trees|reeds|rocks}. It does not look back.

events.name: The shadow comes home
events.text: The missing shadow comes back at dawn, looking pleased with itself, with a bit of someone else's shadow caught in its teeth.
events.twist: Somewhere nearby, a very angry Silver-ranker has a hole in their shadow.

events.name: An ember of the Phoenix
events.text: A feather of golden fire drifts across the party's path. Anyone who touches it feels the edge of the world, and wakes the next day fully rested.
events.twist: It is an ember of the World-Phoenix. It belongs to whoever guards a world's borders.

events.name: The rising island
events.text: An island rises out of the sea in the morning, steaming and covered in {shells|old statues|sleeping crabs} and ruins. By sunset it will sink again.
events.check: Survival DC 15
events.failText: the party leaves late and has to swim the last stretch as it goes under
